reviews.comment: Never take is professor if you want to learn from his class.

Discrete is known to be an EASY intro to cs course, but drew makes it difficult. Recitations feel mandatory. Only cs1800 instructor to give us a project. Boring lecturer, does not explain well. I'm a 3rd year CE/CS major and somehow this class is harder than my higher level cs classes.

Good class structure and really good lectures, but it definitely gets harder towards the end of the semester, and the material gets more theoretical/harder to follow, so it's easy to fall off/stop paying attention towards the end, which can have a substantial grade impact.

Drew was awesome. Theory Of Comp is hard in general, but I really like the quiz and homework set up. There was very little that was unexpected and he prepared you well. He is so awesome personally, as long as you pay attention. I love him hes so goated
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a good professor, but unlike most classes, it's actually somewhat hard to get a good grade in CS3800. He is very reasonable and helps students even outside typical work hours through the online forum. My only complaint is his handwriting, and I really think he should just type out his slides.

if u take his class ur choosing the more challenging route. hes really nice but im a ds major and didnt need to take algo so his "setting you up for algo" was not helpful for me and just made the class more difficult. Trust i work hard and this is the only B on my transcript for a reason.

Yeah this guy is the goat. His classes are test heavy, but he sets you up to succeed. The tests do not deviate from what he wants you to learn, and it's pretty obvious what that is. Taking theory of comp w him right now, and not much has changed. If you don't want busy work and actually want to learn this is your guy.

Definitely a way harder class with him than with other professors. However, this sets you up better for Algo in the long run. You should take the time to make sure you understand everything as you learn it so that you aren't overwhelmed when studying for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Insanely hard intro level class. Most ended with Bs or lower and the homeworks were a lot. Does not provide support to students and will not explain well in class. I attended every class and he does a terrible job at explaining. I'm a smart student but this class took it out of me do not take it with him unless you are a teacher's pet

The class was challenging, but definitely not anything unmanageable. As long as you pay attention during lectures, particularly the practice problems we do, you should be able to complete the HWs and quizzes just fine. Drew is always happy to help clarify/re-explain concepts, and I genuinely feel that I learned a lot from the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Quickly switches through topics without fully explaining the concepts. Will include things on exams that he barely went over in class. Take someone else if you can.

Professor Van der Poel is the best professor at Northeastern by far. Explains concepts so clearly and makes learning fun. He does make the class a little tough but it is 100% manageable if you put the effort in and would really recommend him to anyone deciding

Drew is a nice professor, but the course he taught was VERY difficult for an introductory discrete class. His section was at least double the work of discrete sections in the fall semester. I don't recommend anyone take him for discrete or discrete in the spring at all. You will be doing more work and getting a worse grade than the fall sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drew is a nice prof, but the class was very challenging. He's willing to help in class and office hours. Most of the grade is based on 2 midterms that are each worth 26% of the grade. They were also each only 26 points which made it harder to get a high grade. For an intro class to logic, he made it harder than it was. Other sections were easier.

Professor van der Poel attempts to help and provide resources for his students, but this class is impossible to do well in. Homework is extremely hard, class lectures do not prepare you for HW or tests. For an intro level logic course this class is extremely difficult. Would not take again.

Drew is a really nice guy, but this class is super hard to do well in. There are 2 midterms each are worth 26% (52% total) very little other opportunities to bring grade up if u bomb one of them. He said like 20% of people get an A and 80% get a B or lower. Great prof, always willing to help, but for a first-time logical thinking class it's tough.

All of his homework needs to be typesetted and my homework grades are inconsistent with my friend's even though we did our homework together. There isn't much feedback on the homework either, making it hard to understand and learn. Tests are hard and he doesn't give out curves easily, and the two exams are worth more than 50% of the entire grade.

The teacher asked us to type the answers, some mathematical symbols are hard to type out, it waste a lot of time. The assignments were graded strictly, the answers were formatted strictly, a lot of the homework comments weren't clear, and it wasn't even know why we lost the grade. He was extremely reluctant to re-grade.
Extremely good professor who is nice and cool

Drew is a nice dude. Took algo with him and loved it. For Theory of Comp, the course structure is awkward. We spent most of the time on FSA, the relatively easy stuff. On undecidability and complexity, he went through large amount of content in a short amount of time. The assignments are only out of 30 points so there isn't any room for error.

Instructor that has no clue how to teach the content. Quizzes will have material way more advanced than what we saw in the lectures and homework. The only good thing is that there is a curve of like 40 points. If his is the only section available, take this class another semester. Otherwise you'll regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded only by 4 exams. I studied heavily for all of them and failed all. I was barely above class median each time. The curve was insane and even that didn't save me. Don't waste your time. I learned a lot and for what? He makes every exam problem vague/trick question, testing knowledge in the most bizarre, unhelpful ways.
His curriculum was completely different from normal Discrete classes and he made everything more difficult than it should've been.

The class is online and asynchronous which it convenient. The homework can be quite time-consuming and challenging. The exams were too difficult, a 60+ was an A, so there was a big curve. Take it if you need to do a summer class and want to stay off campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just dont waste the time and money. Just take it with someone else .
Rough class don't take this as it will actually nuke your gpa. Will make you question your existence. Although Asynchronous class best if you take with another professor in person.

don't listen to people saying this is a good class, 4 exams that's all your grade is nothing he asks on the test is what is on the slides no matter how many notes you take you will not be able to get a good grade for the exams, take any other teacher but him

i got disowned after this class, i can't describe how xxxxx this class is and he is, i would walk into ongoing traffic rather than ever see this man again. i hope he is very happy with all the lives he has ruined. do not take this class
i genuinely believe he hates students and wants them to suffer, and i did. i will never get back the semester i spent crying over this course. don't take him.

Yes he recycles his lectures, I understand, but he constantly updates his lectures if needed, and he's very accessible to ask questions directly. Best asynchronous course I've taken, challenging but you learn a lot. Tests were creative focusing on actual learning not just "using" what you memorized. 
Sad to see my favorite professor rated this low.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
FYI: The low ratings on here are from the few students who failed the class and won't be of use to you. 

Info you want --> There are 4 exams (25% each) and weekly HW is purely for practice. All exams are open-note (take notes from his lecture videos and you'll be well-equipped). Exams are super tough, but he ends up curving the class generously.

bro like just don't do it tbh like i thought since it's online it'll be chill NOOOOO the lecture vids r from 2016 and the tests r not related to them at all and he doesn't give u any indication of what's going to be on the test. i stopped looking both ways before crossing the street bc of this class.
Yo this jit will nuke ur grade, class is rigged. The exams are so cooked compared to what we learn. Like we're expected to build the burj khalifa using IKEA instructions.

This class was genuinely one of the most terrible experiences of my entire life. He does not teach anything, but the things he does talk about aren't even on the tests. There is no credit given for anything other than the exams, and the average for most was a 30%. The green line is looking really enticing right now.

This is genuinely the worst class and professor I have ever had in my entire academic career. He uses lecture VIDEOS from several years ago. Neither the lecture slides nor the videos are related to whatever questions he threw at us on the exams. Our entire grade is based only on exams and he made them so extremely difficult. I am so sad and tired.
Professor is not

don't take his classes please!! I wish he cared more about getting his student preparing for his EXTREMELY hard exams then just using a bunch of videos from many years ago. The concepts are exciting but I can't say I've walked out of his class learning anything. I felt like i just wasted tuition money, great guy but very bad professor.

CS3000, online algo class. I'm not sure how lecture videos from 2016 are supposed to prepare me for the hardest exams I have ever taken. Your notes will not help in the slightest. Prepare to get 50% at maximum. It does run on bell curve tho, so you probably wont fail. Your gpa is taking a beating tho.
Awful, dont choose
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM

Dr. Aerni is amazing. It is a hard course, and you will have to study, but she makes the exams only about 50% of your grade so if you put in a solid effort, you will get at least a B. The subject is inherently boring, but Dr. Aerni understands that this is material students struggle with. I hate math, but learned a lot and no longer hate stats.

I took Aerni's first semester teaching Wetlands- the course felt a bit disorganised and if I'm honest, I would have benefited from more homework in the class. Sadly I did not learn as much has I'd hoped, but she is caring if not softspoken, and in that class you do get to go play in the mud which rocks. Could have done with better class culture

Very helpful in class and led very interesting lectures which helped make the curriculum feel accessible. Grades pretty easy and makes her rubrics for projects very understandable. Participation is very important in her classes, but you can choose to attend through Zoom instead of in person. Hard to reach outside of class except in office hours.

The class was great, you got out of it what you put into it. Lecture-heavy, easy homework, professor very understanding, personable and smart. Participation graded but you were able to attend class virtually. Only problem would be that she is a little hard to reach outside of class/by email. overall would recommend and I want to be her friend

Loved her class, can be attended online or in person. Lectures are engaging and educational, and in class she is very helpful with questions/concerns. Only issue is she is very difficult to reach outside of class, never got an email back. Many opportunities for your grade, optional extra credit final and projects have super clear rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Held lectures on zoom and in person at the same time(you can still attend classes while sick in bed), great lecturer and easy to take notes for. Class content was easy. Dr. Aerni was very friendly and helpful in one-on-one interactions, came across as someone who genuinely wants students to learn and enjoy classes.

ENVR1400- Goes pretty fast through the slides but if you pay attention you will be fine, and lab is important for this course. She's really nice and personable but takes a while to grade sometimes. Canvas can be unorganized but she will always move due dates back if you express you had online issues. Participation required but you can join on zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable scholar and ready to talk about any topic. First professor I've seen who genuinely cares about each and every student. Class has a LOT of readings but as long as you participate you will receive a good grade. She does tend to go on tangents but discussions are engaging.

What ruined it for me was how this class was fully online, even though I registered it to be in person. She goes overtime while I told her multiple times that I have another class after hers, so she gives me only 3-5 minutes to get to my next class. No modules page, no slideshows, and boring discussions.

The class was switched fully online after registration, which really ruined it for me. Two-hour Zoom classes with little structure or slides were unproductive and boring. Grading was mostly completion-based with minimal feedback, and emails often took days to get a response. This course would've been much better in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Anjanette is so sweet and genuine. I didn't love the amount of readings and presentations, but she makes the class such an interesting and comforting space. The class is fascinating, and if you participate often, you will do very well. Loved her!

Best professor I had at Northeastern. Highly recommend taking afro-asian relations in the americas. Chan Tack is a brilliant scholar, extremely personable, and genuinely cares about making connections with her students and making sure they learn.

Chan Tack was, without a doubt, the best professor I have ever had. She is smart and cares for every student. Her lectures are amazing. She assigns a lot of reading, but none of it feels like busy work. She is a fair grader and prioritizes the learning of students over cramming the Syllabus. I cannot recommend this course enough!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Literally the kindest ever

She is so sweet and caring and it is clear she genuinely cares about her students. She never made the class stressful and made any rules/guidelines clear from the start of class. She made me enjoy writing again! Her TA is also very nice and chill.
Best Professor in the world!

Professor Emily was great. Highly recommend this class because since there is a service aspect you have way less homework than other first year writing course. Professor Emily is super sweet and super understanding if something happens. Her TA is useless so no need to pay any attention to her.

The sweetest professor ever! She is super caring and wants the best for all of her students. The class itself is chill and is a very collaborative and welcoming environment. I honestly looked forward to class every week because Emily is very passionate and optimistic. Overall, this is a great class to take 10/10!!

BEST PROFESSOR EVER. If you plan on taking any writing class, please take Emily. She is super kind and respectful to her students. She dedicates so much time to the course, which creates a sense of community within our class. Emily is very open-minded, optimistic, and understanding so assignments are not only easy, but are stress relieving.

Great professor, accepts late work and is super understanding if you can't attend class or something, just email her. Class is often discussion heavy but you don't have to participate if you don't want. Honestly a really great semester. She doesn't have an intense rubric for most assignments but if you ask she'll give specifics

Thought this class would be a pain, but I really enjoyed it! Professor Avery-Miller is super laid back, her writing assignments are fun and thought provoking. Really got to know people in my class and looked forward to it every week, if you need ENGW1111 take it with her, highly recommend!

Emily is super sweet and an easy and helpful grader, but kind of exhausts group work. I feel like I barely wrote in this class, it was a lot of creative assignments. Feels like a high school class. She isn't a super engaging lecturer but overall her class was easy and the assignments were totally manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Extremely easy 3rd year writing class. No lectures, just occasional readings that you don't get tested on. Just remember to do your discussion board posts on time and put marginal effort into the 4 main assignments - and you will get an easy A. She is also extremely nice and caring. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a great professor. Cares about her students, and her class is not too tough if you do what is asked of you.

Usually, if a professor has a low rating but is an online class I will still take it because how bad can it be? It's bad. For exams he gets rid of the modules 2 hours before the exam starts. He makes you take it on zoom and lockdown which takes 30 minutes to set up. Releases hws 2 days before there due.

As he did in the positive rating below, Nick makes spelling mistakes among the other irritating things he does to ruin simple material to get on your nerves. You may think I'm joking, but absolutely no one in the class found this course useful. I'm probably going to raise a complaint against this guy.

Honestly, I think Dedeke is over-hated. He puts in effort to make lectures less boring, even though the content itself is pretty dry. I didn't do great on the exams, but I still got an A thanks to the curve and tons of extra credit. Overall, if you have a group with at least 3 responsible guy and do the practice exams, dw you'll be fine.
Worst professor to take

The kind of professor who makes you want to join Squid games instead. Every lecture made me question what I'm doing at Northeastern. He must have some leverage on the admin, because it's hard to fathom how he is still employed.

One word - RUN!
Two words - RUN AWAY!
Three words - RUN AWAY QUICKLY!

oh no. just no. i scrolled through pinterest in class and participated like once a week and did fine but omg his lectures are so incredibly useless. he read directly off the slides and talked about nothing of substance. i dont understand why this is a required class for business ive never hated anything more.

SUPER boring lectures and just reads off slides. Tough grader and quizzes are hard due to content heaviness. Sit in the front and participate, will be more lenient with you. In general, not recommended, a boring subject, a boring teacher, and a tough grader. DQ at 7 AM was annoying, and readings often had nothing to do with lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly I don't get the hate? Some people say he's hard to understand-- I didn't encounter this problem. DQs due by 7am for most classes (like 5 question quiz based on reading, not hard). Random groups given in beginning of semester you have to complete occasional HWs with. Tests are hard because its content heavy MCQ + boring lectures & subject

Here's how you do well in this class: Sit in the front and participate. You will hear Dr. Nick clearly, he will learn your name, and he will give you opportunities to answer questions. You MUST pay attention. If you want to sit in the back and half-listen, don't expect to do well. Lectures are boring but it's up to you to make something of it.

Honestly, when I saw the reviews before the class, I thought they were an exaggeration, and I walked in with an open mind. But after taking the course, I can say the concerns were accurate. The exams are extremely brutal compared to what is covered in class, and the lectures are often unclear and difficult to follow. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

This class is a joke. I'm convinced that Nick himself has given the higher ratings because I'm convinced no one in my class even remotely liked this course. Terrible exams where students lose points for trick questions. He isn't clear when he speaks, and just makes it very difficult to learn anything. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you make an effort to participate, this class is a lot easier because he cares a lot about knowing people's name and group discussions. Good extra credit opportunities that helped bump my grades up, but lots of group assignments. Tests were hard but it's a lot of memorization of the slides and following his practice exam that he gives.

Despite it being an online class, deliverables are due every Wednesday and Saturday night, and assignments are locked to the Monday or Thursday before, respectively, only giving 3 days for every assignment, no matter the length. This becomes a huge issue in group projects in an asynchronous setting where your groupmates are unresponsive. Beware.

take someone else if you can. his class is very confusing and disorganized. studying for tests is torture. the midterm review videos and practice test had different answers (even though they were the same questions?). the group projects could be hell if you have a bad group. never responds to emails. don't expect him to help you at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class is pretty tough with a large volume of work. He gives a lot of DQs, but they are easy and you do them at home. He has 2 big exams, but posts a detailed study guide and review slides. He is very passionate about the class and overall very sweet. He gave us 4 different extra credit opportunities. I recommend taking his afternoon sessions.

Guy always does his best, and his best is pretty good. I don't understand why his rating is so low, yeah his class is hard, but this is Northeastern, suck it up. He gives great out of classroom opportunities to meet high level business professionals (amazon, IBM, etc.) for extra credit.

Nick is a mumbler and a rambler, so not a great combo. Its so hard to understand him, and he just goes on and on about useless jargin. I really wish his slides were less packed, they are full with info that wont be relevant or on any exams. There is little to none real study material for the class, which makes studying and doing well on exams hard

He's not horrible but proceed with caution. He's very knowledgable and passionate about MIS. It's also clear he cares about his students. However, his canvas page is a mess, he makes diagnostic quizzes due at 7am, and his exams are brutal (gives a curve). If you take him, go in with your guns blazing, and he will respect the effort.

Absolutely do not recommend taking this class with this professor. Unclear rubrics for assignments with differing templates, lots of group projects which are hit or miss, and very harsh grading. Did not learn a lot either and the most disorganized class I've ever taken. This class stressed me out a lot and will stress you out too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dedeke is very nice and you can tell he's passionate about the topics and he often tells stories to try to enhance students' education. However lectures are super boring. Instructions for assignments are often confusing and vague and there are a number of group assignments throughout the semester that take much longer than they probably need to
Very difficult grader, barely curves, nobody gets an A in his class. Boring lectures he justs reads off slides and grades every single assignment difficult.

He didn't know the material he was teaching. Asked what topics we wanted to review, ignored them, read off endless slides, then said questions were "already covered." Put incorrect answer on a practice quiz, reused question with different correct answer on test, refused to give the point back. Said curve made up for HIS errors. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!

His lectures are EXTREMELY boring and useless. He grades everything out of 3 and is super tough with the grading. His Canvas page is a mess and all the instructions for the group projects are poorly made. All his tests are in class, on paper, and the questions don't make sense. I don't know how he got hired by Northeastern. DO NOT TAKE DEDEKE!

While the lectures themselves weren't too bad, a lot of group projects were assigned and made up a good chunk of credit. They were also graded harshly, so you were out of luck if you had bad teammates. Professor Dedeke's exams were also very difficult, with multiple choice answers being very similar to each other.

Hands down the WORST professor I've ever had. Assignments/quizzes are not testing you for knowledge, but for nitpicky wording of questions. As a ESL student, I felt like I was reading for trick questions rather than the content. Also, theres a bunch of games you play as assignments. Absolutely useless assignments, I learned nothing in this class.

This guy gives homework quizzes that are due at 7 am, so sometimes I'd forget to do them and it affected my grade tremendously. Then he gives tests and each question is like "Which of the following is ____" and the answer choices are so similar that you don't even know what to answer. The tests are not a fair representation of what you know.

This professor has to be one of the most horrible professors I've ever encountered in my life. On the first day of class he introduced himself and he makes it seem like he's this very intelligent and caring man, but he just doesn't know how to teach. It's a disgrace that Northeastern even hired this guy. I didn't learn ANYTHING this semester.

LISTEN TO THE OTHER REVIEWS. Assignments are poorly written and riddled with typos. Exam and DQ questions are not well thought through, and even contradictory to class lectures. And don't bother asking for clarification, he will just tell you that he "went over it in class" in the most poorly written email you have ever read.
Horribly picky grader, will take points off for random things that were not specified in the instructions, and will never admit to being wrong if you meet with him.

Very tough professor. I took the online accelerated course for the summer and it was really difficulty because of his grading system. Group work is hell if you do not have a good group. Consistently takes off points off hw for minor things. good luck

At all costs do not take dedeke! He is one of the worst professors in d'amore-mckim. He never sets clear expectations but grades extremely tough. Never admits he's wrong, when frequently there is errors in exams and hw. Also its impossible for each person to get the same grade for group projects because of his grading method.

Nice, but is a very tough grader. His classes are very boring. He did some extra credit, but it does not really matter that much because he is a tough grader. Tests are very hard, and most assignments are group ones. His class was not the worst, but I would not recommend it.

Dedeke is one of the most passionate teachers I have had so far at Northeastern, his lectures were very engaging and interesting. Sure the class was hard but that's life, just read the textbook when you're confused. I must admit I got lucky since I got a great group, but he gave us a ton of extra credit opportunities anyways and a generous curve.
A very tough grader, but offers a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Heavy on group work.

Horrible. Incredibly unclear and disorganized. He puts the wrong answers on tests and quizzes frequently and is rude when you correct him. Spelling and grammar errors everywhere in his slides, tests, and course material. He may have a PhD but he is in no way capable of teaching a class at this level. Very rude to some people so get on his good side

So so so unnecessarily hard for an online class-- I was spending up to 18 hours a week on homework and notes and recorded lectures. Nice guy but compared to other classes this is like training to be a navy seal.

Extremely confusing and disorganized professor. Posts assignments and rubrics a day before they're due. Does not explain himself well, constantly speaks in circles. Exams depend on memorization of content and often contain topics that were never discussed. Group projects were assigned often, but they aren't too hard. Attendance is mandatory.

Professor Dedeke is nice and respectful to his students; however, he is a TOUGH GRADER. Every assignment is counted towards your grade, including DQs (case studies and you answer questions) and group projects. PARTICIPATION matters a lot, and I talk to every class by answering and asking good questions but I still get a 9/10.

Be ready to take notes. Very lecture intensive, read up to 300 slides per exam, 2 exams in total. His tests are very easy, providing the perfect review slide and practice exam to get 95+. He curves the class if everyone performs poorly, he doesn't deserve all these negative comments. Many group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Passionate professor but the material is sometimes a decade out of date. Not understanding of student issues, poor communicator, and failed to learn several students names weeks into the course. Only lecture material which are not relevant to the exams. Materials riddled with grammar errors & all assignments group based - so you need a good group.

Terrible professor, showed up late constantly, and didn't understand the subject material. Clearly passionate about the subject but poor at teaching. He doesn't teach well and constantly has test answers that are wrong and incorrect, meaning students have to correct him. Avoid this class at all costs it's the only class he teaches and it's bad.
Doesn't deserve the hate he gets - he gives good lectures and helpful materials. Class is hard but fair for the most part. Grading is very meticulous and every point counts.

I can see why he is rated so low but he really isnt that bad. Keep up with weekly synopsis videos and DQ quizes. He splits the grading up into a bunch of different categories which is much better than having 80% of your grade based off tests like in most classes.
Dedeke is a nice person but a horrible teacher. The slides are very confusing and the tests are very hard. He was not able to provide an explanation as to why the answer on the test was correct.

Teaches from powerpoint slides which are not well organized and doesn't explain concepts that well. Exams are similar to the homework. Many group assignments and if you and you're group don't know what you're doing you're screwed. He is nice and a funny guy

prof dedeke is super understanding. his lectures are quite long, but he gives us breaks in between. his exams are very similar to the study guide, but he changes a few words so it trips you up. the rest of the class is group project-based - if you don't have a good group, you're done for. he is very dedicated; he writes his own materials for class.

Very kind and funny professor, truly cares about his students. Gives a break in the middle of class each day and you will usually get out a few minutes early. One thing though is that all of the assignments amount to 100 points total, so every point counts in this class. Can be a harsh grader. Definitely have to work for a good grade.

He cares about his students, that's very clear. Terrible teacher. It's hard to understand him, his exam questions are often very difficult to interpret because they are in borderline broken english. The course is VERY outdated, and although he tries to teach excel through the course, it is so abundantly clear he doesn't know how to use it.

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR! He was unclear in his expectations and would change them after students asked questions. He was extremely rude and changed grades after students corrected him for mistakes. Though his instructions would say to give "at least two examples," he was upset that people only gave two examples rather than more, which he expected.
worst.

Class is entirely lecture. Don't recommend taking this class at 8am. The professor has a funny personality and occasionally tells anecdotes. I found the course intellectually challenging but not extremely difficult nor easy either. One big thing to note is that he has quizzes at least once a week that are due at 7am so be sure to not miss those!

Lectures are not engaging, which caused me to zone off a lot. I studied last minute for both of the big exams, which I probably could have avoided. The study guides are very helpful- some of the questions on the test are exact repeats or are very similar. He is also a tough grader so make sure to go above and beyond on the group projects!

Terribly disorganized. He constantly changes lecture slides and homeworks, even with the deadline in a few days. My group was backstabbed by starting early on a project when he changed the assignment's raw data two days before it was due. When we asked him about the points lost, he basically said "be glad I didn't give you a zero".
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally the worst professor to teach this class. you cannot hear this professor at all ... mumbles (i.e. you can't tell when he calls on you) ... slides are disorganized ... on the test, the choices he shows you for a question are different from the choices i got on a test ... can't explain why an answers wrong like idk how i'm supposed to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 26% of the grade are short quizzes that take around 20 minutes to read and do, each worth 2% of the grade. Participation is very important (10%) and you must actively participate to get a high grade. Tests and projects are easy if you know your computers but if not it can be difficult. Overall not a bad teacher for a remote class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dedeke is a really kind professor, and cares a lot about his students. He goes out of his way to talk to every single person in the class, even while virtual. Overall if you pay attention in class it is not that hard, but hw and tests are specific to exactly what he says, and you cant google the answers. I enjoyed the class!

Lots of short 2% tests throughout the course that are really time-consuming and annoying. The tests are pretty difficult and participation is important. I think my main issue with Dedeke was that he's not clear about what he wants. Seems like he doesn't understand what he tries to teach. The class itself is not that hard but he makes it difficult.

Don't understand all the hate he gets on here. He's a super nice guy who is very passionate about what he teaches. Although his lectures and slides were a bit disorganized they were always understandable. Tests are pretty easy as long as you do the study guide, which is similar. Only annoying thing is many short take home tests for 2% of grade each

Professor Dedeke is genuinely a good and enthusiastic person but his teaching method is terrible. His midterm tests are tricky, if you want to score high on them you must memorize the study guide and sample test. I think it is unfair and ineffective. Also, the DQ quizes are tricky in wording and one mistake is worth a lot.

Gives Excel assignments, but doesn't know how to do a Vlookup. Goes over test answers and cant explain why one answer is right and one answer is wrong. Material is outdated. Textbook is free, but you are tested on his slides which are not organized at all.

Nice guy, and relatively easy workload. Tests are just repeats of the study guides, but he changes the words and answers around almost to try to trick students. Also he seems to be unaware of the world around him. Needs a time keeper in class to tell him how much time is left. Will mark you absent if you are not in the room when he's taking role

This class is about modern technology (think hard drives, cloud computing). The problem is 2 things 1) he is teaching it as if it were a decade ago and 2) the guy is clueless and ambiguous. Sole reason why I wouldn't major is MIS. This has been the worst professor I've had at Northeastern. Easy to get a B, impossible to get an A.

Terrible teacher! Unable to understand what's going on during the lecture through all his random mumbling and rants. Disrespectful towards students when they bring up info from the slides that contradict test answers. Half his powerpoint slides used during class are blank. Tests are similar to the study guide but meant to confuse you! DO NOT TAKE!!

Dedeke is a great person and is excited about how we can use MIS to impress coworkers and co-op interviewees. It is a subject hard to understand, but he made it doable. He encourages participation in the classroom and his exams are multiple choice.

Prof Dedeke's class was a joke. Very short, easy take-home "diagnostic quizzes" account for a quarter of your grade, and the tests are very similar to the practice test he provides for studying. If you're serious about learning MIS, avoid Dedeke, but otherwise it's an easy class

Worst teacher I have ever had. I didn't hear more than 5 words every lecture from all the mumbling on random things that were irrelevant to the class. terrible professor and extremely unfair grader, he doesn't even explain any of the assignments EVER BRO!!!!

Dedeke is definitely a Computer Science professor trying to teach business students. He assumes you know things that there is no reason for you to know. SAVE this class for later in college. It may be business core, but you learning nothing. Case analyses are HARD, he is not clear with what he wants. No final, no textbook.
Professor Dedeke doesn't provide any clarification on any topics. When you ask a question in class related to the material, 910 the answer is 'I don't know'
no! please no! do not take his class, thats too awful

He goes about as if he knows what he is talking about and when a student asks a question, he struggles to answer sometimes even answering  I don't know. Unclear as to what he wants and is unwilling to take the time to clarify. When you push for clarification he disregards you and talks down to you. Quite a rude and frustrating teacher

He's really good! I will reccomand him. His class is super funny and he is a easygrader! You can easily get an A just attending his classes. He loves getting e-mail so if you don't understand anything just send him an e-mail and you will recive a better partecipation grade. His class was helpful and he is a very good professor!
This guy is the worst professor I've had so far in my college career
Worst instructor ever. Unclear what he wants all the time. AVOID!!!
bad prof. He said I am gonna receive an average grade, but gave me a C in the end. He seems to be helpful, but not truly.

Honestly, he was a very nice person and really enjoys what he's teaching, but he's unclear about what he wants, and grades harshly if you didn't do an assignment exactly how he wanted.  Nice guy, but his grading is ridiculous.

This is the worst professor I have ever had. I did not learn anything in the class and the work was useless and tedious. He is an unfair grader and does not want to help his students i.e. he NEVER answers ANY question with a straight answer. Do not take this course whatever you do.

Professor Dedeke is one of the worst professors I have had the misfortune of having. He has ridiculously high expectations for case studies that are on fairly simple concepts. He asks you to make the process extremely complicated by forcing you to segment your answers into strange tables that make it hard to explain your thougts correctly.
Extremely boring... grades very harsh and his lectures are straight from his powerpoints... he even gave points off on a yes or no OPINION question (Do you think...yes or no)

Honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. Rambles all class and the information he goes over and cases we have little to do with what you are tested on. Grades really harshly and all cases are really repetitive.

He's hard to follow in lectures. When you ask him to clarify something he never really gives you an answer, he sort of babbles for a little bit and then moves on. You never know what he's looking for on homework or the tests, he wants to to say exactly what he was looking for. No final if missed 2 or less classes. Avoid him if possible!

He was a decent teacher. I didn't mind his lectures, but the his grading on the cases was pretty tough and they were pretty hard. His tests were okay, and he does curve. Participation was a big deal. I ended up getting an A, but it was really hard to do; I ended up writing a final case that was over 20 pages long to get it.

It's not only his teaching that's bad but the course is awful and useless. The work that he assigns is in such detail that makes it unfair and the final assignment is the worst thing ever. I did well in the class but still hate it. His tests are easy but his classes are boringggggg. Don't take him. He's awful

As a person, Dedeke is the man is obviously really nice and understanding. But as a teacher, his grading policies are a little weird and tough to understand. That's what made it hard for me to love this class.

This is one confusing class. I am usually an A/A- student, and found I could only get a B+. He is not the worst teacher, but it is very difficult to know what to study for the tests and what to put into the cases. He refuses to discuss grades or argue with students, even if it is he who has made the error. Attendance mandatory. No final.
Great prof. If you got to classes and participate this class is a very easy A.

Attendance and participation count for ALOT of your grade. 6 out of 8 hmwk assignments are mandatory. there are two tests. If you have PERFECT attendance, the final is optional. Test are extremely hard but his curves are ridiculous. class is long and dull but his dry jokes are meant to keep you attentive. pay attention and you'll do fine.

I LOVED Professor Akbari. He's a great guy, great sense of humor, and he's very chill. He wants his students to do well and is very easy to talk to. Definitely recommend taking him for advanced writing.

Extremely verbose guy to the point that assignments are difficult to parse through to figure out what he actually wants from you. Only 4 assignments for the whole semester, 2 of which are kind of useless. Very slow grader with relatively inconsistent feedback, but easy A if you follow the rubric and scattered instructions in his lengthy documents.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid teacher & good guy, class is very politically polarizing which is annoying. Show up to class and you'll do fine.

I enjoyed Akbari. He's passionate and enjoys talking about currents events. He loves to laugh at his own jokes (which usually aren't funny), but overall I really don't have much to complain about. If you're a strong writer this class will be very easy, but he will also try to push you to get better. The four major essays determine the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely good feedback on your writing. You only get feedback once a paper is submitted. Professor is extremely kind and caring, always available to chat.

Tom is a great professor who really cares about his students. The class was not easy, but he explained our goals for each unit well and allowed us to structure our work how we saw fit. This is the only English class I can say I enjoyed. Thank you, Tom!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hate writing in general, but he's the reason why I still show up to class and want to do my best. He's an overall good person and professor. Ask for feedback and you'll get it, it's a small class anyways. He remembers the littlest things you say, so he remembers you and it makes me feel I am cared for. Nice grader as long as you put some effort.
He is the BEST! His assignments are hard yet interesting and he is very inspiring and caring, but you need to work hard to get a good grade.

Just the absolute best. I've never had a professor that's so engaging, funny, down to earth, and smart all at the same time. You'd be hard pressed to find another professor who teaches a mandatory class (First-Year Writing) with the same enthusiasm. Please participate though, he really values everyone's input, and deserves all your attention.

"How did Tom Akbari treat his students during COVID-19?" Absolutely hands down the best professor I've seen across multiple universities. Helped students move with his own personal van when everyone was kicked off-campus housing, sent emails immediately asking about personal situations and whether they needed help or aid. He ��checked ��in ��!

reviews.comment: This professor was intimidated by actual writing in the sciences. He had no clue about basic scientific literature, and clearly needs to become more updated in the field. I would avoid taking at all costs, this class will make you a worse writer
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I LOVE Tom! He is such a good professor and hilarious. I love when he makes a "dad" jokes and is the only one laughing. Seriously though, he is a pretty chill guy and is super nice. Take him!

I'm having a genuinely great time in his class. He gives a lot of reading and there's only a few papers, but if the class didn't get to all of the reading or isn't satisfied with drafts, he's good about giving more time. Cares more about the craft than running with the syllabus. Plus he's really nice, an I personally like his lame jokes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Don't be afraid if you get 5 hours of homework in one weekend. Deadlines for papers are reasonable for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: take him he's cool

Relies heavily on peer reviews and doesn't give his own feedback on rough drafts before final papers are due. Only grades final papers (only feedback you get is after final grade) & grades as if he told you what you had done wrong & you didn't fix it. Feedback & instruction is lengthy, sometimes hard to understand.  10/10 would suggest dif prof.
he clearly failed at being a writer and now thinks his adjunct professor elective classes are doctoral symposiums on literature.

Thinks everything he says is the funniest thing in the world. Also tries to sound like the smartest person ever. Feedback on papers is hard to understand, given you don't know many of the words he uses. Overall,  class is decent, lots of discussion, no busy work.

Akbari definitely gives good feedback on papers, and they're pretty easy. However, many of the classes we spent entirely peer editing ordiscussing our paper ideas with the class, which was useless. Take advanced writing in the disciplines online andsave yourslef the time.

On the first day of class, Akbari spent the allotted 100 min going the syllabus. He comes to class prepared only to talk about a few topics and refuses to lecture; he relies on the class for discussion, but when we try to bring up slightly more intelligent topics he just stares and continues talking about his shallow topics of choice. Bad prof.

Mediocre Professor. Doesn't really teach anything to help your writing get beyond high school level, but he could be worse. His lectures are useless, but when he gives individual attention to a paper, he sometimes genuinely surprises me with his stellar advice. The best part is that he thinks he's hilarious, doesn't notice silence after his jokes.

I took Advanced Writing in Literature with Tom Akbari. His lectures are repetitive, he refuses to clarify anything, and is very close-minded despite his lip service to open-mindedness. Absolutely do not take a class with him.

He has the worst grading policies, essays are 1000 words long minus the semi final essay which was 2500 words. 5 essays in all. no final but very boring in class. Take this class online if you can. English 302 aka Advanced Writing for the Disciplines
He is a great guy who seems to want to help you learn the material. Sometimes he isnt the greatest for advice but still a great prof.
Funny in class, cares about students, expects a lot from them in class and on writing projects. Really good.

akbari is one of those teachers who seems nice enough, but does not know how to give you any feedback/help on any of the work you've done. he does not follow a comprehensible way of grading papers, so you end up getting docked for random things. overall, he's an alright person, but not a great teacher. look for someone else if you absolutely can.

I think contrary to some other ratings, prof depaoli is super clear on what he wants from students. I have an A right now from just attending, being present, and contributing my ideas despite them being not that good. Take his criticism and you will succeed. Just need to put some effort in sometimes and youre chilling

I am only taking this class because it is required and this one was the only one that fit into my schedule. If you can avoid this professor, I HIGHLY recommend you do so. Most certainly the worst professor I've had at Northeastern. Definitely extremely knowledgeable in marketing but abuses his power and does not want students to succeed.

The worst thing about this class is that stupid Bike simulation you have to do your entire semester and if you get a bad group, you are done for as that is already like 25% of your grade especially the summaries. The HW isn't too bad and defiently look at his feedback to get a higher score on the next one. The entire class is so lecture heav.

Very, very strict on attendance (3 strikes you're out kinda thing.. beware). Not much HW, but very strict on grading (you must thoroughly incorporate his feedback). Open-note exams- lots of flexibility with how you answer which is good. Class is lecture heavy but relatively engaging, participation matters (easy to participate). Teacher is solid.
STAY AWAY!!!!!!! HE WILL RUIN YOUR GPA! I have an A in every single class EXCEPT his! RUN FOR THE HILLS!! HIS TESTS ARE STUPID! HIS HOMEWORK IS GRADED 1-4 but NOBODY get above 3/4 Automatic 75
Very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about marketing! His lectures were almost always entertaining and he always laid out what you needed to do well on quizzes and projects.
Great professor and great guy. I don't understand the bad reviews he's a great dude and I learned a ton in the class. He grades a bit harsh but it's chill.

Professor DePaoli's class was incredibly valuable for anyone interested in digital marketing. We earned HubSpot and Google Analytics certifications and worked on real-world projects like running paid ads and managing a social media page. Highly recommend for those entering the field!
I think he acts the way he does to overcompensate for being short and not getting a bid in college

This man is straight up evil, no words. Run for the hills, run, he ruined my gpa. I have never ended a class with a C. Got a perfect score on the final but ended with a C bc of attendance? Avoid, he is also super nit-picky.

DePaoli is a great professor who definitely knowledgeable in his teachings. There are only four homework assignments and they are worth almost as much as the assessments - this is a double-edged blade but it helps students learn and understand the material. Overall he is very nice and takes time to make sure his students understands the material
Alex doesn't give any direction on how he wants case studies and assignments done. He has TA grade cases which he should probably be grading himself. Super hard grader.

Professor understands the concepts very well and is very good at explaining them although he does so with slight arrogance. I spent little time outside of class reading the textbook or my notes. Tests are online and open book and are not very difficult except there is not a lot of time. Homework's are easy if you put a bit of effort in them.

Very strict grader without good reason, knocks points off for unexcused absences, and is sadistic in my opinion. I always work to improve but rarely scored anything but a 4/5 on all outside-of-class assignments. He expects you to do so much more than what the assignment says to do & doesn't give points back once he made his decision. Avoid taking!
Glad I dropped this class lmao.
The quizzes are really hard!!

Agree that this professor is incredibly sadistic. He will take an incredible amount of points off for things you DID complete, solely because he didn't open the attachment you submitted. He is a poor representation of the university and deserves to be severely audited as his grading practice is frankly ridiculous. Save yourself and don't take him.

The professor goes out of his way to make students miserable and feel bad. I completely agree with another review that described the Professor as sadistic. He wants to get students in trouble and finds pleasure in their failure. His mistreatment is unreasonable and unjustified.

Professor DePaoli has very interesting lectures and he knows marketing very well, but he punishes students who do well out of pure skepticism. Many students like this professor, but for those who do not, it is mainly because of mistreatment and disrespect. He has negatively influenced my idea of marketing and of the university.

Although Alex is very knowledgable in marketing, I would look at other professors if you know that marketing is not something you want to pursue in the future. He is incredibly lecture heavy, is quite a strict grader, knocks points off for unexcused absences, and is honestly kind of pretentious in my opinion. Some will love him, some will hate him

This professor can be perfect for some and bad for others. Super lecture intensive, with his classes being him reading of a presentation the entire duration of the class. He wants you to learn, so his quizzes are based heavily on your response rather than a correct answer. Super participation focused, after 2 missed classes he knocks your grade.

Alex is a nice professor and he always has interesting lectures. Sometimes they can get a bit long/redundant and too in depth for an intro course. He grades pretty harshly and does not give many easy assignments--tests are very detailed and rushed (he expects creativity) and homework are too demanding and time consuming.

Definitely have to work hard and show up to class, but you learn A LOT. The class is very well structured and you can tell he cares about his students and their learning. Make sure you participate. He's always very accessible if you ever are confused.

Really interesting lectures, but the actual quizzes are really difficult. If you want an A you'll really have to work for it. I personally wasn't a fan of him because of his really odd grading but if you value learning over an easy A I'd take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very cool and engaging. Powerpoints are very useful and the course load is not too bad. He is kind of a tough grader on tests though. Textbook is recommended but most of the info is covered in his lectures anyways. Great guy

Prof. is a very nice guy. However, he is definitely tough on grading. You can get through the homework thinking you are doing very well (no negative feedback), but then do very poorly on quizzes (worth 10% each) or the presentations. He expects more than he lets on. Be prepared to put in a lot of work, but then you will do well.

Professor DePaoli is very knowledgeable and it shows. However, he is a little high-strung and has explicit guidelines with everything. Feedback is very vague most of the time, and his response to just about anything is very matter-of-fact. Don't buy the textbook, it is a waste of money and you learn everything in lecture. One big group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of those rare professors who actually makes it their goal to educate you. Not to test you, not to waste your time, but to make you learn. There is no pity given to lazy students. If you work and participate you can get a higher grade, but you have to struggle for the A. Hes also very direct and well spoken which is a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Alex DePaoli is the most sadistic and unfunny professors I've had in my life. He picks on students and makes jokes about them that just humiliate them. He has no morals when it comes to students with disabilities as he didn't allow one student to get extra time since he submitted his form late to him even though he had a debilitating disability.

DePaoli is a legend. One of the best professors that I have had at Northeastern. He is very funny and witty. We stan. His class lectures are very interactive and heavily relate to the world. He is very receptive to students' thoughts and opinions (coursework, lecture style, topics to discuss, etc.). You SHOULD DEFINITELY TAKE HIM for 2201/2202

I love Alex. Course is easy as long as you participate, turn assignments in on time, and try. His test are hard, but designed to give points even on wrong answers. He has an interesting and fresh perspective on marketing so he lectures are fascinating. He's witty and modern, so the class is relatable. Class was refreshing and fun. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall a good class, good prof. Tons of cases but he will make them shorter. On that note, he is really good about asking how to improve the course throughout. One big group project/ business plan, but easier than most other Business class projects. Tough grader, but a really easy B, a little harder to get an A. Would take again.

STAY AWAY. I don't get why there are so many good reviews, perhaps these are only for his intro to marketing courses. I took his class for MKTG3301, and I wish I didn't. His grading is unfair. Even if you participate lots and work hard in his class, it doesn't matter. Prof. seems to take joy in students' pain and none in their success.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 2 or more absences - grade lowers. You will also have to participate and talk in class to earn participation grade. Exam grading may be a little vague and disputable but that is because marketing isn't math. Overall, good and experienced professor who will make you work for a good grade.

Was very well aligned with the student's interests and makes it very clear on how to approach the class. He is a humorous guy and his lectures are quite engaging. Recommend 10/10, extremely solid and knowledgeable professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof DePaoli was such a gem to have. His lectures were very clear, engaging and funny that they will make you want to listen. All the relevant information is on the ppts for the exam and his exams are not too difficult, but he is a definite fair grader. Such a funny person with a friendly personality too, made me LOVE the field of marketing A LOT!
The best teacher I have had at Northeastern University so far, 10/10 would recommend him as a teacher, and I would definitely take his class again!

Prof. DePaoli is by far the best teacher I have had in my freshman year at NEU. His lectures are amazing, and the class discussions he holds are very interesting as he allows you to be open but at the same time contribute effective towards the course. Tests are not hard, but you must know your marketing knowledge which he provides in his ppts.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Most knowledgable professor I've had. He seems to know everything about the world, its pretty amazing. His exams are actually enjoyable and really interesting because they relate to current real-world stuff so well. Would definitely take him again
He lectures and lectures are interesting and engaging. Prof. DePaoli provides clear grading criteria and would willing to give you feedback. I would choose him again if I could!

Prof. DePaoli is an interesting and hilarious person. You wouldn't feel his lectures boring even though it is merely intro to marketing course. He would quickly reply e-mails you sent asking questions. CHOOSE his if you can.

I choose him for 8a.m. course with no regret. He gives amazing lectures and welcome to questions. Prof. DePaoli is smart and charming, he grade stuffs nicely and always respect his students. Choose him if you have the opportunity to do so, maybe you would even shift your major to marketing!

He lectures but lectures are interesting and you always get chance to participate in class (give examples or explain terminology). Prof. DePaoli provides clear grading criteria and always try to give grades to his students. You can ask him questions and he can give you good answers. Choose him for your intro. to marketing course with no regret!

Alexander DePaoli is always accessible outside class, you can just shot him an e-mail and he would respond quickly towards the question you ask. He also has the capability to make intro to marketing course funny and interesting. Even though A is not granted, he always see the effort you put into this course. Good professor, strongly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. DePaoli is a good prof and really smart, he makes marketing pretty interesting even if you aren't a fan of the subject. This is his first time teaching at NEU, or undergrads in general but he solicits lots of feedback to try to improve. Overall the class is NOT hard, but attendance (BE ON TIME) and participation are really important.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I don't love the field of marketing, but he makes it fun and engaging, plus he occasionally roasts annoying students which is fun. As long as you are paying attention in class and add to the discussion, participation won't be a problem. Very little homework, which is just part of participation grade. Textbook and slides are all you need to study.

First year teaching undergrads, so it was a very demanding class for intro to marketing. Participation is mandatory so is attendance, very strict on those two. Lots of reading before class. First test was difficult with lost of case studies, second was easier and less content. He does ask for feedback in class, so he is trying to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: EVEN IF YOU TRY YOUR BEST, YOU WILL STILL GET B

Brent is amazing. He is the most caring and understanding professor I have at the moment. He doesn't stresses students out but offers everything he can for students to get a good grade. I highly recommend you to take his class.

Brent does not really teach much and mostly sits in front of the class waiting for questions. It is not exactly bad, since you just do your own work. His grading criteria are clear, and if you ask questions he answers in detail and is always patient. Best to check your work with him in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor that I ever had in my life. The highest grade in my class is lower than the average grade in other professors' classes. And all the grades are graded when the course end, which means that I have no chance to improve my grade.

He is a really good professor. He is kind and knowledgeable, if you ask him question he will answer you with patient. However, to get an A is a little bit hard. He cares about detail and often hopes his students to create high quality work. Otherwise he is a good teacher.
Super hard, impossible to get an A
Very hard to get an A in this course
Really hard to get a high grade and unreasonable comments under your assignment. Attend every class still got a very low participation score.

Well, Professor Griffin is conscientious in teaching. I can learn a lot in his class. However, for a freshman, his course is more intensive and the requirements for paper and participation are very strict.

reviews.comment: Well, he really gave me a hard time with his unreasonable grading system in my first university semester. Never want to take his classes again.

reviews.comment: really hard to get a high grades
