reviews.comment: Professor Griffin is one of the best writing teacher I have ever met. I learn a lot in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Brent is the first English teacher that opened my eyes to a lot of writing techniques and honestly, I write a lot better than I did four months ago.

Not the greatest professor I would recommend for an 8am that no one wants to be at but is mandatory. He is strict on attendance. Can't be a minute late or he will make you which effects your grade. He can have his bright moments and you will learn and progress better as a writer but his attitude and tendencies make it not a good class.

don't recommend. very strict and ridiculous. time is a factor in this class. even if you are 1 or 2 mins late, you will be marked for it, even if you are printing assignments and projects for the class, which will waste a lot of paper. he is good at teaching and you will learn but his rules & strictness needs to lighten up to make the class better

Not best professor if you are planning on coming into class 1 or 2 mins late from printing assignments and projects for his class. He marks you tardy and it effects your grade.  He also doesn't work really well around students schedule if you're busy. basically he does know his stuff and you will learn but he's ridiculous & strict. don't recommend

Really interesting class. I didn't love the readings the first time around but after thoroughly discussing them in class I really liked the pieces he chose. Fair/easy grader. Speak up in class and be on time and try your best and you will do well. Take advantage of office hours.

I took the college writing class for speakers of other languages. This class will be very tough for foreigners, many of my classmates drop this class in the half of the term.  The attendance is also mandatory and strict. If you really want to learn something and challenge yourself, you can have a try.
Extremely  intelligent and helpful if you need it. A relatively easy grader. Just speak in class and he will love you.

the readings are dense but by the end of each unit, you do have a much better understanding. many drafts for the main papers, but he provides helpful feedback. encourages students to ask for help, but attend class/participate to get on his good side

He is a good teacher...looks like a college student and lovessss the material covered in class. There are about four or five main readings which are all VERY dense and tough to interpret. griffin does a good job of explaining them. homework almost every night, four main 6-8 pages paper are the bulk of the grade....he punishes those who skip class t
RUN if you want get A

I love Elizabeth and will take her for any class I can. She deeply cares about her students and is super approachable willing to help you out however way she can. She has offered me great advice and guidance not just in INTB1205 but also INTB4983. Truly pillar in her industry and amazing mentor and role model.

I had her at 8am which made it hard to enjoy, but she's a good lecturer who cares about students. The material isn't hard, but the test format makes exams difficult. Participation is graded harshly, and the group project is a big part of the class.

I LOVED Elizabeths 1205 class this semester, her tests were multiple choice, which I struggle with, however, there were SO many other ways to raise your grade. You can tell she really cares and wants you to do well so she'll give extra credit assignments. The 2 things worth the most are a group project and participation, but she's a fair grader!

Professor Moore is the BEST. She loves what she teaches and makes you love it too. Although her class is not easy, it's so worth it for the amount of learning you will take away. She posts all slides on Canvas, so there is plenty of study material. By far my favorite Professor, if you have the chance, take her class! Can't recommend it enough!

Really cares about the students and wants you to succeed. Knows the material well and makes the lectures interesting and entertaining. Long exams and semester long group project (2 presentations + one optional paper). Accessible outside of class, rubric a little confusing sometimes. Participation does matter.

Overall, she is a good professor and does her lectures well. I will say she tends to like certain students more than others in a very obvious manner. Her tests aren't bad, if you go to class, pay attention, study a bit before exams, you should be fine. The group project has aspects that are unclear since she has a lot of rubrics that she releases.
Great lectures, wants you to do well

exams were really hard and tedious. nevertheless, I genuinely enjoyed this class' lectures, homework and group assignments. Professor Moore also genuinely cared about each student and is entertaining to converse and listen to speak. I highly recommend taking her for International business
Elizabeth is open to accommodating if you need help, if you need a test deferred for a 10% reduction, and is flexible; she has helped me out a lot.

she knows a lot and class is interesting. attendance not mandatory but if you miss class you will be lost. a normal amount of homework, participation matters and get ready to present and work in groups. overall would take again, not an easy A tho.
Great Professor, loved learning from her! Extremely knowledgeable and approachable

I feel quite bad giving this score considering Professor Moore is genuinely so kind and cares (would take any in person class with her) but DO NOT take her online class. Was disorganized, her test questions were literally no where in the textbook or slides (likely just mentioned in lectures), and was generally just impossible.

She is very enthusiastic and you can tell she likes what she teaches. Her grading was fair and all of the classes were mostly lectures, she does go very fast but it was manageable. I didn't do so good on her tests but she gave us ways to boost our grade up so my final grade wasn't terrible. No final too which was so nice.

Dr. Moore is SUPER passionate about INTB which is great- very engaging. She is extremely harsh on grading (blames it on Business Department cracking down). You can participate 10 times in class and still get a B+ on participation. Exams will break your balls but can make some up through presentations and hw. Good luck that's all I have to say.
Professor Moore was the best. Very professional, efficient, knowledgable, caring, and smart. She works to make the class enjoyable and not stressful.

I loved Elizabeth so much, one of my favorite professors here! I had class 4 hrs a week from and she would give us a break and often let us leave early. Her lectures were engaging and I learned so much! Her tests were around 60-70 questions long, mcq and short answers. You should study for her tests but if you review her slides you'll do great.

Elizabeth is an extremely knowledgeable professor who makes every effort to connect with her students. She is caring, thoughtful, intentional, and well-traveled, and wants every student to truly comprehend what she's teaching. Her passion for teaching and research is tangible - I would take any class she teaches a million times over.
Impossible to get an A. Extremely tough grading.

I took Prof Moore in both this class and 2501 at the same time and she was great! I took this class once a week for 2-3 hour blocks ending around 7pm and even with that I looked forward to attending her class. She relies heavily on participation but the assignments are pretty manageable and interesting. Highly recommend!

Please take a class with Dr. Moore - I've had the chance to have her twice in my three years at Northeastern - never have I looked forward to getting to class more than when she teaches. Come prepared, be respectful, be engaging, do your homework and you'll be just fine!

loved this professor and the class! only hw was the online debate (200-word post twice a week), and as long as you do them on time, she'll give an A. 3 online exams were pretty manageable. group project is a lot of work, so just hope you have a good group. cares about peer reviews, which is nice. would definitely take another class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An amazing professor, I looked forward to this class weekly! It was challenging at times, especially the tests, but I genuinely feel like I left this class a better student and learner.
This was my favorite class I have ever taken. Lectures are extremely interesting/engaging and the debates are fun! Would definitely take again if I could.

Dr. Moore is such a great professor. Although this was not the easiest class I have taken, I feel like I got a lot out of it. Her tests are hard (there are 3 throughout the semester and the last one is sort of optional). Group project is a huge part of the class and there are 2 parts of it. informative lectures, doesagreatjobkeepingtheclassengaged.
Suffering class
Exam too difficult, hard to get a good score
Excellent professor, very caring!
Class was purely on memorization with little teaching
Awful.

Cream of the crop. She is engaging. She is caring. She is clear. She is informative. I have learned so much. Her tests are somewhat difficult but serve its purpose -- if you truly are grappling with the ideas and nature of what she is saying they shouldn't be too bad. Also shes super understanding in case you have any issues.

Professor Moore is absolutely amazing! She is not only knowledgeable about the subject matter but is also very passionate about it. Her lectures and supplementary materials were very eye-opening and I learned a lot. Group projects are common and participation matters, but this is all to help you become a better global manager. Definitely recommend!

Professor Moore is genuinely one of my best professors, not only because of who caring and generous she is, but also because of how she challenges you in class. She made my love for international business grow fonder while giving the class exams and assignments that were well thought out, not feeling like busy work. She's amazing and reachable!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Moore is wonderful; I liked her from day one. Her tests are hard and practically impossible to get an A on. BUT, she's seriously a fabulous teacher who pushes you and has your best interest at heart. Very sweet, approachable, cares for her students. Very experienced too. I would highly recommend and can't wait to take another class with her!

Wonderful teacher! Had her my first semester for freshman year and she is one of the most engaging and interesting professors. Speak up during lectures and actually participate in class because there are a lot of discussions and opportunities to participate, and if you do it will make the class that much more rewarding.

Best professor ever!! I seriously cannot say enough about Elizabeth. Let me say that this was NOT an easy class by any means, the material is tricky and you definitely have to work hard, but her lectures are very interesting and the work/grading is fair! Not intimidating at all, awesome instructor for my first semester of college!

She is probably the best professor I had so far in the program. Her lectures are amazing and clear. There is a lot of work but it is actually interesting. I really like this course and the professor. If you had the option to have her as a professor, would recommend to def pick her class.
Elizabeth is truly an amazing person. She's extremely smart, personable, and cares for the materials and the students in her class. If you get the chance, try to take a class with her !!!

Moore is hands down the best professor for any class you need to take. She is interested in her work and brings that passion to class. The lectures are super interesting, but there are a lot of group projects, and you'll stay in the same group for the whole semester. She's really accommodating and works with you through any issues.
The best teacher for any INTB class, no doubt about it.
Without a doubt, the best teacher for INTB1203.

best teacher i have ever had. very interesting lectures and makes class so much more enjoyable with great content and engaging debate activities. 3 non-cumulative tests and a big project but no final. best teacher at northeastern!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Liz is fantastic! She truly cares about students and making sure everyone learns. I really hate statistics but I am so glad I had it with her because she could make even the most boring subject fun, exciting, and understandable! She is always available to answer questions or meet with student outside class. Would take anything she teaches again!

Liz is the coolest teacher you'll ever take. By far favorite teacher of the semester, she's nice and her class is interesting. You learn a lot without feeling pressured and she is very understanding about the amount of course work given. Wish I could be in her class next semester.

Professor Wolfe is very clearly passionate about this class clearly wants you to perform well in his class and does his best to try to make the content interesting (imo failing because it was just completely uninteresting) Most of your grade comes from weekly, fairly easy quizzes and online progress checks.
He is an amazing professor who cares about the success of his students. As long as you're consistent on quizzes and do all the extra credit, you should be able to get an A.

He talks to us like we're like 5 but it works when the topic is complicated. Participation is through PollEverywhere which is nice because it gives everyone an opportunity to take part in class. In the class, there are 10 quizzes and a final, two of which are dropped. If you study and understand the material the quizzes are pretty straightforward.
really passionate about what hes teaching and gives great support and feedback
Chill dude. He's the goat.

Prof Wolfe is super nice guy. His lectures are boring and I didn't really pay attention ngl, but that's finance for you. The tests are hard but as long as you study the assessments/hws A LOT you will be fine. Overall difficult class but he makes it a lot better and is always willing to help.

Super nice guy and he clearly wants everyone to succeed. Every test can be taken using excel and with a cheat sheet, but even if you don't do great on the tests, he offers lots of extra credit opportunities that go a long way.

Attendance isn't mandatory, but you're graded on participation for each unit using polleverywhere. He allows cheat sheets for both midterms and the final, and a bunch of easy points assignments and extra credit opportunities. I barely studied for this class (mostly just by making my cheat sheets) and got a solid A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very nice guy but the class is entirely based on Connect assignments which can be random and not reflective of what we practice in class. The midterms and final are all on Connect, and they were a lot harder than the homework we had been given or the problems we did in class.
great guy and great teacher overall
Chill guy, reasonably difficult class. I sold with my grade, but that's on me, not Professor Wolfe. Zero complaints about the guy and would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love this woman for Russian which is saying a lot. If you just show up to class and participate and try to match her energy it'll reflect on your grade. Some homework nothing too difficult and tests are easy too. For a very difficult language I could not ask for a better teacher.

I have previous Russian experience which def made this course easier for me but I thought Olga was generally a good professor. Class is participation heavy/interactive rather than lecture which helped with practicing.
Stick to rules, harsh, treat essays like linguistic functions rather than creative impressions.

This is the worst teacher I have ever seen. No one who has taken her class will give her a positive comment. Although the atmosphere in her class is very good, she is extremely cruel after class. She won't give you a chance to correct your homework and will only give you a very low grade(50%-80%). No one gets an A, and almost no one gets an A-.
The class was not hard but she seems inexperienced and fearful, not the vibe I want from a mentor
I do NOT recommend. no substance and poorly organized imo

TAKE HER CLASS, shes so sweet and her classes are honestly so fun. They're very discussion heavy so as long as you yap you'll be fine. There is a good amount of reading/ movies but honestly if you skim them you'll be fine. Her papers are mostly opinion based and casual. She will also cater the class to what your class wants to discuss. Shes awesome

Took 3301 with him. Professor Murray was the best. I truly learned so much from him. I am not one to participate in class, but it is truly necessary to succeed and get a good grade in this course. Lastly, his exams are super fair and have no multiple choice.
Best professor!!
Great Professor! Extr
bob's great. he has great speakers and interesting personal anecdotes. he still skis all the time which is insane... overall, i really enjoyed his class and my friends did too. i recommend :)
The prof is awful, I was at a high A and but my final grade was something else. He did not disclose as to what my grades are for participation and negotiation. All my efforts went to waste.
In SCHM6318, you get more than a crash course in all things supply chain, you also get the opportunity to guess how your professor wants you to write your answers!

He definitely makes an effort to make a somewhat dry subject (if you're not interested in it, that is) engaging. A decent amount of work every week, but it's necessary to stay on top of everything. Gives plenty of opportunities to ask him questions and really cares about learning.
I learned a great deal and although it is a lot of work, he is an incredibly helpful and caring professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Bob was an awesome and inspirational supply chain professor. He made a seemingly boring subject so interesting that I'm pursuing it as a concentration! We did write a lot of small case analyses which he graded fairly and quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was nervous going into SC because I heard that it was very tough, but I found Bob and I really enjoyed going to this class. He has lots of real life experience, and friends in the field that come and give guest lectures. Prepares class for the tests very well, fair grader, makes sure everyone understands the material and overall class avg was B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Bob is a great person who cares for all his students. He takes attendance and participation greatly. Learn from all the materials in class and you should end up with a pretty good grade. He brings in speakers and offered students who are interested in internships with connections.
Great class. If you are serious about learning more, I'd highly recommend. Workload is very manageable.

Bob Murray is a very down to earth, nice guy. Very much enjoyed having him as a professor- he is super intelligent, has worked in the field, is well connected and is passionate about what he teaches. I would highly recommend him and if you put in honest effort into the class, you will do well.

Methodical approach to how class operates. 1 page executive brief every week, 2 tests, and a case study presentation. He comes straight from industry holding multiple VP roles and organizes his class towards the real world. Incredibly smart and teaches you a lot. Put in a decent effort and you can get an A.

Bob is absolutely an awesome guy, both as a person and as a professor. He really is one of the good ones. He is incredibly knowledgeable about supply chain and has decades of experience in the industry, and it proves so worthwhile in class. I hope to have him as a professor once again, I've really never learned more  from a professor than from Bob.

The professor is nice, but he mainly reads from the slides and tries to be engaging, which makes the class quite boring. He assigns readings every week but discusses them in class. Very few assignments and quizzes are take home and open notes

Genuinely the easiest A ever, the only annoying thing is that attendance is mandatory. Some lectures are actually engaging, though, because he uses modern pop culture examples to teach certain units. 3 online quizzes, one written op-ed, and a few class activities make up your grade. No final.

He is really sweet and caring for his students. Class is pretty boring, mostly lecture and some awkward participation. But you only have 3 quizzes and most are online. Lots of boring readings but he goes over them in class so you don't need to read them in depth.

Very boring lectures, he just reads right off the slides. It felt like we learned the same exact thing every class and was repetitive. The class was really easy, simple in-class assignments and online quizzes, no midterm or final exams. Overall, pick a different class I don't feel like I learned anything.
He is so nice. Class is an easy A if you participate a bit and skim the readings. He's a bit boring as a lecturer but really nice to chat with and tries to engage the students.

Incredibly boring and irrelevant, I learned nothing new as the lessons were designed possibly for an entry level high school course at most. The readings were dry, and the discussions were dryer. However, there were virtually no assignments or work or responsibilities. Waste of money but an easy A.

This course was not good. The professor was not engaging in lectures, he wanted us to participate but did nothing to motivate us to do so. His material was not engaging and the in-class activities were made for middle-schoolers. He read off the screen and his notes and the material were boring when the class title seemed engaging.

One strength about Professor Banalieva is the way she taught classes. She encouraged class discussions on reading materials or to challenge and expand classmates' arguments. This created an inclusive learning environment. If you have to take INTB1203, take her, she's is probably the best INTB1203 professor here.
Grading is a bit weird she grades some things easy and other things harshly. Exams were pretty easy, a lot of your grade is dependent on your group. Overall decent class shes nice.

This was a very hard class and she is a very tough grader but she is very kind and wants to help you. The exams weren't that bad, as long as you studied what was on the rubric. One group project whole semester, and you get to choose your partners. She is a stickler to formatting and will take off points if you forget page numbers.

Phenomenal professor who genuinely cares and wants to see you put in effort to get a good result. Participation matters and she respects if you put in effort in that way. Choose a good group... will be essential for how easy/difficult this class is (besides exams). She is very qualified and passionate about her work. Strongly recommend. Loved it.
loves her job and is knowledgeable, i would say pick ur groups wisely because group projects are worth over 40% and be ready to put in the effort

She gets confused by technology a lot, which is annoying. She is very harsh with her participation grading. She's not the worst professor ever, but it's just very boring, she isn't very helpful, and she gives a ton of group projects with unclear instructions.

Basically all group projects, so choose your group wisely. Students pick the format of the exams. The questions are based off of her lectures not the textbook, so go to class. While I loved her as a Professor the amount of work felt like she thought we were only taking her course. If it says to start something early on the syllabus start it early!

Incredible professor -  my favorite class I've taken so far. It does involve a lot of work, specifically group projects,  but as long as you take it seriously you will do well. Don't bother reading the textbook and make sure to participate!!! Also, the test are basically just about lectures so make sure to go.

Pick your groups wisely because there will be a lot of group activities and projects. Follow the syllabus and you will be fine. Two exams for the whole semester where the class decides on the format and questions to the exams. 4 online "quizzes" but they're just 2 multiple choice questions each. Very fair professor with a lot of hands on activities

She is a decent teacher and knows what she is talking about. There are 2 tests but some test content is not discussed in class. Your grade is also highly dependent on group projects so choose members wisely because you'll also be working with them for the whole semester. I would say this is a B+/A- class if you actually try.

She was a great professor and really nice. Interesting class but be prepared for lots of group work. She does grade tough on certain assignments but at the end slightly curves grades. A- is very attainable if you put in the work you can pull away with an A. Overall would highly recommend Professor Banalieva.

It was honestly a very fun class. I learnt so much. I have almost completed 2 sems and INTB has been my fav. It was a bit of work but fun work, interactive work, where we learnt. We had class structured debates and presentations. So so fun. I would love to take the class again. She really did not like me, regardless I loved the class.

not too hard but it's a waste of time if you're trying to learn something usefull. The study guides and exams contain a lot of material that is not covered during the lectures. She will harm your participation grade if she doesn't agree with your opinons, and spends a lot of time doing discussions about content with little to no value.

Great professor with engaging lessons and class activities that make you think. A lot of the grades rely on group projects so make sure you choose members wisely. She clearly lays out the requirements and grading rubrics for assignments and gives good feedback so they are relatively straightforward and even enjoyable.
Lot of work but its fun
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: She did an awesome job delivering the class materials to students. Very engaging lectures! If you want to do well in this class, make sure you participate in class discussions. She introduced so many perspectives for students to debate and discuss. I heard great things abt other INTB professors but prof. Banalieva is definitely a solid choice

She can be unreasonable. She took my midterm away when I hadn't finished for asking a question (after she answered it). She is not nice if you don't agree with her opinions. Exams are straightforward, it's easy to do well if you go over the study guides. Participation grade is worth a lot , and grading is subjective since it's not a small class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. B has really good in person lectures that require participation. She grades tough, so be prepared to answer every question during presentations. Read the book, it helps. DIscussion boards used when we went online, so my grade improved. 2 Tests & no final, but lots of projects! Overall, a good class! She wants you to succeed and really cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: THE most enjoyable class I took last semester. A lot of class discussion and many people offering their opinions. Not a difficult class content wise, but there are many projects and papers. Make sure you choose a smart group, because your grade will be heavily dependent on their work. Participation matters but still possible to get full points.
The tests are really easy if you look at the study guide she provides. Class discussion was probably the best among all my classes as everyone gets involved.

Amazing professor, in fact my favorite professor I took last semester. We have 2 tests, no final, 1 group debate( very interesting topics ), and 1 group project. Professor Banalieva allows her class to be an interactive lecture and is more than open to others opinions. SHE IS A MUST TAKE FOR THIS COURSE!

Participation is important in  her class, and she can be a VERY tough grader on papers and presentation. However,Professor Banalieva is definitely a passionate and caring teacher, and she definitely knows the material. The slides and her lectures are very engaging, which makes the class fun. Exams are not too bad. I would recommend.

Professor Banalieva's class is not an easy A by any means, however, if you want a challenging class where you will learn a lot take this class. Her grading for writing is difficult and her exams are very fair. She wants you to learn and do well in her class. Her lectures are very enthusiatic and informative. There are also two large group projects.

Professor Banalieva was really great. If you put in the work, go to class, participate, and are actively willing to do well, you will succeed. There are a few big projects and papers, but expectations are very clearly laid out in the syllabus from Day 1. She genuinely cares about students. If you want to learn a lot, definitely take this class!

She's a very tough grader and refuses to give people A's even when she admits that their work is outstanding. Avoid taking her at all costs if you want to do well because she gives people low grades for participation (worth 150 points) even if they've shown up to class everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst professor in my entire college experience. Avoid if you can

Sweetest person I've ever met. Loved her; absolutely hated her class. There were 3 separate group projects for the one class and they were graded so harshly.  Only two exams, no cumulative final.  The exams are not in synch with the review guide she provides.  The workload was crazy, I felt like I had to choose between this class and my others.
Dont take her if you dont want to suffer!!!!
Worst experience of my life!! Avoid her

Banalieva's class was probably the worst experience of my life. She thinks that INTB is your only course and assigns an insane amount of work. She seems so sweet, but in reality she'll take off points on your assignments for no specified  reason. Also she rounds down, if you have a 94.9 she rounds down to an A-. Pretty sure an A is impossible.

She is a hard grader and deduct huge points(30 out of 100) for not handing in unrelevant things like peer evaluation. Also make unrealistic and vague requirements for papers. Loads of work and need to be avoided!!!

Banalieva is a very good instructor, she was enthusiastic about the topic's she taught, and her class discussion not only made class interesting, but I really learnt a lot. I have to admit that this course was challenging, and that at times you do have to fight hard for a good grade, but I did learn a lot at the end of the day. Definitely recommend
Alot of reading, most of it optional but sometimes gives pop quizzes that aren't very hard. Pretty interesting class but she expects alot of participation.
i wish i can write something nice about her, why she still

The prof is a nice person, very respectful. But the class is tough. Too many reading, writings, projects. I feel like I am majoring in IB in this semester, doing IB things everyday. Her lectures are interesting, but participation is mandatory. Grading in writing is also harsh... Avoid her if you're not ready for tons of readings and writings.

Great class if you are motivated and willing to put effort. In addition, we learn to think analytically and gain first experience in collaborating with other. Not a class for those who are seeking an easy way out.

There is a lot of work, and you spend a lot of time outside of class, but she is very fair.  I learned a great deal from this professor, and really enjoyed the class. Participation is a must, and reading is a must.  If you are looking to coast, this isn't the class, but it is a beneficial class!  She is an excellent professor.
Interesting class and nice teacher. She is passionate about the subject and wants student to succeed. Quite a lot of reading, fair tests and project. Do not hesitate to take her!
Very nice and professional. Has a passion for the subject. Would recommend.
She is amazing! Fun, caring and resourceful teacher that makes everything easy. However, she does have a HUGE preference for foreigners.

Banalieva is amazing! I thoroughly enjoyed her class; she's knowledgeable, engaging, and helpful. The class is a fair amount of work, but the projects and debates are enjoyable. Participate and read the class pack.
Good teacher overall. Does have a significant amount preference towards foreigners, ESPECIALLY Frech students. If you are French, she will love you.
Amazing teacher. Very nice, professional, and willing to help. Encourages questions, and is not afraid to explain her point of view unlike some professors who get angry for questioning them.

Highly recommend this teacher for anyone wanting to take international business. She is extremely nice, always available to meet with you, and clear on telling you what she expects in work. Have 2 Tests the entire semester, 2 news article write ups, and a major IB project. Must show up to class, participate. Do this and ur guaranteed a good grade.

The best professor ever. She will always help and encourage you. You will learn a lot from her, not just about International Business, but also about life. Attend every class, it is an enjoyable class. Don't be afraid to participate, just say what is in your mind. She will not embarrass you even if you have a stupid comment. Take her for INBU203!

Very knowledable, helpful, and sweet professor. She really knows her stuff. When we went over the syllabus on the first day of class, I was overwhelmed. This class is a lot of work but I learned A LOT. This has been one of my favorite classes because you learn a lot and it's a fun class. TAKE HER!
A LOT of work but fun teacher

Majority of grade is based off of participation, attendance, and in class excercises that are guaranteed 100's. I did not like this because I never went to class. However, if you aren't intelligent and would like to be graded more on coming to class, definately the one to take. Final project and hw counts for almost nothing.

Extremely straightforward professor who makes her expectations really clear.  Showing up to class guarantees you at least a B on exams ... EVERY SINGLE QUESTION on her tests has been discussed in-class.

random inclass exercises, only three written homework assignments, exams are 160 points 4pts per question, know slides for exams, CLASS PARTICIPATION IS IMPORTANT so if you're not into joining in on discussions (which is pretty much the whole class) then maybe you should stay away from this class.

If you don't know anything about international business policies and organizations then you better be ready to study extremely hard! Participation is a MUSTT and she's a really hard grader.  If you don't understand something it's really hard to catch up.  There are a lot of random graded exercises, and the exams are all multiple choice, 4 pts each.

Good professor, very clear about what she wants. Tests are multiple choice, very easy if you stay on top of the readings. Has very little tolerance for students that come to class unprepared (ie not doing the homework / reading). Very engaging during lectures and tries to make the class interesting. Good overall.
I am unsure as to why there are so many negative ratings. Professor O'Connell is very nice, and his class is engaging. It can be a lot of work, so make sure to stay on top of things.

Avoid this class unless you have nothing else going on. Mandatory volunteering plus 3+ assignments most nights, each taking 1–2 hours with tedious steps. Grading is harsh, the late policy is unforgiving, and getting a response outside class is nearly impossible. If you can get out of stacked cornerstone DO IT AT ALL COSTS
He chill and shi

Stacked cornerstone is a weed out class. I often had 40+ hrs of hw a week, group projects were very intense and grading was harsh. He's a very nice guy but has very high expectations in an INTENSE class. You will be LIVING in fyelic if you don't have a foundation of coding before this course. This class will erase your social life. Good luck.

O'Connell is a passionate, good professor. He is open to helping students at a moments notice almost 24/7 through teams, and is focused on leaving students with a solid understanding of the course curriculum, which is very important given the nature of the course. Put in some effort, don't expect to have your hand held and you will do great.

O'Connell's great. Available, gives good feedback, answers questions promptly. However, stacked cornerstone is so miserable that I wouldn't recommend anybody take it. The flipped classroom method means half the lectures are useless. The group project is frustrating. Do not take 1501+1502 if you have other difficult classes running concurrently.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His directions for group projects often is contradictory. The rubrics were different than the guide and it ended with us at one point getting a 65 on part of a project. With weekly assignments, I felt more self taught when it came to graphics and coding as the learning style was reversed and he would just show a presentation. He is online for help.

The overall class isn't that difficult, but taking stacked cornerstone is so much work, like 30+ hours a week. O'Connell is a pretty decent professor and responded to my questions and messages within a couple hours. I felt that the lectures did not connect with the homework. I would not recommend stacking cornerstone unless absolutely necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nothing that conceptually hard about the course but stacked cornerstone is grueling. 25-40 hours a week. Never take stacked cornerstone by choice unless you have a lighter schedule. Nothing bad to say about prof oconnell but his class was kind of dry. If you must take stacked try to work on the homework in groups to save yourself time.
classes were completely a waste of time, as we were assigned to learn the same thing online before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The workload for stacked cornerstone is absolutely insane and you will spend 20-30 hours a week doing homework outside of class. The instructions for his assignments are vague and often make no sense. Avoid taking stacked cornerstone if you can.
The instructor was very proficient in all of the course's aspects and was able to explain anything a student could have a question on.
he definitely is a fan of what he teaches, and that much is apparent, whether you agree with his teaching methods or not

Most of class is major group projects, but he uses a god-awful digital textbook software called tophat that integrates discussion posts and makes a few of these due a week. Class itself isn't that hard but turnaround time on projects during the summer is very fast, and discussion posts are inherently evil. Cool guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Was available for help, taught concepts well and was well organized
Very responsive. Lots of enthusiasm/passion. Frequent office hours and helpful online.

I think the professor was fantastic. They were very helpful in all aspects and were understanding when a student was having trouble. Coming to class was really helpful bc we would start assignments in class. He held frequent office hours and was always available to respond to messages on Teams.

The instructor did a good job explaining new software/coding languages. While there's some criticism about the difficulty of the course, you are in class to learn, and O'Connell provides an amazing environment to learn in.

He's very accessible outside of class and answers within minutes. This stacked class is extremely heavy, many all nighters are necessary. He is very helpful if you reach out to him. Assignment details are vague and can be difficult to follow when you don't even know what its fully asking. I would recommend him over the other professors for stacked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a very content-heavy class, but Prof. O'Connell made it extremely manageable and easy to get an A if effort is put in. He is always accessible and responds quickly via Microsoft Teams, which helped me out during difficult homework assignments. The class ramps up during the last few weeks, but O'Connell supported us through the process!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: O'Connell is awesome. You can tell he really loves teaching, and his lectures are interactive, interesting + funny too. He is easy to reach out of class and always responds very quickly. The class is a lot of work, but it IS an 8 credit combined class. He is very easy with grading, and it is easy to do well if you do the homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear lectures, clear assignments, and is willing to help outside of class. However, I don't think having a good and likable teacher should be top priority in a class with such simple material, escpecially when the workload in his class is much more than most other 1501/02 professors. Avoid if you're schedule already has high workload classes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is willing to work through things with students when they need help and is very accessible during the projects. He is fair in that if you communicate to him, he is understanding, and if you do not communicate with him, he will not be as lenient.
He was always prepared for class and was always willing to help. You can reach out to him at any time of day, and he is always there to assist.
He's a bit of a "tough love" kind of teacher. He teaches you a lot, but you have to work for it. Very well organized and gave lots of additional resources to reference for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: O'Connell is by far the best first year engineering professor. While his class is marginally more challenging, he is available at essentially all times and provides vey clear instructions for the course.

Professor O'Connell is always available for help, whether in person or on Teams. His assignments are challenging, but he is fair with grading. If you communicate well with him, he is understanding with work/deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He does not deserve the bad ratings! Really nice professor, answers every question, and is more than willing to help you. Also, he responds on teams almost instantly. Compared to the other stacked cornerstone class, he was a much more relaxed professor, and even gave us a lot of extensions on assignments. PRO TIP: GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS!!

O'Connell's not a bad professor but do not take this course unless you have to. Way more than double the work of a regular cornerstone class. The assignment descriptions are vague and lots of the homework includes parts of software you have never seen before. If you don't understand them and you're doing it over the weekend you're kind of screwed.

Of course its a hard class, it is your first engineering class. Go to lectures. Do the in class portions, in the class. He is incredibly understanding, and he'll help you reach your goals if you help yourself. He is very knowledgeable and open. He teaches and grades strict because that is what engineering is like in the real world.

O'Connell is super accessible outside of class. Anytime you're struggling with homework or anything at all just message him on Teams and he will respond right away. Lots of homeworks and work outside class but if you go to FYELIC and message the prof in time it's great. Very understanding and great specific lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I literally switched out of engineering after his class. Terrible professor. Though I did take this class during the height of the pandemic so everything was online, but judging by the previous reviews, not much changed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Every SINGLE class will be him reading from slides, he doesn't show/ explain any of the important material enough and if you need to take your attention away YOU WILL fall behind on the lecture, and if you're coding you might as will give up he will not let you catch up. Learn to teach yourself PLEASE, do not waste your time with him if you get him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You will receive little to no help on assignments, have a plethora of software to barely begin learning at the exact same time, and google will often be your friend. Good luck
Learned a lot from him this semester, and he was always willing to help inside/outside of class. Don't know why the ratings are low.
Not a good Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Legitimately not sure how to describe how bad his class was. All of the other reviews are true. Literal constant homework assignments, grading is incredibly harsh (Canvas' "mean scores" tell-all), easily the meanest professor I've had in my years at NEU. Don't even consider asking about a grade received, it does nothing; may make things worse.

All of the other reviews are correct, he is very impatient and unclear about deadlines, really no time to learn and mostly force feeds poorly presented info. Final project has nothing to do with course content. FYELIC will be your best friend, really didn't learn much despite hours on hours that I put in. Take other profs if you can if not goodluck
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was lucky to have a small amount of coding experience prior to this class. Professor O'Connell claims that the class is for an introductory level coder; however, I was reliant on a lot of my knowledge prior to the class to get through the assignments. If you do not know a topic prior to the class, expect to learn it on your own.

If there was a rating for their ability to crush any remaining passion I had left for engineering, he would get a 5/5. Maybe he's fine in other regards, but in this class, homework was overwhelming and he went way too fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Possibly one of the worst professors I've ever had. He reads off of lecture slides at 1000 mph and doesn't give you time to read It or think about It yourself. He doesn't teach he reads, I could do that on my own time. Assignment due every 2-3 days and It usually takes that time to finish an assignment. never get a break. never take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In class, we go over a bunch of slides where the professor reads it outloud like were unable to read on our own. Doesnt really explain what were supposed to be doing properly which causes a lot of confusion and lots of hours spent on assignments. Be prepared to go to tutoring for every single assignment if you dont have prior knowledge of codin
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I do not recommend taking Prof O'Connell for cornerstone 2. Lectures consist of vague slides and him typing code on his computer and showing it on the projector with little to no explanation on what he just did. Unless you have prior coding experience, be prepared to get help on homeworks of which he gives a substantial amount of.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have no coding experience going into this class, you're lowkey screwed. Often times the homework is much more complex than what you learn in class so to get a good grade, get used to constantly going to tutoring sessions, working with upperclassmen, or just straight up teaching yourself. Very lecture heavy, most classes you work in silence.

Worst formatted course I have ever taken. Info in the slides is vague and not helpful for actual assignments. Lectures are not presented well. Quizzes are impossible to prepare for. Workload is astronomical. Worst of all he put all assignment info on TopHat, very unorganized and couldve been provided for free on canvas. wish I could rate 0/5.
Super chill and nice guy, had him for full cornerstone so he definitely worked us pretty hard but it was nothing I couldn't handle.

I do not recommend taking a class taught by him online. His slides and method of teaching is very choppy and does not make sense most of the time. Lots of typing code in silence and then sitting there expecting us to understand what he just did. Also a fairly harsh grader, and loves participation and attendance. Taught myself most of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: O'Connell is an amazing guy. He is well passionate on topics discussed in class. One major down side about his course is that you really need to acquire a solid background on what is taught. The fact that all lessons are posted online, and his expectancy of students to teach themselves, makes it hard for beginners to reach their goals.
Course should be taught online

O'Connell consistently gives more work and grades harder than other Cornerstone professors. However, he is also a better teacher and all around great guy. If you're willing to work for the grade, you will learn a lot from him.

Prof. O'Connell is a really chill guy. He is really helpful and clear about the group project assignments. However, his lessons for new software can be hard to follow and are mostly meant to be self taught. This makes the homework assignments really difficult, especially for students who do not have any prior experience.

The professor is a great guy but never teach/lecture in class. Every assignment and new program (for CAD and coding) are expected to be self-taught. This makes it very hard for beginners to learn a new program for the first time. An online class might help more. Give MUCH more homework than other professors of the same course.

He's pretty laid-back and doesn't care if assignments are handed in a day or two late. The class was pretty easy. He was a generous grader on AutoCAD/SolidWorks assignments and on our final assignments but was tougher on memos and presentations for our group design projects. The lectures were pretty useless but he took attendance randomly, so...
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Prof Zullo overall is a good teacher and he knows the information well and is good at explaining it. The no laptop policy during lecture, Ipad is fine as long as it is flat. Some of his policies are unnecessary. If he sees a phone on the table, he will call you out, he defers everything to the TA, seems like he likes to make fun of students.

DO NOT take him. Incredibly frustrating professor who does the bare minimum. He mainly just reads off slides, does not allow computers or any technology, and does not answer any questions about exams, nor does he provide any study guides/ adequate preparation tips. He tosses off all the grading to the TA, and his demeanor is pretty condescending.

Don't let the negative reviews deter you from taking Zullo. He's a solid professor, and I felt the level of work and expectations aligned with tax being a 4000 level class. Just stay on top of the readings, assignments/projects, and studying and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Will he teach you tax? Yes. Does that mean he should be a professor? No. 

If you have the choice for your accounting elective, don't take this class. There are group projects that you are left alone to drown with and a final that is all multiple choice. Choose the other elective, the credit hours is not worth all the pain this class is

ACCT 6231 - Don't pay attention to the negative reviews. Those tend to come from students who may not have been prepared for the level of rigor Prof. Zullo expects. He runs his course much like a law school professor would: be on time, be prepared, and be ready to engage. He sets a high bar and holds students accountable.

Very good professor who values getting work in on time. If you can't adhere to schedule and submit assignments when you are asked to, don't take his class. If you are ready to learn, his class is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you are going onto a masters program or taking the CPA exam you want to take him for tax. You actually learn  how to do it unlike the other teachers, if not take sm else.

I really liked his lecture style as he does a lot of in class practice with questions very similar to the tests. The hardest part is the group projects as you have to figure a lot out on your own but if you ask questions about it in class he is more willing to aid. Just make sure you show up and participate and you'll do well.
Just a bad guy overall. He's there to make fun of students and give them a hard time with grades. Northeastern please address this issue!

Professor Zullo gets a bad rep because he has high expectations, but if you show up to class and put in the effort to understand the course concepts then you will definitely meet them. He wants whats best for his students and is very understanding esp. if you prove you care. If you aren't willing to put in the effort then this class isn't for you.

Actually not bad at all. Expects students to study and is strict about deadlines, lectures well. The exams and projects were fair. Accessible during office hours.

Class takes some work (for me, >10 hours/week), although this workload is probably a given since it's a 4000+ class. 

I enjoyed his class, and I think he's a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No leniency at all. I feel bad if you have to take him next semester. Not qualified enough to teach at northeastern and seems to take out all of his anger on students from his boring life
Worst professor at northeastern. Surprised he has any good reviews. pretty sure he writes them himself
honestly a really good prof. if you pay attention and actually try to learn, you will do so and do well in his class. couldn't recommend more

It's pretty hard to make to make an income tax class engaging, but Zullo tries his hardest. There is a lot of content and the class isn't easy, but if you put in work it's not impossible to get an A. For each exam you are allowed a written cheat sheet. There are two group projects that are pretty difficult and he doesn't provide much guidance.

Prof Zullo is hands down one of the best professors ever. He is funny and kind and cares deeply about every one of his students. If you show up to class and engage with the materials you will do well because he designs his class for success as long as you put in the work. He is not just a great professor, but he is an overall amazing person.

Super nice guy. As long as you show-up to class and participate it's not too bad. Homework assignments aren't bad at all (just a few connect problems each week). Professor Zullo is so kind and funny which makes the class great. He does take forever to grade assignments but other then that, I recommend this class!

Prof Zullo is a great teacher who cares about his students. Glad I didn't listen to the other reviews and took his class. Paying attention during lectures and doing the homework is the key to doing well on the tests (although lectures can get a bit boring). For group projects, make sure to read the rubric carefully. Put in the work and you're good

Each week, a new chapter to read, each ch 30 around pages. Had to do tax return project without ever doing a tax form together in class. Only 2 exams. You need to be independent in this class. Don't take him if you're not the best reader or if it takes you a lot of practice to get concepts. He wont be providing many practice problems for you.
Wasn't as bad as I expected honestly. If you're one of those students that just slacks off and complains when you perform badly, well you should've expected that. Put in the work, and youre gold.

He is a tough grader and has the driest lectures where he talks at you for an hour and expects the entire class to participate, then the class average on each test is a B- and he refuses to curve or adjust any grades, honestly any other professor would be better. he's an accountant who obviously doesn't understand the impact of low grades
DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS

Super surprised at how much I liked Zullo! He gets that tax is tough and he makes sure to go over concepts thoroughly and invites questions. I didn't think he was a tough grader, I'd say average. He managed to make tax interesting and funny. Class was a combo of lecture and example problems, which was perf. Would definitely take him again!

I'm so glad I didn't listen to the negative reviews on here. I absolutely LOVED Prof. Zullo! He made some hilarious dad jokes throughout his zoom lectures, and made sure that everyone participated. He will call on you if you don't actively participate. He was very clear with his expectations and explained things very well. I would 100% recommend!

I made the mistake of reading the harsh reviews on here before taking the course & was so worried but they couldnt have been more wrong. Prof Zullo made lectures enjoyable using humor & his extensive expertise in preparing tax returns for many clients. Take this class,youre going to learn such useful info even if you don't plan on becoming a CPA!

He's pretty good at teaching the subject in general, in fact the subject is fairly easy too. But is tough grader, espcially for cases. Nobody gets over 92% and is very strict about being fair. For example, he won't give answers to personal case questions, since "it's not fair", which I thought was pretty irresponsible. The tests are like average.

Took this over the summer and it was the biggest regret of my academic career. Zullo would rush through a chapter a day, skipping through slides for the sake of saying that we "covered the material." Really puts no effort into each lecture and made exams unreasonably difficult. Was absolutely ruthless.

EXAMS ARE SO HARD. He said certain things would be on the exam but the opposite were. Even if you completely understand a topic the exams will make you feel dumb. This professor does not even curve the exams for some reason. Please professor if you are reading this take it into consideration.

RUNAWAY!! TESTS ARE SO HARD AND UNCLEAR. BIGGEST MISTAKE was taking a class with him! Take with someone else, he's so hard and his midterm and finals are unnecessarily difficult. Worst. Take another prof, you'll thank me later!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was one of the most useless classes I've ever taken. Prof Zullo makes no attempt to make his class better for students. Every single class was a 100 minute lecture through a powerpoint.

Zullo's Managerial Accounting Class will be one of the more memorable classes I have taken in Northeastern. He's a great professor and a funny person. His grading can be harsh but reasonable. Would definitely recommend.

If you are the type of student who likes to be babied, given special treatment, given extenstions, etc. then Zullo is not for you. He makes things very clear and fair for everyone and he does have his own weird rules but they are made with the goal of being equally fair to everyone. Exams aren't difficult, lectures are pretty good, grading is fair.
Brutal. Avoid. Sucks. Better off professor who is in other deperarmtnets, he not nice and give BAD exam to all his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Zullo worst professor I take at neu. Hard examinations and tests - does not explain class and teach from powerpoint. Avoid.
worst professor EVER!!! he didnt reply to my emails, and when I went to his office hours he was rude and unwilling to help!

Prof. Zullo is a cool person all around, but as a professor he is a little hit or miss. He follows powerpoints, made by other professors. The homework is fine, my class was small easy to participate, the case studies however were always graded a bit too harshly in my opinion, the midterms were easy/medium, but the final was absolutely brutal...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Ron is a terrific guy. Always makes class enjoyable. Grading can be a bit tough but the material is relatively easy and the pacing is extremely manageable
Zullo is a good teacher and makes managerial easy. Pay attention in class and you will do fine on tests. Case studies are a bit more difficult but aren't graded harshly.

Professor Zullo is my favorite professor I've ever had. You definitely have to put a lot of work into this class to do well, but he makes lectures interesting and enjoyable and he's a great guy. Someone you can go to for help whenever you need it for whatever you need. He made a boring class so much better than it should've been.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Zullo really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. But, get ready to work hard and you will learn a ton of practical stuff. Talks a lot about real world clients. One of the best.

Zullo is by far the worst professor I had experienced in NEU. Zullo is good at his job of being a tax preparer, but he is SO terrible at teaching. He held the students to a high standard, even scrutiny, but give himself a huge slack when it comes to his responsibility. Tough grader, tricky test, need to work extremely hard to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Clearly knows material. Lectures are interesting, however, reading the textbook/ doing the homework is extremely boring/ confusing. Homework is not submitted/ graded, but it should be completed to keep up with the class. Grading on projects was tough. Exams consist of  mc - computational problems are very tough. No curve.
Teaching is good however very hard grader. Avoid
Prof.Zullo is a great teacher but a hard grader! His classes are not easy but because he teaches the material so well,   I recommend him highly!

Prof. Zullo is an amazing teacher. He made the class enjoyable for me. His class isn't easy, but if you do the work you'll be fine. Zullo is very fair with his grading and reasonable with his expectations. He will push you, but at the end of the day you will learn something.

Good class but not easy. You have to study for every class, material is not easy. Read slides before class, do all your homework and study for tests, I would say its an easy C+ B- if you are willing to study you should get a B

Professor Zullo is awesome. Although this class is difficult, he truly does everything he can to make his students succeed. He does plenty of examples in class and always asks for questions. He is very fair and will tell you exactly what concepts are covered on tests and exams. He is often available for extra help and makes the class very engaging.

Professor Zullo is really great!  He does take attendance so you should show up, but it's honestly fine to miss a few days, he doesn't care that much.  The quizzes and midterms are fair, not hard but you do have to study to do well.  The online homework isn't too bad.  He is a really funny guy and is always willing to help out!

I absolutely love Professor Zullo! He's a great teacher and also has a great sense of humor. I struggled a lot in this class (I'm a music industry major) and he was always available to ask questions, extra help, etc. Really laid back and isn't afraid to give it to you straight! Definitely one of my favorite professors at Northeastern. Awesome!
Very unhelpful professor. Would not recommend him to anyone
Great professor and just an overall cool guy.  Classes arent that boring for accounting.  Not super easy but not hard by any means.  He is really helpful especially during office hours.

One of my favorite professors so far at northeastern. the class is not super easy, but Zullo definitely cares about his students and wants them to do well. If you read and pay attention in class youll do fine. He also loves when you ask questions and go to office hours. I would recommend him!

Class is fine, very, VERY easy, lectures are great. MAKE SURE your Final Project team is good. But be sure to read instead of skimming or expect to lose tons of points (sometimes a % of your grade!) on completely random, arbitrary things

Class is OK, videos can be long but the requirements aren't much each week, class def depends on your final project group. Project requirements are long word dumps (think 2-5 pgs) and you can expect to lose points on things you SWEAR aren't there but actually were: 5 words about something needing a trait n losing an entire half letter grade for it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Extremely heavy workload. Expect to have a major project due every 2 weeks, on top of tedious course modules due every week. And on top of that, a final project which has an extremely long rubric of items, while you are forced to work in a team of only 3.

Also, the professor comes off as really pretentious in his assignments i.e. smile emoji spam.

THIS MAN IS A LEGEND. The lecture videos are so well done, and he is passionate and ready to help outside of class. If you want to make games as a hobby, or are pursuing the major, start by taking a course with this guy. ++

So much homework. SUPER HEAVY WORKLOAD!!! Sometimes one homework was not due and he already released another one. Homework has extremely long instructions. Takes up to 24 hours to finish. Submission's a pain in the ass. Does learn a lot and make a lot of projects but none are useful unless you tryna be a game programmer.

Avoid unless super interested in Unity/Games. You can learn a decent amount if you apply yourself, but be warned that Calgar has some... let's just say issues when interfacing with his students, and that's if he manages to reply to your emails at all. If you do take this class, follow assignments exactly, and just avoid Calgar. Then you're fine.

DO NOT take HCI with him if you actually want to go into UI/UX+already have experience working with clients. This class is only helpful for students who are minimally interested in UX design because he doesn't teach industry-standard tools. He teaches the design process as if there's only one way to do it and uses Axure for the course and not Figma

Took him during the summer for the summer classes in Seattle, can be a bit condescending at times but can be funny. This class is based off of a group project so if you get a crappy team, be prepared to do all of the work yourself, get a good team, this class will be a breeze.

Sarcastic, condescending, and spends a disproportionate amount of class time expressing disappointment and frustration at students.  It would be better for everyone if the professor could maintain a level head and positive attitude, and put more effort into understanding why students are not enjoying the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Yildirim is the GOAT, and easily one of the most respected and beloved professors in Khoury. I've gone back to his lecture notes to prep for interviews, since he does an excellent job of explaining things effectively + concisely. If you're going to take DS3000, make sure you take it with Caglar!

Cared a lot about students and put a lot of effort to make sure even the people who could not make it to live lectures be able to understand the materials and participate with other students for group projects. Well organized lectures and materials, inclusive environment. I'd take all classes with him if he were teaching them! Highly recommend. <3

Without a doubt, one of the best classes I have taken! Prof is super friendly and loves Harry Potter! Course is extremely well structured and everything is laid on the table in the first class. Gives ample time to complete the big assignments and encourages class participation. He's very responsive to questions and makes sure the load is balanced.

The Professor did an AMAZING job curating online course content. He had prerecorded lectures with accompanying notebooks that could be watched at the students convenience. On alternating class days there were (very) short lab activities. He was also easily accessible, and sent out weekly correspondences reminding us of upcoming activities.

Brilliant, funny, and clear professor. You almost felt sad for him - he was enthusiastic beyond belief but the long class and intro level material meant noone was paying attention by the end. You can work on a cool ML project come the end of the class as well, and the class is usually taken just when you want projects for your resume. 100% take him

Quizzes are amazing, can help with grade. Homework assignments are straight forward, Can Be Done. No in-class tests and no final exam, but there is a final group project. Project is mainly stats- and presentation-based. There's also in-class assignments, so that gets you to class, but they're 10% in total. Great professor, major hogwarts fan.

Calgar's great! No exams. The few homeworks, in-class exercises, and quizzes were all doable. He offers extra credit, really listens to the class, and is understanding if assignments or quizzes are missed or need extensions. Would highly recommend.

This professor is super enthusiastic and willing to make the class engaging and fun by her humorous tone. She definitely wants to bond with students during class. You should take her, she is amazing, and her class is super chill. Mostly based on group projects and some quizzes.

Professor Coleman is very kind, taking the time to get to know all of her students and very engaging for an 8 am class. There are pop quizzes but not too difficult, but doesn't give easy 100s on homework assignments. There is a semester long group-project that is randomly assigned and worth most of your grade. Definitely important to participate!
Yes, there are pop quizzes, but she drops the lowest. She is super kind, and she wants you to succeed. Build a relationship w her too, she is great

Professor Coleman reminds me a lot of a high school teacher in the best ways, she's super caring and very easy to get along with. The class itself is super easy all year and as long as you get along with your partners you should be fine for the group presentations.

A kind and caring professor who loves discussing business. Participation matters, and she enjoys engaged students. Expect group projects and presentations in 1101. She's a tough but fair grader and accepts late work.

Super kind and her pop quizzes are easy if you do the readings (they are short). She does have favorites so just participate. The whole class is based on a group project. Do go to class or your grade will take a hit. Very easy to reach her outside of class. Overall a fun class that is not difficult. Be prepared to present a few times!

reviews.comment: A very enthusiastic and sweet professor. Makes it super easy to contact her, allows students to text/call her when needed. I was required to take this class, and I didn't find it super necessary.. but she's great. Kind of harsh grader so make sure you follow rubrics and feedback.

Very supportive teacher but lectures are hard to follow. Exam questions are hard because info is often barely covered in class and wording is off. She is lenient about late work and you can negotiate grades usually/retake a quiz

Professor Santelices is a nice woman, but the class was boring. She just reads off the slides. There is a ton of work and readings, and it doesn't follow the syllabus in terms of dates, which makes it hard to follow along. The mid-term was difficult. Very approachable professor, though, and wants her students to thrive.
An angel on earth. Not a single complaint. Great slides, even better lectures, and a genuinely kind person. I'd take her again.
It's an okay class. I personally don't like lecture-heavy classes. Professor is nice.

reviews.comment: so so boring but not too hard

Prof Santelices is amazing! She makes her lectures engaging and always ties them to personal stories and research. When she assigns papers, she lets you send drafts beforehand for feedback and is very accessible in and out of class. She is kind, accommodating, and overall incredible. She will change the due dates to what works better for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Claudia was an AMAZING professor. I took her biology class and had absolutely 0 complaints. If you pay attention in class, do the notes, and just put in effort, you will do just fine. The quizzes and tests always align with what she teaches in class, which is always appreciated as a student.

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher! Clearly explains the material, with interesting personal stories. Workload is quite manageable and requires little work outside of class.

Claudia was very sweet! You could tell she cared about her students and wanted them to succeed. Her lectures were very interesting and her grading and tests were very forgiving. Her unique perspective as an anthropologist with interests in public health shaped the scope of the class in an interesting way too!

Claudia is the best! She's so easy going and wants all of her students to do very well in her class. She's always willing to work with students about anything, so don't be afraid to ask for assignment extensions or extra help with something. DON'T buy the book!! You don't need it, she'll assign readings but then she goes over everything in class.

Claudia is a fantastic professor. She is clearly passionate and experienced in her subject and her stories tie into her lectures well. FLEXIBLE: if whole class agrees will move due dates. BREAKDOWN: 4x 1 page reflections, 4x (usually take home) quizzes, midterm, final, one long paper. manageable workload/INTERESTING lectures. PAY ATTENTION IN CLASS

Amazing professor. She is caring, approachable, and gives inspiring lectures that are based on her own experiences. She wants her students to succeed in class and will help you achieve an A if you put in the work.

Professor Santelices is so kind and is willing to work with students who need quiz retakes, missed class, and allows the class to pick midterm and quiz dates.  She gives great feedback and uses her own research as examples so lectures are engaging. I loved her class and didn't need to spend much time outside to get a good grade.

Really liked the class and most quizzes and reflection papers were take home. As long as you try, she will give you a good grade. There were 4 quizzes (3 take home), 4 reflection papers (3 take home), a midterm and a final. She is very kind and sweet, she has come a long way from her previous reviews because the class and canvas were organized.

The class is super easy and she is a very easy grader. Everyone in the class got 100 for every reflection paper and take-home quizzes. the Lecture slides are boring and mostly common sense, so you do not need to study hard to get a 100 on her exams. Check canvas! She changes deadlines and posts assignments without mentioning them in class.

Class material is pretty dry but prof did pretty well making it engaging with her own stories/examples. Very kind person who wants you to succeed. Assignments are chill and based off the material on slides

Prof. Santelices was so understandable and very kind when it came to class! She is easy to talk to, and for me personally, finding a professor I can converse with in Spanish is nice.
