One of the best professors I've had. I took Anthropology of Latin America as a Spanish minor and totally changed my worldview. She shares her personal experiences in Chile as well as fieldwork, and shares profound, often unheard perspectives on the "third world" countries, capitalism, indigenous resistance, etc. I was captivated every lecture.

I found her lectures super interesting and she wasn't a super harsh grader. You need to study the material on the slides really well. The tests weren't hard but definitely harder than what we learned in class... She's not super great at communicating and will definitely forget your name even after meeting her multiple times; not very genuine.

Prof Santelices is a caring and enlightening professor. Amazing stories and experience in Anthropology. A bit iffy with technology and expect all assignments to be pushed back and delayed in grading. However, she really makes an effort to know everyones name and hear everyone out. IMO amazing professor, love coming to lecture. PARTICIPATE!

The class was an actual waste of money, as in the fact that many classes were cancelled and recorded for online. The most helpful part of the class is the slides, and I did actually come away from the class with helpful info. But was it worth the money spent on the class, no. Look for another class or even better, another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved her! She was one of the most caring professors at Northeastern! Through her personal stories, it is clear she is a professional and teaches for her love of learning. Her class was very lecture-heavy, but her material was always accessible, and students learned a lot. Grades depend mostly on exams, quizzes, and projects, not attendance.
Very kind, understanding woman. Barely knows how to use technology. I barely went to class and did well - if you stay on top of your coursework and STUDY THE CLASS SLIDES you'll do well.

Claudia is a really genuine, caring professor who has amazing life stories and lectures that brought me to tears on several occasions. It hurts to admit that she is all over the place with technology and deadlines, if she had a little more structure I'm sure she could be amazing.

Obviously cares a lot about the subject and has interesting stories, but lectures were hard to follow. Assigns way too much pointless reading. Assignments and exams were confusing, complicated, long, and frustrating. Not good with technology. Attendance was not taken but missing lectures does not help for later on. Class was all over the place.

Kind, passionate, good lectures. Everything else not so good. Horrible with technology. Extremely busy outside of class and didn't seem to have time to actually be a good professor. Her assignments can be confusing, especially the tests. Cancels class often, which is not a good thing. Could be good if she actually had time to focus on the class.

Dr. Santelices made lectures more interesting by adding her own experience of working in the field. You could really tell she was passionate about public health and how she has contributes and how we as students can further contribute. Assignments were based off of videos. As long as you pay attention to lectures and review, you'll pass. :)

Prof Courtney's Cyberlaw course is an absolute must-take. He's one of those professors who's clearly smart but never makes the material feel intimidating, always prepared, engaging, and genuinely great at running a discussion class that makes you think. One of the best undergrad experiences you'll have, easily one of the best professors on campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kyle is an awesome professor. His lectures are fun and interesting and he always has a story to tell. He has a great sense of humor and is very respectful of everyone. I highly recommend him. I wish he was my instructor for every class. Real nice guy.

By far the best course I had in the MSIA program - actually he's the best professor I have had at Northeastern. Never let him go. Best class ever!  He is very knowledgeable and makes the class interesting.  Not only does he provide contextual information but also uses current examples which helps drive the material home.

Relatively easy GE1501/1502 class. Lots of group projects, but enough class time is given for them not to be a huge burden. Quizzes and tests were relatively easy. Generous with grading assignments and tends to grade on the process, not necessarily the product.

Bala is the GOAT. Easily the best first year engineering teacher. His jokes can be corny but he's genuinely the most caring person and that's why everyone loves him. Bala, will you marry me?
hes alright, the class is easy

Bala is the man, though he has a knack for wasting entire class periods without teaching a single thing and doesn't always (ever) make sense. Nevertheless, he's still wicked chill and the class is pretty easy.
He's good in Physics, but is the worse in Programmin C++.  He can't teach programming, all he does is joke around.
No Comments
No Comments

Bala is one of the greatest professors I've had.  The material isn't terribly hard but he still goes the extra mile to teach his students.  He'll help if you need it and explains every concept from the ground up.

Sure he is a good guy, and he can teach physics, but stay away from this guy for programming. He can not teach C++ worth****. I did not learn anything from him, everything I learned was from having to look at other people's programs. Never stops talking.
bala is a great great man.
Easy A
he's kind of boring because he talks a lot, but he's a great teacher and his name is bala
BALA is the best.
No Comments

Prof. Maheswaran is a very nice guy. He cares if you get something or not and tets on what he teaches. There are no real surprises. The class is hard because it is Physics but it could have been worse. He's a pretty funny guy and really layed back.
Gotta love this guy...I still say hi everytime i walk by him
Very good guy.  Do the homework, and you will be fine.  He tries to be funny by being sarcastic (and most times it works!)

A professor that consistently teaches material of which the homework is due the same week, or in some cases, the same day. Insane amounts of homework, yet exams can cover niche topics or sometimes theorem that are only available in class notes. Dislikes students who seeks his office hours unless they spend more than 8hrs outside class.
good teacher and lecturer, really nice guy. tough class.

Awful. If you didn't understand something, he would have no way of explaining it differently and instead you make you feel dumb for not understanding it. Office hours were not helpful and often inaccessible. Homework took hours. Textbook was as unhelpful as his too fast lectures.
Prof. Craig's class was challenging. Material was hard to grasp, exams were harder than what was taught & homework was heavy. I suggest considering other professors before choosing this course.
He is a good professor and explains each problem by citing an example. His office hours are simply amazing.
He can't explain things clearly, class is boring, hard homework. Just terrible.
Weekly quizzes, but they're always a 1 line answer and the midterm is no harder than the homework

Prof. Maloney is a "real Math professor" who is not there to teach "Real Math". He explains numerous math methods that are helpful to model and solve any mechanical/physical/chemical/biological phenomena. Pay attention to his lectures, do homework sincerely, you will ace the exams and excel in using math as tool. Thank you, Prof. Maloney.
A REAL scientist, humble, respectful and fair.

I had a 93% for all tests + HW, weighted as per criteria he gave in the syllabus, did ok for final, and got a B, on a really easy course on Grad level Math. What's more is that I talked with a bunch of people to realise that it wasn't just me and that the other professor who taught the same course gave As for half of his class. Would not recommend
Really Easy! Took Math and he is always dancing in the class
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Lee is great! She truly cares for her students, but, as other reviews have noted, her class is very lecture-heavy, and the exams are hard. If you pay attention and put in the work outside of class, you'll be ok, but the whole class basically revolves around 3 exams (worh 60%).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework assignments were all long, but doable. If you pay attention in class and do the hw then the tests are easy. Doesn't provide extra credit, but is available for office hours. Hard to bounce back if you do bad on one exam. Professor Lee took the time to learn all of our names and would ask us all questions about ourselves.

Professor Lee was awesome! She made sure everyone understood the concepts, provided many examples, and was always eager to answer questions. Additionally, she was really nice and caring and you could tell she cared about her students.
Prof has a lot of assignments. Harsh with late deadlines and attendance. A bit boring at times during class. Don't expect a good grade. A DS class is prob more useful than the MIS classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Carol Lee is a great professor! As someone who didn't take Stats in high school she made it really easy to understand.There are no quizzes but there is a final group project at the end of the semester which she gives you plenty of time to do. Carol Lee is such a friendly professor and she just wants the best for her students.

Professor Lee is one of the most caring and underrated professors at NEU. She never wants to overwork her students, gave us breaks during class, and even snacks after exams. She had three equally weighted exams which were not bad if you did the homework. Class can be boring at times but you won't regret taking Professor Lee for any of your courses

Carol is nice, but seems a bit under qualified, struggling to answer questions in class. Textbook reading is useless as she just recites the readings during class, which can get monotone and sleep-inducing. She was an okay teacher but didn't offer many practice problems or much feedback and didn't feel very invested in teaching our class.
Very boring. Cant hold the attention of the class. Wont learn anything from the class.
Does not show enthusiasm and lectures are boring. Assignments are long and brutal and it is horrible if you get placed with team members who do not care. Harsh grader at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Fundamentals of Info Analytics with Professor Lee/Sah 1) kind and lectures are interesting 2) Tough grader- for many of the assignments the questions are randomly assigned points (usually not that many questions so they're each worth a good amount- mess up one/two/three could get -15) important because hw is 30% (worth the most- more than final)
Horrible class, unclear assignment instructions, and arbitrary grading. Avoid this professor if you can because she will make your life more difficult.

He's a nice guy. However, his feedback is extremely cryptic and not helpful. He repeats the same 3 ideas/topics over and over again. Exactly like a broken record. The entire class is a massive group project that doesn't make sense half the time. If you can, take the class but avoid this professor if you actually want to learn something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Just be a half decent student and he will love you. Literally just google the titles of the readings once and a while and then talk in class and he eats it up. It is so easy.

Very passionate about the class but grades as accurately as possible. Some may say he is a difficult grader but not hard to get an A. Very understanding/wholesome and easy to listen to. Lectures can be sometimes boring or really interesting. Homework's are readings or group project work.
harsh grader, makes us guess his expectation, teach the concept after we present, always have comments about everything but expectation not clear

I haven't taken the final yet, but I have an A which is obviously very good. However, during the group project we all worked really hard, but nothing was ever good enough for him. If he doesn't like your product that you base your final presentation on, even if the class likes it, you don't do well, and it's almost 40% of your grade. Don't take!!!

absolutely horrible. i am an extremely hard worker and my group and i follow guidelines exactly, but he was never satisfied. It wasn't just our group. extremely and unnecessarily a hard grader. all other inno classes had easy professors. i also have heard that i am one of VERY few students who had an A, my group members all had B/C…. Do. Not. Take.

half of the class is a loosely formatted final group project. Mark doesnt help all that much and he barely preps you for the final. its possible to get a good grade but he doesnt really teach you anything.

Very nice guy overall and is passionate about teaching. There's a final for this class, which doesn't make sense because the majority of the class was a group project. If you don't like your group in the beginning, get out of it because the group projects reflect heavily on your grade. Assignments and discussions are not difficult, just do the hw.

One of the best teachers I have had at northeastern. He's very knowledgable and knows what he's doing in class. Also he's always there to help. I don't know why an exam is necessery but its doable and it's a very fun course overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I was torn between giving a 4 instead of 3 for difficulty. It's not that the course is hard, but he is all over the place, will teach you concepts after you write a paper on them and expectations aren't clear, but then will give you harsh feedback. This class took up a lot of my time & didn't really listen to students clearly.

Carla is a wonderful person! She is always accessible outside of class and very helpful. At the start of the semester, she was very good at explaining things in detail, but as we got into reaction mechanisms, the explanations were rushed and honestly pretty bad. I felt like I was drowning in the material by the end and it was very stressful.

Really engaging lecturer and cool grading policies (50% corrections on exams). However, her tests are just insanely difficult. The practice exams are not similar at all to the real thing, making it hard to study. She has very little leniency for personal circumstances but is always willing to meet with you. Would've taken Orgo 2 with her if I could
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is super hard and content heavy but Prof Staton gives you everything you need to pass. Having test corrections was a godsend and you really can improve your score a lot if you put in the time.

I loved taking Organic II with Professor Staton. The class is difficult, but with 50% test corrections back on the three midterm exams it's more than fair. She is readily accessible outside of class and genuinely seems to care about her students and the course itself. I definitely recommend for Orgo II.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great prof for Orgo. She knows what shes talking about and can explain things super well. Lectures and canvas are organized very well. Her tests are SO difficult. Corrections for midterms make it easier to get a good grade and tons of padding w. extra credit, homework, and participation.

Take this class if you're worried about getting doing bad in orgo 2, but not if you're aiming for/think you can achieve an A/high B. She's a very nice professor and she does genuinely care about her students. Her tests are just too hard (even with 50% test corrections), so her grading criteria makes it so no one fails but no one does great either.

She is an amazing prof and I genuinely learned so much in her class. Her exams are very tough and she prioritizes her students understanding concepts but if you do the weekly practice and homework she gives you will be able to succeed. She is the best professor I have had so far.

She taught in a way that was easy to understand. She provided many resources to help like test corrections.She falls behind grading and it's really frustrating to have to wait. It would be nice if she communicated when things were taking her longer, she would promise us grades back by a date and then give them back 12 days later.

Prof Staton is great at teaching, however grading takes too long(we still don't have our third exams or workshops back after the final). The final was hard and workshops don't resemble tests so our averages were low. It's her first time teaching it, her lectures had a lot of depth. I just wish there was practice that resembled test like questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Staton's teaching style for Organic Chemistry I really clicked with me personally. Her tests are difficult, but in the non-Honors section, you are offered test corrections where you can get 50% of your points back. I also found the test corrections really helpful for incentive to review content that you previously got wrong.

If you want to truly understand orgo 1, I'd take Staton's class. She's not the best at grading assignments promptly, (just the took the final and assignments from week 4 are ungraded), but her quality of teaching is great. Exams are HARD which can feel really unrewarding and discouraging especially after studying so hard but, her class is do-able.

Lowkey the goat idk her test corrections come in clutch and the content/practice she gives lowkey reflects some of the exam material. Her exams are extremely hard, but with test corrections its not that difficult to end with an A/B. Just study a lot and really try to learn the conceptual stuff. She's really sweet.

Honestly, a very kind and sweet professor, but those exams were ridiculously long and complex. Despite corrections, I felt like I was in an honors class. Since exams determine most of your grade, just go for another professor; it's not worth the headache. She is not generous at all with partial points; it might as well be multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved her class so much; she made organic fun and enjoyable. She offered test corrections over the summer, which were very helpful. Her office hours are amazing! She cares about her students and wants everyone to understand the content.

She is very nice and approachable. Orgo is an incredibly hard class but she makes it easier to digest with her lectures, which are easy to follow and very detailed. Her tests are very hard, harder than other orgo profs from what I've heard, but she gives you the resources you need to succeed and her test corrections are very forgiving.

I took Summer II Orgo 1 w/ Prof. Staton and loved her! Yes, the course goes fast but that's just the nature of orgo. She did a great job at giving clear lectures and providing time outside of class for students to get extra help. Test corrections were offered for most tests and extra credit opportunities were made. She clearly cares for students!

Took orgo 1 in the summer (6 week course) with carla. she's a great teacher but had to go quick bc of how short the class is. I was able to succeed in her course by her quiz and test corrections and really studying her problem sets (semi similar to her quizzes and tests). orgo isn't easy, you have to really understand it conceptially to do well

Prof Staton gives you everything you need to succeed in orgo 1. Her exams are pretty difficult, but she offers corrections; lectures are clear and easy to follow; and she is great at answering questions. While she isn't perfect, she is very 
respectful and open to feedback, and she actually takes it. Prepared me well for orgo 2 and the MCAT!

Professor Staton is one of my favorite professors. She is super approachable and cares about her students. She is always looking for feedback and is willing to adapt her teaching based on it. She explains everything well and finds fun analogies and stories to help students remember content. Definitely recommend her for Orgo 1.

Prof. Staton is a great teacher. ORGO is a tough class, but she is a great lecturer and gives you a lot of opportunities to learn and get help. Her exams are hard, but she gives test corrections, which always helped my grade. I definitely recommend taking her for ORGO I!

Dr. Staton's exams are the most difficult--by far--out of any in the entire Organic Chemistry department at Northeastern, but she is very fair with grading (her "Follow-through policy") and gives test corrections, so you have many chances to bring up your grade.

SO GOOD- those complaining need to remember this class is hard but she gives you every possible opportunity to get a good grade. Bonus points, lower grade scale, easy HW points, test corrections, you name it. Talks fast, but still manageable and gives so. much. practice. Really works your critical thinking skills in a good way.
Amazing orgo professor. Although she goes fast, she provides the resources necessary to do well in the class, and she has test corrections to ensure that you can correct your mistakes

Though I didn't do as well I would've liked, she is very knowledgable and overall a wonderful professor. Coming from having an awful gen chem prof, she made me love and actually enjoy orgo, no matter how difficult it was. Orgo in general is a hard class, so be ready to do a lot of work outside of the class. Take her! Best prof I've had yet.

I really do not understand all of the negative reviews. She is the best professor I've had. As someone who hated gen chem, this class made me love chemistry. It truly is not that bad if you lock in and go to office hours. Many people on here complain about exams but I honestly found them not bad, especially with test corrections. Take her!!!!

She was super nice and a good lecturers, but everything relied on the lectures. The exams were rough and I honestly thought I failed the final but the test corrections were great help. She wanted students to succeed, but you definitely had to put in the work. I  thought she was a great lecturer and would take again. Also her fits were fire

She is the WORST professor EVER. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS unless you want to be in an eternal stress. She allows for test corrections which it's the only good thing but she gives tooo much content for so little time. She expects you to know everything. Do not take her.
Lectures and notes were tough to follow unless you dedicate your life to this class. Very unaccommodating and does not seem to care for the students.

Lectures and notes are extremely difficult to follow. If you aren't ready to dedicate your life to this class then I suggest finding a different professor. Attending office hours is basically mandatory if you want to stay caught up. Overall I found her to be very unaccommodating and inflexible

Very caring & nice but def the most difficult prof to take for Orgo 1. However, she does do test corrections + partial credit & the grading scale is "lowered" (a 90 is an A, for reference). Wish she had given us more practice material bc the textbook questions didn't reflect what was on the exams. Office Hours were only helpful for gen questions.

Is obviously very knowledgeable about the class and cares about students, but the lecture notes are very unhelpful regarding review. Office hours are PACKED and are the only time homework problems are ever reviewed, so it becomes very easy to get behind or stuck if you cannot make it to office hours.

Her class is very difficult simply due to the fact that the exams are much more advanced than the class itself. The only good thing is that she gives test corrections, which boost your test grade. so far the exam averages after the corrections have been in the low to mid 70s, so that means that the raw scores have to be somewhere in the 50s-60s

the 1 star reviews have got to be rage bait... staton is the goat of the chemistry department. if you study and put in the effort, you will do just fine. she gives a ton of partial credit and so much opportunity for remediation. this isn't a class you can cram last minute, you have to learn the material in order to do well.

The negative reviews are uncalled for and just plain rude. Professor Staton is easily one of the best professors at NEU. She is an incredibly smart woman and cares a lot about her students. This class is difficult, but remember she is teaching a very difficult subject. If you're planning on taking Orgo 1 or 2, take it with Staton, she is great.
amazing person overall for those who are rating her a 1 she is hard but this is college man
full time studying on your own basically
If you like taking exams take this course the exams are challenging and a good way to prep for the dat or mcat but the teaching style is not helpful at all!

She is very nice but I spend a lot of time outside class teaching myself the material. I wish she covered more of what's actually on the exams. Her TAs aren't helpful and seem bored and unmotivated especially in the Zoom recordings.

She's a great teacher but can be condescending. She expects us to fully learn the easy material she lectures on and gives us barely a minute to two to try problems in class. However, the problems don't reflect the exam, which is frustrating. For Exam 2, there was no ranking, yet the problem set had tons of those questions.

She's very easy to understand during lectures and when going over her slides but the exams are really difficult and don't match what we go over in class. It's great to be challenged but it would help if that difficulty was also part of the lessons. The test corrections are helpful but I'd prefer to understand the material the first time around.
Whoever is giving her a 5 is crazy. i literally took 40 pages of notes and still failed the unit 3 exam, and know many many many people that studied sooo much and did horrible..
FYI I'm pretty sure all the bad reviews are by the same person. Likely someone upset they didn't do well on the third exam. Take that into consideration, because Staton is an amazing professor.

I have no idea what the other reviews are talking about. She's understanding, kind, and wants us all to succeed. Her lectures are comprehensive, and although her tests are challenging, she provides us with the foundation necessary to help us understand the material. I did AWFUL on her third test, yet I still got an A as her grading is forgiving.

Staton is the best. Her tests are hard, but she sets you up to succeed. If you get a 50% on a test, you can get back up to a 75%. Her grading system is so forgiving. A 90 is considered an A. Organic chemistry is hard. Not understanding this course isn't Staton's fault, it's just the complexity of the material. TAKE HER.

I love Prof Staton, she's so kind and thorough with her lectures, and even more so in her office hours. Her tests definitely aren't easy, but she does test corrections which have saved me. Downsides are that she doesn't post enough practice problems and recorded lectures, but overall I managed fine in her class. Attendance is done through PollEV

I was terrified to take orgo 1, but Prof Staton eased my worries. She's so kind and thorough with her lectures, and even more so during her office hours. Her tests definitely aren't easy, but I found that her exams were pretty similar to the problem sets. Attendance is taken by polling, which do make up a small chunk of your grade.

STAY AWAY from this professor. As someone who is usually a straight-A student this class has made me reconsider my entire academic path, major, and career. I ended up guessing on the entire exam because the content felt completely disconnected from the lectures. The lectures may seem easy but they don't adequately prepare you for the exam.STAY AWAY

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE IF IT'S TAUGHT BY HER. SHE SEEMS LIKE A GREEN FLAG AT FIRST BUT IS ACTUALLY A MASSIVE RED FLAG. I HAVE NO IDEA WHERE ALL MY HARD-EARNED KNOWLEDGE IS GOING. HER TEACHING STYLE IS WAY TOO SIMPLE IN CLASS AND THEN THE EXAMS ARE RIDICULOUSLY COMPLEX. NOTHING LINES UP. IT'S FRUSTRATING AND COMPLETELY MISLEADING.

Also, it is very hard to study because you don't have references to see how hard the exams would actually be compared to what is shown in class. She also doesn't even record her lectures, which is a HUGE disadvantage to people taking her course.

I've studied so much for this course, but the professor only reviews the easiest topics in class—almost like elementary school. It gives a false sense of understanding. The exams are completely different and expect advanced thinking we were never taught. She's one of the worst professors I've had—condescending, unhelpful, and misleading.

She doesn't give any review at all for her midterms, and for her final, she doesn't even give a final review of the exam at all. Also, do not even bother using ChatGPT or AI to help cause her problems are so complex that you would still fail and get the questions wrong even after using all "outside sources".

When it comes to office hours, she gives much easier problems than what's on the exams, her lectures are fine and she is great lecturer overall, she needs to understand that we are not 4th yrs ready to take the MCAT and that we are 1st years just recovering from Gen Chem at best. Also, she teaches the course in a much complex way overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Beware: She seems nice, but her materials are way too easy compared to how insanely hard her exams are. You'll think you're ready, but nothing she gives actually prepares you—you'll be completely blindsided. She's also petty and arrogant about regrades.

BEWARE!!! THIS WOMAN IS THE MOST TOUGH GRADER OUT OF ALL THE ORGO SECTIONS. YOU WILL STUDY FOR HOURS ON END TO RECEIVE A C+ AT BEST. You may think that you would know what ur doing inside and out, and her questions will still stump you. Trust me; take Danahy instead. PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF. When it comes to her exams, they are significantly harder!!!

Took this class her first semester of teaching. She is a kind person but her tests are significantly harder than the other orgo sections. Try to memorize every small detail on slides. The practice problems given are way easier than the exams, beware. Very strict grading on tests.

She is very kind but can be condescending at times. Her exams are very tough, but you get test corrections, which help boost your grades on them by a lot. Since the exams are open ended, if you do not study all of the information down to the specifics, it is hard to do well, especially on exam 3.

By far the best professor I have ever had at NU. She is clear with expectations, extremely fair, and does not waver in her stance. It is a tough subject and you have to put a lot of work into this class but once you understand how she grades her exams it is within reach to get an A. I absolutely encourage you to take Dr. Staton for OChem.

Professor Staton is the best professor I have EVER. HAD. She is so amazing at her job, spends all her free time and helps students in office hours or scheduling one-on-one sessions. She teaches a very difficult course but does it beautifully. She is helpful, and responsive, always open to help, very approachable, and wonderful.
She is an awesome lecturer. She is caring and can explain hard topics very easily. She allows for test corrections and overall wants you to do well, She is enthusiastic and very smart.

The lectures were extremely informative and helped me learn the material. Tests are difficult and focus on the small details, but they don't focus on just one thing. Wouldn't take if you just need the credits, because there are easier professors, but she is really good if you need to take orgo.

Lecture-heavy but easy to follow if you pay attention. Office hours are very helpful. She does not provide enough practice material/homework, and her exams are very hard but she grades fairly. She is kind, passionate, and receptive to feedback, so I'm sure her class will improve, especially as a newer professor.
The most subjective and discouraging professor I have ever had. Led me to change my major and consider transferring

She honestly is one of my favorite professors! She acknowledges how difficult the orgo material is and she teaches it in a way that is really simple and easy to understand. She also is very generous with test corrections and grade curves. My one complaint is that her slides are hard to follow if you fall behind in class. But, overall super caring!

She's really sweet and goes over a lot of material in class, office hours are such a huge help! A lot of her material is covered in class and she is very accommodating. I would recommend her over other professors, she genuinely wants you to learn the content so the tests are a little hard but offer test corrects to help with mistakes&MCAT questions

The test material is solely from what she says in class. She also refuses to record her lectures. Her handwritten notes are impossible to follow. Minimal study material. Other teachers allow test notes, but she doesn't. She will take points off correct answers if you don't use exact language. You need to use the textbook, or you won't do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AMAZING. Best professor I've had at Northeastern by far. She is so kind and puts in so much effort to make herself available outside of class. Makes complicated topics easy to understand. Her exams are difficult, but certainly doable. Offers test corrections. She is clearly extremely passionate about orgo and makes me excited about it too.

She is a great lecturer. She asks a lot of questions during class and practices a lot of active learning techniques which helps a lot. She is young so she understands what the students are going through and she is  a great professor. Her tests are hard but she is a fair grader and wants her students to learn as much as possible.

This guy is so awesome. You don't learn a single thing but he is a free A and you can use this as a chill class or like a study hall. Any assignment turned in is a 100, his quizzes he give you a 100 regardless of what you write. That said, you do not learn from him, but he is good for gpa.

I used this class as a study hall. I didn't learn a single thing which is honestly fine because the project is self-driven and he wants his students to end with an A and makes it pretty easy to get there

He's definitely a sweet guy, and you can tell he's passionate, but he's not very good at teaching. He made us by his $30 book (only could pay cash to him) and I never used it all semester. I didn't learn anything all semester because he just rambles, but a good GPA booster. We basically spent the whole sem working on symposium project.

He taught the class out of his own textbook and I never really had a full grasp on the content so if that bothers you he probably isn't a great prof for you. That being said he is very sweet/ very easy to get a high grade, he wants you to succeed and learn a little about a topic he's passionate about which I really loved. It was great for my GPA.

His lectures make no sense, he makes up his own terms (can't find them on Google), he makes you buy his own textbook, etc. However, this class is an easy A. It is way easier than any of the other inquires classes. If you turn in the assignments and take the quizzes you will get a 100. You can write literally anything related on the quiz and get 100

very nice guy, but cant teach. his lectures are all over the place and impossible to follow. he makes up his own terms for things, so you can't even ask google if you're confused. no one learned anything in this class. however, he doesn't give anyone below 100 so its an easy A

O'Malley genuinely just wants you to do well in his class. His lectures can be convoluted and hard to follow, mostly because he just really loves what he teaches, but he gives you every possible opportunity to get an A. I really just used his class as a study hall. He is generally a funny and caring guy, so do your GPA a favor and take his section!

It is a great class. He is very nice as he brings candy to class to encourage participation among students. As long as you know something on the quizzes he will give you an A or allow you to make it up to get an A. The group project is really easy and he will help you with anything. 10/10 recommend taking his class! The final is a one-page paper.

Do your GPA a favor and take him! His class is very lecture-heavy there are open response quizzes which he will allow anyone who gets less than an A to redo. As long as you attend class and are somewhat knowledgeable about something he will give you an A in the class. No final exam just a paper. He's a great guy take his class!

Prof O'Malley's class was a joke. I attended class but you really done need to. Grade is based on 3 major tests and thats it. April 14th and no grades have been put in yet. The slides are wordy and he goes off on tangents a lot. Nice guy but I don't think his main interest is anatomy. Book is unnecessary, first test is hard others are prac tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don's class is the definition of lecture heavy. Longggg lectures that even I couldn't keep up with note taking just bc of how boring they were. He is sort of nice but kind of sassy and also thinks he is smarter than his own doctor (which he told us). DO THE PRACTICE TESTS!! Grade is not posted and our final is in three days...

His tests were just the practice tests. Literally same position and everything, I learned nothing in this course but just memorized the practice test the day of and got one of the best grades on the final.
Lectures are misleading and not helpful for actual exams, which are so difficult and not like any of the practice he gives you. Is nice but not a good professor, I'd avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I genuinely think he's a really nice guy who cares about his students and is very passionate. However, in class, you focus more on why something is the way it is rather than actually using or applying the formulas, etc for a test. So homework is basically you teaching yourself chemistry. The tests are pretty different from class problems
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Practice problems are so different from test
Never curves even when tests are hard
No empathy for students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really awesome professor. Never took chemistry before, but he helped me understand everything. Even when I bombed a test, I still felt proud of what I learned, and I eventually improved. Gives lots of extra credit on exams, has good policies, and tries to help you succeed. Just a really great professor to have, especially for such a hard course.

Very caring and fair professor. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and cares about their wellbeing. Easy to get help outside of class. Tests are a bit difficult and require critical thinking but he gives 3 extra points on every test. Lots of homework but ample time to complete it. Only critique: study guides often didn't match actual tests.
He was such an amazing chem professor. He made the concepts seem so simple and was so nice. The homework wasn't too bad, just a little tedious.
loved him! just do the homework and go to office hours if needed

Very kind and accessible and a great, great professor (like the best I've had thus far). Material was tough but if you come to lecture and go to office hours he's great at explaining things. Also gives extra credit and practice problems on Aktiv are super helpful on exams, and he'll replace your lowest midterm score so a good grade is very feasible

Super kind and caring, and great at teaching (like the best I've had yet). The material is hard but going to lectures and office hours made it seem very simple. Very feasible to succeed in the course if you put effort in, he also gives extra credit which is nice and will replace your lowest midterm exam grade.

If you're taking CHEM1161, take it with Dan Matthew. I would recommend the chem ramp up (it was extra credit but it was actually helpful). An A is totally achievable by completing all the homework (unlimited tries) and studying using the practice exams and aktiv problems. Of course, try your best to stay proactive the class can move fast at times.

The actual goat. I had zero chemistry knowledge coming in and finished with an A, and that's all thanks to Dr. Dan's teaching! Take notes on the homework, study the practice exams, and focus on what you're struggling with. Also the ramp up is helpful if you have no idea (like me) what to expect coming into a chem course. Thank you!!!

I would absolutely recommend Prof Matthew for gen chem!! If you attend class regularly and do the homework assignments you'll be set up for success in his class. He's a good lecturer and easy to follow, he takes notes during class that you follow along on. Attendance is mandatory, but he allows a couple of absences. He's also super nice :)

By far the best Chem professor I have ever had! He cares about how the students are learning more than grading, and his lectures really made me understand the concepts so much more clearly. Plus, he gives many opportunities for extra credit. Recitation can feel like more of a chore but you get a bump up in your grade if you go to all of them.

BEST PROFESSOR SO FAR! I was so worried about taking a good chem professor because the class can be difficult, but what you put in is what you get out. Biggest advice is follow along lectures, and you will be perfectly set. I went to almost all office hours and he bonded with all the students, taking hours out of his week and day to help. love him!

DAN MATTHEW AKA THE BEST PROF EVER!!!! He is an amazing professor. He really knows how to teach. He gives 4 midterm exams and a cumulative final exam. If you score higher on the final than one of your midterms he will replace your lowest midterm grade with the final exam grade. He gives tons of practice and is willing to meet with you anytime!

I LOVE DR.DAN! He is one of the best professors I've had here at Northeastern. His lectures are straightforward and the activ practice questions he gives really help for his exams. He really helped me enjoy chemistry and solidify concepts that I forgot in high school. If you understand the material well, the exams should be straightforward.

Dr. Dan is the best! If you're taking chemistry, definitely try to take it with him. He takes notes with the class, so the lecture stays at a good pace. He's willing to reexplain anything if a student is confused. He's so easy to reach outside of class and his office hours are very useful.

I love this man. So amazing at seeing what works and does not work for students and changing his teaching style around that. There were so many resources for the exams. He is so kind and very approachable at office hours. You will always get 100 on the hw because you get unlimited tries.
Good professor and makes the most out of lectures. Notes are really helpful, and going to his office hours are too.

Cool dude. Genuinely cares about his students understanding the course content. This slows down his lectures heavily, but he helped me actually learn some things I had memorized and forgotten in high school. Though while the material was often familiar and low-level, his tests reached into dimensions class time couldn't dream of.

Take him for Gen Chem! He can be reached outside of class and really cares about his students. Also, instead of having slides for his lecture, he writes out his notes along with his class, so it goes at a natural pace. He structures his class with the textbook (not essential), but you do have to purchase Aktiv (practice problems). Overall, great!

Challenging for those uncomfortable with chemistry. He did not curve any exams but he gave extra points at the end of them. If you make a good-faith attempt, but come up with a D by the end of the semester, he will boost your grade so you will pass. He is a safe bet, but the other professor did curve exams which would've been extremely useful.

Dan is one of few professors I've had who genuinely cares about students. If anything were to happen, whether its falling behind, simply sleeping in, or an emergency, he's gracious and understanding. Chemistry is not easy but he taught it well. Homework and class work is easy to get 100s on despite the tests being difficult, so avg grade is boosted

Dr. Dan cares a lot about his students and wants you to succeed. He provides a lot of study/review resources for exams. I liked his teaching style too-- he walks you through the notes/example problems on his iPad. Highly recommend!
Dr. Dan was an amazing teacher. He did a great job at explaining the material in a simple way. He also gave us tests from the previous semesters to help us prepare for exams, which was super helpful.

Overall the class was pretty good. I like his lecture style (he writes his notes in notability) and he cares a lot about his students. The one thing I did not like was how he stated he purposely wanted the tests to be harder. Better than other professors for gen chem.

Dr. Dan is a fantastic professor. You can tell he really cares about his students by how he always stops to answer questions. His tests are very reasonable and have questions that appear in the homework.

If you want to have a (fairly) easy time in gen chem take it with Dr. Dan. I withdrew from chem class my 1st semester and thought just I wasn't cut out to understand the material. That all changed with Dr. Dan. He's a great lecturer and cares a lot about his students. He's very personable and hosted in-person review sessions before every exam.

I liked his teaching style (actively writes out notes during lecture) and his tests were fair. He is generous with partial credit. An etextbook and 2 online accounts are required to be purchased for this class.

dr dan is a tougher prof than people say - he even prefaced this semester by saying he knew on rate my prof he was known to be easy, but he's not anymore. this class isn't impossible, lectures are good (though a bit rushed), he's amazing with extra credit on tough exams. my biggest piece of advice? stay on top of lectures and USE THE TEXTBOOK.
I was not a fan of the way he lectures. His notes were not conducive to review after class. he also mentioned that his goal is to make his exams harder than past semesters.

Great professor, despite his tests being a bit challenging. Writes his notes with the class, making it easy to understand and visualize. His practice tests were not like the actual exams in terms of difficulty, but if you understand the material you should be fine if you study outside of class. Great guy, super nice and approachable.

Dr. Dan was fantastic! Such a caring individual who puts in the effort for you if you are willing to do the same. Exams were slightly difficult, but as long as you prepare with the resources he provides, you should succeed.

great, intelligent professor with riveting lectures on fascinating content. very engaging and allows abstract concepts to make sense. 
class moves very fast DO NOT fall behind, exams do not match up to practice tests or problems in terms of difficulty. exams are tricky and challenging. hard to earn a good grade. deep concept knowledge guaranteed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Dan during spring 2023 and he was one of the best professors I've had here! His lectures were so helpful. He usually takes notes while teaching in front of the class and makes them accessible for everyone at any time. Notes are clear and everything on the tests will be stuff that has been in the lectures. He's genuinely a great guy too!

He started off the year strong and was a great prof. He made chemistry understandable. However, his exams are way harder than they need to be. He said he purposely made them harder than past exams. He often would recognize that they were harder then they needed to be b
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dan's pretty easy. 3 exams before the final and attendance is mandatory but he takes attendance by giving out a code at the beginning of class so if you have friends in the class it is helpful. The exams are pretty easy but get harder as the semester goes on just because of the material. He posts all his notes online so it should be fine.

Awesome guy, made me love Chemistry after I hated it in hs. Honestly a very nice dude that goes over all the content clearly in his lectures and his tests are all very fair. If you show up to class and do HW then you will be fine, he also gives out a lot of extra practice problems that prepare you well for the tests.

I dreaded chemistry coming into college but Dan has made my chem experience amazing. His lectures are clear, not overwhelming or over complicated. Would 100% take him if you think chem is not your best subject because he makes the material understandable. VERY generous when grading exams. Exams are difficult and long but manageable.

Wonderful professor. Reminder, always go to his lectures, unless you want to miss a TON of materials. Class pace was incredibly fast but his lecture and explanation were super detailed. Exams are VERY DIFFICULT but very fair. Get ready to study a lot for this course, and if you do you will learn a lot and in good shape.

Prof. Matthew is an amazing lecturer. Instead of slideshows, he opens up pages in notability & writes notes with you which is a much more effective way of learning/teaching chemistry. His tests are also fair, simply practice & make sure you fully understand important concepts (conceptual questions are asked). There is also always a bonus question!

Dan is super approachable, and knowledgeable about chemistry. His office hours and extra help sessions were helpful, and he posted lots of practice problems. It wasn't all good though, he would say his class was too easy in past semesters and purposely made exam questions more difficult or trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although I really enjoyed his lectures, his exams tended to be extremely difficult. He does give practice exams before every exam, and when I would take those, I would get high 90s. Then when it came to the actual exam, the questions would be different formats and would ask you to do things that were never taught in class.

Dan is great at explaining. Only thing I would say is that they can word some test problems weirdly, and it just throws me off. I don't understand why they can't just clearly state open response questions. Other than that, great professor, there were 3-4 exams + 1 final. Go to class, do your homework, and study a lot, and I think you'll do well.

Professor Matthew is a great professor. He explains concepts very clearly and cares a lot about his students and the subject. Tests were not too difficult as long as you studied, and the weekly homework assignments had unlimited attempts, so they were good practice.

DAN SLAYS but it was a difficult course due to the material. As long as you stay on top of the homework and do the practice exams you will do good.Dan is really caring and his office hours help a lot.
As long as you put the work in you can get a decent grade.

Expectations are very clear. Most of the class finished with an A- or an A. Lectures are easy to follow and he makes the concepts easy to understand. Go to the class the week of Thanksgiving for extra credit!!

Dr. Dan is amazing! He is very clear about grading. There were 3 midterms and the final exam. Participation is mandatory and he gives weekly homework assignments. He explains everything so clearly and always answers questions.

Dan is such a great teacher. He makes concept very simple to understand. His office hours are very helpful.   Exams are fair and he post a lot of practice exams/questions (+ easyy bonus points on every exam). Attendance is mandatory every day which is meh. Other than that, no other complaint, loved the class and the teacher.
I love Dan!!! Everyone loves him. He makes the information so understandable and you can tell he really cares. He is very accessible outside of class.

Professor Matthew made general chemistry a breeze! I hadn't even thought about chemistry since sophomore year of high school and he made everything engaging and easy to understand. He posted practice exams that were almost identical to his tests. Class averages were consistently above 80%. Every test has a bonus question for extra credit.

Overall, the class is not too hard, he teaches well, the only complaint is sometimes it is frustrating that class is mandatory especially if you have taken a course like physics already and know some of the material.

explains everything in a way that's easy to understand and will take the time to make sure you understand topics. assigns weekly homework but it can normally be completed in about an hour. tests are very fair and he gives you points whenever he's able to on non-multiple choice problems
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably the best instructor I've ever had - take Dan if you can! He is very clear and lectures while he projects his own notes which is super clear. Fair grading, accessible, and great explanations. I took chem in high school but this class has left me with a totally higher level of understanding.
You can just tell he really care about his students and how they do. He is very reasonable with grading and genuinely teaches well. I would take more of his classes for sure
Took Chem1161 from him in Spring 2022, very easygoing and is a very fair grader. Super accessible outside of class and does his best to make sure all of his students learn the course material

I loved professor Matthews' class. I had such a hard time with chemistry in high school, but he made me enjoy it. There's weekly homework assignments (they're fairly long), 3 midterms, and a final (score will replace your lowest midterm grade), as well as attendance in lecture and recitation that goes into your grades. Work hard and you'll succeed!

Professor Matthews is the best professor I have had so far at Northeastern. He gives amazing lectures and makes sure students thoroughly understand content, and is always available outside of class for help. He also only tests on what he lectures, so there are no surprises on his exams. For new chemistry students I couldn't recommend him more!

Amazing professor! I hated chem back in high school but he made the class enjoyable and he taught concepts extremely well. He is always willing to help and there are many different tasks that make up your grade, so it's not just based on exams. Take the class, you won't regret him as a professor.

Take this class! Dr. matthew makes all the material very interesting and does a great job explaining it, he also uses his ipad to write lecture notes during class which makes it easy to keep up. Clear grading and gives a good amount of partial credit. Weekly homework assignments and exams make up most of the grade.

Really good teacher! He explains concepts very well and is always willing to help and answer questions. Also a really nice guy. He gives fun bonus questions on tests like, "What's your favorite place to go in Boston?" and they're usually worth a lot of points. Chem is hard and you do need to study, but he makes it a lot easier and more fun.

Wonderful professor, his lectures are very clear and easy to follow. If you struggled with chemistry take him, as he takes the time to explain theoretical concepts. I would definitely take a course with him again.

Dr. Dan was a really good professor for gen chem. He took the time to explain the concepts in class through his interesting teaching style which is writing on his iPad and we copy down notes. His tests were very true to what we learned in class so you wouldn't expect any surprises on the test if you study all the material from class.
Great for chemistry - teaches well and is understanding

Wonderful professor, goes every extra mile to help with student understanding and is great at explaining theoretical concepts in understandable ways. Also just a super cool dude, really patient and makes a hard class (chem 1 and 2 accelerated) understandable for students. Would definitely take a course with him again.

Dan is a really knowledgable professor. He's clear, direct, and caring for his students. I really enjoyed learning with him, and I think that other student's did as well.  Homework was genuinely helpful.  Unlimited attempts and no point penalty for wrong answers. He encourages guesses in lectures because that's how you learn.  Highly recommend!

Best professor I've had at neu so far. Love the way he teaches lectures; he basically writes the lectures on his iPad as he is teaching you, making them very easy to follow and visualize what he is talking about. He explains concepts simply and clearly, and is very accessible for office hours. 10/10 would take again

Dr. Dan is the best professor I've had at Northeastern. I took gen chem 1 and 2 with another professor before and withdrew from the class because I was struggling and unsupported but I have done well in this class. Dr. Dan is an amazing teacher, his lectures are easy to follow, and he cares deeply about his students' success. A rare find, amazing.

I don't understand all the bad ratings. She gave one take-home exam with a clear grading format, lots of individual work, and no final. The only thing was that she gave us one in-person proctored exam, but she gave us a study guide and lots of materials with open notes. Not bad at all, and she is very nice and accommodating, 2 exams worth 10% each

The content of this class is not of personal interest which might have influenced my rating, but the lectures are confusing with weirdly organized slides and she has an irrelevant assignment every class for each table group. The worst part she rarely gives full score on any of the assignments, including participation so forget an A!

reviews.comment: Do not listen to any of these reviews. This class is minimal work and prof is so sweet. It is extremely hard to do bad in this class. Both tests are online. The only thing that may affect your grade are the HW analysis but it is just really hard to get an A. With that being said I have not received lower than a B on one. TAKE THIS CLASS I PROMISE.

reviews.comment: the worst class ever actualyl pointless and has NOTHING TO DO WITH MY MAJOR. so much work for no reason i couldnt care less about computers

reviews.comment: The worst. How is this her primary job? She's reading stuff of her slides. I just hope she retires and spares future students the torture.
Good professor
There are likely better options out there.
dry lectures & grades aren't rounded up.
What a bore! She really needs to reevaluate her career choices. Currently the worst professor I had and probably the worst professor I'll ever have.

Lots of small writing assignments, and you need to make sure to specifically follow her writing format. (Bullet points only, no big paragraphs). Lectures were overall not super interesting, and there was a lot of groupwork throughout the class. The 3 tests are all online, and I think that she grades lighter on you if she likes you, so participate
I'm convinced that all her positive reviews are written by her. Such a terrible professor whose lectures are a snooze fest. I've got a good grade, but didn't learn anything at all. What a joke.

such a sweetheart in the class. can be a mix of lectures and group work in the class (i hated the group work). 3 tests which are all online and 1 final project and assignments were sometimes difficult to understand since she wanted specific requirements (no paragraphs, but bullet points instead). only annoying thing is she kept us overtime.
She is super sweet and definitely appreciated if you make any sort of effort to participate, certainly recommend her!
Decent class, but she definitely favored some groups over others when grading group projects

She is such a sweetheart! Despite the reviews, her grading really isn't that tough if you make sure your responses are thorough and you follow her format. DO NOT write case studies or discussions in paragraph form. Also make sure to participate, because that grade really matters to her. Overall, the course was easy if you follow instructions.

Although professor soule can be a very tough grader, the class is not super difficult. So long as you do the assignments on time and put effort into it, as well as attend class and participate, it should be an easy A-. She is a very kind professor and cares about what she teaches. Just put in the effort and you'll be fine.
dry lecturer, but the class is okay. there is a lot of HW that are reading assignments and quizzes on it. Tests are not too hard if you study the case analysis well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Nice person, but an extremely dry lecturer and does not teach well. She barely explains concepts in class, and spends the entire time explaining complex concepts we were rarely tested on. You are expected to read the textbook and know everything before classes, which makes you question what you're paying for.

Don't expect an A, because she does not give any. You will not learn anything helpful in this class. Almost all of the topics are outdated, and only the surface is scratched for each subject. Attendance is mandatory, but either way, no one is paying attention. B+ is very easy to get as long as you put minimal effort into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice professor but unclear guidelines on written material make it impossible to improve after she gives you 80s on every case study which is worth most of your grade. Even if you talk to her in person she is still vague with how she wants you to complete the assignments. If you want an A in this course don't take her.

Dry lectures which feel outdated, have few examples, and just dull material, and still expect participation in every class. Papers every week and 2-3 small quizzes every week. Begins the class by saying A is basically not attainable, and she stayed true to her words; no one got an A. Very demotivating thing to start with. Never curves.
DO NOT TAKE HER! Her lectures are not engaging and her grading is very unclear. You will never get an A in this class because she does not give them. Stay away from this class if you can.
sometime take attendance. She covered lots of material without digging further, literally learn nothing from her class. lots of quizzes and boring classes.

Very lecture heavy in class but she likes to include some group discussions a few times a week. She wants you to read a chapter of the book every few days, but you can get by withtout reading. There are case studies as assignments every week, which are not difficult just very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: WARNING:DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!A lot of case studies and she grades harshly, providing little feedback. No one ever gets 5/5, highest always 4.4/5 when they're worth ~25% of your grade. 2 tests that were also very difficult w/ questions unclear/broad. You need at least a 94 to get an A so not only does she grade hard, you also need to work harder.

very average professor. my biggest gripe was how slow she was with grading and a bit unclear on her criteria. when she did provide feedback though, it was decent. she tried her best to make class engaging, even though it usually didn't work. they're revamping this course though so hopefully it's better whenever you take it.

Grade based on Individual + group case studies, chapter quizzes, 2 exams + Capstone assignment. Exams are kind of confusing, they follow the case study format and aren't multiple choice. You'll do well if you follow the case study format. Lectures are kind of confusing but she is super sweet and will help if you ask her. Quizzes aren't difficult.
This class is hard, and this professor makes it harder. Don't ever take it. I prepared so much before every class, but still confusing what the professor is talking.

Professor Soule is a nice lady, but a horrid grader.The material is given from the text and is supported using case studies. She doesn't offer individual corrections so that one may learn,rather she posts broad guidelines. The exam I took was the broadest, most unclear exam ever.Little to zero instructions were given. No one knew what was expected.

a lot of quizzes but its easy, a ton of individual and group case studies that she grades really hard on and doesn't provide individual feedback so you have no clue what you did wrong, very condescending, doesn't respond to emails, tests are stupid hard. i learned nothing. thank god this isnt my concentration.

reviews.comment: Professor Soule was very kind and always available to answer questions. She valued student feedback and worked very hard to make this boring material engaging and encourage conversations about the material. If you used vocabulary and frameworks she presented in class you can get an A on every assignment.

Prof Soule is kind and enjoys what she teaches. Unfortunately she does not know how to teach undergraduate students business statistics. She rarely does examples in class, you have to figure everything out by yourself, is unclear, and if you arent an expert with excel youre in major trouble. She made the class more difficult than it needed to be.

reviews.comment: Handed a lot of case studies, seldom get feedback.

Really enjoyed Cognition with Professor DiBattista. The grade is based on 3 exams, homework, and quizzes you can do at home. She makes a real effort to engage students during lecture and provides plenty of outside support via office hours. Overall, an outstanding teaching style, wish I could have her in more classes!!! :))

She's super knowledgeable about her field and definitely wants her students to succeed! Don't be scared to ask questions because she'll always go back and reexplain things. There was a lot of content within lectures but it's easy to do well in the class if you try. Grade consists of 3 exams, 3 homework assignments, and weekly online hw quizzes.

I love her so much! She let us use cheat sheets for all 3 tests, which were pretty easy. She is incredibly knowledgable in her field, is super easy to talk to, and has fire fits. If you can take her for Cognition, TAKE HER! I thought I wouldn't like the class, but she made the content interesting and presents it in an easy to understand way!

It was a very insightful course overall and prof D is very knowledgeable in the psycholinguistics field. She gives extensive feedback with the chance to improve with rewrites. Research proposal assignment is very fun and makes you think critically. She grades fairly and is always available by email or office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor DiBattista was the best professor I've ever had. She is incredibly passionate about cognition. I was dreading taking this class and surprisingly she has made me very fond of the study of cognition. In fact, it was my favorite class of the semester mostly because of her stellar lectures. She cracks some jokes and is very approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: if u pay attention in class you'll end with an A, if you dont, I dont see how you can get above a C. class was interesting.

Professor DiBattista is very passionate about her subject which makes the class super engaging and easier to enjoy. Her lectures were well done and very interesting. As long as you followed the lectures you would do well on the tests and assignments.

Professor DiBattista is very passionate, and is very helpful about reviewing material if you have questions or need clarification. There are a few tests and homework assignments that she gives you plenty of time to complete. Although attendance isn't mandatory, most of the content on tests is covered during in-class lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a great professor and really educated in her field. Three exams throughout the semester, in-class but open note (no final). Exam questions can be difficult to follow sometimes, so it's important to understand concepts, but the course material is interesting. Pay attention during the lectures and take good notes

Great professor! Knows her stuff and her lectures are full of things to learn. Homework is interesting and helps with the exams. There are 3 homeworks in the whole semester and have 7-8 short answer questions each. 3 exams in the semester (no final) which are MCQ and open note - easy if you take thorough notes. The course material's intriguing.

reviews.comment: Easy class. Wish I took it as an underclassman as a lot of the course materials were review from other Psych classes, so it was really boring to take as an upperclassman psych major. Then again, don't mind an easy elective my senior year!

Best lecturer I have ever had, hands down. Prof DiBattista really knows how to connect with her students and create an engaging class. Lectures are very interesting, exams are open note and easy if you take thorough notes in class. She is very accessible outside class. Highly recommend this class, it made me minor in psychology.

reviews.comment: Professor DiBattista really cares about her students and gives good feedback. There are three assigned papers for this class. The paper's content is mostly covered in class.

reviews.comment: this course is a waste of time.

I found that the lectures for this class were interesting and I learned a lot. You should go to lectures because a lot of the spoken points showed up on the exams. She does give points back on exams and a bit of extra credit towards the end. The textbook is necessary to get full points on the homework assignments.
