reviews.comment: Learned many interesting things. One of the best psych professor I had.

Prof DiBattista is super nice and well informed. Even though her lectures are hard to follow cuz theres a lot of info, she genuinely tries to keep students interested in Cognition. Content consists of a lot of theories & experiments to remember. 3 noncumulative exams & assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I love Amy DiBattista. She is a real gem. She's so knowledgable and clearly knows what she's talking about. She's always willing to meet with people and answer their questions. Tests are based heavily on her lectures, but if you miss her lectures, she posts review questions on Blackboard.

I absolutely love her and she is one of the best professors I've ever had. The 3 HW assignments are easy and the tests are fair and totally based on powerpoints plus she gives study guides. She's super enthusiastic about the things she lectures on and is willing to look into questions she can't answer right away and get back to you with an answer.

Very knowledgeable about cognition and psychology in general. Her lectures were pretty long with a lot of info, but she was very clear about expectations and gives review questions for exams. Exams were pretty fair and straightforward. 3 exams and 3 one page assignments (manageable). Very helpful and caring!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: While she's very sweet, her lectures are a little boring and confusing. Even though I never missed class, studying for her tests was always the worst just because there is so much content and she's not very good at explaining things. Regardless, she tries very hard and is always willing to help (especially if you visit her office hours).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The best Professor ever, without qualification. Her lectures were interesting and filled with information and she had a command of the material. Questions were encouraged and the tests were fair with good review. Helpful after class and in office hours. I took 4 total courses with her, including a 1-on-1 session she agreed to so I could graduate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures felt quite dull as they mostly consist of her talking off of her slides. The slides are ridiculously uninformative as most have some keywords without any definition, so if you didn't make it to class then you won't know what they mean. There are no slide notes with more information so the few words on the slides are all you'll get.

She's incredibly nice and very straightforward. doesn't use the textbook at all and is very lecture-heavy. talks straight through but throws in jokes and examples of the experiments to make things easier. totally willing to meet outside of the classroom to help and she gives extra credit if a test seemed more difficult (all mult. choice)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor DiBattista is one of the best professors I've ever had.  Her lectures were always interesting between her quirky humor and extensive knowledge on the subject, I didn't want class to end. She made me realize how much I love cognition! I took statistics with her too.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are not always the most engaging and quizzes and exams are quite difficult. He is also a bit of a tough grader. He says attendance isn't mandatory but it basically is, so show up and participate and he will like you. He does also try to give a few questions before exams and throw students a bone sometimes but not an easy A by any means
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is very cooperative and helpful with feedback. Gives extra credit; the "pop-quizzes" are announced/heavily hinted at and the first quiz is basically group work so everyone gets an A. Overall highly recommend taking this class.

I clearly remember checking his rating before the start of fall semester and a 2.5 scared the s**t out of me but he is actually great! The exams are tough and solely based on lectures/detailed PowerPoints (no point in cheating). He is very lenient and cooperative, gives extra credit and actually wants everyone to do well.
Super interactive professor. He's lenient and gracious. Since it's an intro class, it's easy and very manageable.

PLEASE IGNORE THESE REVIEWS!!! Professor Nace is one of the most amazing professors I have had so far at Northeastern. He deeply cares about his students and how they're doing in his class. He responds very quickly to emails and has time to talk after class. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND.
HW assignments every Friday and an hour-long simulation every week. So give or take around an hour and a half of homework per week. Quizzes are easy, the final is take-home and online.

I swear every good rating on here he wrote himself cause the amount that he brings up his Rate My Professor is insane, especially the first week. Literally used AI to try to catch us using AI and spent his entire break doing it. Marketing is such common sense the majority of the time and he overcomplicates it so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lectures are mandatory but irrelevant. He loves to talk about his old job at Bose- he should probably stay there for everyone's sake. He's reachable and knowledgeable, but a questionable teacher. Tests are hard and irrelevant to class discussions, and he never clearly states what's on them, so you're anxious all class not knowing what to write down
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: hard quizzes. so much reading, not worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: switching my major to finance because he made me hate marketing SO MUCH
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't take
He curves down so only a certain percent of class can get As. Yes it will grow you, but yes it will also take a blow to your gpa if you're into that sort of thing. Would stay away if you can

Nace is very passionate and a nice guy, however, his grading and stance on GPA is pretty bad. He believes it does not matter but in reality it really does. Teaching wise, he is very good and once you leave the semester you will have a strong understanding of marketing. I would recommend taking him but you're going to have to work really hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: (For BC)... David Nace is the Goat... tough class but rewarding if you try. Exams were difficult but I learned a lot about marketing... important to do well on group projects/participate. Has inspired me to possibly pursue a career in marketing/advertising.

Participation is really important and he ends up rewarding those who come to class by rounding their grades. The final was insanely difficult for no reason though. Overall you'll learn a lot but he does make an intro class a lot harder than it needs to be. Also don't really like his stance on GPA as he thinks it doesn't matter.

Prof nace is a nice guy but not a good teacher. His quizzes aren't THAT bad, but his final was crazy hard and everyone ik bombed it. Also, he grades harshly on the paper and in general, so A's are rare. Basically no HW tho. I think he genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed, but he needs to brush up on some things lol.

passionate guy who tries his best to keep lectures engaging by encouraging class participation. He writes his own tests and quizzes, which are pretty hard as you can study for hours on end, but the quiz will be on something else entirely. I liked his class in general though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this professor. He's incredibly engaging—his lectures are so interesting I don't even need my laptop. The lectures are very conversational which I enjoy, and he truly encourages you to ask questions and won't make you feel dumb. He's also super personable and easy to connect with. One of the best professors I've had!

Professor Nace is very passionate about the field of marketing, and his lectures are engaging at times. People are overreacting about the difficulty of the course. It is a lot of memorization, but if you read the textbook and put the work in, you can easily do well. He was very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Nace is really nice and laid back and is definitely funny at times, but his class had lots of reading, lectures werent actually lectures they were discussions which felt like you were teaching for him. they were unhelpful so i stopped coming to class. Also he changes his syllabus and other course stuff all the time. class wasnt too hard tho

Class is hard for no reason. It's an entry-level class, and it shouldn't be this hard. Nobody is getting an A in my class. He also says he will keep the average grade around B and curve down if the average is higher than B. Be ready to read 40 pages textbook for each class and extremely hard exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is difficult for no reason. We literally were tested on things I learned in my managerial accounting class. I talked to other kids in the same class and their tests/quizzes are so much easier. He's not fair, he needs to understand that.
changes the syllabus every once in a while. Class is difficult for no reason. wouldn't take again for a marketing class

Dave Nace is the GOAT. He's lecture-heavy, but he engages you in the lectures and asks questions. He gets to know each person and really cares about you. He responds well to student feedback about his teaching. The final was online, and hard, but he warned us. If you truly want to understand marketing, take his class.

I don't entirely agree with the other reviews. His lectures were engaging (stories, etc.), and I walked away feeling I knew more than prior to starting the course. The caveat is that he gave an extremely tough final exam, and did not help us in preparing for it. He offered many opportunities for office hours and responded to my emails quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He changed his syllabus without warning and says that he doesn't know how to help when you ask questions. The final was NOT AT ALL what he said it was going to be. Quizzes are strictly based on how much info you can fit onto a cheat sheet. Came off as understanding at first but then did a complete 180. Don't recommend at all!!
Professor Nace was an amazing guy, very personable and lots of experience, but his class was very challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I feel it is fair to mention it was his first time teaching the course. HOWEVER, personally, I would NEVER take a course with Nace again. He likes to say GPA won't matter in the future and teaches like he believes that as well. I have never been so frustrated. Expect a ton of textbook reading, no study guides, and “I don't know how to help you.”

Nit-picky grading. SPSS is challenging software to use, minimal class time is dedicated to it, and projects require its use. I agree with a previous review that she is kind, but her classroom practices are not. Two tips: she doesn't care much about prose quality and adds additional extra credit during the term.

While Professor Yang is knowledgeable in her field, I found her teaching approach hard to follow. The workload was excessive, and course material was not always digestible. Many students, myself included, were accused of academic dishonesty over (correct) midterm answers. This experience left me feeling discouraged in the learning process.

Loved the class. Lecture on Tuesday, quiz on Friday (only content from Tues). Also labs/tutorials on graphing on Friday that basically help you finish lab assignment. Alternates between lab assignment (visualization tied to question(s)) or a reading + discussion post. She gives a lot of opportunity for extra credit. Drops lowest quiz score. Loved
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very by-the-book, but still kind. Many opportunities for extra credit; like so many. Class content isn't difficult, there's just a lot of content. Could be more understanding/flexible, but also does what she can without going out of order if that makes sense. Sufficient amount of assignments to be graded from.

Very kind and understanding. Class was at 8AM, but the content was delivered well. She really wants you to do well. She's kinddd of intimidating but it's because she's so organized and objective. I honestly loved her and the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and don't take this class if you can help it. Professor can't convey the material well and doesn't properly answer questions. She's nice when you approach her, but her classroom practices are not.

I tried to give the benefit of the doubt, but the instructors lectures are confusing to follow. She never answers questions, she is unforgiving as far as late assignments and life events go. She seems kind, but her practices as a professor make you forget that. People have lives outside of school and she is not willing to work around it.

Took this class for INSH 6500 for the criminal justice graduate program. I would not recommend this class. It is incredibly R heavy, the midterm is timed with an R portion to it and long complicated theory questions. Homework is very time consuming and intense.

Unclear grading scheme and feedback. Pre-recorded lectures were tedious and hard to follow. If you didn't understand something in the in-class lecture, you were left behind. Prof often refused to answer questions.
Class avg. was ~70 for the midterm and ~60 for the final, fortunately, she offered a lot of extra credit to bring the grade up.

Unorganized and long lectures. Confusing instructions with errors. Incoherent lab notes. Assignments were challenging and took hours. Professor is unwilling to cooperate with the students. Please do not take this class, I literally did not learn a single thing.
Not much HW, the instructions are not clear, professor herself doesn't know what she is teaching. The class is super boring. Midterm was hard. The lecture was not clear. Horrible class
Fade fade fade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Velazco is great! He's very lecture-heavy and values participation a lot. There are three exams that are difficult to study for because there is so much material (textbook + slides), and grading/expectations are not always clear. The class is hard, but if you show up and truly try, you'll be ok!

Professor Velazco overall was a great professor! His classes are discussion based so be prepared to be called on but he makes it a fun environment to participate in. I will say although he is great, his grading is a bit all over the place. He isn't very clear with his expectations and his grading reflects that.

This class is genuinely confusing, difficult tests, no study guide, many students are failing, just gives us a handbook and practice tests, which closes down the night before the actual test. Many students don't know where to start studying or where to go, as he only refers to the textbook. Tests are also really inconsistent, DO NOT TAKE AT ALL.

He doesn't teach at all in lectures. If you take this class, you're kind of on your own. His lectures are pointless. The only examples that you do in class are math calculations, which make up a small part of the exams you take. There are 3 exams in total. He does post practice exams, but he makes you use a lockdown browser to take them?? Avoid!!

Honestly the professor is not that bad the only reason he's getting a 1 star is because he is not consistent with his tests. The first exam was 90% the same as the study guide. So you would assume that's the best way to study. Nope the next two exams are completely different and doesn't match his teaching style. If u can avoid it's better

Lectures wise were not that great for me. He's ok with grading and he rounded my final grade up after I asked. I would say definitely a good professor to talk to, especially if you are into SC as a career. Be active and ask him for clarifications on assignments and you will be fine (above B). Final was online. Tests are tough, but fair game.

Prof Enio is a nice guy but structures his class like it's the only class you'll be taking that semester. Group projects are intensely difficult with untold strict guidelines and bad group mates, & he does nothing to remedy how lost everyone in the class is. Take only if supply chain is your life passion or if you hate yourself!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely evil professor, not in the way he interacts with students (he's a nice dude), but straight up just how he grades. Long assignments, terrible group projects esp if you have bad groupmates, and he's really unclear with every guideline. DO NOT TAKE unless this is the only class you're taking that sem or your rlly passionate about schm.

Professor Velazco is a great professor and a really nice guy. He moves through lectures quickly but uses good examples that the class reviews together. He keeps everyone engaged by asking for their thoughts and opinions at random. I'd definitely recommend him, but be ready to work!
He's a great professor who's always available during office hours and genuinely helpful when students need support. He does tend to call on students during class, but overall he's excellent.

He's a tough grader, doesn't give enough guidance on what he wants. For the group project (50% of our grade), not all expectations were spelled out in the syllabus. In a 1 month DOC, there was not enough time to adjust to his expectations. A lot of us were unpleasantly surprised by our final grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's honestly the best prf I've had. he's funny, caring, and witty. material was engaging, and even though he's a tough grader, if you stay on top of the work and put effort into it, he's way more understanding. Just show up, join the discussions, and you'll walk away having learned a ton.

Lectures were helpful, but his tests and projects just seemed wasteful. He doesn't go into depth with concepts past what the presentations say, which had useless information that never got brought up again. He wasn't helpful outside of class, and his feedback is awful. He also doesn't care about the test averages (our midterm average was a 67).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Projects are 40% of the grade, so just pray your team pulls their weight. He loves teaching but he won't curve so just be ready for a low test average which is 30% of the grade.
Prof Velazco is super passionate and knowledgeable about supply chain. Lectures are not super helpful, but the group projects are super fun.

Prof Velazco is a super nice guy and is very passionate and knowledgeable about supply chain. His lectures aren't super helpful, and he just repeats the textbook material, so if you need good lectures, this class might not be for you. no final in the class, just three exams throughout the semester. Overall would recommend.

He is a very interesting professor with lots of cool stories and engaging lectures. He is passionate about supply chain and makes his students intrigued as well. There is a lot of work and tests are not easy. There is lots of textbook HW, multiple written assignments, 3 tests, and a project. It is a lot of work but you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really like him regardless of how others may feel. He is strict but wake up people, it's an upper level college class in a tough major, it's not supposed to be a breeze. His class is a great refresher from my other classes that are just Exam 1 + Exam 2 + Final. There is a massive variety of projects, case studies, and other interesting content

He's awesome! I love that he does many things not just tests. There are many different projects and such. He also always has good stories about working as executive in the real world so it is not just lectures and textbook

Many of the reviews tell you to avoid him because of his harsh participation. However, I believe this is not the case. Professor Velazco provides ample opportunities for you to participate and is really just looking to see if you are engaging the classroom. As long as you put in an honest effort, you will do great things in this class!

Professor Velazco is a wonderful professor who spices things up with a wide variety of class activities. There are several different group projects, case studies, papers, and readings that make his class much more exciting than an average lecture heavy, textbook-only course. He is a tough grader on participation though, so speak up more!

Beware of the participation grade at the end of the year. It dropped my grade very low. For the case presentations, his rubric is unclear and he's a harsh grader. His tests were very difficult and didn't match his material. His exams were online with lockdown browser but it was still difficult and the class average was low but he didn't curve it.
I would recommend taking Enio's class. Slightly disorganized and vague in his requirements for papers and projects, but for the most part if you put in decent effort you will do well.

I was doing well in his class, which took a lot of work and effort to be consistent in, but he ruined my grade with participation. Beware you must participate throughout the semester or it will kill your grade by the end of the semester.

This class is based on 3 tests, that are not related to the LONG lectures given by the professor. All the projects are impossible to get a 100. He is passionate about the class, but his way of teaching is of the 20th century. If you want to learn with a mediocre grade take this class, if you want a good grade avoid it!

This class is hard. Everyone I know, regardless of professor would say SCHM is hard. The exams are also very difficult to get the grade you want on. Despite this, the professor is still amazing. He is very passionate and makes lectures fun. Of all the SCHM professors, I would recommend Velazco the most.

Nice guy but very difficult class. Could've gotten a B+ but the prof refused to bump my participation grade 5% despite actually participating in class. Most of your grade comes from the three huge tests that are throughout the semester which are confusing and cover content that was not gone over during class. Do not take SCHM with him.

He is a nice guy, it was his first semester at school. I learned a lot because I read all the chapters, not necessarily from the class. The major problem was that the exams were extremely confusing and hard.
The material taught in class didn't match what was on exams. It was difficult to prepare for exams given the differences between the information in the textbook/slides versus what was on the exams.

Two open-note online quizzes and a final. Attendance allows 2 drops; absences excused if sick. ~5 HW plus easy grade boosters. Simulation is standard but limited presentation guidance; good guest speakers. Grading is strict—90%+ is rare for HW/Quiz. Must justify each MC. B+ to A- doable, A is tough.

The class consists of 2 online ‘quizzes' and an online final. Every class is the same with a lecture and slide deck that he goes through. The class is simple and only requires the bare minimum effort and if you do end up struggling, just ask for help. Bike sim: even though my group finished last we got the best grade bc our slide deck was the best.

A.I's all his slides and homework, convinced he uses A.I to grade everything which explains why he gives weird numbers as grades and why no one was able to get an A in his class. Boring lectures but participation is needed. He's a good guy, but a pretty bad professor. If you want an A- take it cuz that's easy to get but an A is impossible.

Don't think anyone in my class got an A since his grading system makes it impossible. Open note quizzes and final exam but don't help since timed and everyone in class used A.I on all assignments including the exams. Boring lectures tbh but participation matters. Take a different professor to get an A otherwise an A- is really easy to get.

Mandatory attendance, participation is graded, and his grading system prevents you from getting an A. Great thing though is that all quizzes are "open note open web," but what sucks is that he makes you give JUSTIFICATIONS FOR YOUR MCQ ANSWERS. Don't take him if you want an easy A. He's a great person and accessible outside of class though.

Wants success for his students! Lecture heavy, but take notes on the slides as he presents them and its manageable. Group bike simulation project for most of semester is main homework plus a couple others. Unique grading format for quizzes and tests that gives students the best opportunity to do well. Talks kind of quiet so sit towards front.

Great professor. The class is lecture heavy and participation matters. There are two quizzes and a final; there is a bike simulation group project that you complete for most of the semester and present at the end. The quizzes are done on Canvas and he has a unique grading scale - I recommend him overall, very caring, respectful, and experienced
take her if you can! she knows how to teach and makes you like accounting.
She is born for accounting and makes you love it too.  She is very clear and extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Bogdani made me love Accounting! She is a very nice person with tons of knowledge in accounting.
If you learn all year you get max grades. She is fair and professional.
She is very very well prepared and makes you love Accounting. The grading system is super clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Bogdani is well-versed in accounting, clearly communicates information, and is very organized. That said, she is a bad test-maker. Her quizzes do not fully reflect the material and one missed question can make your score a C- from an A. She also never curves test grades which is ridiculous given that many of the quiz averages are below 65.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She is an AMAZING professor. You can tell she wants all her students to do well in the class. She is very helpful in and outside of class. Only annoying thing in the class was homework, but it was very manageable. She does over extra credit; we just have to attend events.
By far the best Professor at Northeastern University. She is very very well prepared and knows the subject inside out.

Teacher was very confusing with her lectures, it was very lecture heavy and my brain would get jumbled. The tests were very difficult and you HAVE to read the textbook to pass the test, even then you might not. Basically a question of whether you are good at math or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She cared a lot about how her students did. She would always make herself available outside of class if you needed help. She was a clear professor and also cared a lot about the content she was teaching.

Professor gives you everything you need to succeed through practice questions and handouts. However, as a professor she is not great at explaining although she is very open to help. Homework's are easy, and quizzes can be difficult. 3 exams 2 are 10% and one 30% which are difficult but she goes through practice papers in class which help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is really nice, understanding, and truly cares about her students. She makes herself very available and responds to emails quickly. She provides lots of practice problems to prep for the exams/quizzes. This class is harder but if you do/study the practice problems and open response practice then you'll do well. Overall loved her!

She's one of the better accounting professors. Weekly homework, easy at first and gradually gets harder given the nature of the content of the class. One of the sweetest and most generous professors, but accounting was just a tough subject for me.

Prof Bogdani is a great professor who truly cares about her students. Overall class is not hard with lectures and practice handouts about the material. There are four quizzes, but she drops the lowest one. Most of the material is taken directly from the lectures and handouts. In the end, she wants you to do well, so take her class!!

Dr. Bogdani is easily the best professor I've ever had. She is so caring and really wants her students to succeed. She even took the time to learn all of her students names. She provides so many resources for practice including practice quizzes and problems in class and is always willing to meet outside of class if you need extra help. Take her!!!

Easilly one of my favorites! Class is easy to keep up with as long as you put in the work! There first quiz was probably my worst one then I learned her teaching habits. I use lectures and the textbook, and I have an A in the class. She is very caring and compassionate. The TAs also help a lot, and she's always willing to help in any way! Love her.

Professor Bogdani is a wonderful teacher that clearly loves accounting. If you do the work it is not hard to get an A, I struggled at first but then got better throughout the year, read the textbook before the lecture! She is great at explaining and giving lectures, as well as providing extra practice for exams and quizzes. She can also be funny:).

His class will be easy to take if you attend all classes, tells you what's gonna be on quizzes and tests. But if you miss a single class for any circumstances, be prepared to struggle and be lost for the entirety of the rest of the topic, and probably struggle with the quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy is genuinely the most passionate professor you will have. He cares about his students and wants everyone to do their absolute best. Quizzes are chill and midterms are clearly laid out. Just go to class and pay attention.

Very enthusiastic, but not the most effective professor when he teaches. Clear favorites, but if you are able to study alone, quizzes and exams aren't bad at all. Often goes on tangents about personal stories and opinions. Try not to sit in the back if you don't want to be picked on lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: cant even lie i felt like i was listening to google translate with an accent. he was telling stories more than lecturing. quite easy to finesse a grade in tho so ill give him that

I passed this class because I took AP Calc in High School. His tests and quizzes are super easy and he tells you what is on them. He prepares you well for the final, but if you don't know calculus going into this, don't take this class.

Before each quiz/exam, goes through each question & tells u exactly whats on it. Responds to emails quickly. *Go to his office hours he will help you* Grades very fairly, will reconsider points off if you talk with him.
Sometimes a bit scary. He's from the Soviet union, so thats just his personality. He wont hate you unless you never come to class.

Prof. Karapetian was a great teacher and I felt he prepared us well for each test. If you attend class and pay attention, you will be fine. Weekly quizzes that are pretty easy and have extra credit questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Karapetian is alright. He gives quizzes weekly, but he tells you exactly what is on it so if you write down what's on it and study the quizzes are super light. Midterms are the same. He is absolutely hilarious and often goes on rants about random topics during class. One time he told us to go to China and work as engineers there.

Ok, this dude is hilarious. Hands down one of the funniest guys ive ever met, and it's not because he tries to be. Lectures are a bit all over the place but you'll know what's on your test. I thought he was a great teacher and his stories were awesome. SIT IN THE FRONT ROW (I promise it matters).

First two weeks of lecture were confusing and unrelated, don't feel overwhelmed. Lectures are disorganized but tests are EXACTLY like what is covered. tells you ahead of time what the test Qs are. likes to call/call out students, makes lectures fun. lectures go really fast; if you're confident in calc 1 class is easy. No HW and tests have bonus pts

Prof Karapetian was such a funny guy. In class he walks you through exactly what you need to know and teaches to understand. He tells you exactly what will be on tests/quizes and offers extra credit questions on most tests. He can sometimes go off on tangents about the American education system which can seem targeted but he really cares.

He teaches the class like we already know the material. During his lectures, he moves too quickly to grasp the lesson, and then he pauses and says "everybody understands?" and wait a second and then move on. If you ask a question about what he just tried to explain, he flames you for not understanding and your old teachers for being unable to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: textbook was HORRIBLE and he's not great at explaining things either. it helps to review the topic before class because he works so quickly on the board that you WILL get lost if you dont know whats happening. however it's hard to get lower than a C on quizzes because the partial credit is crazy generous

He can be very nice and friendly in class AS LONG AS YOU PAY ATTENTION. He clearly outlines the exact types of questions in the exams and quizzes and provides practice questions. He can sometimes drone off on unrelated tangents and he can be condescending to individuals depending on your major. (If you're a business major, don't tell him.)

Very passionate guy. He clearly cares about his lecture and about the subject he's teaching, and he's pretty funny when teaching. But, be prepared to learn everything during his office hours or by yourself (Organic Chem Tutor was a life saver). Edgar moves really fast through his lectures and for the love of God I could not read his handwriting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a hard course, even if you took Calc 2 last year. He can be difficult to understand at times and moves very quickly. However, he will answer your questions and is VERY helpful during office hours. He doesn't sugarcoat anything, which can come off as rude, but he doesn't mean it in that way. Also, the exams are a HUGE part of the grade.

Amazing teacher and cares about making sure that students understand but can be tough in class. if you ask a stupid question, he will say you should know the answer and your past teachers failed but then he will answer the question as clearly as he can. you will either love him or hate him.

Edgar Karapetian is by far the worst professor I've ever had the displeasure of taking. I'm telling you, you should never, and I mean seriously never take his class. Even if you need the class and he's the only open section just wait until next semester even if it delays your graduation. He's horribly rude and discouraging to students. Bad teacher.

He moves extremely fast and does not make sure students understand the material. He is hard to follow with his handwriting and the lack of explanation he gives. He doesn't fully walk through problems and instead just does them and yell at the class. Very mean and condescending to students. Most unprofessional and rude professor i've ever met.

If you already know calculus, this class is very easy. If you're new to calc, the professor may be challenging because his teaching isn't very clear. Attendance isn't necessary, but keep track of test and quiz dates. He can be a picky grader. He always tells you exactly what q's will be on test+quiz. Also kinda funny, but it gets old.
He basically tells students exactly what is gonna be on the tests/quizzes ahead of time. Super funny, his lectures are very entertaining. Best math teacher I've had.

Probably the worst teacher I've had in my life. Not only can he not teach, he is also a very unpleasant person. He spends half the class time ranting about how we shouldn't be allowed to become scientists and engineers and then tries to catch up to where we should have been so he always holds us over time. Horrible professor. Do not take his class.

Don't take Calc 2 with him. He's disrespectful, condescending, and has an inflated ego. His lectures are confusing, and he mumbles. He always publicly shames students for mistakes, creating a hostile environment. Additionally, he makes inappropriate, racist comments. His notes are messy and hard to follow, making the course even more challenging.

Great prof who really wants you to learn. Not for very sensitive students, but if you can handle a bit of pressure he's awesome. Tells you what's on the tests, gives similar practice, super generous cheat sheets, funny, fast-paced but manageable, and truly passionate about math.

This professor is very rude, disrespectful, moves very quickly, hard to follow his handwriting, and patronizes students when they ask questions. The ONE single benefit is that he tells you the questions on his tests beforehand. He WILL publicly embarrass you in front of the class for a variety of reasons (it's awful when you don't know an answer).

reviews.comment: Professor Karapetian can make learning Calculus stressful. During lecture, he often shouts at his students, going on fervent tangents about the school system. In my class, he said that we are all on a fifth grade level and we should not be taking Calculus. It is hard to ask questions during lecture because of the fear of being called out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not seem to care for his students. He moves extremely fast, even knowing the material it is hard to understand. He does not wait for students or make sure they understand and he bullies students for asking questions. He is very condescending and I i never felt comfortable asking questions. He also has no tolerance for missing quizzes, ever.
Great guy, very chill. Clear about expectations. Give out random extra credit. Very reasonable, just make sure you show up to class and do the homeworks and you'll be fine.
TRUST. He's the one

Lectures and provided class materials are pretty useful even though attendance isnt mandatory. Cold calling is a bit scary at first but it honestly helps you stay on top of stuff and is super chill (mostly to get people to follow along). Homeworks are fair and easy to complete. Overall nice prof

Professor Bogert is one of the funniest professors out there. I really enjoyed his class. You can tell he's really loves data viz! Don't understand why he has such a low rating here, but I think those students are the ones who never show up to class and clearly don't pay attention to what's going on! Highly recommend taking his class especially

This is definitely a tough class if you have no experience in Excel or coding. Lectures are pretty fast-paced but Professor Bogert is very easy-going and will answer any question. Attendance is not mandatory, but I don't recommend skipping. If you go to class, pay attention, and do some light reading of materials on canvas, then you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: Idk why bogert has such a low rating, pretty sure the ppl that dislike him r fully just haters. Hes super clear about expectations from the start, the avg grades r pretty high, just PAY ATTENTION in class and youll succeed. Its not easy, but you learn a lot. Hes strict ab small things, but its js to prevent cheating. Love this prof, hes a G

Great professor, if you pay attention in class and study, the exams go very smoothly. Cares about his students' success and was very helpful. MISM2510 was really helpful in getting better at Excel and SQL (even Python), so this class was really useful for future careers in finance/business. Highly recommend taking any class with Professor Bogert.
Just pick him trust, he's chill and funny (spams the 67 joke), pay attention in class, and do the practice questions, you'd be good for the exam. He also allows cheat sheets.
Loves to punish his students, and categorizes them into "good and bad." Weird guy.

reviews.comment:
Don't feel like I learned anything but he doesn't gaf about attendance and is a lenient grader
Feels like he expects everyone in the class to already know everything
Two tests and 3 hw assignments, tests require some effort but hw graded loosely
Reading the textbooks right before test will not help(pretty sure I would have failed if he didn't curve

This course has a reputation for being tough, and I believe that depends on the student's background. Those comfortable with data and can learn software (Tableau) fast will do well, while the opposite is  also true.

Prof. and TAs want you to be successful & go out of their way to offer help.I loved this class, but understand why some find it hard.

reviews.comment: Each question on Exams & HWs are worth a lot, so it's easy to quickly lose points if you make mistakes, but it's a very easy class, so if you're attentive, it should be easy. Very lenient grader (gave everyone 100% on the project). Office Hours are very helpful. Professor was amazing! Accommodating, lovely, caring, respecting & knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly I don't know why he has such a low rating. The class is definitely hard and requires attendance (although he does post the video recordings) but he's a great professor. Provides more than enough practice to ace the exams and homework. 1 group project but easy to score in as well.

He is smart and is passionate about what he teaches, but he isn't a good teacher. He cold calls, asks hard questions on purpose, and exams are oddly specific questions that you can't answer even if you follow along in class.

Doesn't properly teach how to use Tableau,just expects you to know everything off the bat even though he made us install it for the 1st time. Super biased to his own tastes when grading assignments, if you use a color he doesnt like,he'll mark you down.Assignment criteria is terribly unclear and with the lack of actual teaching makes the class hell

I would say I was shocked by how many low rating scores he has, but I'm not after seeing how many people don't show up to his class and then expect to do well on exams. Bro literally makes it so easy for us, if you actually show up to class, he tells you past test questions (that more often than not show up on the test). Just show up, he is chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Writes his own 'textbook' readings. Explains complex technical stuff in HUMAN LANGUAGE. I love this guy. Not sure why his rating is so low, as I have had a great experience. He may lack a little bit of enthusiasm and he does cold-call, but he is a great instructor nonetheless. Just do your readings before class, dude!! They are amazingly helpful.

Honestly one of the best professors I've had so far. I had no prior coding experience and still got through it with a good grade. Yes he cold calls but that made me pay more attention in lectures which made me do well on the tests. Type of class where if you pay attention and do the work he recommends the work will pay off.

I'm shocked that Prof Bogert doesn't have a higher rating. To be fair, his assignments & exams were pretty difficult. However, if you put in the effort, the class was very fun and enjoyable. He always came prepared and is truly knowledgable about what he teaches. He also really cares about the students and just wants to see you perform your best.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly not sure why he's getting so much hate. The class is difficult, but I never feel like I'm being asked to do something I'm not capable of (I had ZERO prior coding background). Bogert is a great professor, very clear during lectures. Midterm and final you get a  front+back cheat sheet. Homework is weighted heavily and difficult, but doable.

Bogert is actually the worst professor I've ever experienced. His lectures are extremely dry and boring and his exams are unecessarily specific. His grading on assignments and projects is very harsh and you have to make dashboards to the way he likes them rather than what might look good to you or others. Don't waste your money and time on him.

Just don't feel like I'm learning much compared to other professors that teach this course. I'd agree that his rating is low for many of the reasons others have stated. If you could take another professor's course definitely do. His way of teaching isn't giving at all - at least not for me and those I know who take him.

Simply expects you to know how to use Tableau, Excel, SQL, etc. already. Doesn't take into account of beginners. Lectures just go over the textbooks, nothing new being taught. When he does teaches, rarely, Tableau, Excel, SQL, etc. he teaches very quickly so you have to really focus. Assignments lack instructions. Exams are off from what he teaches

He is an awesome professor! I am taking him for my second class now and he's still great. reviews.comment: Professor is extremely knowledgable about the subject and while directions for exams/assignments aren't always obvious, if you attended class and paid attention they shouldn't be a big issue. Great professor & class and you'll learn a lot. Was scared of the RMP reviews but I think it's been a good experience. reviews.comment: 3501 is a good class. You learn so many amazing skills. HWs are time consuming because he wants you to go above and beyond. Very doable class. reviews.comment: Prof Bogert is a cool guy but it is really hard to follow along in lectures because he goes so fast. If you have no experience in Excel, Python, Tableau, or SQL this class may seem really overwhelming and difficult to grasp. His office hours were very limited. The class content is very valuable, but I wish there were more resources outside class.

Avoid at all costs, impossible to understand any of the material, way more advanced than what it is supposed to be. Does not take into account people with no experience in Computer Science. It will just make your semester hell

This professor teaches very fast and it is easy to get lost, plus he doesn't open the exam answers after grading so you can't see what the wrong answers were. The homework is impossible to answer if you are not a cs major. TA office hours were always fully booked and you could only book a 10 minutes spot, impossible to get answers to all questions
This man is teaching nothing in class and expect you to be an expert in the test, literally the worst professor ever
don't come unless you want an F or a D.

Harsh grader with no guidance. Expects you to know everything, and will not explain or help you on things when you're confused. His assignments are hard, and are not clear. He flys through all his lectures, which makes it hard to follow and understand what is going on.

The upsides of his Info Visualization class are that you learn valuable Tableau skills, and get useful feedback.
The downsides are that he goes way too fast when teaching Tableau and his exams questions are very specific to lectures and textbook readings. He is also reluctant to answer questions because he wants you to figure them out on your own.

I was able to do well in the class & I learned valuable Tableau skills but at the same time, the class kinda sucked. Tests weren't based on class but rather on the readings. I couldn't tell if he cared about his students bc it seems like he has really thought through his lectures but also refused to give us a study guide or anything for tests??
Lectures will put you to sleep

reviews.comment: Class time is exclusively spent on lectures and he is a very tough grader. Is reluctant to answer questions about the case studies or tests due to potential academic dishonesty, and takes participation so seriously that he'll stand there and wait until someone who hasn't talked yet raises their hand to answer a question.

Professor Faber is so knowledgeable and passionate about the topic that his lectures are super interesting. I learned so much! All of his test answers are given in his lectures, although attendance isn't mandatory. Be ready to watch a lot of movies, as many of the classes are just taking notes on films. Best class I have ever taken!

Best professor ive ever had, his class is so interesting and important to the real world. He gives you answers to the tests in class, if you go to class youll be fine, I ended with a 99. Long lectures but very interesting and informative.

Professor Faber is very knowledgeable about the environmental movement, and has a lot to say about everything. He is good at explaining topics, but has a tendency to spend half of class going off tangents. Additionally, the Canvas page was very unorganized and he doesn't respond to emails. The self paced aspect of the class is nice though.

Faber is knowledgeable and passionate about his course material and I learned a lot in his class. Attendance is optional but sometimes he explicitly gives you answers to exam questions in lectures, so I recommend showing up. There are homework readings which he doesn't check for completion, but you do have to cite them when writing papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Faber is hands down my favorite professor yet. He truly cares about the topics discussed in class and knows how to integrate real-world pieces into his lectures. Although attendance wasn't necessary, I actually enjoyed going to class. I had to take this for an NU path requirement and wasn't sure at first, but it was the best decision.

I feel like no matter what you're studying you should take his class, even if it's for an NU Path I think you can get a lot out of this class. It definitely changes the way you see things about sociology and environmental science if you weren't already aware of what's really going on. 2 tests, 2 papers, go to every class and you will do just fine!

"I give students the opportunity to get a better grade" Sorta what he said.
He grades his written papers very leniently.
If you're not used to lecture hall style classes it can be hard.
Part of the hw is watching films.
Easy to talk to and knows a lot about what he does, so much so that he's essentially memorised the slides

Professor Daniel Faber is very passionate and extremely knowledgeable about the topic of environmental sociology. I loved his class because the content was so applicable to every part of my life, and without being too challenging I learned a lot. His course is reading-heavy but they were manageable. I recommend him as a professor!

She is very nice, but the language barrier is an issue. reviews.comment: This class is honestly not bad at all if you attend class and pay attention because she goes over EVERYTHING and how to do absolutely everything that can possibly on the exam. This class is very midterm and finals heavy because of how little points are in this class. I would not call this class hard if you just simply attend class and participate.
Cao Fang is a great professor, most of the assignments and tests are on the computer and she will randomly call on people from time to time for participation.

Professor Fang is easily one of the best professors ive had at Northeastern. She shows up to class every morning with so much energy and a smile on her face. She respects her students and makes the class actually fun to go to. she uses great analogys and I feel like her grading style is extremely fair. Her class is fit for real life .

Ferd is a great guy and very knowledgeable. He tries to make the lectures interesting, but unfortunately the new CS3100 curriculum is fully AI slop. Given the circumstances, I would say he handles the course pretty well but it's difficult with poor material. Course project and homework are fairly straightforward, they let you use AI to code.

Lectures are very dry but the course material isn't too hard to understand, just do the practice test posted before exams and you will do fine. The curriculum kind of sucks and ai generated but it isn't his fault

Great professor unfortunately stuck with many classes in an unorganized and AI-generated curriculum that was not designed by him. Curriculum contains too much information to fit into 50 minute lectures and labs, and it is unfair to expect Vesely to cover all of this. Despite this mess, he is very understanding and flexible to help students.

Despite what most people think, Ferd is a very genuine, smart dude who like computer science. It's a shame he got stuck teaching CS3100 for this semester because the new curriculum is an abhorrent mess and 100% AI-generated and we can tell he hates it, too. Take Ferd if he is teaching any other class than CS3100 because they need to fix that class.

Ferd is a great teacher and an expert at his field. However, progress reports has been hell as of fall 2025. Piazza is kind of a mess as well, and a hit or miss whether the teachers will respond to the questions or not. It is better to access his help during office hours or after class. Class could be boring due to the nature of the topic.

the assignments were released on Friday and the material is fully taught by Wednesday or even Thursday, which makes us rush the assignment to done by Friday evening. the exams were decent, but the level of difficulty is way harder than the practice exams. very messy and I'm guessing the people that did pass somehow used ChatGPT to succeed

Excellent lecturer, clearly an expert in topic and genuinely wants to teach you what he knows. Willing to take the time to go back and explain topics differently to make you understand. He is a funny teacher and good lecturer to a degree, can come off as boring at times. However, his class is completely disorganized. We don't know how we are doing in the class because he takes months to grade one assignment.

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but I'm giving a terrible rating because he has not returned grades in months and completes ghosts his students online. Ferd is a fun professor, I had him for another class before & it was good. CS3650 just SUCKS. Assignments 2 months ago? Not graded. OHs? TAs constantly cancel w/out updating. Piazza? No responses. please grade the homework or exma please please please please

reviews.comment: Ferd is knowledge+passionate about computer systems. I am not. He assumes too much prior skill and covers complex topics quickly that are hard to understand. somehow I feel I don't learn in lectures. he goes through some examples, but when I do the assignments I feel sort of lost. his office hours help me with the assignment. the exams are hard. i'm lucky i didn't have him for Fundies 1, 2, or OOD, i would've learned nothing if he was my professor

I don't often praise professors... he is a 5 star Systems professor. Lectures are top tier. If you can take his course, take it. Thanks!

Overall a good professor, lectures can be dry at times but he makes up for it by being helpful and very flexible when needed. The overall course was well paced though I would definitely suggest going to class to avoid being lost. Ferd is a kind and open teacher who shows care and I would definitely be willing to take a class from him again.

Super nice professor, very cooperative, and answers every question in the best way he can. Sometimes he goes very fast through topics, but overall I had a great experience with Ferd. Amazing professor.

I think CS2500 has one of the worst class structures of any classes I've taken. It's not practical and seems all over the place. Teaches irrelevant concepts. Vesely is cool but this class is pretty awful.
Good lectures, but project/assignment requirements weren't always clear, announcements varied in where they were posted, and grades took FOREVER to get back.

Very dry lecturer with a monotone delivery. Explanations are overly technical and lack empathy for students. Takes over a month to grade assignments, which is especially frustrating during finals week when assignments are still due. Not an enjoyable experience.

Professor Ferdinand has very dry lectures as other posts have mentioned. He tends to go on tangents and very frequently, homework does not have much to do with the lectures. Also, he is not very accessible outside of class, which is a problem when homework are not very detailed and riddled with vague instructions.

Very poor communication when updating assignments, withholds information about assignments for no reason, extremely boring and uninformative lectures. He and his TAs took over a month to grade most of our assignments (only a few hundred lines of code each), and offered no real feedback. He is associate for a reason.
Wasn't a huge fan. Lectures were long and dry, and he often went on tangents/got sidetracked easily. Assignments took a VERY long time to grade, sometimes almost a month.

I am currently in his CS2800 class. It is absolutely terrible. I have taken 12 classes at Northeastern University so far. This is, by far, the worst. There is no structure, no help, no preparation for anything that'll get graded, no communication between instructors and professors, etc. The bottom line is that this class is miserable as a student.

I am taking CS2800 with him, and it is his first time teaching it. He is unhelpful, there is no structure, the course website never gets updated, we use an IDE from the 1950s, and it is in ACL2, which is absolutely terrible.
Ferd is a great prof, he posts class notes 1-7 days after class which is nice but can also be annoying if he hasn't posted it.

I get what other people meant by he's wholesome since he tries being uplifting and encouraging. Lectures are basically him coding on screen how to do problems in Racket. He posts copies of his notes to Canvas which is nice. He's one of the professors though that will ask questions and wait a while for a response. Doesn't do exam reviews :\

Ferd is a very kind person and is not intimidating at all. His lectures can be a little bit boring but I think that's more cuz the class material is boring. He knows what he's talking about and you learn a lot in class. However, they take long to respond on piazza and emails sometimes.

Ferd is one of my favorite Khoury professors so far. He is passionate and caring, lots of energy during lecture, and has a good sense of humor. He did a good job at conveying lecture material and explaining concepts. Take his advice and don't code in class. Sit in the front if you can, and stick around after class if you have any questions.

CS2500 is a course taught by Vesely and Shivers together, and man it is a rough time. The syllabus with REQUIRED READINGS was updated once with week 1's readings and never again. Lectures are difficult to follow without prior knowledge from other coding or the textbook. Homeworks are difficult and tests are super important. Discouraging class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ferd is the most wholesome professor I have ever had. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He tells you on the first day of class not to code during lectures and is rightfully hard on people who do. Sit in the front row and it will be your favorite class, I promise. I wish he'd ask for our names though. 10/10 prof

He is very wholesome and kinda awkward, and wants you to succeed in his classes. Ferd tries to make the subject matter as interesting as possible. He seemed to care about giving clear and comprehensive lectures on the topics, and would go over material as needed when that didn't happen.

Ferd is one of the better professors in Khoury for me. If you're taking CS4530 you've met a fair share of professors who can't teach to save their lives but goes out of their way to be a donkey on piazza. Decent lectures and he dropped a lot of mind-bogglingly stupid requirements profs from other sessions had (public peer review), A+ in my book.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you don't sit in the front row, you won't learn anything. Vesely judges will judge you if you have stupid questions or if you try to correct him during class with the code. I learned nothing from him because he just codes in front of you as if you know already. I had to rely on lecture videos from Prof. Derbinsky (my respects to him). I would definitely never take this class with Vesely again.

As someone who had never coded before, I felt a bit neglected at times. It was a little hard to conceptually understand what was being taught. He was such a nice professor though. Really into computer science.

Although Ferd means well he ends up being a bit lacking as an instructor. His lectures are rather dry and, due to how CS2500 is structured, he has very little input in helping you fix grade-related issues. He's useful during one-on-one office hrs (only open at very specific times on Tues) to ask conceptual questions but that's about it :(.

Ferd is one of the nicest professors I've had. You can tell he is really passionate about what he is teaching and definitely knows a lot about it. He doesn't judge at all if you have stupid questions or if you get something wrong. He is also willing to admit when he makes a mistake or messes up, which is unlike some other professors I've had. 10/10

Ferd is a great professor. He has a good sense of humor and hes obviously knowledgeable. The one thing holding him back is how dull the lectures are. I wish he was a bit more engaging like some of the other professors.

Seems like a nice guy. He's always happy to answer questions during lecture, and treats the class with respect. Lectures can be a bit dull, but that seems to be more the result of the nature of the course.

Loved Ferd was an absolute treat to work with in Fall 2020 for Fundies 1. I talk to him consistently now as a Teaching Assistant and he's such a relatable and down to earth person. His lectures are quite engaging as long as you participate!

His lectures are kind of boring, but he's also a newer teacher so I don't know how familiar he is with the material. He often gets sidetracked so you most likely will need to check out the supplemental materials to truly understand it all. He isn't mean and open to answering questions and checks in with students an adequate amount.

Grad student here. Undergrads might have a different experience. He is great! He teaches extremely well. He is eloquent, and knows his stuff when asked questions - obviously he's a professor, but he understands and articulates very well. His homework is the right balance of hard and educational.
All he does at school is teaching and he's not even good at it

Perhaps one of the greatest professors I ever had the pleasure of taking a course with. He prints out notes for each lecture and walks through them with vigor and understanding. If you miss a class he's always happy to recover things for you. Bad reviews just didn't get it. You gotta live the Farhat experience
Those who are giving this guy bad reviews do not know ball. This is a professor who tries fervently to help his students understand and appreciate the field of EE.

Farhat's lectures are very engaging and explain the material well. He provides notes in-class and has office hours multiple times a week. Farhat loves to do everything on paper, including homework submissions which are due at the start of lecture. The tests are not forgiving and require you to actually understand the material.
He is very tough but everything that he says is incredibly useful. He will make you do it right.

Horrible all around - NEU please donate my tuition to one of the Youtube creators helping us get through this course. Amir assigns hideously long HW that is unrelated to course material. Frequently goes 10 minutes over class and only goes over surface level concepts. For an electronics class, why is everything submitted on paper and handwritten...

Professor Farhat is definitely the hardest professor I have ever had. While he might have been the hardest, he knows everyone can succeed if they put in the work. He taught me more than any other electrical engineering professor at Northeastern and honestly teaches at a much high caliber than most professors at this school.

reviews.comment: Assignments are not based on the book; he makes up questions that can't find any clue online or in the textbook. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.
Unnecessarily challenging, abundance of HW, tests are brutal, little help given. avoid at all costs

I took Prof. Farhat's class for EECE2412 Fundamentals of Electronics (not 2142). I was quite unsure of taking a class with him and thought that I might move to the next section. But when he started to teach you could tell that he is an incredibly experienced professor who knows the content inside and out. His tests are hard though.

Beast of a prof.

would take again
This professor is just disrespectful in general, also does not pay attention to the lab section of the class so there's a good chance a project, assignment and lab report are due in the same 3 days.

Don't take a class with him! He provides you his hand written notes and occasionally will mention something different. That something different will explode all over your midterm and final. He never answers questions directly and is VERY subjective with grading. Two people can have the same wrong answer but one person loses more points.

Very good teacher, explains everything you need to know in class.  I never used the text book because his notes had everything, prints out the notes for you. Doesn't answer your questions directly but helps lead you to the answers.

At Northeastern University, I worked with Dr. Fahrat as a TA. I had just arrived; an international student not much familiar with the university, city, english, etc, etc. I found him very helpful, clear in his talk, friendly, and easy going. I wish him best. I spotted him couple of time outside of school, he was warm and friendly.

Very good professor. He is thorough when explaining a concept. He also has a great vocabulary and uses strange words like "caveat" multiple times in one lecture. When you ask him a question, it seems like he is not answering you, because he responds so quickly to a complex question. Just listen to his answer and it will make sense. He is a genius.

Very good professor. He is thorough when explaining a concept. He also has a great vocabulary and uses strange words like "caveat" multiple times in one lecture. When you ask him a question, it seems like he is not answering you, because he responds so quickly to a complex question. Just listen to his answer and it will make sense. He is a genius.

I had heard from other students that this prof. was a good prof. for electronics class but he sucked at teaching digital logic.  he never answered any questions asked and his notes would be useful if you did not have the book otherwise his notes came straight out of the book.

He was unhelpful when asked questions, unwilling to show derivations, and expecting the students to know them for later assignments and exams.  He'll give you the entire course in notes, but he'll leave you to learn it yourself.
No Comments

Farhat has to be one of the most thorough professors for rehearsing the most bottom-level functioning of digital electronics.  I left his class with a clear understanding of the material and material from the past that I had forgotten.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Study guide solutions are wrong. When a majority of the class failed a quiz, he gave an extra credit assignment as a grade booster, BUT THEN NEVER UPDATED THE GRADEBOOK. He told us one quiz would be on two chapters and then added questions from another chapter. How he is still employed at Northeastern is beyond me.

SCHM 3310 is honestly the most boring class I've taken. The professor is unclear, doesn't follow the syllabus and makes you present just to grill you and say you're wrong. Tests are weirdly written and teaching isn't helpful at all. Would not recommend. Save yourself unless you want to suffer with a boring class for a whole semester.

Professor Huq is a great supply chain professor! You will need to put the work in to do well but it is worth it. He is extremely passionate about the material and has lots of stories to share about his time in his career. I will say, he doesn't update the syllabus so be sure to double check with him if something seems off.

Took 3310. He would constantly give us the wrong information (especially when it came to the algorithm/work problems) and then when we were completing them wrong, would try to gaslight us. He truly believes he's never wrong. Also used outdated textbook slides for his lectures, never replied to emails, and had extremely unclear grading criteria. ugh
This professor is not clear about expectations.

I took Professor Huq's morning SCHM 3310 course. A lot of his information was out of date and just flat out not right. Professor Huq also always thought he was right and could never be wrong. The tests were really weirdly written for no reason, and difficult to understand what he was actually asking. You need to participate a lot if you want an A.

I took SCHM3310 with professor Huq and the class was very enjoyable especially if your interested in transportation. The professor is very knowledgable on the topic and makes the class an engaging discussion based class. Participation is very important to your success. Group projects have a large affect on your grade so you do them well.
run! DO NOT take his class

The class content was really boring but he cared about it. Very knowledgeable in the subject. If you didn't participate he didn't like you. If you disagreed with him, he did not respect that. The simulation assignments take a long time but aren't too hard once you get the hang of it. He curves grades which is really nice. Nice guy, ok professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class online, and it was A LOT of work. Definitely not unmanageable, but probably the most time-consuming async class I have taken at Northeastern. Exams are difficult and heavily weighted (60%). The professor was easy to meet with - hosted office hours twice a week for two hours each and was willing to meet outside of those times as well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible. His solution sheet for his practice exam will have tiny tiny differences in the question itself making the answer completely different and you have to figure it out, he will not tell you. His due dates are incredibly inconsistent, he will not provide clear guidelines or rubrics, then grade very harshly. The final module also takes 6 hours

Prof. Huq was great! His lectures are interesting, and I enjoy his teaching style. If you read the textbook chapters and participate, the class is engaging, and you will do well on tests. His office hours are helpful. The simulations are time-consuming but enjoyable and a nice break from regular work. I would 100% recommend you take him!
I love Dr. Huq. He's like a father to me.
excited to teach and enjoys supply chain. If you put in any respectable level of effort in participating he will like you

HORRIBLE. I got the highest score for 3 out of the 4 exams but still get an A- because he gave me a 7/10 for my participation grade even when i went to all of his classes. Don't take him if you don't want to ruin your gpa.
Avoid if you can. Not good at all.

He is hilarious and entertaining and clearly actually passionate about the subject. The simulation modules will kill you once you get to module 6 it takes like 5 hours on your first try at least

As long as you put in the bare minimum participation wise he will lowkey love you and you'll probably do well.

Avoid at all costs!! His Canvas page is extremely hard to follow with two or three different due dates for the same assignments. My group never knew when anything was due and he would be very vague in his emails when we asked for clarification. He doesn't grade anything until the end of the semester, so all his feedback is useless.

I have never had a worse professor in life, avoid at all costs. He does not seem to care about students actually doing well in the class and he doesn't know how to teach an asynchronous course effectively. None of his content is original. He doesn't provide consistent due dates. Terrible teacher NOT a professor.

professor huq is a great person and a great professor! he is very engaging and cares about schm a lot. the drawbacks of this class are the group presentations and projects. there is no clear rubric for presentations, and the simulation is ridiculously long (it took my grp around 7 hrs!!) his grading seemed to be relative to the rest of the class

Professor Huq was not a bad professor but he also wasn't good. The class was pretty hard and I didn't think that the material was all that interesting which made it harder. The class was pretty straightforward and if you study for the tests and quizzes you'll do well. The simulation module was super long though so be prepared for that.

Dr. Huq is very knowledgeable, I learned so much in this class. The quizzes (10%) are multiple-choice and pretty difficult (I did fine with the curve). The midterm & final (25% each) also curved. They were easier than the quizzes because they were more problem-based. There is a graded simulation with unlimited attempts. Good to know stats before.

He is a harsh grader who lets you go to his office hours but doesn't explain. He says this is the answer and assumes the students know why. Exams are challenging, and everyone dislikes his teaching style because he reads off the slides. I participated and never missed a class, but still got lower than a 7/10 for participation. Avoid him SCHM2301

Lectures "require" attendance with only a 0.3 point addition to Exam 2, in which attendance is taken far too inconsistently. Lectures are unprepared and rushed. Assignments are never created timely, come out with mistakes, and submissions release late on the deadline. Professor and TAs are condescending and the class is treated as if it is a joke.

This guy decided to create a new assignment a week before the group project was due stating that It would help with the group project. When most groups had already gotten past that part of the project which was the easiest part. Also very condescending according to others, I never paid attention much to see this happen tho.
He was asked to leave his previous job at SMU for being racist btw
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the most realistic response for this class.His exams are pretty difficult I failed both despite studying a lot. For the second exam he lied about what would be on it, and he's genuinely the sassiest professor I've met. He rushes lectures ESPECIALLY the final project. The ONLY reason I passed was extra credit, and he only gives during class.
The lectures were not that great, and he often had a condescending attitude. The final project is difficult and rushed, with limited support.

Very divisive for a few reasons: he's a very knowledgable professor who (I think) cares for students. However, his general demeanor in class, while amusing at times, can be questionable and discouraging for students. Also, gives extra credit but grades harshly, and the final project is quickly paced and not well supported by class lectures.
Avoid this professor. He is very condescending and does not understand that students have other obligations and cannot always make his class their highest priority.

Dr. Fontenot is far and away my favorite professor at Northeastern. Aside from great teaching skills, he's a great human. Always available to connect outside of class and cares deeply about his students. Also, if you have the chance to apply to the dialogue he runs, 10/10 recommend. Great professor and great mentor, if you can handle a little sass.

Took this course when he taught it Spring 2025. He made sure that EVERYONE got something out of the class, whether it was through lectures or group projects. He made sure that everything came together nicely so no lecture was ever useless. Fontenot taught us important industry concepts like RAG and AWS.

Definetely one of my fav professors at Northeastern! Lectures are super engaging and as long as you pay attention in class you should be fine on homeworks and tests. Don't understand the bad rep he gets tbh the guy's hillarious
Fontenot is obnoxious and dislikeable.

Taking his class Fall of 2025 and wish I listened to the negative comments here :( only responds to questions with sass and pomp. I'm a girl, and a lot of us actually made it a point to only attend office hours as a group to get away from "Creepy ReMark"... heard a ton of things about people needing to go to the dean to get him to settle down

Hiis lectures are literally useless, spends more time reminiscing about his time in industry than the material

Final project was impossible with his rushed semester schedule

I'd avoid this professor like the plague if you don't need this class to graduate

Don't take this class if you want to learn anything, especially for resumes/co-op interview

His lectures were really clear and did a great job setting up for success on homework. You get extra credit just for showing up to class, and there are tons of ta office hours to help with the final project.

Fontenot is a great lecturer and his classes are enjoyable. You learn a lot but he's slow at grading and responding outside of class.
