This semester, he introduced the concept of 'Practicals' which were like mini projects so in total we had 4 HWs (if you submit early you get 2 bonus points), 2 practicals, 1 final project, and 1 exam. Fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hate to give him a low rating because I genuinely enjoyed his class and what we learned. But the grading is so slow. Stuff we submitted in  February still hasn't been graded and we have no idea how well we're doing throughout the class. Also very rude in class, makes students feel uncomfortable by calling them out and drawing attention to them.

Fonte is awesome. Genuinely very caring, hard working, knowledgable. If you put in effort in his class it will pay dividends. Prof is dedicated to creating new engaging assignments that go beyond the book and teach you real skills.

Project is, as he puts it, "trial by fire." I wish the last phase of the project had been released way sooner - it's very time consuming and you need to teach yourself how to do a lot of it. My low rating is due to his attitude - can be rude and very quick to anger. Almost made my entire class retake an exam due to one student's behavior.

I took this professor for a summer section of OOD. He didn't know what we learned in Fundies II and what we were supposed to learn in OOD other than Java. He spent more time making snarky comments and setting up his PowerPoints than actually teaching. The homeworks were often unrelated to or far beyond the scope of the material covered in class.
Easily the best professor at NU and if you're up in these posts complaining about him you should look inward

Funny reading all these reviews given that no one I spoke to who took his class had anything positive to say about it

The worst if you're trying to learn actual content and grow as a developer

Ditto that if you're looking for an easy A or a project you'd be proud to talk about for an interview or something

Creepy and disrespects women/minorities
Love this guy. A lot of the bad reviews are people who never come to class and then are surprised when they do poorly on projects and exams. Just come to class and you won't regret it
By far my favorite professor I've taken here. Funny and gives lots of extra credit.

Reviews are polarizing for the right reasons. 

If you want to learn, you will learn more with Fontenot than the alternatives

If you don't care, you should take someone else and leave the seat open for someone who does

Prof. Fontenot was a character to say the least; couldn't keep control of his classes and resorted to snarky comments and passive aggressiveness to get his points across. Inflexible outside of class, and spent more time mingling than teaching. Lectures left much to be desired, and projects had little in common with lecture material. Glad to be done

People think he's rude, but its just a matter of tone. If you have 1 on 1 conversation with him or go to his office hours, you'll realise its just a consequence of only talking to him in a large class setting. Lost of extra credit, and he's very knowledgable on the subject and on professional advice.

Fontenot's lectures are filled with tangents, and key concepts are rushed, especially for the final project, which relies on barely taught material. Grading is extremely lenient, with low engagement. Expect random discussions and unprofessional behavior, including singling out students in discouraging ways. If you value structure/respect, beware
professor is p unorganized. but the class is easy so its a free A. Regardless if I did not have previous knowledge coming into this class i wouldve done a lot worse.

Group project was very infuriating but Dr. Fontenot was amazing overall and doesn't deserve any low ratings. If you need one to one support, he's very helpful during his office hours. He gives tons of extra credit so just do his homework early and do well on the exams (very easy btw) and you'll be fine. Not a bad class overall

Classes are heavy, sometimes takes attendance as extra credit. If choose cs3200, make sure to find reliable team members, start the final project earlier! First hw for ds4300 is difficult: write the logic for binary search tree in python and run it. If you meet problems just go to his office and ask him. Final project need you go to every classes!

Dr. Fontenot is a fantastic professor. Teaches content well and is very accessible outside of class. His TAs are helpful too. He gives soooo much extra credit and is a lenient grader. Databases is an easy A. Personality-wise, he is funny and witty, but sometimes his sarcasm is kinda condescending (although usually warranted). Highly recommend

My fav course this fall since I actually looked forward to coming and hearing his funny observations about us. Every few lectures he'll ask us to write names on paper for extra credit. hw keeps getting posted too close to the deadline so that's a bit stressful. Definitely form groupchats early on to bounce questions off each other

The class content is very learnable, but he expects you to self-teach during the 2nd half of the semester. 6 easy HWs, 2 exams, 1 big final project. Final project uses Python. He is pretty disorganized, which affects the quality of the class. Most of the HWs were posted very late. The TAs are, truthfully, unapproachable and snarky.

Professor Fontenot clearly cares about his students and wants to prepare us for the real world. However, while the material is good and the class has a reasonable difficulties, the TAs and in some ways the Professor are rude and condescending. When questions are asked, TAs will just respond with snarky remarks, trying to assert their power.

I dont have anything to say about his humor like others. His class is hard, 2 exams, VERY lengthy project, and the TA's are literally no help and will only reply in sarcastic comments or make u feel like shit for asking questions online. Its not clear what the exams cover and the slides are only 60% of prep. Overall pretty restrictive teacher.

His class is extremely easy, teaches like he assumes everyone is learning for the first time. Extra credit just for showing up to class (amazing). Has a lot of office hours. +10 essentially to all exams (2). Very sarcastic but only to those who truly do not care about his class at all. Pay attention, just show up to class, easy A, nice guy

A lot of criticism is unfair. The final project scope is a little broad given what the class covers, but it forces you to learn. Decent lecturer and in-class problems are helpful for homeworks and exams. Also many extra credit opportunities. He can be sarcastic, but calling him rude is a stretch.

I've never taken CS classes before college, and I've often felt intimidated, but not in this class. He creates such an entertaining atmosphere (if you can take a joke...which based off the reviews people can't). He explains concepts clearly, and doesn't make assumptions on what people already know. He will call out students who obvi don't gaf

Too much hate. He isn't rude, he is sarcastic and dry that is his sense of humor. If he ever believes someone is hurt, he talks to them after class. If you can't take a joke don't take his class. He explains concepts clearly and isn't afraid to go over simpler concepts to make sure everyone understands them. He is available via slack. fav cs class!

Maybe I'm insensitive, but anytime he snaps back at students or makes comments that sometimes people take the wrong way, he is very obviously joking. I don't understand these bad reviews. I get that he is a pretty tough grader, so I honestly think most reviews reflect that and not how he is as a person. He wants us to do well and is always helpful.

Fontenot gives you extra credit for showing up to class. Show up and do the world and you'll be fine. He is extremely sarcastic, but he's a nice guy who cares about your success. He adds extra office hours to make sure that he is always available to students, and responds to slack messages quickly.

He is amazing! Very caring and takes time before and after class to help students debug issues with their homework, as well as holds many office hours. Gives a lot of extra credit and it should be simple to get an A in if you do well on the tests. Homework is sometimes long but are definitely doable in the time span. One big group project.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His teaching skills are bad, I'd rather go study on my own than go to his class... He doesn't have clear guidance for projects and when you're trying to reach out on Slack his efficiency's terrible.

I get that students either love or hate Fontenot, and to me, his jokes are pretty mean and doesn't really care about his students. He barely answers questions from students on forums and rarely posts solutions to his answers. I can't remember a single thing from the lecture. One good thing is that he has a bunch of extra credit opportunities.

I can see why Dr. Fontenot is a little polarizing on this page. Some students find his snapbacks funny and laugh it off with him but some students perceive them as condescending. 

The course material itself is great and the end-of-semester project is a great combo of real-world tools that are key for anybody who wants to do literally anything inCS

Mark Fontenot is genuinely the worst teacher at Khoury. He is rude and constantly belittles his students. He insults them on slack and in class, and his teaching skills are incredibly subpar. He reads off of powerpoints and doesn't cover material remotely related to the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Super understanding! love him

Whilst this class was very time intensive, as long as you attended lectures and reviewed materials from labs, everything was very doable. Additionally, I found Fontenot's lectures very engaging and easy to follow.

OOD was challenging, but it was definitely doable.  The projects took a lot of time to complete and were related to lectures.  Some of these other ratings sound like upset students who didn't want to actually do the work.  If you want to have a challenging but doable experience, take this prof.

Professor Fontenot was honestly a pretty good teacher. He is clearly very knowledgable about java and computer science in general. I liked his assignments and projects, and the tas in the class were always available to help people. Despite this, I generally just do not like the guy. He ignored my emails and messages, and just was not respectful.

No doubt about his knowledge of Java but I think he couldn't convey it to the students. The overwhelming amount of things due(which he later realized about) meant that we had something to submit every day which was OK at first. Then it turns out that I am basically not learning much in lecture that I would use for the PA/HW.

I learned more about OOD outside of this class than I did during his lectures or doing his PAs. He covers the basics, but his demeanor in class is so unfriendly that his sense of humor just doesn't make up for it. He yells at students during class for not paying attention, which is really disruptive for the students that are actually trying to.

Professor Fontenot is very understanding and caring. He can come off as snarky or irritable, but he's genuinely a nice guy who is knowledgeable and funny. Assignments are difficult, but interesting. His lecturing and slides often contained little info & felt under-prepared. Learning how to do the assignments taught me more than the lectures did.

Mr Mark fontentot is very knowledgeable about the things he teaches but seemingly does so begrudgingly. He is good at teaching students new concepts but only a small portion of the concepts he covers are helpful in completing the assessments. These factors in tandem with the course's difficulty led me to drop the class.

Compared to all of the other CS classes I have taken thus far at Northeastern, OOD with Fontenot was by far the best. Despite the fact that this course was condensed over Summer I, I felt like I learned the most. Fontenot clearly cared about his students and was there for us every step of the way.

I took Fontenot's CS3200, then CS3500 over the summer. Long story short, everyone complaining should understand that they took a 4 credit course over the summer.. and I personally learned SO MUCH from Fontenot and feel much more real-life equipped now than before. He brought the theoretical concepts we learned in Fundies 2 to more applicable things

classes were prety much useless. He came in 10 min late, read slides, and ended class 30 min early. Too much material that should've been covered in class wasn't covered at all or crammed into labs that dind't explain things clearly. But the PAs were not too long and did cover a lot of content (15 h on average).
I would be a husk of a human without my acquired knowledge of SOLID principles.

he came into OOD without understanding what cs students have learned in fundies 1 & 2. He expects students to pull all nighters every week. Taking this class is like taking 8 credits. The projects aren't spread out in a reasonable manner. He expects you to have knowledge of algo. The written exams expect you to have full knowledge of code.

Mark Fontenot demonstrates expertise in the subject but has an off-putting attitude, making learning difficult. He offers minimal guidance on projects and provides delayed feedback on assignments. Communication is sparse and undermines student confidence. Taking the course with another professor would be a wiser choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mark Fontenot's demeanor is a huge disadvantage. Despite his expertise, he's unresponsive, scoffs at questions, and brushes off concerns. Steer clear if you can and save yourself the frustration caused by his discouraging attitude. Wish I never had to suffer through his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is actually a good teacher, but not very good with people. Everyone focuses too much on his personality and overlooks his impressive teaching ability. You can tell from his course materials and website that he puts a lot of effort into them and is very passionate about what he teaches. I believe he's underrated

Avoid Mark Fontenot at all costs. He's rude, unhelpful, and fails to create a productive learning environment. Asks for feedback but retaliates when given. Lectures are useless and assignments unclear. Took CS3200 for learning, left with pure disappointment.

Mark Fontenot is, by far, the worst professor I've had. His lectures are a mess, and he's extremely rude to students who ask questions. Don't expect any help from him. Unbearable arrogance and a complete lack of empathy make for a terrible learning experience. Avoid CS3500 with him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mark Fontenot is a frustrating professor to deal with. Despite CS3500 being an easy class, he's really condescending while answering questions, making whole learning process extremely difficult. His rudeness destroys class morale. Do yourself a favor and pick another prof if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mark Fontenot is the WORST CS3200 professor ever. He's always delaying assignments, changing grading rubrics without telling us, and breaking promises. It feels like he's purposely making our lives difficult. The class is a nightmare because of him. Avoid at all costs!
Great professor, although flexible, a bit messy when it comes to assignment structure and sticking to dates which can cause a bit of stress.

Dr. Fontenot is a really personable guy and I loved getting to know him this semester. The course material is important but he makes it really easy to learn it with his lecturing style. He also teaches you a lot of practical knowledge and breaks it down into small chunks so you never feel overwhelmed. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

If you can take this course with another professor, consider your other options. Dr. Fontenot is very knowledgable, but is difficult to work with. He is dismissive and passive-aggressive, as well as incredibly resistant to feedback. His attitude creates a negative learning environment that in turn makes the class a negative experience.

I took a course with him last semester and unfortunately, I cannot recommend this professor. While they are undoubtedly knowledgeable in their field, their lecture style was a hindrance to my learning experience.

The professor had a tendency to go off on tangents.
I would never take his class again.

He was not a very helpful professor. He barely answered any questions, especially towards the end of the semester, so we were left with very little direction on our final project (which was not very well explained and haphazardly put together anyway). We never even received grades for half of our things by the end lol.

Highly recommend taking professor Fontenot for Database Design. I learned a lot of practical knowledge in his class, and he cares a great deal about his students. If you take the time to really learn the material, an A is more than attainable.
Tough but fair
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Charvet's tests and grading are tougher than average. Negative reviews probably from students not putting any effort and expecting to coast anyways. CLosed book and expects you to know most of the material. Fair teacher, knows a lot and uses real-life examples.
Worst professor ever!! Never take già class! Very hard-graded. Hates every international student
I was interested in Supply Chain before taking this class...Worst Professor I ever had! DO NOT TAKE HIM!

Worst Professor EVER! Doesn't want to give full credit (always finds some lame excuses to not give 100%), and the only way you can get a good grade is by memorizing his incredibly boring slides. Quizzes are hard and final exam is comprehensive. DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!

If you expect an easy A, don't take this class. Don't expect to get 100% for particiation just by being in the class. My experience have been great with Prof. Charvet. His class actually prepared me for the real world. When you get out of school, don't expect much hand holding by your managers.
Hard hard hard class. Hard grader, boring and way too much HW. So much reading every day and crazy about participation. Got D for participation for attend every class, and speak out once per class.

Worst professor in the supply chain dept.  takes the subject of transportation and makes it even more unbearable.  assigns way too much reading for each class and online book is difficult to read.  professor simply does not know how to teach effectively.  Slides are confusing and tests are hard.  Class is much harder than it should be.
I was very interested in Supplychain management before I took this class. He should learn how to teach.

His tests are extremely difficult.  Assigned a simulation to do every week, before he taught us the principles behind it.  Does not speak clear and is very hard to understand.  Must read and try very hard to do well in the class.

Professor Ferris is great, take her especially if you care about understanding the actual material (like if you need to take the MCAT). She has lots of practice problems and practice tests that are graded on completion to pad your grade a little. No extra credit, curving, or bumping grades. Cumulative final, hw due daily but it's low stakes.
Chuddd.......

Orgo 1 and 2 are very difficult classes and she covers a lot of subjects super quickly in order to fit them in. If you pay attention in class and do the homework carefully you'll understand the material. She tests very fairly and will explicitly tell you what will be on exams, also her office hours are super helpful.

She is an amazing professor. She really wants the best for every student. Yes her class is hard but orgo is hard in general. You need to put the work in, in order to do well in orgo in general. She is super nice and wants every student to succeed. Please take her and enjoy her class.

All the negative reviews are just from people who did bad in her class. Organic Chemistry is a hard class and is known as a weed out class for a reason. Her practice exams are very similar to the exams and there is a decent amount of practice. Her tests are pretty hard but fair for the content of organic chemistry. She cares and is accessible.
Retaking this class with a different professor and its going so much better AVOID
She's really good at explaining the material in a digestible way. Even though OChem is a hard class, if you put in the work for her class it really pays off.
Ferris provides way too many materials rather than focusing on a single textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are really good and make a lot of sense. Very accessible outside of class with office hours and TA's hosting recitation sessions. Biggest recommendation is finding worksheets online from other teachers and practicing those cause the aktiv PS are not at all like the tests. Orgo is bad no matter who u take it with.

Exams are impossible difficulty our averages for them were very low. Everyone who says we didn't dedicate enough be for real we have other classes that are also difficult I studied for week and half earlier and still did bad.Most of the class  ended with Cs. Other Ochem profs classes had retakes, extra credit, curves and ended with better grades.

Grace Ferris is one of the few Orgo professors who actually wants you to learn the material and do well. Is Orgo hard? Yes, it's a weed out class. But she provides extensive resources to understand the material and truly understand the class.

Very difficult class because she just expects so much compared to the other professors but if you are able to keep up you will leave her course set up so well for further classes. She's very funny/personable and I don't think she deserves the hate she's got on here recently but I will say she isn't super understanding when the class gets hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ferris was amazing. She made organic chemistry easier than gen chem. Her lecture slides make it so easy to follow and understand the material. All you need to do is read her slides and do the exam exactly how she does in her examples and you'll get an A.

If you wish to have no life,24/7crash outs,live in Snell,no final exam practice,75%of your grade based on 4 exams that look like nothing like the lectures that you sit in everyday, NO EXTRA CREDIT, HW ARE EZ BUT TESTS 20x HARDER, STUDY GUIDES ARE FIGURE IT OUT YOURSELF, “ORGO IS MEANT TO BE HARD” SO SHE CAN SCREW U EVEN FURTHER W NO REMORSE OR HELP
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very over-hatted professor. Orgo is supposed to be very hard and other professors are easier and offer extra credit, but this shouldn't warrant bad reviews for Grace. She is an incredible lecturer and cares how the student absorb the material. If you go to class and study hard, it is very rewarding.

Professor Ferris is really nice and clearly feels passionate about ORGO. That being said, her grading criteria makes it crucial for you to spend a significant amount of time studying for you to do well. It is possible to get an A in the class it's just really really hard. However, this does make sure you really understand the material.

She explains tough concepts well and is always available for help. She's the sweetest and genuinely wants us to succeed. However, textbook/Aktiv problems are not like how she writes them, but that is the primary resource we have for practice. My biggest piece of advice is to study EVERY day. You cannot get by with only studying the week of an exam.

This class is difficult, but its orgo. While it would be nice if she were to allow a test retake, give extra credit, or add fluff to the grade -she really knows how to teach this class. She knows what she is talking about and wants students to understand all the concepts. Her office hours are so helpful and she gives to many resources for studying.

If you want a good grade, don't take her. If you want to actually learn the material then take her. Orgo is generally a tough class and it's unfair that she doesn't give extra credit or test retakes, however if you actually put in the effort and understand how to study then you can do decent in exams but it's really hard to get an A in this class.

Worst class I have ever taken in my life. Such a sweet woman but that's all she is. The homework assigned is so time consuming and irrelevant to the assigned lectures. The midterms are insanely hard and the practice tests she provides are almost nothing like the actual exams. The final was agonizing. Select a better section if you can.

She is such a sweet person, but save yourself. Not generous at all when it comes to exams, they are very difficult and she gives no EC, corrections, or curves. Class averages were usually in the 60-70 range with no curve.
Literally never again. So unhelpful shows no care if you do bad and wtf was the final.
She gives us practice exams which is a benefit but gave us no clarity or guidance on whats on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very nice professor and has very clear and engaging lectures. Homework is helpful to solidify topics but is time consuming. The only negative is her exams are VERY difficult and you really have to dedicate a lot of time.

Grace is tough; this is true. If you're looking for an easy class to coast by, do not take her. If you truly want to understand the concepts and feel confident in your abilities, then she is the best possible. Her lectures are clear, and she gives many examples and practice problems. Put in the work, and her class will be rewarding.

I loved Professor Grace! She's a breath of fresh air. Orgo is tough, but she makes it manageable. Go to office hours and stay on top of the work, and the class is very doable. Her tests are fair, but you need to show up and put in effort. I truly gained a mentor. Don't wait until the last week to study! All-nighters will not work for orgo! TAKE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It starts out great. Then it just gets worse. She's so kind and truly does seem to care about the success of her students, but her tests and grading are impossible. The homework progressively gets harder and harder until it will take HOURS. The tests are completely incomparable to all in class work and homework. Lectures are great, but don't help.

Grace is a very kind person who is clearly passionate about organic chemistry. Her lectures style, practice exams, and Aktiv in-class questions made it seem like exams would be a breeze. Until you find out everything that you thought would be on the exam isn't on it at all and you realize you wasted hours studying to basically fail.
Her lectures are fine, but her exams and homework are awful.
do not take her.
Literally everyone is lying I study for 20 hours like a part time job and still fail.

Grace is an amazing teacher and is one of the best lecturers in chemistry. Her practice exams are exactly like her actual exams. I personally am doing well and learning so much. Compared to other orgo teachers at this school she is amazing. If you are someone who actually wants to put in work you will do well in this class. Disregard cruel reviews.

Everyone who is on here being disrespectful needs a reality check. Just because you cant study doesn't mean the professor is bad. Orgo 1 is meant to be hard. There are chances to improve grade with attendance, homework and practice tests. There are also many outside of class opportunities to get help. If you don't have the time to study dont take.

ok yes she is a good prof when it comes to explaining but her exams are just too hard and unrealistic unless you're just cracked. When I asked her for some advice and comfort, all she said was to review study guide and rest. REST??? I am always at snell and still can't do well. There's so much covered on the exam and not enough time.
You will cry a lot and your gpa will go down. Test grading is insane. No curve. No extra credit.

Lectures are pretty engaging; her way of explaining things was pretty intuitive for me. Pleasant and understanding if you have an issue during office hours. The material is really difficult, but she has it set up in a pretty digestible way. Just be ready to spend a lot of time outside of class on review and practice.

POV im at snell for DAYS on end, stomach grumbling, tired asf, nothing in front of me except my hope and dreams and my ipad obvi. Study sessions are 10+ hours. You take the exam feeling alright, tears in your eyes though. Then it gets graded and you failed. Ya i know this will probs happen to u (sorry) so dont take her class, unless u r cracked..

This professor has given me nothing in life. When I think of life, I immediately think about my life before this class and how much better it was. Mind you this professor went from a 4.1 to a 2.7. I want to change my major because of her. I think my life expectancy just insanely dropped because of this lady because THIS CLASS TOOOK YEARS OFF LIFE.

Beware. If you even want a chance of getting anything above a B- do not take this prof. She grades extremely harshly and does not ever consider another opinion, especially during regrading. She makes up her own "rubric" or criteria for what she wants because of her superiority complex. You will not touch an A in her class, and lots of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I got well above average in class 100% in the other categories, and still don't have an A. Other teachers at least curve!!no test corrections, no ability to move up a grade. Study for about an entire week before exams still dont do as well as id like. Doesnt regrades even when I wrote the same thing as the answer key, at least give me one point.

This teacher has a very unfair curriculum with no curve, extra credit, and abhorrent grading. She genuinely grades so hard and expects us to read her mind on tests. Other teachers offer curves and extra credit, I know people in other sections of Orgo 1 that have 100. How is that fair? It's not. I studied 30 hours and did not do as well as I wanted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This review is for Organic Chemistry 1. The grade breakdown is that almost the entire grade is dependent on the exam grades (3 Exams, 1 Final), with around 10% from other work. If you are struggling with the content, she offers NO opportunity to improve your grade (make-up exams, notecards), which can make it hard to pass the class. Never again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grace Ferris is a great person and I appreciate her humor. However, I spend 2 weeks studying for her exams and still don't do that well. Her lecture slides and homework problems are so much easier than the exams. Every single other Orgo teacher gives some sort of grade redemption except for her so keep that in mind when you're picking classes.

2311:  Studied for more than a week and still  did bad every exam. Other ochem professor offers something to help curves, notecards, exam corrections but she gives absolutely nothing. She just reads slides and shows ridiculously easy examples nothing like the exams. Homework is long and brutal, the textbook is useless, and office hours don't help.
Chopped cheddar cheese
changed my major in the middle of lecture. i think that speaks for itself.
I literally purposely stopped in front of the T while walking to class in hopes i wouldnt make it
just run far away

I have shown up to every lecture, I went to office hours, took extra notes from the lectures, and I would still NEVER take this class with her. She reads off the lectures, which you can do at home. The homework is always 40+ questions, and the practice exams never reflect the actual. RUN. I would rather retake Physics 2 than Orgo with HER.

Great professor. I definitely would recommend taking her for Ogro 1 and 2. She wants you to succeed. Orgo is hard to begin with so do not blame the professor blame yourself if you are not putting in enough work. Do the homework, do some practice problems and you will be fine.

I would rather walk through the fiery pits of hell than walk into her lecture. She's a nice professor, sure, but probably the worst professor in ALL of my eons. I never see my home, my family, my life because I'm consumed by orgo. If you can LITERALLY take any other professor, do it. Because if not. ALL of the life in your eyes will become drained.

Please NEVER take her. I never see my home anymore and i am constantly at snell because of this lady. This makes my life 10 times harder and she does not do corrections or retakes so actually makes me want to give up. If you like crying and being miserable take her, but if you like life, don't.

Teaches by literally reading off a lecture for an hour and 40 minutes and expects all students to fully understand everything. Tests are nothing compared to what we do in class and my class averaged 67 and 70 for the first exams. SHE DOES NOT CURVE, GIVE RETAKES, OR ANY EXTRA CREDIT ANYONE WHO SAYS SHE DOES IT LYING. God awful teacher don't take

Grace Ferris is an angel that actually made gen chem as well as orgo concepts make sense, it is not an easy class but she explains the material clearly and in depth. I got a C- in gen chem but am doing well in orgo thanks to her. GO TO CLASS. If you miss even one you will have a VERY hard time. If you work hard you will definitely succeed.

One of the best science professors I have ever had. Lectures were easy to follow along, and she explained concepts and reactions incredibly well. Not much homework, but exams were somewhat difficult. Spend a few minutes each day outside of class rewriting reactions and going over her slides before exams, and an A is very doable. Exam redo is nice.

I loved having Grace as a professor so much! She really cares about her students, and teaches in a way where you really get to understand the material. Her class may be slightly harder to get an A in compared to other ORGO profs, but if you really want to learn the material, taking her class is the way to go. 100% recommend her, best ORGO prof imo
One of the best science professors I've had. She truly explains material well, and her lectures are easy to follow. Exams are not easy, but if you devote time to studying, an A is very achievable.
great teacher but wouldnt round up my grade 0.2% to bring me to the next letter grade.

I absolutely adore this woman. It's obvious that she actually cares about her students and genuinely wants them to do well. I really liked her lectures, her slides were very organized, and she explained things really well. I went to her office hours every week just to absorb knowledge because she was so welcoming and inviting and such good vibes.

Grace is such a great teacher! Super nice and breaks down concepts very well especially if you go to her office hours. Took me after the first exam to get used to her style of exams, but there are no surprises everything covered in lectures is what she tests you on. At the end of the semester you can also retake an exam which helped me a lot
She is a great professor, and honestly should teach every chem class. However, her exams are very specific and challenging. She does provide good buffers tho.

I LOVED Grace. She was a great lecturer and made the material easier to understand. Her PowerPoints and annotations were very helpful. While her tests were hard, she did cover all the material in class but sometimes focused on smaller parts that weren't emphasized in class. Very funny and made the class enjoyable. Would definitely take her again!

Homework/lecture is super easy. Tests are not. Tests are sometimes worded strangely and have topics barely touched upon in class. But, her exam redo policy is very generous and can only help your grade, so A's and B's are very attainable.

Professor Ferris was a really great professor for organic chemistry. Her tests were tough but if you prepare and work hard throughout the semester you can do well. She makes an effort to get to know all her students and even has an exam redo policy where you can retake one exam at the end of the semester

Super easy class. Provides comprehensive reviews of the topics/problems that will be presented on each exam. Only 2 exams and a noncomprehensive final. One group case study that he gives more than enough time for. Worst part is sitting through boring lectures and rants every class. HW due every week. Bad Prof but easy class, take him.
Super nice super chill teacher. Class is just yapping so might not learn much but the class itself is very simple and easy to learn/understand. HWs are simple, and exams are easy. underrated prof

This guy is extremely difficult, if you have the option to avoid his class, I would. He spends most of his time discussing his history with general electric and osramslovania along with his kids accomplishments. He rarely responds to emails, gaslights any confrontation of an error, and doesn't teach or care about how his students are doing. Avoid!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I wish I could take an exam on his life because he talks about it for 80% of the class time. Very picky about how he wants things done, specifically with the Excel assignments. The subject itself is not difficult at all compared to financial accounting. The exams are relatively easy and straightforward.

Easy A, the hardest part is sitting through class. He's a chill guy but just talks SO much. I somehow made it to every single class and we usually got out early, he's a caring and good guy, but doesn't know his audience. Must but Mcgraw hill. Almost all serious due dates were flexible. Final exam study guide didn't really help.

super easy class but such a boring professor. if you can drag yourself out of bed and sit through his life stories to get the attendance points, it's the easiest accounting class you'll ever take. beware that all assignments are on mcgraw hill, so you'll need to pay for that. but otherwise such an easy class

The practice tests and study guides helped a lot. Got sick once, emailed him about it, he ignored it, and dropped my attendance grade even though I literally couldn't get out of bed. Honestly talks more about his life than accounting. I basically know his whole life story that I didn't ask for, because he tends to ramble a lot during classes.

Professor Glencross truly loves accounting and cares about his students. He tells you what to study to help prepare for exams, is pretty understanding, and is available outside of class. The cons are that his class sometimes lacks engagement, and he doesn't provide many extra resources/practice questions other than the textbook and slides.

He was a super chill professor and was pretty flexible when things came up for students. He moved a midterm and was super accommodating for students that had already made plans. His lectures felt a little long sometimes, but he's a nice guy and I learned a lot in his class.

He is a very nice guy but his lectures don't really help with exams. For quizzes he does let you know what's going to be on it which is helpful. The average for the last quiz was so bad that he had to drop it the average was around 40%. Overall, he is a nice guy but not a good professor.

Professor Glencross is passionate about accounting and loves to talk about his work experience/life advice. Weekly assignments and group project are easy good grades. He tells you questions on every exam (including final), but lots of the material is self taught and many test questions are not straight forward. Lots of work put in outside class.
absolutely terrible. he does not know how to teach and thinks his students care about his family's accomplishment. i dont care! can u pls teach

I don't see why glencross doesn't have a higher rating on here. For all quizzes/exams he tells you exactly what to study for each question, minimizing study time. Weekly homeworks aren't hard. Gives out bonus points throughout the semester for the final. Lectures get repetitive but he's j a sweet old man. J show up to class & study what he says

This professor is mean forget about sick days or even wellness days if your not there even one time your grade will go down. The homework is honestly not bad but the test and quizzes were difficult. Overall not the hardest class ever if you are willing to put the work in but he was just not a good professor.

Glencross is boring and talks so much without any of the information he says being important.He doesn't even review the slides he's presenting before class, and spends more time talking about his son's accomplishments than accounting.I survived his class by self studying everything before the test.Don't take this class if your goal is to stay awake

Not a hard professor, but does repeat the same personal anecdotes over and over again throughout the year. He's passionate about what he teaches, but doesn't know how to structure his lectures very well. Relies heavily on the slides and usually ends up repeating them back to you, so just take notes on what is posted online and you'll be fine.

He is a very nice guy, but does not know how to teach. He spends the entire class telling personal anecdotes and attempts to connect them to the lecture but it does not work. He repeats the same stories over and over all semester and barely teaches you how to do the actual material.

Glencross may be a bit eccentric in his lectures, but he gets the point across. For each of the exams, he provides a study guide as well as goes through the content that will be covered. This was extremely helpful in preparing for exams. He hosts office hours 3-4 times per week, and you can always get your questions answered. Definitely take him!

Yes, his lectures are not super engaging, but he gives out GREAT study guides (basically the exam). He does not deserve a 2.8 rating. He is pretty boring, but you will learn a decent amount and get a good grade. Take this class for an A. It's accounting, no professor's lectures are interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very boring professor, not difficult but spends the entirety of class rambling about irrelevant  life stories and advice. Didn't learn much from this course, but not hard to do well.
No comment.

This was my second time taking Financial Accounting. he is WHY I PASSED! Thank you so much Dr. Glencross... He taught so well and easy to understand. He didn't move on until everyone got it and he kept lectures interesting. Great guy.

His lectures are boring at times, and he does talk about his personal life stories a lot. His class isn't difficult if you put in some slight work though, and he's an extremely fair grader who really does want to help his students out.

Dr. Glencross is my fav prof. The last few reviews had to be written by the same dude... He relays life stories and talks about his personal life, without fail. But it did not take up a majority of classes. We spent most time clarifying back and forth with the Prof. He wouldn't move on unless we got it. Will tell you what's on the exams!

Avoid Professor Glencross's financial accounting class at all costs. His teaching is appalling, with nearly all discussions focused on his USELESS "life stories" &  achievements rather than the actual course. The class's performance throughout the semester was abysmal.

AVOID Professor Glencross's financial accounting class. He's a poor teacher, focusing mainly on his son's achievements, not the actual course material. The class final average was a dismal 67, with some test exam scores as low as a paltry 37. I got a C+ in the class, my lowest Northeastern grade. Professor Glencross should be fired immediately.

DO NOT RECOMMEND!!! worst accounting class ever. going to class felt pointless, never taught during lectures, only shared life stories (the same ones throughout the whole semester). felt extremely unprepared for the final had to teach myself. northeastern needs to get rid of this guy.. HE CAN'T TEACH!!!  and i never wanna look at accounting again.

Lectures consist of 60% monotonic speaking, 20% completely irrelevant, gibberish personal stories (such as how his son got a job [nobody cares dude]), and 10% pithy life lessons that can be deduced by a middle schooler. The best thing Northeastern can do is fire this guy as he is doing a disservice to his students.

I took his ACCT1201 class. The guy is a former shoe salesman (so he has said), which should tell you all you need to know. He's a nice guy (sometimes) but teaching is not about being nice, it's about educating your students. At that he is a complete failure.

Professor Glencross was a terrible professor and I'm so glad I will never have to take his class again. Super boring and the material is very tedious. This class is made worse due to the fact that everything we learned how to do is now done on a computer so the material is outdated. I hated this class and prof Glencross is not a good teacher at all

Lots of stories but always cover what we have to! Most application learning can only be done through homework anyways. Spoon-feeds exam content as much as possible and provides so much information on grades and expectations. Lectures are fine, it's a boring subject but he makes it enjoyable! Won't move on until you get it. Very sensible and sweet!

Prof. Glencross does care about his student's success, but he simply reads his slides instead of explaining what the slide is trying to convey. He brings up examples from his own days as an accountant that lead to other tangents about his own experiences instead of the concepts we need to learn. Learn by doing the homework and textbook problems.

Prof Glencross is one of my favorite prods. a sweet man with the best of intentions for his students. you can tell he wants us to learn, not just from the textbook/lectures, but also from his experiences. he strays from the class material, but the only way to really grasp accounting is by practicing anyway. plus keeps us awake from boring material!

Glencross is nice but his lectures are about 60% him talking about his career in accounting, 30% him telling a story he told last class but forgot, and 10% teaching the material. His tests are quite easy throughout but the final is made by the department head and you will know nothing because of his non teaching style. Prepare to teach yourself.

He is a very nice and organized professor who cares about his field and the material he teaches. Sometimes he can go off on tangents, but his stories are entertaining and we always remain well on schedule. He hopes that we all become future accountants.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Glencross is very caring and easy to talk to. I always felt comfortable in his class and he always wanted the best for his students. Lectures can be boring and the class requires a lot of studying but having him as a professor made the class more enjoyable. He is super nice and respects his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor does not teach very effectively. Class time wasn't very efficient as he tended to read off his presentation slides and repeat the same stories of his life as an accountant. He seems very knowledgeable about accounting but is not great at teaching the material. I learned more from self-studying on Youtube than from his lectures.

He doesn't really teach you how to do the actual maths in accounting but is more focused on theory so you'll have to teach yourself. He also tends to go off-topic by repeatedly talking about his experiences. However, he is very kind and wants his students to pass. There is a lot of homework but it is very helpful when it comes to exams.

ACCT 6200 - He's just great. I want to retake his class just for the stories about Sylvania, GE, and his current AP consulting project - hilarious. Do the HW.. He's extremely reasonable and he wants his students to succeed in understanding the way financial statements flow - he's not interested in making you memorize useless accounting jargon.

Prof Glencross is definitely a little old school but he's very kind. He makes his own study guides so the exams were very doable and the homework's easy. Tells a lot of personal stories but still covers everything he needs to in lecture. He made accounting bearable.

The guy is super outdated in every aspect in his life. Incredibly boring and inapplicable, goes on about the same stories from his life over and over again. Homework is alright, but will not curve any grades. We had a 60% mean for an exam and he just does not care if it is hard or not.
Nice guy but assigns A TON of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Really nice guy but he spends entire class telling stories of his experiences. Long winded stories that are somewhat relevant only because he was an accountant. Heavy use of power point, each slide he would tell a story. I had to do a lot of learning on my own because we couldn't get to relevant material. Not necessarily a tough teacher though
Because, He explains the topic with the examples which is easily understandable and also he is very much friendly
Super easy grader, but he has no idea what he's talking about. Drones on and on about his work experience, which is almost entirely unrelated to the subject matter.

took cost accounting with Mr. Glencross.  he relies on power point a lot, but did an overall fair job compared to others at NEU who use power-point as a brain substitute.   you can tell he enjoys teaching and is not just coming to class to earn his tenure.  if he lectured he'd have been that much better because i think he really knows his stuff.

generally a sweet guy who genuinely cares how you do. your biggest advantage is studying outside of class, lectures can not be helpful at times. its lecture after lecture after lecture which can be draining. tests are few and far between but if you didnt study it will show, just study and youll be good
He provides a lot of materials to work on so just make sure you use them. He posts lecture recordings after each lesson so you don't need to go to every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great professor; I wish he taught higher-level Bio classes so I could take another class with him. Great mix of keeping lectures interesting without going off topic, and he is very accessible during office hours. Lectures are entirely recorded and attendance is not graded. Pay attention during class and you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy class, fair, and worth taking over the other professor.
The sweetest, most caring professor. He still reaches out and wants to keep in touch with his old students.

Dr. G's class has been one of my favorites! Classes are lecture heavy, but they are really engaging and he structures them in a way that is easy to understand and pick up (they are also recorded, which is helpful). He gives you so many resources to do well in his exams (do the practice problems he makes!). Definitely recommend taking him.

He does a great job of making difficult concepts a more digestible. Lectures are recorded and not mandatory but going helps a lot. You can tell that he wants you to do well, but you have to put in the effort. Exams are entirely multiple choice, which I found to be tough. But, he replaces your lowest midterm score with your final grade which helps

Dr. G was an incredible professor; he presented information in a way that made sense and gave plenty of practice material that reflected the questions well. Questions could be a bit conveluded some times but if you put time into practice they shouldnt trip you up. He was very passionate about the subject and I reccomend attending each lecture.

Brilliant lecturer. MC tests can be a little wordy and tricky at times, but college-level readers should be prepped for them. Practice quizzes and lecture slides provides everything you need for the exams. All lectures are recorded. Useful review lectures prior to every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grabiner was a good professor -- he's very passionate about what he teaches and he knows a lot about it. Attendance is not mandatory he records every lecture. However, his tests are difficult and for those who don't know how to study the material will struggle -- it's mostly memorization. If you're willing to put the work in, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: straight As till i met this guy. his tests are weighted heavily, very few mcq with multiple options, u can't even learn from ur mistakes cuz hes a paranoid delusionist so u get to look at the exam 10 feet away on his computer screen (2q limit) i studied my heart out rewatching his lectures word-word and still his tests were confusing and very wordy

I didn't really have any interactions with him, but he has a very lecture heavy class. His tests felt more like reading comprehension questions and would be worded strangely. Very exam heavy, make sure to do the quizzes he assigned over and over again to get the hang of how he likes to work questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unengaged and rude. Take another professor for BIOL 2301.

I'm gonna be so honest, I just didn't like him. He clearly has no desire to be teaching, is rude and condescending to students who simply ask questions, and majorly overcomplicates simple concepts. His exams were wordy and often focused heavily on concepts only mentioned briefly in lecture. Exams are also very few questions and 85% of your grade.
Good Teacher…just make sure to really understand the topics

I would avoid him if you can. His lectures are very tedious. No matter what, you will have to go back to the lecture slides, and it still won't have everything you need for his exam. I don't recommend going to his office hours; he is very condescending and doesn't help at all. If you don't understand the way he teaches it, you will fail.

85% of your grade is exams. He does drop the lowest exam but I would spend hours studying and still just do mediocre. He talks super fast but records lectures so you can go back. He gives a good amount of practice I just wish wasnt so exam heavy. You also don't ever see your full exam! Good prof and nice guy just a rough if your're a bad test taker

He's a good but not a great professor imo. Great organization and resources on canvas, exams are on paper but you def have to put in a good amount of studying for them. Quizzes are online and he gives a lot of practice problems which really helps. If you put in the work you'll do well in his class.
Your entire grade depends on the exams, but honestly just go to the lectures, take good notes and you'll be fine. He's a great lecturer!

He records lectures but tests are difficult like A B C AorC or All of the above (application based), little room for error since tests are 85% of ur grade. To see mistakes u have to go to office hours where he pulls up the question on his computer (2 questions limit) so u never learn from ur mistakes or even look at the test. Avoid for ur sanity
If you dont look over your notes you will drown in his class. I suggest taking the other professor and try to avoid him if possible.

grabiner was honestly one of the best professors ive had so far in college
he's quite chill and his exams aren't the hardest imo as long as you study the lecture slides and lectures themselves (which he records if you don't want to go to class since attendance isn't mandatory) you're pretty much guaranteed at least an A or A- 
big enjoyer of him :D

Prof Grabiner is a good lecturer and gives plenty of outside help if needed. Class is very test-heavy; grades are based on 4 unit exams and a final. There are a few online quizzes, too, but they're not worth much of your grade. It is attainable to do well if you just start studying for exams early and use the practice problems.
Classic lecture style class. Questions are tests are very reasonable, and if you pay attention in class, you should be able to get a good grade. No homework aside from quizzes that you can retake
Awesome professor. his tests can be a little challenging, but overall they are fair.  You will be fine as long as you do the practice quizzes, go over the slides, and the practice questions.

I was very intimidated for this class, but Dr. Grabiner was an amazing professor. He reinvigorated my love for cell biology and explained complex topics in a very digestible way. The lectures are very well structured and everything you need to know is covered. He is available outside of class and always willing to help. BEST Genetics Prof by far!

Professor Grabiner was great at explaining concepts, which made it really easy to understand the content. He was really fair with grading, and the exams never had any curveballs. I was able to do well in the class because he was very clear in teaching the content as well as outlining expectations.

GOATED Professor, Really cares about the class and about students. He tries his best to help students to get the best grades. Attendance is not mandatory and lowkey is not really necessary because all you need to know is going to be on slides. All exam questions are based on slides material, you don't need anything else to do well in class.

Really great teacher and provides all the material for you to succeed in the class. Tests are 85% of your grade (mcq based) and 15% review quizzes (3 attempts). Would've been perfect but some of his mcq were really tricky and 2 answers could have possibly worked. If u want an A, you need to master the material and work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: grabiner is super approachable and makes lectures engaging and easy to understand. go to class and study for tests and you will do just fine!!
Goated teach DrG. Take him and don't cram the day before the tests study well in advance to make it easier for urself. Hes funny and sassy which makes the class even better.
Very caring teacher, does a good job tying biology into the real world.

Dr. G is one of the most passionate professors I've had at Northeastern. He's soso caring about the wellbeing of his students and honestly just wants people to learn. He has 8 online quizzes throughout the semester, but you have 3 attempts on each and they're honestly super helpful for learning and making sure you're on track. Tests are super fair.

I really like Dr. G, but it is not easy to get an A. You really have to put in the work to do well since the 4 unit exams are worth over 50% of your grade and have around 35 questions each. I really recommend doing the practice questions he offers if you want to do well!

This class is NOT an easy A. There are some tricky mcq on the exams and you definitely need to know the material in and out to do well in the class. Attendance is not required, lectures are recorded. Prof Grabiner is a great professor, and he gives you all the material you need to succeed..but you have to put in the work. 4 exams, final replaces 1
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Professor Grabiner during my first semester at Northeastern and would highly recommend him to anyone who is taking Gen Bio! At first, I was a bit nervous to talk to him, but he's a really nice guy and wants you to succeed! He posts lots of practice material for every chapter leading up to an exam, so go to office hours and do those!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor G was great. The only thing to be worried about if you take him for bio1111 is that you are graded on very few things; 4 exams, 1 final, and some online quizzes. I'm very glad I took this class with him!
Best professor I had first semester without a doubt. His styling of teaching and his practice tests genuinely made me LEARN the material. He cares about his students a lot!!

Tests are super easy, all of the questions come from the lecture slides. To get less than an A in the class you have to try and do bad on the tests/not study at all. Lectures are recorded but are generally very dense and wordy. Overall this is basically high school bio, and an A is achievable by just reading through the lecture slides.

Grabiner posts all of the recordings online. I didn't go to lectures much because of timing, but I listened to the recordings, took notes on the slides, and retook the weekly quizzes to prepare for exams. There were really no surprises. All MCQ exams are very reasonable. Grabiner is a cool dude!

10/10 would recommend! There's four unit exams and one cumulative final exam. He gives study guides out in advanced so you know what to expect on the exam. My advice: Go to class and preemptively study for exams using the study guides - to get an A you really do need to understand what is being taught.

Grabiner was a wonderful lecturer. taking notes and studying a reasonable amount will get you a very decent grade. He is also a very nice person and is very easy to talk to, I highly recommend going to talk to him if you don't get a concpet

He's a pretty good teacher. Grades are based mostly on exams so be prepared for that. Your lowest exam grade can be replaced by the cumulative exam at the end of the year. Quizzes have 3 attempts, so you're guaranteed a 100%. He does a review before each exam which is super helpful. Finals was a back-to-back Unit 4 exam and a cumulative portion.

His exams are poorly worded and there are very few questions on each exam, so you need to do perfect to get an A. The lowest exam gets dropped. During finals week he assigned an essay, a unit 4 exam, and a final back-to-back so it Was hard to study for everything. I think the other teacher is better bc he has online exams.

Dr. Grabiner is a brilliant lecturer who provides many practice problems, but his exams are extremely challenging and heavily weighted. Even dedicated students often struggle, and one bad exam can ruin your grade. Don't be fooled by reviews claiming it's easy; those are likely from exceptional test takers. Be prepared for a tough course.

He's a very good professor but make sure to take notes on what he says and not just the slides, because a lot of the exam is based off what he says. Also, the exams are multiple choice, and they are not very difficult as long as u study the material well and go over practice questions and quizzes!

Lecures were extremely helpful and slides provided most of the information needed for the exams. Exam 1 and 2 were quite manageable, but it progressively gets harder with exam 3 & 4 being quite difficult. He is just strict about his policies which is sometimes disappointing and annoying especially if you have an unforeseen circumstance.

Professor Grabiner is very nice and approachable. The class does not require attendance and the lectures are all posted online after class. Grading consists of online quizzes and exams so it is test heavy, but the tests are all multiple choice and not too difficult. If you take time for studying for exams and taking good notes you'll be all good!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was nervous to take biology but Professor Grabiner made it super comprehensible!! His lectures are dense, but he records them so you can go back and listen/watch them. Attendance is not mandatory. If you take notes on the lectures and put in the time to understand the content, you will do great on the exams (which are not particularly difficult).

He has engaging and detailed lectures with just enough dad jokes and good opportunities for participation. He includes practice questions for every section, and the answers can be found easily in his slide decks. The only outside assignments aside from self-studying are quizzes which you have the option to take multiple times.
One of the best professors I've had at Northeastern.

The lecture is very helpful. He is very caring. He inspires students to do research or at least keep in touch with new things happen in biological world. Very great professor and person. Definitely recommended.

For Dr.G's class, you definitely gotta know the content inside out. He can be very sassy but aside from that, he is awesome. Lectures are clear, informative and recorded. His tests are all MCQ and 85% of your grade. Just rewatch lectures and study everything under the sun, and you'll be good.

Dr. G is definitely very passionate about biology and it shows. He is very eager to answer questions during lectures, and his slideshows are very well-made. He gives some practice questions that you can use to review the material, and his lectures are also recorded which is nice to go back for studying. His tests and quizzes are also very fair!
Prof Grabiner was great he always was very transparent about test content and provided a lot of practice
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are very well organized and delivered. He always makes time to thoughtfully answer students' questions. All homework and exams are multiple choice. If you study the practice problems and quizzes you'll be golden. Easy A.

Dr. G is great!! He is pretty chill, but sometimes the lectures become a bit of a drag because it is a ton of information. Nonetheless, he is very good at explaining things and giving lots of practice and tips for success. Plus, he records all of his lectures! His quizzes are open-note and are really great practice for the tests. Would recommend!
You will learn a lot in his class. Everything you need to know is in his lecture slides. Organized well and relatively easy if you stay on top of the material.

He is a very smart, and knowledgeable person, and he teaches pretty good. His classes are just lectures with good slides. Overall, he is good. His quizzes are helpful for studying, but he doesn't post enough practice problems. I found I had to find extra practice online.

Dr. G was easily one of the best science teachers I've ever had. His lectures are easy to follow and accessible online. Your grade is based almost solely on tests (the quizzes don't count for much comparatively), but if you actually pay attention, participate, and study, the tests themselves really aren't difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Grabiner is very knowledgable and passionate about the topic. His slides were very helpful and the lectures were clear and helped a lot. exams are difficult but fair. lowest exam grade gets replaced by the final if your final grade exam grade is higher and lowest quiz gets dropped. I would definitely recommend taking him for bio.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wow. One of the best professors I've ever had at Northeastern. I am not great at science, and this class was hard for me. However, he is easily accessible and makes his content as easy to digest as possible. Don't underestimate the difficulty of the exams + put in the work to truly succeed. He is so passionate about biology + a really kind person.

Dr. Grabiner is hands down the best professor I have ever had. Not only is he super passionate about biology, but he is also so good at delivering hard information in a clear and understandable way. If you put in the time to study and take his practice quizzes, you will see the effort pay off in your grades. Office hours help a lot!

Class is well organized. He has the slides and lecture recording posted for you to look back over. He also posts practice versions of all the quizzes which are extremely helpful when studying for the exams. The tests are all multiple choice which is nice but they are also not very long so there is little room for error.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was an excellent teacher. His lectures were always very thorough, so make sure to show up to those. The majority of your grade comes from 5 exams (including the final) that are spaced out through the year. As long as you are going to his lectures and doing the practice problems he assigns for (optional) homework, you should be completely fine.

Really great class taught by a very passionate and well-spoken professor. Each quiz gets 3 attempts (keeps highest score), and then your lowest test score is replaced by the finals grade (if you do better). I recommend doing practice problems and using Quizlet (use study guides as template for Quizlet) to prepare for exams.

Dr. G was an ok professor. Despite the exams being multiple choice they were a little difficult in terms of the wording. I was left second guessing a lot. With that being said the exams make up 85% of your grade and quizzes are 15%. I felt like it was hard to get an A in the class because of how exams are weighted. Was helpful to rewatch lectures.

This was honestly one of the easiest class I have ever taken. There isn't a lot of work besides from attending lecture (which isn't mandatory), taking quizzes (he drops the lowest), and taking unit exams (he replaces your lowest with your final exam grade if your final exam grade is higher). Just attend the lectures, take notes, and you're all set.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you take him he is not the worst option. If you don't go to class or office hours you won't understand what's going on unless you have a strong background in Biology. Other professors do exam corrections, he doesn't so it kind of screws you if you are a bad exam taker. He has a lot of office hours so its really what you put into the class.

His lectures are concise and well put together - provides structure for notes. Exams can be deceivingly easy, but not too difficult to get a good grade. No homework or outside content for this portion of Gen Bio.

Great professor! Gives us clear and concise information, is great at answering questions, has a good sense of humor, and gives us opportunities for discussion in class. Posts his lectures online so you can go back and rewrite your notes just because it is a pretty dense class information-wise. Recommend him over and over for genetics!

Dr.G is a great lecturer and does a good job of breaking down complex concepts. This class is not lecture-heavy and is more of a Socratic seminar. Be prepared to work on your public speaking skills because you will have to do (casual) presentations. class conversations and well as peer presentations are great preparation for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: real good. grade is mainly determined by exams, but they are all multiple choice with fair questions. attendance is not mandatory so you could honestly pass by just reviewing all the lecture recordings on your own time (not recommended but still possible). all around, a solid professor and a manageable course.

This class is a great class. Anyone interested in Biology, I highly recommend take really any class with this professor. Not only is he good at answering questions, the class is of a reasonable difficulty and all tests are multiple choices. Participation is helpful, and I highly recommend asking questions. I'm not sure why he has bad reviews, 10/10

reviews.comment: Grabiner is a great professor who gets the class involved in discussion about the papers. The inquiries section I took with him is on the ubiquitin proteasome pathway. Coming out of it I have a significantly greater understanding of the pathway, along with increased ability to read scientific literature and knowledge about the process of science.

Dr. Grabiner is a great professor. He is really nice and accessible outside of class. His lectures can be a little boring but he clearly covers all the information necessary for exams. All the exams were straightforward and reflected the material taught in the lectures. Definitely recommend taking him for genetics!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Honestly I was shocked that his rating was so low. He's a pretty great lecturer. I don't do much studying, but I did attend and take notes every lecture.

Exams are all mc, there are online quizzes each week (3 attempts allowed so almost guaranteed 100)

If you show up and pay attention I think you'll do fine. I'm glad I had this prof.

Good professor! Gives all the materials and support you need to succeed and do well in class. Cares about students grades and will help you out if you need it. Shows a genuine care that students are actually learning and is clearly passionate about teaching.

He's a chill professor and is willing to re-explain concepts to you if you don't understand. The material was easy, but his lectures were kind of boring so I ended up falling asleep a lot and had to rewatch the recordings. The only work outside of class are the quizzes which are easy. Overall, you'll get a good grade if you study.

reviews.comment: He was a solid professor and definitely has a love for the subject. Overall grade was primarily determined by 3 midterms and a final, but one midterm grade gets dropped. Only criticisms are that his presentations are pretty vague and the practice material for the midterms are not really thorough. But lectures are recorded for you to rewatch.

I didn't attend a single lecture and still got an A. The tests were so easy, the content was basically taken straight from the class lectures, which were all posted online. Just watch the lectures the day before a test, take notes, and you'll be fine. Everything was super straightforward, and Prof. Grabiner explains the course material really well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought Dr. G was a great lecturer, they were very engaging. But his exams were extremely difficult, and we were not given the exams back ever. The only study material he gave were broad overall gist questions, but they did not help prepare for the questions on the exam. If exams were fair, the class would be great.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems like a good prof, very knowledgable and everything on the tests is in the lectures. There are weekly online quizzes, but the grade was mostly made up of 3 midterms and a final. Requires a lot of studying outside of class.

His exams were about 30 questions each and filled with unfair, confusing and difficult questions. Questions were correct because he said so. He would just tell us to study more. He does
not even hand back exams and gives very broad feedback via gradescope. Plus exams make up most of our grade. Although he is very dedicated and explains things well.

Prof G's lectures are very good and you do not need to read any textbook to study or learn material for his exams (all MC). Weekly online quizzes to boost your grade + one midterm grade is dropped if you do bad. All lectures are recorded so attendance isn't required but being there definitely helps understanding. You can tell he cares about biology

I'd say he's pretty much okay. He does grade by a few things (3 midterms, final, and quizzes). Quizzes were easy but counted for a small percentage of your grade. As for the midterms, I suggest using his study guides he provides and rewatching his recorded lectures. One bad grade on the midterm can take a toll on your grade so beware and do well.
This class was really easy as long as you reviewed the slides before the tests. The tests were pretty much entirely based off the slides and if you knew those, the tests were easy. All mc tests.

Professor Grabiner was amazing at lecturing! The class was straightforward and based on assessments. The quizzes were online with multiple attempts, but the exams were in person and not very difficult at all. If you come to class, or watch the lectures on zoom, take notes, and do the study guides he provides you should be able to succeed.

He is a good professor, he is very lecture heavy, but you do not have to attend class because they are posted, yet it is recommended. I took him for BIO 1, but this course was the only option to write a review under. Overall, good class only thing that's frustrating is your grade is completely 10% take-home quizzes, 60% midterms, 30% final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved his class! He's a really good teacher and knows the material inside out. I took Genetics with him and thank God I had him and not one of the other professors. reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures were over complicated and under explained. Took AP stats in high school and somehow that did not help at all. Homeworks come from textbook but he rarely teaches straight from the textbook. He likes to teach his own way, use own definitions, and his own examples. Textbook will not help you at all for his self-written tests and quizzes.

The whole class was a mess. He expected us to know STATA without teaching it. He overcomplicated the math while repeatedly getting the problems wrong. Then for the tests he would tell us exactly what was on it, because no one knew the material, then he would forget a part and we'd get points off because of it. Overall, nice guy, bad professor.
good professor
had him for econ online over the summer. very engaging course for it being asynchronous.

Prof Roy is great for any class. He is very clear on what will be on the exam so you don't waste precious study time. You'll be pleased with a semester with Roy.

Prof. Roy is awesome. His econometrics lectures were more than bearable at 8am, he was a very fair grader, and there wasn't a ton of homework. Most of the course & grade is based around a research paper that is spread throughout the semester. If you end up with Roy, you will be happy. He knows his stuff.
