reviews.comment: Professor Hertz is awesome! He is super enthusiastic about the material and the projects. Everyone I talk to absolutely loves him. I learned a ton in his course and the course-load was fast-paced but manageable. He even helped me outside of class with a side project I was working on with the skills I learned in the class.

A great professor and an even better guy. Extremely caring and organized - every single assignment is planned out to a tee. I feel like I learned a lot more in Cornerstone than a lot of my friends in this department who had other professors.

Amazing teacher who truly likes to teach and is good at it. he is very willing to help and i highly recommend going to office hours. compared to another cornerstone teacher, i think he does give a bit more homework, but i'd say the class is worth it because you learn a bunch of cool stuff

Professor Hertz is amazing. He has a warm aura about him and is always willing to give good feedback or extra help. Definitely recommend taking his Cornerstone classes as they're really fun with his lectures. He gives a weekly assignment, which is never too hard but is very relevant for future engineering co-ops/internships and other classes.

Hertz has been the best professor I've had so far at Northeastern. Admittedly, if you have previous experience with basic level engineering, this class can be a bit easy or boring at times. But his projects are fun and engaging, and he is really great at making each student feel comfortable at engineering.

Professor Hertz is amazing, he is an interesting teacher and is really good at answering questions in class. While attendance isn't graded it is really important to go to class to learn the information you will need to finish homework assignments that are a big part of your grade. Overall Hertz is a great prof. who really cares about students.

Made an account just to rate Prof. Hertz because he is just that amazing. Breaks down fundamental engineering concepts very well. The weekly homework is interesting and challenging, especially if you do the extended work options. Exams are very easy, and the projects for both semesters were a blast. Cares about all his students and is just amazing.
At the begginning of the year I was failing. LOVED HIM!

Joshua Hertz is one of the best professors Ive ever had. He somehow manages to condense course information so that it is presented in a way that is both interesting and extremely easy to understand. You only have to know whats actually important. Incredibly understanding and down to earth guy, exemplifying great care for his students. Learned ALOT
Best first year professor

Professor Hertz is one of the best professor's you'll ever have. He cares about his students and conducts the course with passion. Comes off a little quirky at first but by the end of the course he's a blast. Could not recommend him enough. His class is also project based, while focusing on fundamentals. Would take again in a heartbeat

Dr. Hertz is just all around an awesome guy. He's always happy and enthusiastic to teach, and makes the lectures engaging and fun. The coursework revolves around multiple different topics, (usually multiple per class), and can sometimes feel overwhelming. But Hertz is around after class and active on the online discussion board for any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: My absolutely favorite professor; he teaches material in a very understandable way and he is incredibly personable and respectful. The class is fun and if you do the work/grind through the group projects you will get an A.
This guy almost has a 5.0 rating for a reason. He's AWESOME and so nice. I wish all my professors were like him. He actually makes the class fun.
I've been with Hertz for a semester and he is the best. Definitely better than all the other options.

Two years later, I still use Professor Hertz as my standard for professors at Northeastern University. He is a pioneer in education and treats you as an equal. He doesn't just teach, he gives you the confidence you need to bring your own ideas to life. Glad to see that other students are having as great an experience as I did.

Hertz is a fantastic teacher. His lectures are organized and feel relevant. As a teacher he's relaxed, funny, but provides a lot of chances for extra challenges. He takes pride in his students and the work they do and is always willing to help out.
Easily my favorite professor. He's clear, helpful, and genuinely cares about your learning. Hertz is more than just a great professor, he's a great person.

Hands down my favorite professor. He's clear, NICE, and caring. He makes this my favorite class. Probably the best Cornerstone instructor. I got lucky getting him as a professor. He also makes the class very laid-back and not stressful but we learn a lot!

By far the best professor I had my Freshman year. Not only is he an extremely adept and intelligent teacher, but also just a great, relaxed person. He really focuses on his students being challenged and learning, rather than the grades. If you have the chance, you'd be missing out by not taking a class with him!

Best professor ever! Really helped you understand what engineering is about and made you feel inspired to work hard. He focuses on learning and not grades, and that is exactly what college should be like.

Hertz is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. He not only is a very likable, fun and quirky guy, but also great at explaining difficult concepts and willing to help you out. His lectures are generally pretty fun and he adds to them with his good personality. Homework and workload isn't too bad either. Overall, great guy, great prof.
love this guy. great prof.

Hertz is a great professor but an ever greater guy. If you take his class, you'll see that he isn't teaching because its his job but because he genuinely wants to see his students succeed. He is very approachable and helpful when you need it. Very fair grader and great at teaching how to code, use AutoCAD, etc

Hertz is not only a great guy, but a great teacher as well. He teaches you everything that you'd need to know for tests, quizzes, etc, and always is happy to help you out when you struggle. He's super nice, always responds to emails, and is available to help you a lot too. He may have hard material sometimes but it's definitely manageable.

Challenging course, at least for me, but I learned a lot. Prof. Hertz is definitely one of the best professors I have had at Northeastern. I learned a lot about programming, having no prior experience. Very reasonable grader, and really willing to help you succeed. Wish I could take more classes with him.
Prof. Hertz demands quite a lot of work consistently, but it's definitely worth it because it's work that you benefit from. His classes are fun and informative.

Hertz is a really thoughtful professor who truly cares about his students and their learning.  Although his lectures can be a little boring sometimes, they are a great time to catch up on homework in his class.  His homework includes memos which aren't super fun but aren't terrible.  Overall he just wants you to succeed so he'll be there for you.

Prof. Hertz was my favorite teacher this year. Not only did I actually enjoy his class, but he really cares about his students learning and it shows. I am super pumped he is teaching my class next semester as well. I wasn't really into engineering yet and I had no experience with coding or any design software he was great teaching it!

Professor Hertz is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He, unlike most others, really cares about the students. We took frequent surveys for him, where he asked how we thought the class and his teaching was going. He challenged us, and was a very fair grader. I learned a lot about coding through his class. I definitely recommend him as a prof

Great teacher. Knows a lot about the topic, but lectures can get a bit dry. The class becomes a bit hard, so it's very up to you to teach yourself a bit of coding. Huge payoff, though - you come out knowing so much more about how to code than other GE1111 students.
FREE A, that's all you gotta know, he loves rambeling on lectures, and they are somewhat interesting, but his tests are easy, and you are basically guaranteed a free A.

Professor Livanis is super knowledgeable and passionate about the topic. He makes you think about global politics from a new perspective, but be prepared to hear about Greece a lot, even when it isn't too relevant. You take three pop quizzes in class, and the lowest grade of those is dropped. Assignments are engaging. He is great!

So incredibly kind and wants to see you succeed!! Though, lectures may ramble off topic sometimes, he will always make sure you get what you need to do well. Also incredibly accessible outside class and will take time to walk you through assignments/concepts. Cannot stress how kind he is.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I really genuinely like the man, however, it must be said that he is very out of touch with his students to think that anyone is paying attention in his boring lectures. I wish I actually learned something for the time/money spent, but was an easy A... 

Also don't bother reading past the 3 basic theories of you have any common knowledge.

Just a great guy overall! Take his class if you want an easy A + interesting lectures. They're not very engaging as he tends to wonder off and ramble about Greece, but if you lock in they're like a nice podcast. No extra credit, but he is very generous with grading; as long as you do the bare minimum there's no way you get anything under 90%.

Hes fabulous—intelligent, compassionate, organized yet laid-back. Very Greek, so brush up on your Greek history. The clss is chill, but he yap in lectures. Grades are attendance (not mandatory), weekly posts, a take-home midterm/final. With IR/POLS background, you can skim readings, but talk to him after class. He's awesome; I'd take him again.

Ioannis is very passionate about international relations, so he has great points, and you learn a lot from his course and he's sweet and a nice guy. His class is very lecture-heavy, so he gets carried away a lot, but the assignments we have are useful, and I did learn from his class. He is also willing to listen and wants everyone to do well!
His lectures can be a bit boring and long; he likes to yap a lot and go on tangents. But, I would say overall I enjoyed his course. It wasn't challenging, and it was sometimes fun to hear him yap

Big talker and rambler. Very knowledgeable and smart. You can ask him basically anything about the political and economic state of the world right now and he will have an answer. Didnt learn much tho beacuse I would always get bored. There is no class engagement so its easy to drift. Get ready to write a lot every week.

First of all, great guy and super sweet -- reminds me of a golden retriever. I didnt learn that much in this class mainly because it's almost impossible to stay engaged during the lectures. The class is genuinely all lecture, and sometimes it just feels like foreverrrr unless you are incredibly interested. The HW is reading HEAVY, and online tests

Super great professor! He truly cares about his students. His lectures can be long, but you can tell he is super passionate about the topic and he knows a lot. Definitely talk to him outside of class if you want to learn more. He is easy to meet with outside of class! Great professor, I'd recommend.

Prof. Livanis is a very nice teacher who is passionate about IR. He gives 3 pop quizzes throughout the semester, drops the lowest score. He also randomly takes attendance, but other than that the class is very straightforward. He is caring and is always available to help students. There are a lot of papers, but you will learn a lot. Great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Livanis is very caring and accessible, and willing to work with you. He doesn't take attendance. You will have a homework assignment per week. There's two tests. Professor Livanis is a boring lecturer, but he is a nice guy and sometimes pretty funny.

Prof. Livanis gets off topic sometimes but is extremely knowledgeable about IR and is an interesting perspective to learn from.  Very caring and reasonable man, just communicate with him and you'll be fine.  Show up to class though- he doesn't grade attendance but he certainly notices when someone's not there.

Dr. Livanis is very personable with his students and cares a lot for them. He will put your mental and physical health before any grade. Also a great guy to sit down and have a conversation with! Recommend 100%

Great professor, it's evident he's very well versed in IR and current happenings. His passion for the subject helps keep students interested. He's easily distracted but on the more lenient side of grading. Although attendance is not mandatory he gives 3 pop quizzes (dropping the lowest grade). Overall great class and would definitely recommend it!

Livanis is a good professor and I learned a lot from his course as he connects lectures to current and historical examples but sometimes gets lost in his own thoughts. There are 2 big papers and 2 take home exams. He was helpful in office hours for the papers and the textbook is very useful for the take home exams! Solid class and fair grader!

Professor Livanis is a really interesting guy who gives great lectures, but his class isn't super structured. If you're type A, be prepared to let go, and trust that you know the material well enough to write the papers and take the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This teacher relies on only lectures and dozes off most of the time when teaching, he usually is never on topic and has interesting slides but boring lectures. He is extremely passionate towards international affairs. Easy class if you do assignments, overall easy A, but not if you actually want to learn about the topic.

lectures are just him ranting on and on but a very sweet person

as long as you put a little bit of work into your assignment then you get an A+

grades: research assignments (mini essays 300 words) and two exams (take home--24 hr window)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ioannis is great. He's super kind and willing to help you out with anything outside of class. Easy grader and you just have to complete weekly discussion posts. His lectures are boring but the course content itself is sometimes interesting.

Professor Livanis is a good guy but his lectures feel super long at times. The homework isn't overly difficult. It is a weekly discussion post usually due Tuesday and a response to a classmates post due the following day. Midterm and final were both take home essay questions. They took a long time to do but he grades them very fairly. Easy overall.

He is a great professor and I learned a lot from him. However, he sometimes gets lost in what he is saying, so paying a lot of attention is important. I enjoyed his class and the topics he taught a lot!

Prof Livanis is great and knows his stuff. Always has (tangentially related) anecdotes about Greece, which are always fun to hear. His lectures take up most of the class time, but there are some group discussions. I wanted to go to class, even though it wasn't required. Has some homework due on non-class days, so make sure you know what's due when.

This class was a breeze to take. If more than half the class showed up, no attendance. Midterm and final were take home w unlimited time. Very lecture heavy, but interesting for the most part. The reactions every week are easy if you read the guidelines. Very fair grader. He also gives lower grade textbook in syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Livanis has good lectures, but they can drag on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He definitely lectures a lot, and tends to get off topic, but he's aware of it and will try to catch himself when it happens. His class was really fun though, and it's very informative. He's an easy grader and will try to help you if you don't understand something.

Very lecture heavy and reading the textbook definitely helps. Such an easy grader!!! Get 100% on most of the work just by writing something that kind of makes sense. He also does make the material easily understandable in his lectures but READ THE TEXTBOOK because there's a lot more information.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: OMG HANDS DOWN ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS AT NORTHEASTERN. What a gem! If you had the chance to take his class, do not miss it! He is such a nice and relaxed professor and super smart! Definitely would love him if you communicate with him after class or when you need help. I personally would love to take his class again. Exam grades are important.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I thought taking his class was such a bad choice at the beginning because he tends to speak in a monotonic way with his greek accent. Lecture so heavy that students barely have chance to participate and it makes students sleepy. Midterm takes the biggest chunk of the overall grade and it is HARD and LONG. However he does provide help + INTELLIGENT

Livanis is very relaxed. He gets his material across and is a lenient grader, and instructs his TAs to be so as well. Very accessible by email, and willing to meet with you and help you out if you need it. Tends to go off on tangents but does catch himself eventually. Would for sure take a class with him again.

Really enjoyed the class! He clearly knows his stuff and grades very forgiving. You're likely to get full credit if you're simply pointed in the right direction. The readings are helpful, but not particularly necessary. I learned a lot and had a great time. The pop quizzes are easy, but they're true pop quizzes, so be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Regret taking this class it was an utter waste of time. Livanis rambles on and on about material that doesn't pertain to what he's teaching and the lectures are extremely hard to stay awake in. He gives 5 pop quizzes a semester and doesn't tell you when.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Excellent professor, knowledgeable, conscientious and willing to work with you outside of class! He practically helped me write my papers!

Heads up Intl affairs majors - if you took POLS 1160, this class is THE SAME THING! Prof Livanis is clearly passionate about intl affairs but goes off on ridiculous tangents that don't make a whole lot of sense. Made class hard to pay attention to. You dont need the textbook it was a waste of money. Tests and essays where easy & straightforward.

A lot of reading, although not all necessary to read in depth, some will be tested in exams. 2 papers and 2 exams (mid-term and final). His accent is quite strong so listening to him for 1hr40 can make it hard to concentrate and understand everything. Can be funny and picks on foreigners to get a perspective from non-americans. Easy A though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Livannis is a fine prof. His lectures aren't particularly interesting and he often goes on tangents. Class grade is based off of 2 exams (20% each), 2 quizzes (3 total but he drops 1, 10% total), 2 papers (12.5% each), 3 newspaper reports (5% each), and participation (mostly in recitation, 10%). Class meets 2 days/wk and recitation meets 1 day/wk
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a great person and as long as you go to lecture, you'll get an easy A. There are two experience assignments that are fairly easy to get an A on. For the midterm and final, you just have to memorize the definitions that he has on the powerpoints and you'll do fine. The pop quizzes are guaranteed 5/5 as long as you show up for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: class was interesting, lectures were a bit long at times. the two papers are so easy to get an A on. two tests are relatively easy.

Livanis is a great guy, he's super personable and has a dry sense of humor. INTL1101 was an easy class; I skipped once a week and ended up with an A. Just pay attention to his lectures, especially keywords. The midterm and final were easy, just memorization, I never opened the book. He's willing to help out in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Livanis is a funny professor. He tries to make each class as fun as he can. 2 papers are due through the semester, and 3 newspaper reports. These are generally easy and do not require that much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Livanis is a great professor. He is easy and does not try and trick students. He lays out clear criteria and makes it easy for you to follow it. He cares about his students but can be arrogant sometimes. Overall, he knows the stuff REALLY well and provides many examples. Expect a lot of examples about Greece. Easy A.

Very clear about expectations and if you follow his directions on tests & quizzes ,the class will be rewarding and you will get an A, lectures are sometimes off topic and a lot of the things he says are not on the exam but READ THE BOOK because thats the material he will test you on. Participation in recitation matters. TA grades everything

I REALLY enjoyed this class. I thought although his accent can be difficult to understand sometimes, this professor is incredibly knowledgeable and really wants the students to understand and be inspired by the concepts. You have to read a lot, but (pop) quizzes were simple and lectures were very helpful. Doesn't really take attendance, but go.

I was confused by his Greek accent at first too, it only got more clear to me after the spring break, but he is a funny and easy-going guy. His grading is clear and it's relatively easy to get a good grade on exams or papers. Him always talking about Greece is interesting but sometimes very annoying.

Wore the same thing every day which was amusing. His lectures were sort of interesting for IR, he talked about Greece like 80% of the time though and it was pretty disorganized. Fairly easy A though and the class isn't unbearable. Very nice man and there to help if you need it for sure. Recommend for a good grade that's not overly boring.

Professor Livanis is amazing; he is funny and often gives a much needed break from lecture with an interesting tangent about his homeland, Greece. Exams and papers are very straightforward, and you always know what to expect. I would recommend his classes to anyone and cannot wait to take his class again.
It's an interesting class and Livanis really knows what he's talking about so it's such a pleasure to listen to his lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll want to attend class.

Great professor and great class. It really changed my view on multiple issues in an easy/open way. He does not force opinions like most and his take is fresh and open to discussion (this helped the most). Take this class with him!
He was a sweet guy and funny but so much work! and he's a tough grader I did not do as well as I thought Diane Horn is a much better teacher and easier
Pretty confusing lectures but he seems to know his stuff. Anyone that has taken him will know his favorite catchphrase... "Am i making any sense?" Enjoy!
He is great, very helpful and has super easy tests and quizzes. Also he is an easy grader, you tend to learn a lot about Greece in his class

He puts all the slides online, but you need to attend classes because he tests you on things he talks about. At first the Greek accent is daunting and may seem hard to understand, but it is actually nice listening to long lectures. I would take his class again!!

He weeds out the lazy students in the beginning with the long syllabus, but in reality he is wicked nice and funny. Stay on top of the reading, show up for class and the class will be great. He has two exams that are self-explanatory, five short quizzes, and two short experience papers. Take the time to get to know him, he's a really good guy.
One of the best. Get to know this man. Rocks a black polo like no other.
I really enjoyed Professor Livanis' class. He makes funny jokes and makes IR seem interesting. I would definitely take another course with him.

shes sweet yes, but i think she fails to recognize she is TEACHING, not explaining concepts to people just as educated as her. terms are not broken down, you get LOTS of info thrown at you without a lot of reinforcement. claude will become your best friend. take that how you wish.

Ingemi is a great professor, even if her lectures can be a bit dry at times. Tests are open note and not too bad, and she will go over everything in-depth at office hours. Easy points from discussion boards and extra credit at the end of the semester. Very manageable class if you pay attention, and lectures are recorded in case you don't.

Dr. Ingemi is super nice and very knowledgeable. I would recommend her for any course neuroscience/biology related. Her lectures are SUPER dense but she records them. She does Poll Everywhere in class so you have to attend lectures. Her tests are online but she makes them really tricky. There's a lot of content in this class but she's great

Very nice woman, but her teaching style does not work for me (and probably many others). Lectures are dense, and she talks extremely slowly to the point where it's impossible to stay engaged. Very hard to take notes and slides were unhelpful. However, the exams are all online, so everyone does very well.

Professor Ingemi is a great professor. Class is pretty easy to do well in, exams are online and there are lots of extra credit opportunities. She obviously cares a lot about her students and is very open to accommodations when needed. Makes jokes in lectures and is generally very chill. Attendance is based on pollev and she drops 2 classes worth.
The materials is super overwhelming. You will learn A LOT in this class.
I love her. She genuinely loves what she is teaching. Although exams tend to have trickier questions, as long as you pay attention in class, you will do well. I 100% recommend taking her.

Dr. Ingemi is a great professor who's really passionate about the course material. While a lot of the content is dense, she does a great job at explaining important concepts and is always open to answering questions. Also, quizzes and exams were both take home, but very application based and therefore required a lot of thinking and problem solving.

Dr. Ingemi is very friendly, understanding, and willing to help! The lectures are dense and have a lot of content but as long as you are present in class and take good notes they aren't too difficult. Personally, I found the content really interesting. There are poll questions that count as attendance (not graded on accuracy). Exams are online.

Prof is passionate about the subject matter and that helps make the class more engaging, but lectures are 1.5 hours of dense content. Its extremely bio heavy for a psych class. You have to pay attention to everything she says otherwise you spend a lot of time reviewing recorded lectures after of class. Overall good teacher and fair grader though

Professor Ingemi really cares about her students and is passionate about the material she teaches. The lectures can be very dense at times but if youre interested in the subject material it is a really engaging class. The class is almost completely lecture, and the grade is almost entirely tests (however they are pretty fair).Overall great teacher

Super nice and helpful. Encourages asking questions! She changed the testing style to be all open-ended when I took the class. While this made me nervous, it changed how she taught the class and made me feel like I could actually apply the skills I learned in professional settings. Lectures are dense however so you should always attend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ingemi was helpful and accessible. As an underclassman, the content felt like a bit much. Her lectures were packed full of detailed information so I suggest attending lectures and taking notes. Grades consisted heavily of exams, but also discussion posts and in-class participation.

This class is the most lecture heavy class EVER. The lectures are 1 1/2 hours and just filled with facts that you are expected to memorize. There isn't too much outside work but this means that a large chunk of your final grade is exams. The exams and quizzes are unnecessarily hard and she throws in so many trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Taking Prof. Ingemi's Biopsych class was an absolute dream. I was scared at first because of the lecture-heavy teaching style, but her slides and study guides included everything we had to know. She never turns down a question someone has in class. She seems so passionate about neuroscience and wants us all to succeed. 100% would take her again

Prof. Ingemi is a very nice lady who is very willing to help. She explains concepts well in slides and is very knowledgeable about neurobiology. The slides are pretty dense and specific, and tests can be tough because you really have to apply what you know. Also, tests are worth 80% of the grade. However, she definitely wants students to succeed.

Prof. Ingemi was definitely one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. Her lectures were clear, but interesting. She does tegrity recordings in case you miss class (but would recommend going b/c of Tophat questions). She posts study guides for exams and is super approachable in office hours.

Dr. Ingemi was super knowledgable and (I thought) likable, but the class is 100 minutes of straight lecture. No activities, or any chance to apply what she says. The online quizzes are harder than they should be, and tests are worth 80% of the grade but she was very nice & approachable. Posts all lectures on tegrity
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Reads off the lecture slides. Blackboard quizzes are harder than they should be. Final isn't cumulative which is nice.

He is genuinely a nice and funny guy. He is strict about having devices out and attendance/deadlines. There's a lot of work, but the concepts aren't too hard, and the TA did not grade harshly at all even for the big projects. As long as you follow instructions you will be okay. He doesn't respond to emails and he is not tech savvy.

Learning SolidWorks isn't really something you need a teacher to lecture for. He makes it harder by assigning lots of homework and having a harsh test grading distribution. At least once a class, he finds a way to berate his students/Gen Z population in general. He seems pretty stuck in his ways, and honestly looks and gives off Disney villain

He lacks empathy. It is truly fascinating how he is still teaching in this school, especially because every single upperclassman that I've talked to was just as traumatized. And I can tell you right now, he truly doesn't care what you think of him. There were times I believed he was here for the fun of seeing his students struggle.

Assignment instructions can be contradictory + vague. He often skims through slides without explaining. When he does explain, it's very helpful. You must attend class and show respect in order to do well.
nice guy, doesn't teach well and lecture is very long. Super work heavy class. 10-20 hours weekly.

He sold us his own textbook and every  class session was him reading the tutorials out of the book word for word. Every tutorial is click-by-click instructions. He managed to detract from the value of the textbook by making it distracting to follow along with his bumbling, half complete sentences. He would also insult us in class.

Professor Zeid is much better than many people say he is. Yes, his lectures may be long and boring, however, he does a good job at explaining the info and making sure that students understand the topic. Homework is long but good feedback is given on all of the assignments and help is very accessible. He will call you out for not paying attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the rudest professors at this university
So so class need do some work. Fairly easy. Homework a bit hard and heavy.

Professor Zeid doesn't care how his students study. He was my capstone instructor and he merely responded to your request to meet. Even though he agreed to meet he would tell you he cannot meet before the scheduled time without telling you the reason. DO NOT expect to communicate with him.
Awesome Professor. Tries his best to help our students. TA was accessible too. Helped in getting a good grade.
tests are bad

The course is useless. The entire semester was just aimed to study SOLIDWORKS, which is easy. It's a waste of time and money. If you already choose this. Remember don't spend too much time on it. And It's hard to communicate with professor after class.

Zeid really knows his stuff, and he teaches it right at the proper level for Industrial Engineers learning to write code. Some of it may seem to obvious at first, like the HTML, but trust me by the time you get into the more complex PHP, the level of intellectual challenge will make you learn a lot

Be ready to take notes! Zeid's method is to write on the chalkboard for the whole period and he expects you to take everything down. Willing to help. Somewhat lenient. If you have a decent reason that you couldn't complete an assignment just tell him, he will almost always help you out. Will probably learn the most in the lab though.

She is a kind person but I fell asleep every lecture. She just talks at the class the whole time, it is so boring, and it's hard to follow along with the slides because she goes too fast and doesn't upload them to canvas before class. Be prepared to work on a group project the whole semester. Don't take this class if you don't want to be bored.

She's a rlly kind person but the classes themselves were painfully boring- I wouldn't take her again. I was rlly interested in the topic of Health Psychology and was going to take it as my major, but decided against it after this class. Papers were assigned every week (which I don't mind) but they were the exact same topic just different wording.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I like prof Todorova, but save your money. Classes are just lectures, but keeping your attention as she speaks is hard. There are also a surprising amount of papers due as well as readings for every class. She can play favorites and be confusing with directions. Not hard to get a good grade, but it's a lot of hours you won't get back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I like Dr. Thurston, and she's really nice and everything but oh god is this a boring class. It's fine, take it for an incredibly easy A. The textbook is available through the library which is nice.

Such an angel shes my favee. Quizzes and exams are 70% of the grade but she uses quiz questions for the exam and gives a ton of guidance on whats on the tests. Most people will end this class with an A. Just show up and she will love you. If anything happens during the semester she is so understanding but she does follow the syllabus too closely.

Relatively easy but heavy workload. Quiziz, in person, almost every single class. Weekly discussion posts, along with regular work, too. Very kind and passionate teacher; however, an overwhelming amount of work at times.

I love Prof Khan, she is a great professor! She obviously wants the best for her students and is accessible outside class/responds to emails quickly. Not many things contribute to the grade, so it was my fault I got a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her class really isn't that difficult but it is confusing. Her quizzes and lectures are all over the place. She even said herself that she doesn't make her own quizzes and tests so when it comes time for the actual exams it can get confusing because that stuff wasn't too focused on in class. Overall a chill class but show up on time and participate

Professor Khan is an extremely unorganized professor. She teaches from a textbook, but quizzes/tests do not relate to the teachings in class. She sends weekly announcements recycled from years ago, and left a syllabus from 2020 on Canvas, which created confusion. I would avoid taking ANY class with her, as her teaching style was horrendous.

Very caring and nice professor who genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. Exam questions weren't too hard as long as you went to lecture and did reading. Sometimes will cold call during lectures but not often.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took her in the fall. SIT IN THE FRONT. She will like you more. Nice but not great at teaching, tests are weird but not that hard. Easy grader but usually will give like 95s. Cold calls people but the questions aren't hard.

She honestly doesn't teach you anything. I feel like my dad can teach me better, and he doesn't have a background in marketing. She gives mom vibes and will say beautiful work, but the content doesn't matter as much as how you present yourself to her. She will cold call you if you don't participate.

She requires students to sit in the front and not be late even for a minute, otherwise, she will question you in front of everyone when you enter the door. By the way, she is a bit discriminatory towards students who don't have American looks.
never take her class she has so much attitude and never look or reply to any of your e-mail.
Heavy emphasis on participation and puts students on the spot. Didn't understand half the content she attempted explaining. Take this class with anyone else.
She is amazing. I love her so much. she is great. no joke fr.

Khan is sweet and cares about students. Her lectures follow the textbook and she typically recites slides for the entire class. She cold calls but the questions are never too complex if you're paying attention. I feel that for our project she focused more on confidence and effort rather than small details and content. She never gives above a 95.

Nice person, but not meant to be a professor. You are graded by very little, it's easy for your grade to suffer if you do badly on one exam. She is an easy grader but it is extremely rare for her to give you a 100, she will take one point off for no reason. Lots of favoritism, teaches word-for-word text book, cold calls, boring lectures

Doesn't normally seem too sure of what it is she's going over. Nice, but very disorganized. Professor also doesn't make her own tests, making the exams confusing to do well on even if you know the concepts because they're so random.
Don't take this prof's class. Pretends to be kind but do not respect the students and will cut you off multiple times no matter how polite you are.

At first, her class might seem scary, but she is a very sweet and nice professor. If you show up on time and participate, you will have no difficulty. She is a very easy grader and wants everyone to pass with good grades, as she will say many times. As long as you are respectful and come to class, you will be just fine. Do not let her scare you.

Huge on participation, attendance, and getting to class on time. Will make it clear if she does not like you. Cold calls, will cut you off. Will claim reading textbook is necessary, not a soul in my class did and we all did fine. Incredibly easy grader, easy A. Exams multiple choice. Guidelines say to not claim favoritism, but ask anyone- she does.

Strange. Very clearly targets certain students that she does not like, specifically men. I was not one of them but it was obvious everyone could tell. Incredibly easy grader, pretty awful teacher. Can be scary when she singles you out or cold calls you but all the assignments that she grades are crazy lenient- the lowest was an 84%. Take for credit

Professor Khan might be the worst professor in all aspects. Barely teaches class, reads off a script as if students will fully comprehend what she's saying. Everything she says comes straight from the textbook and its definitions. I can confidently say that I learned nothing in her class. Highly recommend to stay away from any of her classes.

I see where all the other ratings are coming from, she does give a lot of stories and examples of companies (amazon, tesla, Microsoft) or her friends and family which are unrelated but it made the class fun with applicable knowledge for me. She may not be the best teacher but she is a great person and really understanding. I would recommend.
I participated in this class like no other. Literally made it my life's mission and she just gave me a trash grade. AVOID.
Tests were so easy but her lectures were really bad and she only cares about participation and attendance

Zero knowledge of course content. Lectures are essentially just repeating the text book. Makes it almost impossible to receive an A by refusing to give grades higher than 94 on any assignment. She is a nice person but not fit to be a professor of marketing

Dr Kahn is certainly the worst teacher I have ever had. We missed multiple chapters of the text book and classes consisted of her going on extensive rants that are completely unrelated to any course content. I left each class with a migraine headache after the professor had spoke continuously the whole class while not moving past the first slide.

Professor Khan is horrendous. Her classes consist of her rambling about Amazon and Elon Musk. Since she hasn't taught anything the entire semester, the exams are a complete gamble. My grade dropped 2 letter grades after the final. She needs to retire because clearly she is not fit to be a professor at this level. I feel bad for you future students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please take another professor if possible. The class itself is easy -- that isn't the problem. It's the fact that she is the most inconsistent grader of all time and doesn't give any individualized feedback on your work. If you question her, she just gives a roundabout answer that doesn't explain what you did wrong.

I would not suggest taking her. Nice person but not a great teacher. She reads off the textbook and isn't super clear about requirements for the projects. 45% of your grade will be based on 3 exams that have very few questions (the final had 10) and she grades projects/papers unnecessarily harshly. Don't feel like I learned anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher.  Only reason she is not getting a 1 because it is very easy to get an A- in this class.  Almost impossible to get an A.  3 tests worth 45% of grade, but tests vary from 10-20 questions so each question is worth about 1 percent of your grade.  The other 65% she gives students B+/A-, nothing higher and nothing lower.  Stay away

i dont suggest her. little work but quizzes are graded so heavily it's insane. lectures are unprepared and useless. syllabus is worthless and due dates are often unclear. she is really nice, but also rude sometimes and undependable. quizzes are fine if you read the textbook. grade is dependent on a few days of actual work throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Khan is a very kind and fair professor. A few things: participate in every class and raise your hand at least 2 times per class. Secondly, sit in the front rows of the class, it does help. Attendance is also a big emphasis. Unexcused absences will immediately dimmish your reputation in her eyes. Participate and you will get a good grade.

professor khan is genuinely sweet and wants the best for her students but she is a bad professor. Classes seemed unprepared, she tells the same stories over and over. She tries to change the due dates to make it easier for students but this makes everything more confusing If you can avoid her do it but it's not a difficult class to pass on your own
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very disorganized course. I didn't feel like I was learning anything most of the time during her lengthy lectures. While being a heavy lecture course, there are very few assignments given (no homework)making it very difficult to boost your grade. Strays off-topic all the time while also talking in circles. I would avoid taking her to save your GPA.

You have to attend class or else you won't know what's on the exam. The syllabus is pretty unhelpful and unorganized. She'll ask a question and then go around the whole class for a response, but shell judge your answer and cut you off.

does not give feedback or tell you anything that's going on during class. shes super nice but extremely disorganized and you won't know your final grade until the day grades are due. the syllabus is super off and you have to be in class otherwise you won't know what's due or what to study

Although this professor is very caring she calls on students randomly and will cut off your answer, she also does not give time to think and then will judge the answer (this judgement cut down on how much students openly participated). You are also graded on very little in this class: a case study paper, 2 quizzes, and a large group project
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most disorganized and disrespectful professor ever. She was often late to class, the syllabus was never accurate, and she never had a clear plan for class. Actively extremely rude to certain students and simply not good at explaining the course content.

She seems to be caring for her students but she oftentimes confuses me and makes me feel like this class is highly disorganized. Tests are kind of hard and you have to read textbooks. Participation is impossible because she cuts people off and does not wait for people to answer questions. I learned nothing from this class.

Professor Khan is a super caring person and always puts her students first in the classroom. She will always ask what the students prefer before assigning due dates and requirements for tests and projects. Though it is an easy course, she is very unclear with due dates and she can be forgetful at times. Overall great professor though

Professor Khan is a very nice person. She cares about her students but at times can be disorganized. The class has 3 group presentations and a midterm and final exam. The exams were super easy, just regurgitating definitions from textbook. Class discussions include textbook references. No reading and only homework is weekly discussion posts.

Prof Khan was like aight. Her class was so easy, all you have to do is show up and participate. make sure she knows who you are by the end of the semester. Tests are regurgitations of textbook definitions. However she takes random small points off just bc. Heavy group projects with presentations too
She is a wonderful professor, 100% take the class with her. Make sure she knows who you are (your name).

Prof Khan is nice, but the class is so disorganized. There was no syllabus and random unwritten expectations. My class was often confused about what we were learning because there were no modules or assigned readings or really a plan. She also cold calls and often interrupts students when she disagrees with them.

Prof Khan is a sweet person but she doesn't teach this course that well. Her lectures are often unorganized and unrelated to what we're learning. She tends to drag out her stories/examples which can make lectures boring and confusing. The exams/content are overall easy making it easy to get an A in her class but you won't learn much valuable info.

Pick any other prof. Both her class and her Canvas are disorganized to the point that you never know what's due. She cold calls people to ask their opinion on a topic, then shoots them down when she disagrees. Majority of class time is wasted on group projects that loosely correlate to content. Only used the textbook for the vocab midterm & final.

Prof Khan is a knowledgable professor. However, she is very disorganized and goes off on tangents. You can't really take notes in class cause the lectures aren't organized. The canvas page isn't organized either. She is reasonable with her tests though which are just defining 10 vocab words. You're also graded on 3 group presentations.

Professor Khan is amazing! I am currently in her International Business course and every class is so fun and unique. She clearly is passionate about her job and enjoys what she does. Can be a little disorganized with the syllabus sometimes, but nothing that clarification in class won't solve.

The absolute worst professor. She is constantly cold calling and then disrespecting your answers, she literally yelled at us every day, had such unclear expectations but somehow expected us to read her mind, and overall so disorganized. If you have to take international business, literally take it with any other teacher.

Great & funny professor. She is all over the place & unsure of her own due dates but will give extra time if needed. Weekly discussions were very easy, a midterm & final, & 2 group projects. The midterm & final were very easy & included memorizing textbook definitions. Would recommend just be ready to be called on to participate in discussions.

Although she generally nice, she has a tendency to call people out and tell them straight up that their points in class discussion are incorrect. Extremely disorganized. Didnt know my name and I attended every single class. Gave me a D in class participation and attendance even tho I participated in most classes. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: What a wonderful Professor! Although some students found her class boring, she has a vibrant personality that makes class interesting. Class is discussion based with two big group projects. Exams are vocab words and Dr. Khan wants everyone to do well. She was kind, understanding, enjoys what she teaches, and believed in every student!

Khan is a very nice teacher, very easy online midterm/finals. No pop quizzes, textbook optional, highly encourages in-class participation. Sometimes, the class can feel a little long. A little disorganized, but very understanding if there's miscommunications. Theres two group presentations, two group write-ups. Overall easy class!

Dr. Khan is one of the sweetest professors. She really cares about students' needs. Her class is very light on work. No need to read the textbook, just pay attention in class. Group projects and an easy midterm and final are majority of the grade. This class is a stress free one and you should try to get into Dr. Khan's section if possible!

Dr. Khan is a literal legend. Super nice and energetic. She has great stories to tell the class which relate to international business which then truly enhances the course. She may sound mean sometimes but it is simply because English is not her first language. Overall, an amazing professor and a perfect class to start my time at Northeastern.

So disorganized its ridiculous. Doesn't put due dates, tells us not to look at the syllabus because information is incorrect (doesn't bother to fix this). She shares some interesting stories during her letures but honestly I got nothing from the course.

Good person but very disorganized and confusing when lecturing. Never has proper due dates and often forgets student Qs, assignment dates, or her own announcements. Discussion Qs every week, couple of group projects, and 1 midterm and 1 final both just answering 1 question. Interesting course, easy because she makes it, but try for another prof

She is a really nice person but is all over the place. You can get through the course without reading the book if you understand the course concepts easily. The class has 2 projects that are worth almost half of your grade and participation is worth 30%. It was her first time teaching this class and I think it is going to get harder in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he is the best professor I know and its the best to get good gpa
enthusiastic professor!

Ildar is one of the best teachers i have met. He was very well prepared for the course and had many exercises to help us understand the new concepts. Apart from that, he cares a lot about the extracurricular activities of the students. He's such an excellent teacher, his classes are in high demand and hard to secure.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great cs professor, especially for novelty for computer science. Give good feedback on homework.
N/A

one can not maintain good Gpa under him, if u want to increase gpa I would not suggest his class. Exams are too heavy, you need to memorize 20+ pseudo codes, and in assignments also, you will not get full marks always. He is a strict professor and would not listen to what you have to say, if he sets his mind to something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
This course is NOT about algorithms—it's about proving trivial inequalities and guessing what
counts as "obvious." The name should be changed to "CS5800: Do I Need to Prove nº + 7n + 1 >
0 for n > 10." I signed up expecting to learn algorithms, not to play a guessing game where every
TA has a different definition of what needs to be proven.
Amazing lectures. If you do the work, you'll learn a lot.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Very clear and helpful.
No matter how much other students berate him, one can't deny that he is a great instructor for algo. He knows what he's teaching and his lecture delivery style is also clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. He's always there to help his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: People are just fearmongering in his reviews page. He isn't a bad professor. Students just have to pay extra attention to his lectures, and that's it. Exams are very predictable and he offers ample supports to students who approach him for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Iraklis isnt as bad as other people show him to be. They all are rating him low cuz they couldn't maintain their sanity and grades in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Disorganized rubric and poorly structured exams that expect answers in one rigid format. Even correct solutions get zero if they differ (e.g., using a stack instead of a queue). Little concern for students. Take this course only if you can memorize and reproduce CLRS exactly as expected.

I got baited into memorizing 30+ pseudocode for the final.
which i guess is alright to know 
but it didnt feel good when i didnt get to apply my 30+ pseudocode of knowledge on the 5 questions which are on the final
it feels like he said gullible is written on the ceiling and i looked up

The grading practices are excessively punitive, communication is effectively nonexistent, and the lack of transparency has caused extreme and unnecessary stress. This experience has significantly impacted my mental well-being and delayed my academic progress, and it should be formally reviewed.

If you want to sharpen algorithms, this course delivers. Lectures are structured and well paced—until the end, when it suddenly accelerates. But if you're aiming for a smooth learning curve or you're protecting your GPA, think twice: grading feels bureaucratic, partial credit is hard to defend, and the pressure can make learning feel punishing.
Run, worst professor of all time, would ask you to follow EXACTLY how the slides or the book implement the algorithm, or you lose a lot of points even if you are correct.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Algorithms is a very hard class to take in general. Materials are heavy - it's just not a fun topic. But Prof. Herc really tries his hardest to make it work in the short time frame and the knowledge people already have (1st Sem. Grads all the way to PhD).

Poor learning structure. Exams are questions directly from the textbook but the textbook is dense. His lectures help a little with the exams and homework but they are more so supplements. Also, not enough questions on exams, if you miss just one, you fail.

I am pretty sure the good reviews are fake reviews. He is a bad lecturer and barely explains anything. He insists on following the book and visiting office hours and TA's but the book is dense af and the office hours are just a repetition of the class. Given how abysmal he is at teaching it feels almost criminal how harshly he grades. AVOID!!
Worst professor ever seen in my life. I failed by 0.21% and gives direct 0 even if your approach is in correct direction. RUN!!!!

Won't Recommend. 
The grading criteria for assignments and exams is non-sensical. Each exam has 4 questions, so if you commit a mistake in one, you risk falling by a letter grade. Highly theoretical, will not help in passing interviews. Nothing to learn here, stay away. Take some other worthwhile course, and LeetCode if you wanna pass interviews.

Do not even think of taking this class, professor is very rude and does not care about students. Run away from this course and professor. I failed by 0.1%, the professor didn't consider my case, didn't reply to any emails or messages. Grades ruthlessly.  If you mess up even one of the exam, be prepared to retake the course. RUN!!!!!!!!!!

I really enjoyed being in class with this professor. His course work was very flexible and fair, his lectures were very engaging and informative. His class was the perfect length. Overall I feel this was one of the most effective educators I've had in my program this far. I would absolutely take his class again if I could.
run, don't take with him
not a good lecturer

Worst grader I have ever seen. If you do not do things by his book you will loose marks, irrespective of if your answer is right, if it is not the way he has taught the topic you will be loosing your grade. I will not recommend taking this course under him in any circumstance. He refuses to give the answers for the assignments.

agree with other comments. he is a nice guy but an awful lecturer. his slides are just copying textbooks and it is hard to understand what he talks at class. i attended all the classes and felt it was such a waste of time. he is also very tough grader and he makes everything more confusing. this is the worst course I ever took.

Lectures are informative and engaging. Course is very well organized with assignments every week, and grades released timely. 

However, not an easy A, you will need to study and may need to attend OH often. 5-8 hours a week outside of class is expected. 

Grading appears harsh sometimes, but all assignments(and exams) have some bonus points.

The professor grades based on concept clarity. If you understand and justify the concepts well, it greatly benefits you. He is clear on fundamentals and pays attention to details that matter. His challenging assignments prepare you for exams and promote growth. The subject is easy if you're strong on the basics. TAs are responsible and helpful.

This was the worst I've had. Useless lectures with empty slides. Condescending on Piazza and impossible to understand due to his accent.  Grading was insanely harsh. Lost 10 points on a 15-point problem for a small mistake! Even with the right answer, a missing step meant you were wrong.  He also refused to give us homework solutions.
Grading criteria are unclear, and TAs require excessive explanation of basic concepts with no partial credit. very frustrating and inconsistent.

This course was pretty difficult. I took it as an undergrad as part of the PlusOne program. Prof Herc is super nice and willing to help you out. The lectures are informative, but reading the textbook is essential for doing well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cares about his students, is a nice guy, and will answer any question, but is an awful lecturer. You can tell he is really trying to explain the concepts, but he just makes things more confusing and hard to understand. I spent the whole semester working with a tutor and he was able to explain the concepts WAY better.

He is extremely old. He takes almost half an hour to get class started because he struggles to share his screen to the board. He seems like a nice person, but on exams, the written portion is harshly graded. You could get an correct answer and explain it but you will most likely lose points due to not writing in excessive detail.
Not a hard class. But not a very good teacher either.
Terrible class. You don't learn much even if you do well. Prof too isn't great.

Professor Slusser wants everyone to do well, that is very clear. The class is not hard, some homework and 2 exams, which is not too difficult. Show up and pay attention and you will do well. He is also very flexible!
Lectures are fairly dry, but memorizing the content of the class translates fully to the exams.

Professor Slusser cares about the course content and was a joy to see in class. However, his lectures are not engaging and don't hold students accountable to participate or complete homework on their own. It would be an easy class to cheat in each assignment and fly under the radar. He lacks applicable knowledge of technology, which is ironic.

Very sweet professor, and made boring content worthwhile and engaging. Unfortunately, the tests were very heavy weighted, and he was very bland when giving directions for the case studies. More than likely, what you get on the tests is what you end the class with. He wants a lot of participation. Offers zoom if you are sick/woke up late.

Great professor, super nice and caring guy, and made the class interesting. Cases and exams were perfectly manageable. Would 100% recommend this course and the professor. Probably one of the best MISM2301 professors at Neu!!!
Lectures got boring extremely quick, but the content was easy. Case studies and quizzes aren't hard, but tests lower your grade by a bit, even if you ace the homework.
His lectures are long and boring. Ask obvious questions that do not help you learn the material. He re-explains things and almost never finishes class PPT
He is so kind and he is always available to respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The subject itself was easy but stillsuper hard to get an A. I got 90s for all the exams but they don't really help. He wants specific things for those case studies but never tells what he wants and gives no feedback. He indeed is entertaining but lectures are long and not really helpful. No finals but three exams throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Treats his students with respect, is honest, funny and very informative. Can be a tough grader but a fair one.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Better choice out of the other professors. No final exam, just a final project.

I enjoyed the class with Prof. Slusser. He is engaging and wants you to be engaged. There are several (long) case studies (needs to be purchased online) to read and case analyses to write for most of them. But I found him to be an easy grader as long as you follow his clear directions on the syllabus. Get ready to participate a lot in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Not a bad class. I would recommend taking it as he's the only one who does not have a final exam out of all the other teaches in MISM 2301. Nice person. Likes to joke around and wants you to perform well in the semester and has a very clear outline of your grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wants particular things but is not completely specific on what those are. Very little feedback. Unwilling to admit when he made mistakes in assigning the wrong grades to the wrong people. You will spend forever writing the final case study. Clearly had not read his own syllabus. Quizzes okay. Tests were based on things we never discussed.
The quizzes are extremely easy. He also gives out a study guide for test. Compared to the other teachers for an intro level MISM class, he is the best.

Northeastern decided to take away the book out of the course, that was mistake number one. Now his class is based off timed BB quizzes 10Qs in 10min which are taken from these condensed readings that someone wrote up for the department. The readings aren't particularly clear in any way and the questions on BB are vague and subjective. Poor Overall.

Provides insightful thoughts and makes decent jokes. Interesting cases. Always let us go early which was great. The workload is decent except the quizzes can be hard unless you have read the cases thoroughly

I'm not sure what he's like now, but I took him for the required MBA class as part for 1.5 credits.  Nice guy, but makes you write what seems to be many unnecessary cases that could've really just been read for homework.  For a 1.5 credit class, he makes the workload like a 4.5 credit class.  I took him 3 years ago and things may have changed since

Great teacher. Hilarious guy. Quizzes are easy as long as you study and there is no final. Homework makes up half the grade and as long as you do the work you'll be fine. Made an otherwise dull subject pretty interesting.
He's super nice and makes class engaging. Absolute GOAT.
Super nice and caring professor. Doesn't make you feel bad even when you ask obvious questions. Probably the best math teacher I've had in college. Not sure why his rating isn't higher.

The class consists of 2 mid-term exams, both open book and online. There is no final exam. Attendance is mandatory but is only worth 5% of your grade. Group project was quite easy and had 6 HW assignments throughout the semester that were graded.
Excellent professor.

He's a very nice professor and is considerate towards helping his students. He has a somewhat difficult accent barrier. At least you can rewatch his Zoom lectures. Somewhat tough grader for exams and group assignments (He had to curve the grades). You leave 30-40 minutes early every class, which is nice.
Group project is good, and professor is good, but special Indian accent in lecture is hard to understand, and high score like A and A+ is not easy to be get.

Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about material. Moves VERY fast so you either have to be very prepared or backtrack to go over lecture/material again. Understands many frames of thinking and extremely helpful if you ask questions (even if you think they're dumb). Lectures way more useful than the book.
Very easy lectures but assignments are very difficult and class notes are not at all relevant to the questions he asks in assignment and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lecture is very technical, one has to have a solid background in Math to understand the concepts. The lecture is wholly conceptual.  Exams are not the easiest, quite a lot of preparation is required.  The Professor is the best, couldn't ask for a better guide.

The class itself isn't that bad but her lectures are ridiculously dense and repetitive. She requires a textbook that she claims is needed for the course but refuses to answer questions about its content and barely features it on the exams. Worth noting that her friend and frequent collaborator wrote the book.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Professor Berent's slides are extremely confusing, misrepresentative of the exam questions, and does not explain the information well even in office hours. Get ready to spend hours studying.

very nice person but not a good prof. if you miss one lecture you'll be left wondering what is going on. i had to miss a few due to athletic events and it became confusing quickly after. also don't know how to post the canvas hw right half the time so you'll end up missing deadlines you didn't even know exsisted.

This course is not as difficult as everybody says it is. Tests are all multiple choice, and the cumulative final is optional. Professor Berent is super nice, but you HAVE to show up to class to do good otherwise you'll be lost; can't learn from slides alone.
I dropped this class three weeks before finals bro, one of our tests the class mean is 60 something... please do yourself a favor dont fxxking take this class

Take this class if youre super interested in learning sentence structure, if youre not, then don't take it. Class material is not interesting. Heavy course material, I genuinely don't see a point of taking this class lol if it's not mandatory.

She's one of the sweetest prof i've ever had. lecture is a bit heavy, you really have to lock in and focus during class. homework are super easy. tests are all multiple choice. materials are quite abstract, not much of psychology related content. highly recommend to go to her office hour if taking this class just so she can recognize you.

This was the most tedious class as it is so lecture heavy and the tests were ridiculous. LOVE THIS CLASS TAKE IT

reviews.comment: I wouldn't call this class an easy psych elective, but if you go to class, pay attention, and take notes you will really be fine! Only con is her slides can be quite disorganized.

The theories and concepts presented in the class often lack logical coherence. The grading of exams seems to be subjective. While she is a pleasant person, as an educator she is not supportive or helpful. Additionally, the practice tests look nothing like the actual exams, diminishing their usefulness as preparatory tools.

Do not take this class unless you have an interest in linguistics. Not a psych class, and sounds more interesting than it is. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She was genuinely one of the most unhelpful professors I have had at Northeastern. She is honestly sometimes just rude and even will just choose to not answer students' questions in class. Don't understand the low rating, she's one of my favorite profs I've had at Northeastern. People are just complaining because the class is heavy on linguistics I guess? Just pay attention in class - the lectures are interesting, and if you stay present (for the admittedly long class block), you'll do well on the exams.

She knows a lot about the subject but I honestly really flopped in this class and I was trying...she's not a good lecturer. Don't take this class unless you have a genuine interest and maybe even background in linguistics- an interest in psych isn't enough

she's not horrible but she's not good. she moves so slowly and wastes time at the start of class doing a review of last class and repeats herself too much. her lectures are boring and not engaging. the course content could be so interesting but she presents it in the most boring way possible. she greatly exaggerates the difficulty of the tests
Interesting topic and very cool to be taught by a professor with experience in the field

Although this class can be hard, looking back it's been my favorite class at Northeastern. The topic is truly fascinating and you can tell Dr. Berent is passionate about the subject. She's an expert in the field, and though she doesn't talk about it, her own research is fascinating if you look it up! She's so kind and cares about her students.

I loved her class! She was definitely passionate about the material and wanted us all to succeed. Although the class can be slow at times, if you pay attention to the lectures and study, you will do fine on the tests.

The class was very easy, but also painfully slow. It made learning the information easy though - everything was very simple as she seems to think we are all dumb. The material was very interesting and the professor was clearly passionate and wanted everyone to understand the material.

Dr. Berent offers a very interesting course. Linguistics is a challenging subject and she did a great job of conveying the information in a more simplistic way. You must attend lectures! I would not recommend taking this course if you are not interested in the areas of linguistics or psychology. She is VERY open to receiving questions and feedback.

She is very intelligent, if you like to think and are creative this class if for you. She is difficult- but the class is very interesting and her class made me a stronger student. If you spend time with the material and put in effort you should be good- if you like to do minimal studying do not take this class. I think she was great.

the worst professor I've ever come across. She doesn't care about students and everyone saying she was good, I don't know if they were actually in her class. She doesn't care about you at all and she also has no idea how to teach. You won't learn a thing, don't waste your money.

I don't think this course should be a psychology course, it should be called "history of language". It is not related closely with Psychology! Also, the professor is awful, even the TA is better than her!!

She's really not as bad as people think. If you show up to class and pay attention you'll be fine. AWFUL AWFUL AWFUL!! Pointless class. You cannot understand her and when you ask for clarification she just repeats the same thing and keeps going. DO NOT TAKE IT!it will only hurt you

A really cool professor.  He's very down to earth and structures his class like a discussion group more than a traditional classroom, which is great.  Also he schedules things nicely and it breaks up the three hours very effectively.  3 papers, one was longer, but he grades fairly.

AMAZING teacher. Real fun, and swears a lot. Easy grader, and pays attention to each student. Papers are easy. His son has Cerebal Palsy, and he brings him in to talk to the class, that was fun. Class is well structured: movies, mini lectures, LOTS of group activities, and discussions. Never boring. HIGHLY reccommended!!!
Write 3 essays or 2 essays and 1 presentation all semester.  Keeps a 3 hour class moving pretty well and he's not too boring.  It's a really easy class.

Oh my god, she does not show up. 90% of classes are either cancelled or moved to Zoom, but deadlines stay the same. i am NOT a stats person lets make that clear, he made me at least tolerate if not enjoy it. my only complaint is this class for me was 8am tuesday and friday, absolutely BRUTAL. go to lecture is my biggest advice, skip one and you will be very behind. i missed a few bc i got sick and that was rough to come back from. super sweet guy!!

Easy homework (unlimited attempts), easy quizzes (2 attempts), and lectures are very clear. He's accessible outside of class and helps anyone who needs help. Bradley was great for psych stats; grade is made up of TYK, homework, quizzes, tests, and a presentation. Quizzes were taken in groups, and the tests were open-note for a section every time. Good guy. Funny. Easy A if you do the work.
