reviews.comment: Extraordinary professor. Hes super passionate and knowledgeable and very helpful.

This man is the most amazing man I've ever had as a teacher. I am seriously amazed that people on here didn't like him. He makes you work for it but only because he wants the best for his students. HIGHLYYYYYYYYYY recommend taking any class of his you can!!

Lovely is a great lecturer and gave us 5 really interesting books to read for the class. However, He doesn't post grades until the end of the course and certain projects will count for a large portion of your grade. The guy also is very hostile and if something doesn't go his way, your grade will suffer. Wouldn't recommend taking him again

Professor Lovely has been the best professor I've taken at Northeastern. He is a fantastic lecturer, truly cares about students, and his class is fairly straightforward. He goes above and beyond in being available and understanding to students, and is a genuinely nice guy. As long as you participate in class and do the work, it should be easy

Lovely is the best prof I've had in my time at Northeastern. His tests are super straight forward and he's genuinely the nicest guy. He really wants you to do well and if you put a bit of effort into his class he'll like you back.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Would never take a class with him again. He is by far the worst professor I have had at NEU so far. He is extremely unclear, and is quite hostile with students. If you don't do it his way he will not like it. Avoid Lovely at all costs.

Love Captain Lovely. Fmr Marine. One of the kindest, most caring professors and people you will every meet. His classes often don't have a rhyme or reason as he just talks more on what he believes or is feeling, which keeps it interesting. There are a TON of assignments and you'll always be doing work, but if you do it, you'll get an A and have fun
Perfect for those who want to take a class and learn general international business

Participation makes up a huge percentage of the grade in his class.  However when I did volunteer my answers he would often roll his eyes, I'm assuming because he disagreed with me?  Eventually he started to altogether ignore me even if I was the only one willing to answer his questions.  I felt very disrespected in this class.

Professor Lovely is my favorite professor at NEU by far. He made a boring subject a fun class and I never had any problem going. He is a very inspirational man and you know that he is there for you whenever. Studying abroad in the Balkans with him was also amazing. Not the easiest professor but it beyond worth it to know him.

I loved Professor Lovely! He really cared from the beginning and was also there to help us learn. He made sure to make his lectures interesting and had some interesting group projectsassignments for us to work on. I had a blast and wish I could've taken another course with him! 100% recommended.

Lovely is a great person but just an OK professor.  He chooses favorites and rarely hands assignments back.  The class itself is comprised of assignments worth 15-25% of your grade each, so if you mess these up you're screwed.  However, Lovely is fair and will try his best not to let this happen.  One of the best professors for the class.

Professor Lovely is amazing! He cares about each student in his class. He loves teaching at Northeastern. His lectures make what would otherwise be boring material funny and interesting. Go to his office hours too! He loves to help his students.
Motivational.

Easily the best teacher I've ever had. He has a great sense of humor that made learning very entertaining but also very effective. Also, Prof. Lovely is very fair and helpful to all of his students and generally just a great person. I'd definitely recommend taking any class he teaches
Loved that teacher. Very funny and enthusiastic! Definitely take him, he has some really funny jokes! Best part is that he was a Marine soldier!

Great teacher, definitely take him if you have the chance. Even though the course was so poorly designed (the course coordinator's fault not his), he made it fun and did the best he could to help us with the ridiculous quiz questions they gave us. Super helpful with our projects and said we could use him as a reference for jobs and such. Great Guy

Such a great professor.  His enthusiasm and willingness to share his knowledge  and help all students succeed is great.  It was really one of the only classes I looked forward to going to all semester and was such a great introduction into the business program for me! I 100% recommend taking him :)
great prof!!! wish i would have him for another course... you actually learn and have fun doing it.

Very nice person and really cares how her students are doing are doing in class. Make sure you actually pay attention if you are taking her class for accounting because it is no joke. You have to know everything for the exams. Accounting is very hard so its not her fault this class is hard but just be prepared to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite professor by far here at Northeastern. I learned so much. Its clear how much effort she puts into her class. She came early/on time to every lecture and was very organized, which I appreciated. While the material can be hard, she taught it so well that I never felt confused or lost. 10/10 teacher!
She made hard concepts feel very understandable and her class was equally as hard as the other teachers. I highly recommend her for this course!

Honestly my favorite class. Her lectures make material easy to understand and always has good explanations to tricky concepts. She has worksheets for each chapter that you work on as a class. Workload is super manageable with easy weekly homework. If you attend lectures you won't need to read the textbook. Tests are easy and the class is chill.
It was the best class at northeastern that I have ever taken. Exams are very easy if you study well. Gives good feedback, replies to email in seconds. Perfect professor at NEU.

Good overall, but the lectures can be kind of confusing. Shes caring and understanding, easy to reach. Although attendance is not mandatory, if you don't go to class youll get pretty lost. Organized and clear instructions/grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Never responded to my email and was late to her office hours. She can be nice, but can also be a bit passive-aggressive at times

You can tell by her lectures that she took time and effort in preparing, in hopes of making the material easy to understand. Though attendance is not mandatory, going to class, paying attention, completing the required homework, and putting in time to understand the material will help you succeed in the course.

I think she's a good professor, but she teaches like we are in middle school and it gets very frustrating. It is hard to focus in her class because she tends to describe things in a way that is way more complex than needed. She is really nice and caring outside of class and answers emails fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Li is definitely very lecture heavy, and it's often easy to distract yourself from the lecture and content of the class. They can feel long and boring, however the content is not as difficult as it seems if you take some time out of your day and study the material properly. You also have to pay for a textbook for around $100 to access.

Professor li LOVES economics (perhaps a little too much), which is what makes his lectures long/boring. Attendance isn't as mandatory as you think, and people end up not showing up after the first two weeks. content is memorization however if you study enough it's an easy A. u do have to pay125 for a textbook that you will most likely never read

he was very unorganized and had lecture-heavy classes that weren't engaging or helpful. He also put a lot of content on the midterms and finals that we either barely learned or didn't learn at all throughout the semester and didn't have a clear grading criteria.

Seamus is very knowledgeable but lectures bad. I learned most of the course from the textbook and taking notes. He usually shows up ~5 mins late, then takes another two to set up. He's really nice though! His grades and rubrics are very clear and his feedback on the project is clear and thorough. Drops one of three: midterm i, midterm ii, hw grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures boring asf. However, I stopped going to class and did well (attendance 10%). Midterms I and II are 60 MC and if you perform poorly on a midterm, he will drop it and replace it with your homework score, which is a guaranteed A. Also, there's group project that he'll pre-grade and tell you exactly what to change to gain a higher score.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Needs improvement.

Great guy, not a great lecturer. If you have not studied economics and are trying to take an entry-level econ course, you will most likely have a tough time. His class consists of hour-and-a-half-long lectures with little engagement with the class. It's kind of like he's too smart to be teaching a principles course. Overall, pretty difficult.

Professor Maulsby is an excellent professor. She gives incredible lectures, teaches interesting topics, knows exactly what she is talking about, and fosters an amazing environment within the classroom. Her teaching style is exactly what I envisioned college professors to be like. I could not recommend her any more highly

Prof. Maulsby is a true inspiration. She is thorough and kind and sort of "all seeing" She holds her students to a high standard, but also gives them the means to reach high. She is kind to all and non-judgemental. Her class is a great space to learn

Very knowledgeable, inspiring and amazing historian. Her knowledge and amazing story telling make waking up 7am worth it. She is SO nice and encourages class conversation. Has interesting media, movies, tidbits and stories to spice the class topic. But you have to WRITE everything in class.  If you have to take Arch History, take it with Maulsby.
Class taken Arch Modernity and City. Very intelligent. I'd also recommend her book "Fascism, Architecture, and the Claiming of Modern Milan, 1922-1943.
Would definitely recommend. Best professor ever.

She's very knowledgeable but I honestly question her teaching methods, and I think I really need to reflect this because she can be one of the best architecture professor. Her main problem is that she talks way too fast so you probably only get 25% of what she said in class, and her presentations are only pictures so it is quite hard.

Extremely knowledgeable, rarely need to look at her notes during lecture, shows the how much she understands her material. However she doesn't have any notes in her slides so you have to absolutely pay attention in class to know what's going on.

Probably the best instructor I have had at Northeastern so far. Interesting and captivating lectures that convey a knowledge and passion for the subject matter that is above and beyond expectation. Expects much from students but her conversational lectures prove very helpful of gaining cogent understanding of material. Definitely one of the greats.

Professor Maulsby is the Best History of Architecture professor at Northeastern.  While she is demanding, you will learn if you put in the time and effort.  She is very helpful and knows the material well. Take her classes!

Maulsby is by far the best arch history prof at Northeastern currently, i've had all of the others and Maulsby tops them all. She does demand a lot out of you but is very fair, very helpful and very intelligent.

Her lectures aren't that great...she says 'um' a lot. She is obviously a very intelligent person who is clearly interested in architecture but she wants to prove to the students (maybe a bit too much) that she is very informed on the subject.  Tests are slide id and short essay (for world architecture) which can be difficult

Super nice guy, actually engages with the class. Genuinly has made the class laugh a couple times. Actually show up and pay attention to the lectures and you'll be fine. The class has three exams and weekly homework but nothing that intense. I wish the grading wasn't that exam heavy but studying isn't too complicated since he post's the slides.

I had a stone in a lecture class, which made individual relationships impossible, but he is a good lecturer; he spices up his lectures with stories and jokes, making it easy to pay attention in class. He is understanding, helpful, and overall a good teacher.
This professor is amazing! He's so passionate and is an amazing story teller. I come to class just to hear him talk. 3 tests and all multiple choice.
Amazing professor!! He makes his classes so engaging
The best professor ever! Decided to minor in Economics because of Prof. Stone.

Prof Stone is actually the best. His classes aren't mandatory but his teaching style and the fact that you actually learn so much from them, as well as his personality and engagement make you want to go. Still a relatively difficult class but he is so helpful and all exams were online.

While I am not the best at econ, I studied very hard for this class and I feel that his class was extremely test heavy; thus, not a fair representation of my mastery of the class. Taking it online made it extremely harder as it was difficult to reach both the TA and professor for help, so it was a very independent-type class. Good luck!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hands down the best professor I've ever had. He is clearly ridiculously smart and he's just so passionate and enthusiastic and his lectures are amazing. He does a great job breaking down the tough concepts, moving at a good pace, and including interesting/funny real-world examples. Literally joined rate my professor just to recommend him!
Great Lecturer, easy class and easy tests just make sure to show up to classes and do lots of mind tap. Also may give a curve at the end for final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Stone is awesome! By far the best professor I've had at Northeastern. This is a very interesting class, but it is not easy. If you pay attention to the lecture and do all the homework you will be fine!
The lectures are very entertaining, and I never had to read the textbook. The tests are straightforward and very similar to the homework. I always looked forward to the class.

Michael Stone is a great lecturer and he's very interesting to listen to. The workload is minimal and if you study for the tests then you should be fine. Attendance isn't mandatory but I strongly suggest going if you want to learn.

Stone is one of the best professors I've ever had. Made the material accessible and easy to understand as well as being caring towards all of his students. Came to class prepared and always in a friendly mood. Grading based on three exams and hw, as long as you put the work in and go to lecture you'll be fine.

Prof Stone is someone who genuinely cares about his students and the subject that he is teaching. He always came ready to teach and made all the classes super engaging and fun to participate in. He made sure to answer all questions that came up in our class which was relatively large. Would definitely take his class again!
Super funny, super chill and made econ genuinely interesting. Pretty straightforward exams & hw. Great guy, considering an econ minor bc of him.
He was a great lecturer and one of the best professors I have had
Lectures are fun and engaging. Homework is all online and the difficulty is not hard. Recitation attendance is mandatory.

This class was great for an intro to econ. His lectures were not mandatory, and you could just look at his slides if you miss class. No need to read the textbook, which was nice. Makes lectures as interesting as they can be!

Absolutely adored hi! He's an amazing professor who genuinely cares about the subject! Tests are not cumulative, all multiple choice, and only 33 questions and homework are once a week and not difficult to understand!

Honestly one of the best professors at northeastern. His lectures are really amazing and he keeps the class engaged. You can actually observe that he is really passionate about what he teaches and wants you to succeed in his class. Highly recommend taking him. Tests are pretty easy (read slides, cengage prep) and there is weekly HW. Easy A. 10/10
Simply outstanding.

This was a pretty easy class. Stone is really funny and interesting to listen to as well as just a nice professor in general. It's pretty test and lecture heavy so be prepared for that. Study the slides for the tests.

He is a very kind Professor. Lectures go on a lot of tangents so it can be difficult to follow most of the time. I studied very hard for each test and still would not do well. For a 1000 level class, it is very difficult, I suggest taking another Professor.

Stone is nice but this class was so hard. I spent hours studying before exams and would barely pull an A. Study with cengage test prep if you want a chance at getting a decent grade. Exams are in person online. I would take another prof if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Stone is amazing. He is so passionate about teaching economics, and making sure everyone in the class is keeping up with the course's content. Despite this being a big lecture with 100+ students, Prof. Stone could always keep the classes engaging and super interesting. There are three, in person, noncumulative exams, and weekly homework.
TERRIBLE! NEVER take professor stone's class it will ruin your GPA

There's not much to say about prof Stone that has not been said. This guy should be a public speaker. He is so emotive and interesting to listen to. Every class became a conversation where you really got to learn beyond just the lectures. Easily the best professor I've had. Great guy who I can't speak highly enough. Make sure you pay attention tho

Amazing teacher. His lectures go beyond the slideshow and he uses the white board to really nail down topics. Since participation doesn't matter it can be easy to just skip lecture, but you will learn SO much more just listening to his lectures vs reading the slides alone.

Michael Stone is my favorite professor that I have had at Northeastern. His lecture are extremely engaging and he uses real-world examples and analogies to help students understand the material. Tests and workload are extremely fair. Highly recommend.

Super enthusiastic lecturer but goes on so many tangents throughout class. I completely forget by the end what is important to know for the chapter and what is irrelevant. I needed to teach myself everything before the exams (which counted 75% of the final grade, by the way). The course being this exam heavy made it difficult to be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i took this class in spring of 2020 as a freshman & even with the covid transition - i can confidently say a few years later he is one of my favorite professors in college. take him if you can. go to his office hours - he has so much knowledge & wants to help you succeed in his class!

Super nice and knowledgable. Read the textbook and do the practice quizzes and you will get an A. I got lazy before the final and had to settle for an A- but if you just do these two things your good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Excellent professor gives you a lot of information in lectures and tries his best to help out anyway. If you listen to his instructions and follow them it is an easy A

Stone is definitely one of the best professors I've had at NEU so far. His lectures are engaging and funny, and he's always attentive and accessible to anyone that needs help. His grading/tests are also really clear and he gives you everything you need to do well in advance.

Stone is a great professor who goes out of his way to make the lectures interesting and engaging. His explains the concept very well that you don't even have to read the textbook. The test is not hard and everything is basically off the slides in class. He is willing to help students anytime. I would highly recommend him.

Professor Stone gives great lectures. His slides give all the information you need to pass the class, yet attending his lectures is heavily recommended because of how well he explains topics. He really understands his audience, plus hes funny and engaging. I never took notes and just watched him talk, and I did great in microeconomics.

Definitely recommend Stone, he is absolutely amazing.  My favorite professor at NU by far!  He helped me develop a love for economics and is one of the main reasons why I decided to further pursue microeconomics in future courses.

Best lecturer out there. Most interesting class. Easiest tests if you do adaptive test prep on mind tap, which he uses some years. Tests are easy, just don't slack and do the practice problems, which set you up for a high score. Read thru ppts. Couldn't have picked a better prof.

Professor Stone's teaching was engaging, energetic, and thoughtful, especially considering our large 300-student class size. He assigned weekly homework and administered three multiple choice exams, none cumulative. Although reading and taking textbook notes wasn't required, it's very helpful. Also, I'd advise studying textbook practice problems.

Professor Stone explained the concepts well. There were only 3 tests; in order to get an A, you have to do well on each exam with minimal room for error. The tests weren't abnormally difficult and reflected what he taught in class. But, you definitely need to study and complete a plethora of practise problems in order to succeed on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super funny and super invested in the material. His lectures are super thorough and if you pay attention and take good notes, you can cash a good grade in this. He clearly cares about his students too, and he's really entertaining. Great professor, would absolutely take a class with him again.

Here's the thing. My class  ECON1116, fall 2021  had 300 people in it. This poor man had to perform econ standup three times a week to a crowd of fickle students in a literal auditorium. But he really knows what he's doing, is super accessible, and does genuinely cares about you. He's funny and articulates economics really well.

He's fine. Goes on tangents a lot of classes are 300+ ppl. His tests are more difficult than the test prep on the mandatory homework service you buy for like 130$. He seems like a nice guy, just not the best teacher for this class. Probably a lot better in smaller class sizes tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed professor Stone's class. You could tell he really wanted his students to succeed and he would stay long after his office hours were over to get to every student. The tests accurately reflected the homework and as long as you read the material and watched his videos you would do fine.

One of the BEST professors by far! Makes his online lectures engaging and is funny. I highly recommend going to office hours if you get confused on a concept because he does a great job clearing it up and will never make you feel rushed. He is also very easy to talk to. The exams are not bad as long as you put in the work and ask questions!

Professor Stone was my favorite professor during my first semester of college. He was fun to talk to and knew the subject very well so the way he explained things made it so anyone can understand the topics.

He is very animated and puts a lot of effort into his recorded lectures. This course is mainly based on the textbook. If you take good notes and read the book, you'll do fine on the graded homework and tests. Discussion board posts are also part of your grade from your recitation. Overall, if you do the work you'll likely get an A- or A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Smart and helpful, even though its online.

Professor Stone made really engaging lectures which made it easy to understand the material. I was in a very big class so exams were one of the only sources of grading we had, making the class really test heavy. However, if you paid attention in class or looked at his lecture slides it was very easy to do well

Professor Stone is an amazing professor. He is super passionate about economics and makes the material fun and engaging. There are 3 MC exams which are relatively easy and weekly homework. I always looked forward to his class, take him if you can!

Stone is AMAZING! Great lecturer and super funny. He says to go to the TA first, but was super accessible. The tests matter, 3 tests at 33 MCQ, but you learn so much. I took him during COVID-19, and he did an amazing job with the online transition and had video conference office hours. HIGHLY RECOMMEND! He made me look forwards to a 4:35pm class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor! Really funny and amazing explanations, gave new perspective on economics.

I think Stone is one of the best professors I have so far. From a person who never took econ perspective, his class was pretty difficult at first, then I started to understand more concepts by doing more of the study guide. One recommendation is to do practice exams before taking exams because some of the questions were exactly the same.

Tough tests. I will not recommend this class. The professor is nice and patient. But, textbook and homework are not related to the tests. If u want to get good letter grade, u should not be in this class.

Amazing guy, always ready to answer questions. HW once a week, really easy if you pay attention in class. Exams very easy, just take good notes and they're all straightforward questions. 100% would take this class again
Amazing Professor.
Lecture is probably good. But, the tests are usually tricky and tough. Weekly Time-costly homework.
Very entertaining for econ. I didn't mind the class and it wasn't too hard.

He is so passionate about what he's talking about. Never once had to open a textbook. Lectures are super detailed and informative; exams are straight-forward questions. The homework is only once a week, only 3 exams all semester (including the final). Such a great professor, passionate about what he is talking about, definitely knows his stuff.

Phenomenal Professor. Classes are always engaging and funny, and he really personally connects with his students. He knows the material well and wants the best for his students. Would absolutely love to take his other classes.

GREAT PROFESSOR. i can speak on behalf of all the 40 students in his class that he is a solid professor. he knows his materials, makes sure he repeats stuff often so everyone understands. only had a few homework and the tests are doable as long as u read his slides. highly recommend Stone!!!

Stone is a great professor and he puts all his material online for students to study. The majority of the grade is based on 2 exams and a final, so study for them accordingly. Attendance is not mandatory, but he is a nice guy so going to class isn't a struggle. Also he is good at updating grades which is a plus.
Prof. Stone is great - show up to lecture, pay attention, and you'll pass the class easily. He is straightforward and funny, and makes lectures entertaining. GLORIOUS.
His lectures were great and all you needed to know were in his slides or examples. The homework was good because it correlated well with the lectures. Highly recommend him.

2nd yr student and Stone is easily one of the two best professors Ive had at Northeastern. The Econ department is lucky to have him, he's everything a professor should be. He genuinely cares about his students, he teaches in a hilarious and relatable way, he's always willing to help you in his office hours. Take his class and you will be soooo glad

I took Econ as an elective and so far it's the best class I've ever taken. Professor stone  hands down is my favorite professor and would love for him to teach all my courses. He knows the material, his tests and grading criteria are fair and he's the kind of professor who genuinely care about his student.

Great lectures, he basically goes over the textbook in his powerpoints and he is really good at explaining the material. You can tell he really loves econ and teaching and he makes some jokes in the lectures. The homework is good and most of the test questions come straight from there, so make sure you understand the homework as you do it.

Professor Stone teaches the class amazingly well and makes sure that students understand what he is talking about. He is very funny, cracking many jokes and even using entertaining and relatable examples in class. He is one of my favorite professors and I highly recommend him to anyone interested in Economics

Prof stone is easily my favorite professor. I am not good at economics but did relatively well in his course because he teaches beautifully. Very clear, tells funny stories, and really engages with students. He also talks to us about random stuff in the beginning of class which makes him very approachable! I love him. wish he taught all my courses!
Great, easy, and you learn a lot!!
Fantastic Professor. Taking him for Law and Econ and it is one of the best classes I have ever taken at Northeastern. Easily the most enthusiastic professor I have ever had. HIGLY RECOMMEND him.
Easy class! Very entertaining professor. Enjoyed being in his class.
If I could, I would take all his classes. Enough said.

Best professor I've ever had. You do not need to buy books for he has ppt slides that covers everything you need. He is funny, amazing, charming, and his classes are always filled with joy.  And the most important thing that his exams is not difficult so you do not need to worry about fails. Just take his class and you will not regret!

Mr. Stone was a very good and supportive teacher, one of the most inspirational economics professors I've had. Class discussions were fun and if a student struggled, he was always willing to help and explain it over and over again. He is very fair in grading and he is super friendly. Class materials are uploaded on power point and straight forward

Mr Stone is what you want in a professor. He's very thorough with the material, and covers so much in his slides that you don't need to buy the textbook. Online homeworks are hard but allow for infinite amount of attempts. Two midterms and one final that is NOT cumulative. Brilliant teacher who may not be easy but its certainly possible to get A's

Rachel is a great professor. She is super nice and understanding. Her class is lecture heavy but, she gives a break in the middle. There are only 3 exams including the final, all multiple choice and the final isn't cumulative. Really pay attention to the lectures and do the readings. Lots of extra credit (up to a 7% boost in your grade).
Super passionate and kind woman. The lectures are v engaging and interesting and she gives a ton of extra credit. There are only 3 exams (including the final) and it is not cumulative.

Professor Meyer was a great professor. Only 3 quizzes and gives extra credit to boost your grade by 5%. The quizzes are exactly what the slides and lectures cover. There are readings every week, but they prepare you for her lectures. Her class is very engaging and interesting.
She's really passionate about the things she talks about which rlly helps you get through the long lectures lol. highly recommend taking her!!

Rachel is very kind and loves to talk to students. Looking over the assigned textbook chapters is a good way to make sure you are keeping up, but just taking notes during class is enough to do well on the exams. Exams are pretty straight forward, she gives a lot of extra credit and her grading system is to your benefit.

This has been my favorite professor thus far. Her teaching style is incredible. She will explain the same concept in numerous ways to ensure your learning style aligns with one of the explanations. She is approachable and makes class interesting. You must study for the tests and take notes, but they are not tricky. I recommend her highly.
She gives A TON of extra credit. Def more work than other sections but not hard at all.

One of the best classes I've taken at Northeastern. She is an amazing professor—super passionate about the subject and genuinely wants students to care and understand it. You learn a lot, but it never feels overwhelming because she explains everything so well. Readings are reasonable and well chosen. Would absolutely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very intelligent and great teacher who is very very clear about what you need to succeed in the class and provides you with all of the resources and materials to do so. Will assign a good amount of readings but SPECIFIES PAGES and paragraphs so you don't have to read entire chapters, and all readings are super helpful for tests. easy to succeed

it's nice to see how passionate professor meyer is about sociology. it makes lectures very enjoyable and easy to follow along to. her exams are very straightforward. if you show up to lecture and do the readings (not graded), you're guaranteed a good grade. i can't recommend her enough!
Just somewhat pay attention and understand the course material and you will do great!

Prof. Meyer was great! The class was a piece of cake and she gave many opportunities for extra credit even though your main grade is comprised of 3 equally weighted tests. Lectures were straightforward and as long as you took notes on that and skimmed the textbook you were fine.

Honestly if you could avoid chem you should. The class isn't easy but i literally failed two of my mid-terms and still managed to finish with an A in the class. The lectures are sometimes pointless since you have the slides already which pretty much summarizes what the lecture is about. Definitely the better prof for chem.

Murga is okay overall, the lectures are super boring and you kind of have to go for the top hats, there is a lot of homework but honestly if you weren't like me and actually spent a few hours outside of class time to learn the content you will be fine. The extra credit helps a lot Aswell.
He's pretty good- chem is just difficult, but you'll be ok. Just go to class and do the homework

professor murga is my king. his lectures aren't the most enthralling but they're very useful. show up to class, pay attention, study, and you'll easily survive. he gives sheets with equations for all exams as well as helpful practice. viva profe murga.
Lesser of the two evils of freshman gen. chem. Reads strictly off slides and all lecture materials are posted on canva. Decent guy with a fairly lenient grading rubric.

His class is manageable, but don't skip every class and cram for the exams, and you should do better than I did. Class was boring, and I wasn't learning much, so I started skipping and lost many participation points. HW helps to learn the material, but exam questions are quite different.
Lectures are long and hard to follow. But still better than Piatt

Lectures are hard to follow and midterms and final tend to look nothing like the homework questions. He is generous with scaling at the end of the semester, but you will feel like you're failing the whole time. Be prepared to study a lot and not get the best grades. The slides are helpful but you will need to teach yourself most of the material.

Professor Murga is possibly the best teacher at NEU. I completely missed my final and he let me take it right after in his office. He extremely caring and tries to make sure all students have the resources to do well in his class. His lectures are long but informational, so you have to make sure to focus. Tests are hard, make sure to study.

Murga does a very good job at teaching CHEM1151 in my opinion; he knows the material very well and he really wants his students to succeed. He's super caring, and he understands that it's a difficult class but he doesn't make it much harder than it needs to be. Lectures are occasionally boring, but that aside, I'd definitely recommend him.

Just take AP Chem. We got a guy who just reads off his slides, have a thick ass accent where 50% of the time you are unable to understand, only good side is that his exams are multiple choice with no explanation involved and we got  Piatt (by all means dont take her you will regret it her name is enough for you to shit ur pants).
all he does is read off the slides so i lowk stopped going to class 2 weeks in because i can do that myself

Compared to the other CHEM 1151 professor, he is a saint. But based on him alone, I would say he's reasonable. He cares about your grade (gives curves every midterm and some extra credit opportunity), and he is a nice person. But chemistry is hard, and unless you're good at it, it's going to take a good amount of time to study for his midterms.

Bro, Mr Murga is the goat, and on god, anyone saying hes bad or that the lectures don't make sense is lowkey just slow. Obviously, you have to do work outside of class, practice tests, active recall, wtv helps u remember the material he teaches in class. saying he does not explain stuff well is just wrong like pay attention more idk what to tell u

Murga is better than the other Chem 1151 professor, but his lectures can be confusing. He skips steps in math problems, jumps between numbers, and reaches answers without explaining. He also talks fast with a strong accent, so you may need textbooks or extra practice to keep up.

I didn't do well in this class, I had to retake it. But I'm glad that both times I took it, Murga was my professor. Taking this class freshman fall was killer. But taking it Summer 1 is actually doable, even while taking another hard class (i just had no free time). He also provides extra credit. Murga is kind, understanding, and approachable.

Professor Murga is really awesome. He is extremely passionate about the subjects that he teaches and keeps his course really organized. Physical chemistry is a LOT of work but it is possible to do well if you stay on top of the work. The summer class is really fast paced and I had to treat it like a full time job but the prof gives extra credit.

He was exceptionally average. His lectures are somewhat boring and you have to put in a fair amount of time if you want to do well in the class. That being said he is probably the best option for first year engineering chemistry.
Lectures are boring and long. He knows what he is talking about but doesnt know how to explain it. Midterms are not bad final is impossible.

this guy is great i love him. he curves so so so much i should've ended with a 78 and ended w an 82 - he curved the final ten points and curves all of his midterms (unfortunately they're all super hard). he doesn't take attendance but he does top hat sometimes during class so dont lose points on smth so easy. great guy and cares abt ur grade.

The class is hard, but Murga is a solid professor. His lectures are hard to pay attention to and the tests are always harder than the sample tests. The final was extremely hard, but he curved it by 10 percent. He gives really good extra credit opportunities, and it is definitely possible to get an A if you study a lot. Take him over the other prof.

Murga was a good teacher given that he taught chem 1 and 2 in one semester. He was easy to reach by email and overall a nice dude. The class was difficult though, I spent most of my studying during the week on chem. While there are a lot of HW questions, they are SO helpful to learn the content. Content builds, so try to understand the basics.

Murga has a lot of extra credit opportunities but don't let that fool you. Unless you took AP Chem in high school or are ready to spend every minute learning this you are done for. His tests are harder than the practice ones he gives and his lectures are boring and he reads directly from his slides. Best of luck taking this class.

Professor Murga is your best bet for chem. It's pretty easy to get a good grade in his class. He offers generous extra credit—120/100 for recitation (6%) and over 100 in Homework and TopHat.Tests are fair, and with prep, you can score in the high 80s or low 90s(Test 1+2). Lectures slides are posted online, but he occasionally does TopHat in class.

This guy is not meant to be a professor. His lectures are a joke and are a complete waste of time. On top of that, I could only understand 50% of the words coming out of his mouth. Don't take his class, it's the biggest waste of time.

I don't really blame Professor Murga. He's trying his best with what he was given, just like we all are. This is more so aimed at the people who put this course together. They decided to combine Chem 1 and Chem 2 into one course. It's very fast paced and hard. The tests are brutal and the review material rarely helps. Be on your guard from day one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Murga is genuinely a good guy, but has one of the worst teaching styles I have ever seen. There was purpose to go to lectures unless you wanted to see him cite the slides with no supplemental information. The practice exams have nothing to do with the real thing, but there is a lot of other opportunities to save your grade.

Compared to the other chem professor, he's a saint. But that still doesn't excuse his dreadful lectures and his hard to study slides. However, he does give small curves to tests and HW. It really sucks because there's so much material that he has to cover is such an amount of short time, which lowers the quality of his classes. Chill guy though.

lots of HW for only 15% of the grade. The rest of the grade is based on 4 tests for the entire semester. It is messed up, and the practice tests often don't *really* resemble the actual tests given. Also, no practice final. So happy this course will be over soon. Blegh. Only lectures.

If Leonel Murga has a million fans, then I am one of them. If Leonel Murga has just one fan, then I am that one. If Leonel Murga has no fans, that means I am dead. My pookie Leonel Murga is the greatest teacher to ever walk the earth. He can be compared to our glorius king Lebron James, but Leonel is far better in every aspect.

The lectures are very boring and most of the time Murga just reviews the slides that he posts on his canvas. You don't have to show up to class to do good, just study the slides and do the hw assignments. His teaching style is horrible and no beneficial information comes from his lectures.

Dr. Murga is lecture heavy and tends to read off the slides so take advantage of office hours. Atttendance isn't mandatory but he occasionally uses TopHat questions to count your participation and correctness which affects your grade. Much better than Dr. Piatt. If you can switch classes into Dr. Murga's please do. Tests are magnitudes better.

Very well prepared, but heavy-loaded lectures. Dr. Murga gives a lot of chances for extra credit (exams, homework, participation and recitation). He is available outside the class, explains every topic very clearly and gives okay amount of h/w. As a person he is really kind and caring, and what I respect the most he loves to teach his lesson.

He is a pretty good lecturer, but the course is extremely difficult, and you will suffer. Making friends is the only way to survive the course, and in order to get an A in this class... I put in nearly 20 (40 for the final) hours of studying for each exam. You don't have a choice as a biochem major; just make sure to take easy classes with this.

Tests are insanely hard if you don't know the material and he barely teaches it. He reads off the slides and has no personality. To pass you have to do a lot of studying. His tests are all multiple choice and are curved if the class does badly enough (excluding the final). Pray you have a good TA for recitation because that's where you will learn.

DO NOT take his class. He pretends like he is willing to work with you and it is merely a facade. He is awful and his tests often had answers that were intended to confuse students. He makes so many careless errors in his homework assignments and exams which are a deciding factor in your grade. Everyone in FA23 chem was lost, the TA was way better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is all lecture. He is a nice guy, but he doesn't really have much personality in his lectures. You also are "required" to attend lectures in that he doesn't take attendance, but he randomly asks questions that your participation in is graded. His tests are tough, but he posts full explanations for tests afterwards.

Murga tries to make this course as easy as he can considering the amount of content NEU requires him to teach. He posts all the slides, which is good because his lectures are boring. He offers a lot of extra credit points and curves a lot (for those saying he didn't curve the final, he curved the whole class up by 2 points). Exams were all MC.

Professor Murga only read from the slides. He did not make any effort to try to explain without reading from the slides. He also barely solved in-class problems which made it  difficult to grasp some of the topics. The TA was honestly better than Murga himself. It was very hard to pay attention to him as his lectures were not interactive at all.

He is very kind and knows a lot about the subject. However, the final exam had a median score of an F and he did not add a curve. Be prepared to work very hard in this class to do well. Even if you study a lot the exams are all multiple choice so if you get one wrong your score goes down even if you know how to do the problem. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you would like to waste your time/money, just take this professor's class. He has done nothing (except read his posted slides word for word). He rushes through concepts and offers NO extra material to practice. He is hands-down the worst professor or teacher I have ever had. He is rude in his emails and can surely destroy your love of learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: bad final that he didnt curve despite average of class being sixty

Professor Murga was a great person who did a good job teaching. He is very lecture heavy so be prepared. Try your best to pay attention in class because if you don't you'll find yourself lost when it comes to exams. Overall, a challenging class with a good teacher. Don't buy the textbook!

This course is a challenge for most people don't get me wrong but his exams are fairly easy as long as you study up on the topics that are coming up. His lectures are honestly optional because he gives the slides in advance but still shows up.  He gives ways to bump your grade up including homework and tophat questions.
Not bad at all, but it takes you a lot of time to review for the tests.
Professor Murga is the best chemistry teacher in the school!

Sometimes takes attendance depends on the day. VERY lecture heavy but he posts the slides so you don't have to take many notes. Textbook really isn't necessary, just study the slideshows. Really nice guy, not his fault the chem department make the course so content heavy.

The class itself is a challenging class as it is meant to be a year-long class but for whatever reason northeastern decided to make it a semester. You have to put in the work to get a good grade don't slack off and you'll get the grade you want. He gives you cheat sheets on exams with all the equations and it's scaled. Overall solid professor.

His accent is a little hard to understand and he talks quietly so make sure you sit close to the front.  The slides he uses are very informative, but he's just reading from the slides.  if you need help, though, he's always happy to answer questions.  He's very sweet and definitely the best professor for gen chem you can have at northeastern.

He has an accent but it isn't difficult to understand. The tests were online which helped, but the actual content was hard to understand and the course was boring and moved fast in general. Even though I aced the class, I didn't retain anything tbh. He replaced 1 out of 3 midterms with ur final exam grade if it helped ur final grade and scaled.

there is a lot of content, so it's a hard class. Murga does a pretty good job at going through everything, but lectures can get monotonous and hard to focus in. he's really fair when it comes to what goes on the exams and he does usually curve a bit though
i took this class fall 2022

Probably the best option for gen chem. His lectures aren't exactly inspirational but it's a big lecture so don't expect it to be the most interesting class ever.  He tries to relate the chemistry back to the real word to make it interesting when he can but its not always possible

CHEM1151 is really two classes compressed into one, so lectures are dense and fast. Few office hours, recitation was only used for homework. I didn't feel like I learned anything, but at the end of the semester, Murga listened to feedback to improve the course. His teaching is burdened by the chemistry department at Northeastern.

Teaching is done via lecture, with some problem solving. The textbook isn't needed, all the material is on the slides. Class is fast paced and hard, but he breaks down the tough topics well. Reads off of the slides. Very boring, difficult to pay attention. He's hesitant to post practice problems for exams. When asked if he was going to post practice problems for the final, he said that he wouldn't. The exams are difficult. Questions in exams are much harder than the examples in class and in recitation.

Read off slides the whole time. They were helpful but didn't teach the material very well. I learned more in recitation than in lecture. Also, he got mad people were saying Mr. instead of Dr. Apparently, it's so terribly disrespectful to his degree that he had to send out an email and complain about it in class.
the cutest guy in the chem department. paul

This class was definitely hard. Lots of hw, hard tests, and you need to study a lot if you've never taken chem before. He gave extra credit options and was a fair grader.

reviews.comment: Professor Murga is extremely smart. His lectures, however, are also extremely boring. If you work hard to understand the material, you'll learn a lot. Murga's class will better prepare you for further chem-based courses rather than the other professor.

Murga is an all around great professor. The class is not easy but he is consistently available for extra help. reviews.comment: His lectures are somewhat useless because he just reads off the slides. Go to the recitation and you'll be ight

reviews.comment: Honestly, hard work pays off in this class. Pay attention in lectures, go to office hours, and put in the extra work and it's an easy A. There's really no surprises on the exams, and Murga is a really nice guy who is generous with extra credit.
This was an unnecessarily difficult course. The tests were really difficult and the lectures aren't very useful. The homework assignments were only slightly helpful.

Murga is clearly passionate about the material, makes a content heavy class as engaging as it gets. He treats students with respect and seems like a actually good guy. Midterms and final were online. The class average cumulative grade after the third midterm was an 85, so not the easiest class in the world. Don't buy the expensive textbook.

This class is really not that hard if you just keep on top of your work. Murga is super helpful during office hours. Homework assignments take 1-3 hours a week and there are 3 midterms that arent terrible but def require studying.

reviews.comment: He was very nice and approachable in office hours, even met on weekends when we asked. Very helpful and kind! The class was just extremely hard, so many of us really suffered. reviews.comment: A lot of complaints I have with this class are with the department. reviews.comment: professor was bad

He read right off the PowerPoint and he didnt really prepare or review what the final was like. While kind, his deliverance of content made it hard for people with little chemistry background.

Pr. Murga was asked to teach this class last minute and I think he did a great job. He was very understanding of students and always available to help. Im glad I had pr. Murga for this class.
Did a decent job. Have to learn the work outside the class somewhat, but is trying his best and wants students to learn.

I took two years of chem in high school and I felt like I lost information in his class. There's a lot of homework on a program called smartworks which is terribly designed and sometimes hard to use.

It was his first semester teaching this class. His PPts were quotes from the book and lectures were reading the Ppts. Reading the book and doing homework is the best way to learn. Hes hard to follow in class. The exams were rough unless you took AP chem. He gave a lot of extra credit at the end of the semester, which boosted everyones averages.

reviews.comment: Prof. Murga did a fine job. I didn't have any issues with his teaching style and he did his best to answer questions and make the lessons clear. If you go to class you'll do just fine.

Sits at his desk all lecture and talks at a very quiet volume. You could hear a pin drop in the room. Switched out after 2nd week. Stay away!
talks quietly, doesnt explain what hes doing, cant read his handwriting
simply can not teach

You are under spells people!! literally just write down and then learn the things he says in class and you will do completely fine!! 25% of your grade is determined by constitution quizzes, which are quite literally the easiest thing in the world. reviews.comment: The class was graded on two quizzes and a midterm, but as long as you take notes during class you'll be totally fine. If you miss a day get notes from a friend. reviews.comment: Prof Mayer is great. Offers coffee after class for students. Lectures are just him talking so you must take good notes for midterms and quizzes. You can tell he tries to connect with students. Having a TA might make this class perfect as he struggles with technology.

Very very nice professor who tried to connect with all students in the class. Lectures made up the entire class and was him talking the whole time. As long as you take notes and pay some attention the tests can be very easy. He provides study guides for midterm and final, and for the midterm gave us sample questions to practice with.

I honestly love professor Mayer! His lectures just include him talking the entire time but as long as you listen and take efficient notes you will be fine. If you actually put in effort and time studying for the reading quizzes you will also be fine. He's super straightforward and sweet, don't let these other ratings scare you away!

Definitely a harsh grader but if you write down literally everything he says, memorize it, and regurgitate it you will be fine lol! The reading quizzes are incredibly difficult and 20% of your grade...

Avoid this guy. Mayer is smart but is awful at teaching. Class is exclusively lectures in which he regurgitates what is on the Canvas slides. You will have to teach the material to yourself. reviews.comment: The lectures and slides were so boring and hard to pay attention to. Only 2 graded assignments, then the midterm and final. The final is worth 40%. He is very knowledgable, with high expectations. He is also very old-school and not tech savvy.

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable. Lectures well and provides real world examples for everything. If you're coming in with a basic understanding of American Government you do not need to attend lectures. Will occasionally say something very suspicious, but is overall a nice guy.

Just lectures the entire class period little participation or interaction. Can be extremely boring however he is nice enough and is knowledgeable and the class is extremely easy if you put in just a little effort. The midterm and final do make up 75% of the grade though and the last 25% is only a couple assignments.

He does not take accountability, has an awful attitude, grades far too difficulty, and is extremely bad at accommodating people regarding disabilities, etc. He also forces purchase of newest editions of book. Heavy reading, awful lectures, do not waste your time.

Professor Mayer is an amazing lecturer. He is interesting and great at structuring information that helps when studying for his exams. Professor Mayer is adorable and SO knowledgeable on what he teaches. I have now taken two classes with him, and intend on taking more of his classes if I can. reviews.comment: Professor Mayer is not prepared to be teaching from a virtual setting. Lectures were boring and grade was made up of three tests. Took over a month to get exams back. Professor Mayer gets a bad rep in my opinion. He is a conservative professor but doesn't let his views affect lecture in my opinion. reviews.comment: My fave thing about Dr. Mayer is that he's adorable (like how old people are adorable). He stutters a lot and wears sweaters that match the shirt he wears under and he draws TERRIBLY. Pretty much just take notes all class; he likes to give stats/graphs too. We had 1 piece of hw all semester. DON'T BOTHER GETTING THE TEXTBOOK. It's all in the notes.

The year is not done but American Government is a great class that Mayer lectures very well for. Lectures do not have Powerpoints but are clear and he makes what he's talking about interesting. There are very few assignments but his format and content at least for the midterm are unbelievably vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great guy, knows his subject very well. He has well thought-out lectures, and although he assigns readings most of the test material is from the lectures themselves. Only a midterm and a final exam, but he's a fair grader and gives you time to study. Lectures are long, but super interesting if you pay attention. Great professor all around.

great professor- definitely my favorite at northeastern. the lectures are really clear and well organized and the exams are a direct reflection of the material covered. it's very fair, no suprises. mayer made what could have been a very boring 100 minutes a very interesting time. i really don't have any criticisms, great guy, great class, period.

Mayer is a teacher's teacher. The guy clearly loves his job, and sitting in lecture with him is a pleasure. He class is all about connected historical narratives that are easy to comprehend. Tests can be somewhat quizzically graded, but you still learn a lot. I'd recompensed him for any class but quant.

He loves teaching this class, People who don't like him, are just cranky because you don't appreciate the awesomeness that is William T. Mayer. Super Clear, great guy, character, just an awesome teacher, super fair. I admire him greatly and he is very intelligent - Am Pol Thought

Mayer is the man.  Attendance not required but why would you want to miss class with this guy?  He is THE most fairest grader/professor ever.  Aside from being extremely intelligent,  his classes are very interesting.  Study like crazy two days before each test and you got a A or a B.

ok teacher. grades based on a midterm and a final, no attendance necessary, not really necessary to read the texts because he goes through things in class. pretty organized so easy to take notes, just listen in class and you'll do fine. funny guy, but not the most interesting nor intriguing class
good teach

he was awful. i attended every class, took down every note, restated what he said and more on the exams and got graded POORLY along with others. kids who didn't show up got good grades, unfair. boring as hell. will never take another class with him.. class was based on midterm+final. marked things wrong that he said were right in lecture.. AWFULLL.

Yes he's a dork, BUT he knows his stuff. Lectures are straight forward and his notes are clear as air.  Attending class makes it easy to pass without reading the "required" texts. NO HOMEWORK OR PAPERS. Take notes and regurgitate them on exams and you'll do well.

Listen up chumps... Mayer is the man. You can complain all you want, but until you've gotten one of his priceless gambling analogies, a show of his rightwing fury over Bill and Hillary, or some sarcastic response that solidifies his place amongst the academic elite, you just haven't lived. Give the man a B+; except when teaching Quant; that's a C-.

This is simple. He's rude to the point where its almost funny. NEVER take quant. tech. with him because he openly admits he hates teaching the class. BUT his other classes are easy, he's an easy grader, doesn't care if you're there or not, and makes the tests easy because by his own admission he hates grading/paper work.
Interesting class if you read the material. Gives clear notes so you know what to expect on the exam. Pretty easy grader too.
Get over the fact he's conservative- he's extremely smart, and unless you're a total cretin, you should easily pass this class.  It's very interesting, and if you take notes, the tests are a breeze.

Boring+Republican. Stutters like mad. Knows his stuff tho. only midterm and final for grades. I didn't buy the book, and never read anything for the class. If you go to class and takes notes, you'll do okay. Not particularly polite or helpful, but grades easy.If its between him and someone bad, take him. I hear hes not good w/ quant tech.

I'll make it simple. He's one of the worst teachers a Northeastern. Almost funny how rude he is. Way to many things to get into so the bottom is never take this class.For poli sci majors, try to wait until somebody else teaches it. During the first class,he made it obvious he didn't want to teach the class, so don't expect any extra effort from him

I can't figure out why this guy is allowed to teach this class. The class is the worst class I've ever taken. He doesn't make any sense and grades way too tough. Seriously, he'll yell at you for asking questions. Normal? Basically picture this; he's like that mean grade school principal you had. Terrible class, don't take it.
Light course load, only midterm and final.  But I didnt learn as much as i would have liked. His teaching style is a little lame.  If its between him and something you know sucks, take him.

DO NOT EVER TAKE THIS CLASS. He's rude, and very unhelpful. The subject would be simple, but his notes are unorganized and his examples and explanations do not make sense. This is the worst class I've ever taken in my life. Seriously. Unless you're a political science major, NEVER TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!!!!!

Okay, my last review was removed so maybe I was a little too truthful and descriptive, I'll tone it down. He's difficult to tolerate and he teaches a boring subject (Quant Tech) I apologize if I offend anyone but its a tough class solely due to the professor and his "Sicilian" accent. Unless you're Poli Sci major, avoid at all costs.
No Comments

Worst Class Ever.  He went over things about fifty million times and it was sooooo boring.  The final should have been easy but there was stuff that we had never gone over in class.  I would have liked the class so much better with any other professor.

Worst Class Ever.  He went over things about fifty million times and it was sooooo boring.  The final should have been easy but there was stuff that we had never gone over in class.  I would have liked the class so much better with any other professor.
hes a smart man, but not helpful at all, was very unclear, and added things on the final that we never learned.
I loved this class. Not the most exciting teacher, but very smart and helpful. Note: He's a Republican.

Very boring but organized notes. Literally no work, just midterm and final, most reading can be skipped too. A nice class to get a decent grade in that should be simple for most politically inclined students
No Comments
TOTAL DORK, the type u beat up for milk money..big blak was cool tho, Xcept 4 da Pru deal...meyer is a total nerd but since he is my neighbor its OK...lawn MOWERS FOR LIFE GEEK
No Comments
To warn you you will be bored to tears, but it's worth it for the limited amount of work and easy exams, for the most part the reading is unnecessary, easy A
Difficult class, lots of reading, and an impossible final.  What can i say except i might have learned something...and gotten a B, stupid ****
worst professor I've ever had. Do not take her class. She makes it nearly impossible to do well and her lectures are extremely outdated.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: None of her exams match what she teaches in class. Don't take her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you absolutely have to take this class for your major, I don't recommend taking this course if you have other difficult classes to focus on. You will need to consistently memorize all the material. Her exams are all multiple choice, but they are so hard because you need to memorize every word on her illegible lecture notes.

If there is ANY way you can take this course with a different professor, please stop reading and switch immediately. 
You must come to every single lecture, and you CANNOT be late. The attendance code is up for about 3 minutes at most, even though all lectures are recorded, and she'll barely ever answer questions in class. 
Average grade is a B-.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was unnecessarily difficult for an intro gen bio course. She expects memorization of both lecture content & slides, but slides are disorganized, making studying inefficient. Exams are very challenging & feel misaligned w what's emphasized in class. I recommend considering another instructor for Gen Bio I & II if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: exams were so much more difficult than they shouldve been. shes also pretty rude. worst 8am i couldve taken

Mary is extremely rude and demeaning to students. The icing on the cake was when she screamed "whoever cracks their knuckles next is getting thrown out of the room and receiving a zero" while we were taking our final exam in the dead silent lecture hall. Every question asked is returned with a sarcastic and humiliating response.Also awful teacher!!

i was terrified to take gen bio 2 with potts, but i promise she's not that bad. she's very polite (now at least, i've been told she was rude yrs ago), very enthusiastic and knowledgable. she's also generous with extra credit, scatters free points throughout the semester. my advice is do ALL extra credit. i was bumped up from a B+ to an A bc of it.
Gives so many extra credit opportunities. The class is lecture heavy but she reposts her lecture videos so you  can watch them on your own time.

I had her for Gen Bio 2, a 1000-level course which is supposed to be fairly straightforward and on general biology knowledge and concepts. Dr. Potts-Santone makes it 4000-level, extremely detail-oriented, and unnecessarily difficult. It is possible to do well in this course, but expect to spend a lot of hours each day studying the vast material.

One of the most abysmal experiences I've had in a college course. Dr. Potts-Santone is easily one of the most difficult professors I've ever had, and she is not friendly, approachable, nor helpful in any matter. Test/lecture heavy, difficult tests, but the silver lining is that she offers test corrections. Other than that, 1/10 experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Slides are so hard to read and she'll sometimes use black text on a black background for some reason. Her tests are unreasonably hard and really specific. Studying feels so exhausting because there's so much material. Overall though, it is an interesting course and she's usually eager to help you if you have any questions.

I was nervous entering her class this semester because of many negative experiences, but I found her to be a really good professor. Her tests were very difficult, but she gave opportunities to get points back. I think that she is a good professor and would recommend her in the future.

She knows her stuff, but lectures are so heavy and impossible to follow sometimes. Grade almost entirely depends on exams, and the questions for the exams ask for info not presented in class. There are opportunities for extra points, but they only sometimes make a difference. 1/3 of my class dropped because of failing grades so avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Potts-Santone really isn't as bad as people make her seem. She's a solid professor who really knows what she's talking about. If you attend the lectures and pay attention you'll do fine in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 100% not recommended

The tests were super specific. Even when I look back at the lectures, the tests were really difficult. Bad lecture slides. The questions on the tests were not about the slides half the time; they were on random specific things she said in class, so be prepared to listen to every little detail in lectures.

Sure, her tests were difficult and some questions were overly specific, but for the main part, she was very fair. Her expectations were clear so as long as you pay attention and study well you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Bio and AP Bio in high-school and still found Biology 1 challenging. You must be attentive during lectures and take notes. Expect to spend about 10-12 hours studying per exam and very detailed questions on the exam. Professor Potts-Santone is well equipped to teach the class and is passionate about what she does. Expect to put in work!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You don't actually learn anything in this class, you just memorize what you're told to. The tests are unreasonably hard, and she doesn't curve the grades, even when the class average is ridiculously low. She says she cares about our learning and wants us to pass, but she doesn't really act that way. There are lots of typos in her tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most of what's on the lecture slides isn't on the tests. You have to take really good notes on the slides, and the random details she tells you. There's an insane amount of memorization, and she doesn't really present it in a way that makes it reasonable to learn. I've already forgotten most of what I learned, and my final was yesterday.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I normally like classes like this where you're given information and have to memorize it, but this was just too much! So much material and not enough time to actually learn it all. The class is structured makes it seem like she doesn't actually care about whether or not you learn the content. No curve, so there's no room for error. Avoid her!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You're expected to memorize A LOT of stuff, without really learning any of it. The least the professor could do is try to make it interesting, but she doesn't even try to do that. It's just 100+ slides of pointless information for each exam. Tests are ridiculously hard and specific, and to top it all off, she doesn't even curve the grades. Terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had so far. Boring and disorganized lectures. Most of the class time is spent just listening to her drone on. This class was honestly probably one of the worst I've ever taken. I'm a health major so none of the content was interesting or meaningful to me. She tries to be funny and relatable, but it comes off as annoying.

The grade for Gen bio 2 was mostly dependent on 4 tests, which were difficult but not impossible. If you pay attention to lectures (lots of detail), study/rewatch her lectures you'll do fine, but I wouldn't say this class is an easy A. I thought this class was about the same difficulty as AP Bio
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Potts- Santone has it all together. Her lectures are well planned, and she posts recordings of lectures on blackboard. If you study and put in the effort the way she guides you to do so, you can get the A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: LOTS OF INFORMATION. Her tests are tricky and aim to mess with your head. If memorization is not your thing take another elective.

She is very knowledgable and passionate about Biology which made it more interesting to learn from her. She does talk fast and it can be hard to take notes and listen to all she has to say, but as long as you put the work in, should do fine. Recommend to take notes on everything she says, including the small examples and facts. Very good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Talks really fast during lecture, but records and posts every class via tegrity. DO NOT RELY ON TEGRITY! She gives extra credit sometimes to those who show up to her class on a given day because so many people make the mistake of relying on tegrity and those are typically the ones who don't do well. Her tests are tough,  but shes very approachable.
No Comments

Melloni was amazing and this class was great. It's an easy A (tests are online, open note, take-at home) and the material is not too rigorous because tests are online. I definitely recommend taking this class along some other harder ones, it doesn't require much outside work, but still interesting to learn about.

Prof Melloni is definitely one of the better professors I have had at NU. He makes neuroanatomy a bit more easy to understand, and is extremely receptive to questions and repeating things if the class doesn't understand. Your grade is just 5 online open note exams (20% each) and he drops the lowest one.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy A. Class is what you make it. 5 tests, all ONLINE (open note)... do with that info what you will, No HW, also drops lowest test grade. Attendance was never taken. Very good class to choose if you are taking other hard classes and want a lighter work load with this one. If you want to actually learn though, you have to lock in for it. SO chill.

Amazing and knowledgeable professor. He makes neuroanatomy which can be really difficult, easy to understand. He also uses many analogies and anecdotes in class to help us retain the information better.
Amazing amazing prof and person. Lectures were interesting and engaging. Your grade is made up of 5 open-note online tests. Is flexible and understanding, open to rounding grades. Take him!!!

Melloni was great for neuroanatomy. Our tests were take-home, which saves you for this class, because it would have been so much harder otherwise. Exams weren't too bad (the spinal cord one was the worst), he posts almost all the lectures on Canvas, and I think he ended up dropping the lowest exam grade. Grade is made up of only 5 exams.

Really interesting class. The only thing is that you are graded by only exams--no other assignments. This means if you do badly on one, you're cooked (happened to me :( ). I also found one or two of the exams pretty difficult. Overall, would recommend, just lock in and don't neglect studying!

You can tell he really likes the subject when he's teaching and he explains complicated concepts in a really clear way!! Your grade just depends on how well you do on your exams but your exams are all online AND multiple choice/matching!

actually the goat. he simplified neuroanatomy down so well, which is def not an easy task. attendance isn't mandatory and he does post zoom recordings of his lectures, but i would still go to class or watch the recordings because the lectures are super helpful. grade is made up of 5 exams, he ended up dropping the lowest exam score!

Best professor in the psych department and it's not even close. If you're a pre-med major you need to take his class. He teaches all 3 major BNS courses - biopsych, psychopharm, and neuroanatomy. Great lectures, actually cares about the students, and tests are online take home (still difficult though). Makes even the hardest topics make sense. Goat

Prof Melloni honestly made me even more passionate about neuroscience and medicine than before. He taught in medical school and is amazing at simplifying complex neuroanatomy topics. 5 exams all taken online/open note but they can be difficult--final is not cumulative. He really cares about his students and almost everyone loves his classes. 10/10

Melloni is the goat. All tests online, take-home, and if you go to class you'll do just fine. He does a great job breaking down the hardest units into simple terms. And he teaches the big 3- Neuro, Psychopharm, and Biopsych.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE HIM!!!

TAKE THIS CLASS best teacher i've ever had the lectures are so interesting he knows EVERYTHING about neuroscience and the content we do is really interesting. theres 4 or 5 exams over the semester that are only on the recent topic you did (not cumulative) and they are online. the exam average is usually a 90. TAKE THIS CLASS ITS THE BEST THING EVER

Attendance is mandatory if you want to do well, he is a phenomenal professor and I have learned so much from him! He is hilarious, interesting, and engaging. His exams can be scary but you just have to study hard and write questions for him as you review, because he will answer them very thoroughly and always help you when you need it!

Dr. Melloni is one of the best professors I've ever had, his lectures are very interesting and he perfectly breaks concepts down so that they're better understood.
