Going to class was like listening to a Ted talk. The professor is passionate, and gets you to think about how economics has become our culture. Recommend if you want to exercise your thinking.

I did not know what to expect, most discussions on race deal with statistical differences. This class focused on the economic context of what creates statistical differences and highlight the relationship between beliefs and societal outcomes and how culture normalizes and legitimizes based on dominant beliefs. Good course.
really nice and easy course to take with her-- she does a lot of preaching though which are true but not always engaging

Dr. Venkatesan is very passionate about microeconomics and her lectures are usually her going on tangents. She really only cares about making sure you know the material. She said to buy the textbook but I never purchased it and we didn't use it once. There are three exams and there's an in-class and online portion. Its a lot of writing but easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a very passionate and invested professor in class and brings a lot to lectures. However, her lectures are extremely loosely organized, there are no slides and hardly any notes. She seems to just go on tangents. Almost a full month of the course was either not in class or over zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Madhavi is extremely passionate about the subject and has a broad knowledge. Although difficult and time-consuming, the homework and assigned readings push you and make you understand the subject well. In the end, it is well worth it. She hosts talks for extra credit that hold tons of valuable information and good discussion.

Super easy grader, tests are very doable (also she only gives tests in ECON1116!) and doesn't give a formal final. Lectures often go off on tangents about things she's passionate about, but we manage to learn material and she makes it easy to understand. She gives a lot of grace and is willing to hear students out. Easy A with actual learning too.
The class was awesome. Would definitely recommend in my opinion one of the easiest sections of principles of Microeconomics you can get.
She is an extremely sweet professor and goes over the context in depth. You are basically guaranteed an A as long as you complete all the homework and self-study the material.

Prof Venkatesan is my favorite professor EVER. Reading-intensive course, required to write a lot of papers but she did not deduct a point from all the assignments as long as you have a proper citation format. She loves to offer opportunities for students. Greatest professor ever.

Sustainability Econ challenged my notions of the entire field. Prof V is an excellent individual and professor. Some days, upwards of 60 pgs reading nightly, but most students will earn an A in her courses. Lots of writing. Short essays due every day during summer and 2-3 large papers a course. Easy grader, but lots of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Discussion-based class with lots of readings and an assignment every day. I didn't really like the way she ran the class with somewhat random lectures, but overall if you do the work it will be an A. She is generally nice and is willing to help if you need it. I recommend if you are interested in sustainability/the environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Venkatesan is my favorite professor. She does a good job at explaining her concepts clearly. The class made me critically rethink everything I knew about Economics. She is so inspirational and everyone here that says the class was boring are total losers. Dont take the class just for the easy grade, take it if ur genuinely passionate.

Her lectures are long and she doesn't give a break but you can take a break during her lecture as you please. I honestly didn't find the lecture super helpful to the actual assignments but sometimes it was very interesting to participate in them. She's a very nice grader and will ask you to re-write a paper if she can't at least give you a B!
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class required a lot of work and writing. However, I didn't lose a point the whole semester, so it's more about just doing everything assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: amazing prof!

These are facts, not opinions- 1. An assignment is due before almost every class 2. No exams 3. Philosophical talks in the middle of lectures is common 4. Rarely gives breaks in 100-minute lectures 5. Full points for almost all assignments (grades are uploaded weeks after submission) Conclusion- The class is easy but gets irritating quite soon.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The professor will try to give you as many CV opportunities as she can throughout the semester. she is very very understanding, and very passionate about the subject that she teaches. She is a popular economist, one of the very nice teachers at northeastern. Something due every class, its a small writeup, no exams, only assignments. Best for 1000 l

I thought this professor wasn't gonna be bad, but ended up getting tanked with reading and work. Would recommend taking any other professor, my friends took the same class and had half the work as I did. Also, grades very harsh and that says something because I put in upwards of 5-10 hours a week on this course

Talia Vestri is one of the kindest and most supportive professors I've ever had. I highly recommend her. If you just attend class on time and complete all the assignments, you're definitely going to earn an A.

If you do attend every class and complete the papers on time, you are likely to get a good grade. All the papers are graded by effort and completion. The class itself can be a bit boring and non-helpful, but it is a good intro to writing class to take.

All you have to do is show up on time and submit the work.  There isn't much work at all and when there was work you didn't need to spend more than an hour on it.  She seemed to be against university as a system of learning which is strange as a yk... university professor?  If you can write a high school level essay, you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy class, she grades based on completion so as long as you show up and submit assignments on time, you're good. Some of her assignments were a bit annoying and discussions were repetitive. If you speak in discussion she will ask you a ton of follow-up questions, which can get annoying. But she's a good person and tries to make class interesting.

Dr. V definitely cares for her students wants us to learn, and has a nice grading policy (as long as you do the work - you'll get an A). She also gave us plenty of flex time to use on assignments. It was not an unreasonable amount of work at all, and she always gave us thorough feedback.
Class is graded on completion. Complete your work and you get an A. 2 projects, every week you build on it. Should take around 2 hours a week to complete all assignments
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Personal opinions often shine through during teaching, but it usually doesn't get in the way.
Great feedback on essays, strong revision process, very nice in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's fine. Very uninspiring class but Prof V is nice enough. If you can write (e.g. did you take English in hs?? are you literate??) you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: We had homework/reading due for every class but never received any kind of credit so I just stopped doing them. The class was an easy A but we are only graded on the 3 papers. A lot of class is busy work or just working on your paper/peer editing it.

Dr. V is a pretty good English teacher. She does give a ton of feedback, and we have a ton of time in class to work on our papers. While the class is only graded off of three papers, we do spend a lot of time working on them, so it isn't too terrible. She is very reasonable, and she does want to see her students do well.

Dr.V clearly organized every week's schedule and provided ample feedback. We were graded only one a few papers so each one held a lot of wait, but she very much wanted to see every student succeed and was always available to meet outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: We got over HALFWAY through the semester without a single grade. She never put grades in Canvas so you have no idea what your grade is. Instead, she just sent us an email 3/4 of the way through the semester giving us a rough range of what our grade is. The class is graded based on only 3 papers. She gives us homework but we don't get credit for it.

I have no idea why this rating is so low; amazing teacher. Extremely knowledgeable, walks through problems and posts good practice exams. She explains the content thoroughly, so it can be confusing to some.

Veliche is a sweet lady and all, but she teaches old-fashioned with a whiteboard and while half of the class is fighting demons trying to copy down notes, she mumbles to herself proofs that no one understands. this course is too proof-heavy which means self-studying and practicing is a must to get a good grade. This class made me lose love for math

I have never done so bad in a math class. This class was conducted poorly due to the professor's old fashion teaching and only writing on the whiteboard. The entire class time is spent frantically copying down notes on the board instead of understanding concepts. There are also daily homework to be done as a group.

(MATH 2331) Overall good professor and clear lectures.  There is optional homework but if you want an A you should definitely do it.  I managed to get a B without really studying at all and just reviewing before exams, you just need to know how to apply formulas.  Maybe there is a bit more proof stuff in this section compared to other professors.

not the best during lectures, but she gives us a lot of material to work with and if you do optional textbook homeworks as well as the practice quizzes you will be fine for the weekly quiz. preparing for the midterms is also easy as she gives several past midterms to practice with.
She was fire.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Oana is a very nice and caring person and very available via email. Maybe she's just not my style, but her teaching style is just extremely old fashioned. We have exit tickets, notes are often not posted, and she seems to not be fully prepared to explain her thought process in lectures. Lots of arrows with vague labels. I just read the textbook.

ok she's a nice person but she REALLY CANNOT EXPLAIN AT ALL!!! skips over a lot of explanations and jumps around, you will be completely confused about her lectures if you don't already know linear algebra well or take tutors outside of class. Again she's a really nice person but I'm just not sure she qualifies as a math professor
Fantastic professor, very available via email, very caring.

Took me some time to get used to, but I grew to love the class. She is a really sweet person and has your best interest. I would recommend going to class, but she does post handwritten notes and has helpful office hours. The weekly quizzes are a good reflection of the work done in class and past years quizzes are given for ample practice.

Lectures were always recorded but attendance was encouraged because we had graded class problems that were done in small groups. She is a very caring and kind professor, responds to emails quickly, and offered generous extra credit. Sometimes its a little hard to follow her notes but she is always accessible for extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Oana gets some hate, but I honestly dont see why. Her lectures covered everything you needed to know for quizzes and tests, and she did lots of examples in class. Homework is optional and she gives lots of extra credit. She really wants you to succeed on tests and quizzes, so she gives plenty of review and tells you exactly what you need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: nice person but very confusing explanations especially in the first 3rd of the class when talking about gradients. gradewise, doing the homework will result in a good grade even if you dont understand why anything works

Her lectures could not be followed. Professor Veliche taught mostly on the whiteboard, and did not have a logical train of thought for solving problems or lecturing. She would just jump around not explaining the problem well. That being said, she is a very kind and caring person and obviously cares about the course.

She's a really sweet woman but she's definitely not the best at teaching. Homework load is the same as other professors (not mandatory BUT appear on the tests/quiz). Her grading can be pretty strict but she definitely doesn't want you to fail. She's given us take homes after we all bombed a quiz before. Love the woman but wouldn't take her again.
She is a very nice lady, but also a very tough grader. Heavy homework and hard exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a lovely woman, but not a good professor.  Her lectures are unclear and she does not answer question adequately at all.  I would have done a lot better in this class if I had a different professor.  She made me not like calculus anymore because I could not understand it.

This class (regardless of professor) is really tough. However, Prof. Veliche does her best to teach you all the material clearly. Extremely welcoming & helpful in office hours. At the end of the semester she gives extra points for overall attendance and homework (asks you show her all you have done in the semester). Gives practice tests.

She's a very nice woman who is always willing to help. That being said, she is not the best teacher. She sometimes lacks understanding of the material, and students often correct her in class. She does not explain material very clearly, and her thick accent sometimes makes things difficult to understand. However, she does want students to do well.

Veliche is a nice woman but an absolutely horrible teacher. She does not explain the material efficiently or effectively often leaving students unprepared for the final exam. Avoid taking her at all costs if you can.
She is friendly and nice but  did not show command over the material during teaching.
She's good at math, but she's not very good to teach. Confuses the majority of the students.

He does not give clear instructions on rubrics of assignments, so you might get surprise points taken off. He does not write any of it down or explain it, so you have to guess. He also does not teach and just yaps in class. Also bad at organization; the slides he posts are not listed with the chapter they cover but as random numbers.
He gives pop quizzes but they are not hard at all. He is a very generous grader and a very nice guy. He also has great humor.

Fully asynch course but if you needed help getting points, you just imessage or call him. He cares less about the work and more about your success so if you communicate often, interact with the canvas page (he tracks clicks and time on it for participation) you will do well. He really cares about the outcome of his students!

He's a nice guy but it was so hard to read him. It seemed like he was a different person everyday. He was hypocritical. He showed up 30 minutes late one day but scolded students if they showed up 5 minutes late. Super unclear expectations! He said we did amazing on a project, then gave us a terrible grade.

horrible teacher. Avoid at all costs, I dont think he knows what hes actually teaching. You will not learn anything from this class. Use ur tuition towards another class, not this. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Awesome professor! Definitely make sure to get a good group in the beginning of the semester for the simulation. The class is super interesting and interactive. He is very accessible outside of class and always there to answer questions if you have any. The content is difficult, but Prof. Muscolino makes it fun.

He's a nice guy, but if you're not the biggest fan of group work do not take this class. Literally every assignment is a group assignment except for the connect homeworks. The assignments can be long and complex. There are two presentations, a midterm and a final, both online.
Teacher is very responsive and knowledgable on the markets. Easy class but some assignments are very time consuming so plan accordingly. Lots of busy work.

Wonderful man and professor. The class is engaging, and Professor Muscolino does a good job integrating current news and events into behavioral finance concepts. Participation matters and group assignments and presentations are the norm. Find a good group of students and take ownership of the casework for specific companies, and you will have fun!

Overall a good professor. In BUSN1101 you work with the same group for the entire semester on one project, so if you get a bad group that can screw you. But overall really nice and funny guy, he genuinley cares about how his students do.

Professor Muscolino is a wonderful person and a great professor. With the right amount of outside effort and interest I think most people can perform well in the class. He's always accessible outside of class, and genuinely wants you to succeed as a human as well as a student. The course has group projects which are fun and informative. He's great!

Course not required for busn major & not useful, filled with fluff. Demo days were stressful, required hours of prep. Prof was unclear about expectations, lacked organization with his teaching, seems chill but would grade harshly on easy hw's. When asked for feedback he could not give me good reasons either. Group you end up with matters a lot!
If you want to get a good grade but learn nothing take his class. Online organization is horrendous and he is a horrible lecturer. Nice guy though.
The tests are SO hard and extensive to the point where you may not finish even with studying for days.

Really nice guy, but the majority of actual learning comes from the textbooks. Group projects were interesting but I found the combo of too little guidance + grading projects on a strict rubric to be frustrating. Course materials are disorganized, deadlines updated on the fly (keep your Canvas notifications enabled or else you'll miss something).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is a very nice, funny, and lenient professor who is passionate about what he teaches. He covers a wide array of subjects, responds to emails, and gets us working together to create pitches.

Professor Muscolino gives out a year-long project at the beginning of the school year, so choose your groupmates wisely. You must buy the textbook to do Connect assignments. One midterm (20%) and final exam (20%) were both taken upon the professor's decision and the class's preference.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Muscolino is one of the sweetest and most caring professors I've had. Some of his assignments can be unclear if you miss class but he's very willing to help and is extremely accessible. You can tell that he genuinely is passionate about the subject - highly recommend him if you want a prof that gives you industry insights.
Extreme lack of structure, does very little to no explaining. The bulk of his lectures is him going on Bloomberg and talking. Also an unreasonable amount of work for this class. Didn't learn anything
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Firstly, Professor Muscolino does not deserve anything less than a 3. Only downside is that he is disorganized and can be hard to follow sometimes. However, he is not a hard grader, students will always be doing very manageable group work. Exams are online open note and questions are straight forward. Extra credit also offered frequently.

Vincent Muscolino is a very nice man but stays clear if you are not planning to teach yourself all the content outside the normal class time. I hate to say it, but one of the least teaching professors at Northeastern.

Teaches nothing in class other than Bloomberg terminal and he expects students to be prepared for exams. You will not learn anything throughout this class and I highly recommend any other option. Thinks he's the funny guy alive and has no idea how to teach.

TERRIBLE experience. Professor Muscolino was wildly disorganized and painfully dull. Absolutely 0 clarity in what was expected of us for projects and assignments, and asking him questions generated vague answers and even more confusion. I am not sure what the quality of other professors is in this department, but definitely avoid this one.

He is trying to be funny, but he's not. He likes to talk about Bloomberg and other stuff in class. Be prepared to learn all the formulas and concepts by yourself, cuz he ain't teaching in class. The homework is crazy, we never learned anything related to what's on the homework.

He is a caring man who wants his students to succeed. The class material was easy and graded easily, despite sometimes him taking off points without explaining why. Make sure you get a good group because the entire class is based on group work. He was also confusing about what is due, especially readings. Still a nice guy and VERY accessible.

Muscolino is a good guy and tries to be funny, but he is really unorganized and struggles to communicate. His rubrics are napkin scratch that has never been revised. The midterm, final, and projects (emphasis on the plural) were all so brutal. Don't take him for corporate finance if you have any other options.
ONE OF THE GREATEST FINANCE PROFESSORS EVER. Very lucky to have him here at Northeastern University!

I give him credit that he had passion and was always reachable outside of class, but he did not convey the material in an effective manner. Many of the concepts were not explained thoroughly enough to understand for the tests.

Vinnie is a great guy, he wants to be accessible and fun but my god this man is the most disorganized mess. What we should read? Doesnt explain it. Module slides are unhelpful and confusing. He doesnt lecture or teach, half the semester is spend on a stock project. This is the first class I have come out of asking did I even learn anything? Awful
Was viewing rate my professor grades for past professors and glad to see that Muscolino still doing what he does best. Never left a review for my course, but dude is a gem.

He was a great professor. I actually felt like we touched on abstract questions related to investments in class as oppose to the normal NU finance requirement classes where we just read the textbook (via PPTs) in class and work on end of chapter problems (what boring people love doing).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I like his style of teaching, but he is not for everyone. don't take him if you know nothing about investments, extremely hard to keep up if you are unfamiliar with the industry

The greatest. Works in the investment industry and it shows (the course project is on valuing a stock). Dude is also funny if you get to know him (ends class with a joke of the day).
Awesome guy. Really enjoyed the course and learned a lot. Would definitely take a class of his again.

Look, he's a great guy and really cares about engaging students with the subject matter. Excellent prof that gives easy to understand examples.  Saw an old interview online of him on cnbc.  Knows his stuff.
Definitely the best prof i have taken at neu.  He is from the investment industry so he gives interesting realworld examples.  Also takes a lot of time with students. I highly recommend his class.

One of the best professors I had at NEU. I think people who dont like him dont understand how to compbine theory with the real world

He really doesn't teach all that well. He is a nice guy and tries to be friends with his students. He thinks he knows everything and that he teaches us everything, but he doesn't. A lot of self-studying. Welcome to college
Nice but boring

He's a real nice person for sure, but he often appears very distant and unclear. He's the type of professor that you need to see during his office hours for him to be effective. His grading is very fair and likes to joke around a lot.

Prof muscolino was just grand. His class was my favorite ever I learned a lot. His availability was the the advantage of us because he was always available. If you don't like prof muscolino then you don't like finance! Favorite teacher ever

excellent class. professor muscolino will spend lots of time answering your questions and really helps you learn financial modeling. this class is super interesting and follows the stock market closely. a great teacher who really cares that we succeed. this class is worth signing up for.

It was a challenging class, but kept my interest with real world experience of my professor. I learned so much about finance and investments.  It gave me a insight how Finance is so crtical in todays economic environment.

Classes were so boring. Very hard to stay concentrated on the course. Makes Investment finance uninteresting. Very superficial class. I havent learned a lot even though the teacher is really nice. This was a great class.  Professor Muscolino is the best Finance professor I have ever had at Northeastern.  His practical applications of financial theory really helped me learn. Very helpful.  Uses real world examples.  Take this class!

Prof Muscolino was great at relating real world examples.  What really helped me is the time he took to help me succeed in this class.  He made himself available where as other Professors handed me off to their aides!
Professor Muscolino is a great teacher.  He uses real world examples of how to apply finance and valuation methodologies.  I finally understand regression as well.

This class is so boring. No tests, just straight projects. 3 of the same projects per semester... these projects take FOREVER. First project was due after spring break. Waste of a class really... didn't learn anything we didn't learn in corporate finance.

He is one of the best professors in the computer science department. The lectures are amazingly explained, you will gain a lot of intuition just by listening to the lectures and solving the homework problems.
im not a masochist but this class be turning me into one
Very unresponsive

Fantastic professor. Extremely intelligent and passionate about math. Very helpful during office hours and lecture. Asks a lot out of students but very worth it.

I'm here to comment just because of his "some Russians live forever" joke.

Professor Virgil is amazing, and it is very evident he cares about his students. The final grade was essentially determined by an 8-hr midterm and 6-hr final that have a high level of difficulty. Great teaching

Prof.Pavlu explains things very well so if you follow him during the lectures you can understand the concepts pretty well. Assignments are hard but they really helped me understand the lectures better. I learned so much from him this semester and would love to take another course with him again.

reviews.comment: There are many topics that the professor could explain better, and provide more straightforward demos. But overall, Prof. Pavlu does a decent job and this course(CS5800) covers the essential materials. I cannot complain about that.

Smart guy, realistic, and upfront about the difficulty of this class, but that doesn't really help when this class is a core req for several programs. if you want to gain useful knowledge in AI, you should choose other professor

I took Professor Wertheim's negotiation class in the Fall of 2023 and still use the skills I developed almost two years later. Professor Wertheim is an incredibly caring and supportive man that is very knowledgable in his field. I urge everyone to experience at least one of his classes if you have the opportunity to do so. Professor Wertheim is one of the most well-respected professors at Northeastern! The class consists of weekly negotiation sessions, as well as a few assignments and open-book quizzes. fun lecture + wholesome professor, you learn a lot of negotiation skills, weekly negotiation sessions with peers

Without a doubt one of my favorite professors at NU. His lectures are practically stand up comedy sets and its even better if you have a class group that is just as involved. My favorite professor at NU and my most memorable class. He is hilarious and makes class interesting. You negotiate every class but so worth it. Average homework is around 2hrs/week. Please take him if you can! If you try and apply what you learn in class, you'll do good.

Best professor and best class taken at Northeastern. Average hw is about 1.5hrs/week, and the quiz is open notes. If you do what he asks, and reflect, you'll be fine. Extremely interactive class, negotiating every week. You learn a lot.

Wertheim is the best professor I have ever had hands-down. He cares so much about his students and puts SO much time into giving feedback to each and every person. Great class, even better professor. Professor Wertheim gives very clear instructions and feedback that its almost hard to not do well in his class. One of the nicest professors ever, he wants everyone to succeed, it feels like. Loves in class participation.

Excellent, most fun I have had in any class. Amazingly made me happy to wake up at 8:00 on Saturdays. If going into anything related with sales, it is a must!!

She is awesome. If you listen - you are gonna get a good grade. Take notes of the examples on the board cuz quizes are very similar to them and to the practice quizes.
Prof. Wu taught in an intelligent way, made sure everyone understood the material, and was willing to help.  She is the best math teacher I've ever had.

Great Professor! Hard to understand but she's adorable and really tries to help you if you try in her class. The material was a joke but I already had two years of calculus before this class. I took this class because everyone here says shes awesome! You're in for a very bad joke. She has a VERY thick accent that you just can't understand her. Su Wu is an amazing teacher! She is so nice and the practice tests are exactly like the real thing!

She is by far one of the best professors that ive ever had in my life. the review sheets help out alot on tests and if you go to her office hours thats extra brownie points for you. she yelled at me alot for not getting stuff although i had a 98 average in her class. dont ask stupid questions and just go to class cause she knows when you dont go.

Professor Wu rocks my mathematical world! She really squares my roots and and dots my imaginary i's. Her accent is contagious. I find myself speaking like her on a regular basis. Awesome.  She has an accent but if you pay attention to her you get used to it.  she gives a lot of examples and is always helpful. if you go to class pay attention and study the quiz reviews your garunteed an A.  The quiz reviews are almost exactly like the quizzes same with the midterm and final, respect here and shell respect her shell respect y
Prof. Wu is a good math teacher. She gave a lot of examples and explained them thoroughly. She was very enthusiastic and eager to help. I love Prof Wu.
one of the best professors.

Her heavy accent was the most difficult aspect of class. A kid actually got a refund for the class when his dad (a lawyer) complained about it. The kid was just dumb though, and I was equally as dumb b/c I didn't do well but I liked her alot.

Prof. Wu is a great teacher. She explains material well and is willing to help. If you attend the class and pay attention, it is easy to get a good grade. I never did math well before, but I am doing very well in this course.
Prof Wu is the best math teacher i've ever met. I used to hate math. Now i like math because of Wu.
wu is a great math professor. she is patient with us.
dont get on her bad side

Professor Wu is a wonderful person and an excellent mathematics professor. She is always willing to help her students and really cares about their grades. The class project is kind of awful, but as long as you follow the directions, you should be fine.

She is the best teacher I have ever had.  She is extremely nice person. She loves teaching!  She helps a lot! Her explanation is easy to understand. If you don't miss her class, you can get an A easily.
Great teacher.  She explains everything so it is easy to comprehend.  Tests and quizes are very similar to the reviews.  Easy A is you go to class and pay attention.

She is the best teacher ive had yet.  Her accent is difficult to understand at times but to compensate she teaches very slowly and writes everything on the board very clearly.  Grade is based on 6-7 quizes and she drops the lowest grade.  The quiz review mirrors the actual quiz.  I love Wu.
Pretty easy class. Quizzes are based on the Quiz reviews. Just study for the midterm and final. Don't even have to do the homework. Shes a pretty nice woman though hard to understand sometimes.

She is an alright teacher. Sometimes it's a bit hard to understand her because of her accent but she always makes sure to help anyone who is confused.
A very sweet lady. Wants you to know the information and constantly asks students to come to her for help. She's not that hard to understand like some ppl complain about. I recommend her class.

She was a pretty easy teacher. Be careful with the class project... Tests weren't too hard. She's willing to give extra help as long as you're willing to put in the time. Despite her accent, a great teacher.
OH I loved her! Depsite the thick accent, she means well. The reviews for quizzes and exams made the class easier. The final project was ridiculously easy!
shes a good professor.  her accent is a little tricky to get used to, but after that, she's sweet.  She gave reviews for every quiz and major test and made sure we knew the material.
Her accent is impossible and she only helps the kids who already know calc, if you are a troubled math student stay away from her!

shes an awesome teacher. and u just wanna pinch her cheeks shes so cute!! and shes so so nice.

Great teacher...teaches with a million examples which is great. The only people who don't like her are the ones who do bad in the class and blame it on her thick accent, which I didn't find very hard to understand at all. Definitely take her class.
This is the best math teacher I have ever had. Her accent is strong but she more than makes up for it. Her review sheets are a major plus, I wish all math teachers were like her.
Despite her somewhat difficult to understand accent, she was a decent  teacher.  The review sheets were quite helpful, and she wanted people to do well.
Hated this class, she is too hard to understand and only heps the kids that are doing well in the class
Aw, shes soo cute! Def wants everyone to understand the material. Quiz Reviews, etc. are excellent and very helpful! Dont drop this class...it's great!

Very good class.  Review sheets are almost identical to the quizzes and midterm if you do that you should do great.  She wants all of her students to understand the work.  one of the best teachers i have ever had

Best math teacher I have had thus far in this school. Her strong accent takes a little to get used too, but once you get used to it, the class becomes better. She goes out of her way to teach the stuff.
Awesome professor and person, I loved his class even as a non-math person

Peter was a good professor and cares abt his students. Attendance wasn't taken everyday but it was a surprise so people should j go to class. Only 2 tests (midterm and final). reviews.comment: Professor Xu is the first instructor who genuinely made me understand and enjoy math. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would recommend you show up to class; he regularly gives hints for exams and answers for projects. Fun lecturer if you pay attention. Light workload. Easily one of the best professors I've had.

Peter Xu was nothing short of phenomenal. He makes an effort to understand everyone's background regarding statistics and constantly makes time to help you outside of class if you need assistance. I had zero stats history and yes at times not going to sugar coat it I was confused but because of the kind of professor he is I could figure it out.

Really good at explaining concepts, likes it when you ask clarifying questions, reasonable grader, nice person, thick Chinese accent but didn't actually get in the way of any understanding for me at least.
Good prof. Also, this prob is in Business school, not the Math dept.

Peter is a caring professor with a lot of knowledge of stats. He can be frazzled when teaching and doesn't follow a specific slideshow or textbook. The first time I want to write a review for a professor, the best teacher in neu!

There's 2 projects and homework due every week (but not th week there's a project). I would've had an A but I never showed up and didn't realize participation (attendance) mattered. He lowkey doesn't speak very good english but he's honestly a fun lecturer if you're paying attention and the work is fairly straightforward.
The written exams are the worse part of the course because it's memorization.70% of your grade is exams!
Teacher is chill, take them
Not the worst class, but definitely frustrating. Lectures often felt disorganized and assignments required a lot of guesswork.

reviews.comment: Lecture content was a little boring but she found ways to make it interesting and interactive. She gave a lot of examples and content needed to complete the homework successfully.

Weekly at home quizzes that are extremely easy. The final is a group project that is not too much work. There is a few homework assignments, but they are all fairly simple. Easy for a 4000 level class, lectures are boring and optional and she posts the filled out notebook at the end of the week. Definetly take for easy A.

There is a group project, but she makes an effort to pair you with people with similar work styles to you if you don't have someone to work with.

The class itself is fairly easy. The lectures are kinda boring as Prof. Yang reads off the slides most of the time. Going into the first lectures, I expected the class to be very interesting based on the material. Grades based on hw, weekly online quizzes and group project.

She's not bad. Attendance isn't mandatory as class is available on zoom and notes are posted. Homework can be a lot, but she responds promtly to emails. Lecture itself wasn't very interesting but she was helpful during office hours and understanding when an extension is required.

Horrendous. Does not care about you or your education. Assignments, although very easy, are unclear and often blatantly missing instruction. Her lectures are horrible, as she silently copies code from her notes zoomed too far in to follow. If you want an easy A without having to go to lecture, take this course before she gets fired.

Not that bad but the written exams were kinda weird because they tested you on facts some of the concepts. I learned enough about using sklearn and gradient descents. The class is pretty free if you stay on top of the conceptual stuff. Coding exams were probably easiest. Wouldn't recommend though

DS 4200: Lectures are pretty boring and useless. When she codes she just copies down what she has in her notes, it doesn't seem like she really understands the material she's teaching. She can be helpful if you ask and the homeworks and projects are not difficult.

The written exams are the worse part of the course because it's memorization. It's either a hit or miss and 60% of the grade is exams, projects were cut out of the content.

I had to double check that the Professor's name was correct because I couldn't believe the ratings. This class is such a waste of time. Professor Wang is probably too bored to take this class seriously, and it shows. You learn a bunch of outdated tech and buzzwords that won't get you anywhere in the real world. Complete waste of time.

very subjective grader and the lectures are impossible to pay attention to/learn from. somehow i managed to get a 82 on the final studying two days before/95 in the class after barely paying attention or learning anything all semester so take that as you will.

Wang is a sweet, caring, and funny guy. The class is incredibly boring (for me) and the lectures don't help with that, but that isn't his fault. He is a light grader and wants success for us!

Good teacher, but an extremely boring subject. The class feels obsolete. The grading is clear for the most part. Aced the class! The exam was tough, even for open book, but I managed to pull through. The final project was fun.

I came to this course with a limited background in programming due to my field. I spent considerable time and effort, and it proved rewarding. The instructor shared all course materials and codes, which was very helpful for learning and review. I gained valuable insights into data mining and machine learning, and I am pleased with my final grade.

Professor Wang is passionate about the course and very knowledgeable about information systems. His lectures were well organized and he tried to make them exciting. He's caring, encouraging, and fair. The Excel and SQL assignments were actually fun. Overall, I truly enjoyed this course.
This professor is amazing. No joke, lectures are interesting, and his grading seems fair. Not gonna complain.

This teacher is super nice and tries to keep class engaged. Lectures are long and kind of boring but he tries to add in videos to switch it up. Info on PowerPoint slides isn't always in the textbook. reviews.comment: This professor is great. The class is completely lecture based which can get boring but the information itself is interesting and the projects are fun and easy.

Good professor, great lecture.

Prof. Wang's course covers a wide scope of topics but he helped apply real-world company examples and topics to contextualize them. He is knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the topics. Most importantly, he cares about students.

Super chill and caring. Gives credit just for writing your name on tests, I studied 3 hours for each of the 3 tests, and was heavily overstudied for them. You'll learn a bunch. Homework are the only hard thing just take your time and start them a week in advance

Took the effort to learn almost everyone's name in our lecture, which is impressive for a DS prof. Def would take again.

Professer Yu is very caring towards his students and about the course content, and he wants to make sure you understand the content. Lectures aren't always engaging and attendance isn't mandatory, but there are opportunities to talk to TAs or the professor if questions come up. Labs are easy and make up 20%, homework's are long but manageable, only 3. Theres a final project (26%) at the end that's very time consuming but everyone gets an A. quizzes are final 24%.

The HW in this class is HEAVY, but that's the same for every professor in the section. Deahan is very nice and understanding, extremely knowledgeable, and really wants his students to understand the material and succeed. I would absolutely take him again, he was fantastic.

Lectures weren't the most engaging but he means the best for all students. Quizzes and homeworks were mostly straightforward with some challenging applications, but for the most part, professor yu is your guy.
Very caring professor who wants his students to do well. If you do all your work and put effort into the group project you should do well.

Really Nice Professor, genuinely has one of warmest vibes. The HW can be a lot, and some quiz things are a bit questionable, but overall, it's super easy to get an A in this class if you just put a little work in, and you know basic Python.

I appreciated how he learned students names who participated in class and went to office hours. Though attendance was not mandatory I recommend going! Very helpful and nice professor and a pretty easy class if you turn everything in.

10/10 Professor. I didn't expect my any ds professor to care but he have us alot of extra credit. Your final will be a project. Attendance is optional but u should def go. Great Professor. Gives extra credit and is very caring. He gives surveys each class(for extra credit) and listens to them and adjust based on that. The labs and hw are the hardest part. Overall it's a hard class but he does everything in his power to teach and help u understand. Also plenty of gas ta's to help. Good prof.

Prof Yu has been very accomodating with our needs, he actually changes teaching style and deadlines on the fly to respond to our feelings in his daily survey. I don't know why people giving him poor rating, I think he is a very good professor, he explained the material clearly, has a organized logic for his teaching. Exam could be difficult, but if you follow his lecture, you would be fine.
I had a very tough time with him he makes a complicated subject even harder avoid if you can
His accent really gets in the way of understanding Good guy bad at teaaching so your grade suffers try to avoid him if you can

Awesome professor.  I had no problem with his accent, gives a lot of examples in class so there is no excuse for not doing well.  Cool guy.

This guy is the MAN. He's awesome, super clear and gives a million examples in class, plus time to do them in class. I loved her class! I am by no means any finance genius but she truly did care about my success and was always available during her office hours. Her tests were tough but she curves grades at the end of the semester! As long as you come to class and put the work in you will do great!

I took Prof Jang's FINA3303 class and she's very knowledgeable and a caring professor but it's such a difficult class! Be sure to study hard and go to her office hours. She's very generous with grading overall which is appreciated!

She's a super nice person, but her exams are hard in the way that it's super conceptual and challenging. She's a great person, but I just couldn't find a way to do well in her class despite visiting her in office hours and studying forever.
I would totally recommend her class. Not only did I enjoy her teaching in FINA2201, but I also chose to take her Investments class the following semester. She's awesome

Really great professor! Course content was extremely clear. Slides had all the information you needed to master for exams. Her exams were fair and based off of the many in class practice problems we worked through together. She also provides practice tests before exams that reflect the difficulty of the actual test.

The professor is extremely nice and responsive to emails. I took it as an asynchronous class, but the lectures were explained well, and it was easy to follow. The only issue was that the group project was annoying to do asynchronously, but other than that, it was a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took her FINA3301 class. It was 3 exams, 2 group projects, and some hw assignments. Practice exams are helpful; the exams aren't too bad (Canvas in-person exams). Attendance is mandatory (3 absences allowed) and lectures are pretty boring (mostly reading off slides) but overall not a bad experience. Group work is very tedious

Her FINA 3301 class was good. She is the type of lecturer who understands students, she is flexible with deadlines, allows a few absences, and is chill in general. Lectures are on the dry end but occasionally says a decent joke or two. The final exam is tough.
Hard tests, but she gives good study guides. She wants to see you do well, funny at times and nice overall. Enjoyed having her be a proffesor.

Definitely take her if you can! She can be hard to understand sometimes and her tests aren't super consistent with the material but theres a huge curve and shes so sweet/caring! One of the better finance professors at Northeastern

10/10! Very based and will cold call you and make make a joke or two if you get the answer wrong but really cares about her students. Overall good at teaching, took her for Finance 2201 really not that much to be covered but she makes it interesting and def would take her if you can.

Very sweet and caring prof. She makes sure you understand the topics before moving on. She makes jokes here and there and will also ask about you. Has a slight accent, but you can understand her fine. Overall, would take her again.

Class is mostly her reading through the slides– usually rushes through the examples without giving much time for you to do it yourself. But it's really easy to fall behind on the material if you don't attend class and try to follow along with examples. She wants you to do well and gives good practice tests before assessments, plus extra credit!

She is actually very understanding and wants students to succeed. After the first two exams, she gave a feedback survey on lectures, teaching, and exams. Exams are reasonable and open note, but rushed; practice exams help. Homework is completion-based, group project helpful, extra credit available, and effort counts toward your grade.

The worst teacher I have ever had. Awful teaching method. Terrible grading approach. My friends at previous university of this professor (North Carolina State Uni) also had very bad experiences with her. The main reason why this professor came to Northeastern University was that there were so many complaints against her at the previous university.

Her class is awful. she is not recommended at all. Homework takes forever and is very hard, long and kind of useless. The textbook is totally vague and confusing!! Despite all of these, the grading is a disaster!!!
Tough professor, with no flexibility at all.

The professor has a strong materials background. However, this course is quite intensive, covering a broad range of topics including atomic structure, electron configuration, crystalline lattice, miller index, defects, phase diagram, phase transformations, diffusion, polymers, mechanical properties, and strengthening mechanisms. Not an easy course

Her class is pretty intense. I'd recommend it if you really want to learn, but if you're not very interested in research or science, it may not be the best fit. She is a responsible and hardworking professor and sets high standards, especially in research.

I learned so much from Prof Zhu in MATL6280. The course content was vast. There were topics that were more difficult; she gave great attention to those topics for students to cement concepts. The lectures were long but definitely all necessary for a deep understanding of the content. Performing well on the final presentation is a must for an A!

I learned a lot about battery materials, how battery works, and how they're manufactured. This course truly changed my future career plans. I'm very confident I can pursue battery companies after this course.
She is very knowledgeable, and I learned a lot in the class.
I got 94 in the final. She always responds to emails promptly. I learnt a lot in this class. It inspires me to pursue a career in Materials in the future.

I took her class and scored 97 out of 100 on Midterm 1 and 91 out of 100 on Midterm 2. Her class is well organized. However, this course includes many concepts, terminologies, and calculations, so it does require additional efforts to read textbook outside of class. I personally have no difficulty understanding her lectures. Just my experiences.
It is hard to understand the professor. She will help when asked questions but the explanations are difficult to understand as well

I'm in Professor Zhu's Materials class this semester. This Thursday, when I asked her about my Midterm 1, surprisingly, she know every single number-even the exponents-at every step of the solution! Then when I saw her notes, I realized-she had worked through every single step of the exam questions herself step by step in every single number.

When I asked her questions, she always provided detailed, step by step explanations. A responsible professor. However, she seems not in industrial engineering. I'm quite surprised a professor in another field was assigned to teach this senior IE core course.

I took her class in spring 2020, during the hit of COVID 19 pandemic. While many classes faced challenges during that time, her classes always ran smoothly. She was consistently punctual and never missed a class due to COVID. Well, she had an accent. But I'm from Texas myself. I'm proud of my Texas accent. This is where I'm from. How can we blame?

I had the opportunity to work with Prof. Zhu for two semesters in IE4530-first as a student in her class and later as TA. During my time as her student in the Fall 2025, I was truly impressed by her dedication. Despite being 9 months pregnant, she stood and lectured for 100 minutes without any complain or excuses. This left lasting memory.

I'm in her ME2340 this semester. Based on my experience, Professor Zhu is approachable, smart, and passionate about the class. Her slides are well organized. She come to class with sufficient preparation. When I ask her question, she always response with patience and clarity. Meanwhile, she encourage us  to her office hour. She is responsible.
Worst college Professor EVER. Never take her class or work with her. Beware Bad Experience.

Only professor that I've looked forward to going to lectures to. Super funny and makes the material interesting to learn. You have to talk occasionally in his class, but I found myself engaging beyond just to get a participation grade. Would take again.

About 3-4 assignments as week, each having over 10 pages of reading and analyzing. Discussion boards, Perusall, random books, but uses it to fuel a discussion every class so you have to read it. Grades tough despite the class being required for NuPath. No technology in class, and the first philosophy class that you struggle to maintain an A in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
I took Prof. Yelle for his Philosophy and Literature class but it wasn't available here.

Professor Yelle is very cool, funny and open. There is definitely a lot of reading and a good amount of writing, given it is a mix of philosophy and literature course, but it's super interesting and he gives great guidelines. Be ready to contribute in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Yelle is a G. He has very particular ideas about how assignments should be completed, but if you're willing to talk to him, he tends to be more forgiving in his grading. The discussions felt unfortunately prefabricated- he has a predetermined outcome for each conversation, regardless of whether students agree with the readings being discussed.
Really funny and interesting lectures, but a tough grader at times. Forgiving of late work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures were always enjoyable, and Prof Yelle always made an effort to ensure discussions were inclusive. The topics we went over were interesting. He's not as tough a grader as other people here make him out to be, but be prepared to spend a good amount of time on the final paper.

If you are serious about philosophy, don't take his class. He has a strong tendency to avoid tough questions. He grades erratically and too harshly. Essays can only repeat his ideas rather than yours. And must be extremely straightforward, otherwise he will "not detailed enough" and give low marks for any rhetorical questions, irony, and intimation

Professor Yelle was one of the best professors I had. He was always welcoming and inclusive and completely unbiased. His classes were always engaging and funny and I made some amazing friends because of it. I don't know how anyone could leave a bad review, his classes are awesome. He's a harsh grader but college grades barely matter anyways.

Food Ethics with Ben was a MISTAKE. He was not an expert on the topic. Thankfully class discussions were typical, but he would still cut off meaningful thoughts to return to his poor slides. And assignment sheets were sloppy and not representative of how he graded.

If Ben graded his own materials like he graded student papers, he would fail BAD.
Nice teaching but tough grading

Prof Yelle is extremely likable and makes philosophy interesting with seminar-style lectures and no tests/quizzes. He's funny and cares about engaging his students. He is critical about the final project but not overly hard, I'd absolutely recommend taking him!

Has a genuine passion for making his class meaningful. No tests/quizzes. Almost all of your grade is comprised of writing assignments which he grades very harshly. You could follow all instructions and requirements for writing an essay and he will give you an 80 (coming from a decent writer). Generous with extensions
Really engaging class but tough grading for the final project

He is the most fair teacher I've ever had. You will walk away with exactly what you put into the class. He is a very tough grader, but if he sees you're trying he will cut you slack. Aside from that everything is 10/10. Great lectures. Very personable. Understanding with students. Just be ready to work and trust that you will be rewarded if you do.

I had for PHIL2143 (philosophy for children) not PHIL1185, Yelle was a great, energetic professor who fully engaged his students. You're not allowed to have your laptop out/open in class, which actually really helps focus, and I would love to take his class again.

Professor Yelle is one of the coolest professors out there! His classes are super interesting and engaging. He can be a tough grader on reading question assignments, but he gives good feedback. I loved his class and I encourage everyone to take PHIL 1101 with him.

His lectures are super engaging as he encourages everyone to play devil's advocate and analyze the reasoning behind their beliefs. He got me really interested in philosophy, a subject I was unsure of prior to taking the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ben made the classes enjoyable. However, he is an extremely tough and inconsistent grader and the feedback he gave was not helpful. If you want to succeed, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. Make him know you are interested in the class, regardless of if you are or are not. If you participate in class, you will succeed. If not, good luck mate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the toughest graders. You could go to office hours and spend a ton of hours on a single paper just to receive a B. The lectures themselves only require you to listen and sometimes contribute to the conversation. DO NOT take if you're expecting an A, unless you are an exceptional writer, because you won't get an A on your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: you don't have to put much time outside of class. the class had weekly discussion board posts, reading assignments, 2 papers, and one final paper. VERY TOUGH GRADER on papers. i do not recommend if you are a weak writer. however, he does give thorough and specific feedback to help you improve on future papers.
Good.

This class was excellent, and I would ABSOLUTELY take another class with him. I'll be going to office hours next semester just to talk to him even though I don't have his class. Be prepared to write, but I would definitely consider it manageable if you're a decent or strong writer.

More than anything, Benny is entertaining and endlessly fun. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Made lectures interesting. He is a tough grader but gives a lot of feedback so that you can improve on the next paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A good guy and a great lecturer, however he grades papers extremely unfairly, as if the people who are taking his class are doing so for a PHD in philosophy rather than NU Path credit. He also is insistent that you spend the money on the two books, despite his lectures come directly from them - turned out to be a waste of money in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are amazing. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T LIKE WRITING ESSAYS. VERY VERY TOUGH GRADER. but an amazing professor. Would not take his class again because personally, i do not understand his grading.

Professor Yelle is overall a great professor, however his grading on essays was ridiculously hard and he gave almost no feedback. Any feedback that was given was very passive and borderline rude. The essay grading alone makes me not want to take another of his classes, but if you enjoy discussion based classes you will like this professor.

simply a king. very passionate about the subject matter and leads great discussions, I learned a lot about philosophy despite putting in not a lot of effort. you don't realllly have to do all the readings, maybe just skim to know important broad concepts but he leads the discussions. he is a pretty tough grader on papers, be very very thorough

Professor Yelle is very knowledgable about philosophy, and I enjoyed the lectures we had in class. He is quite a tough grader on papers, but if you go in to office hours for help with your arguments he is happy to help you out. I also recommend going to office hours after he grades your paper so you can get very specific advice on how to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Yelle is very knowledgable and class discussions are engaging. Readings are assigned, but not necessarily required because the material is gone over in class. A little bit of a tough grader on papers, but not a heavy workload. Professor Yelle changed my way of thinking, and inspired me to minor in Phil! Definitely take this class!!!

Professor Yelle is one of the best professors I've had. He's able to spark interesting conversation in a 30 person class of mostly first years. Lots of readings that make you learn and grow - this class turned me vegan. Grading isn't bad and I get by with skipping class a lot and not doing all readings. Take this class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof Yelle is clearly passionate about this topic and class was absolutely very interesting. My review of him would've been a lot different if he didn't think of himself and his class as the main focal point in his students lives. most ppl are just taking this class for an elective, and he is an extremely harsh grader to a ridiculous point.

Professor Yelle is really good at explaining philosophical topics effectively and has introduced me to a lot of interesting technological concepts. However, he rarely gave feedback which made his grading style confusing at times (we also did not get any feedback for our final paper aside from a grade).

reviews.comment: extremely tough grader and comments on papers feel like insults

reviews.comment: Professor Yelle is a fantastic professor. His lectures and discussions are incredibly engaging, making the class fun to be in. Regarding homework, there are some small assignments and readings are very important to do, but the workload is manageable. Writing is a big part of the grade also, but he is available for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: tough grader, difficult for international students to get a high grade if you don't spend enough time in reading and taking reading notes, especially for whose major is not in liberal arts,

Unlike other subjects, it takes a solid understanding of philosophy and morals to be a good teacher and prof Yelle is extremely qualified. His lectures hosted some of the most thought-provoking conversations I've ever heard & I feel I'm better off for taking his course. As long as you read the passages and take notes, you'll be fine. Amazing class.

His Technology & Human Values class is very interesting and he really captivates the classroom with his lectures. There are a few quizzes, he tells you when they'll be but you'll need to take notes every day if you want to do well on them. There are only 3 essays throughout the semester, but he is a very tough grader, go to office hours to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Excellent in class conversation. He is truly an amazing devils advocate which forces you to think through your ideas far more deeply
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Usually would hate the idea of any class with pop quizzes, but besides the fact that they're usually easy to see coming, you'll want to be at every class anyway and as long as you briefly look over the readings they're pretty easy. Professor Yelle is really an amazing, young professor who cares about his students and also makes you think.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Stand up guy. *Slow clap*. His lectures are super engaging and he delivers the content in a way that really makes you think. The setup is pretty much based on lectures and discussions and most of your grade is made up of papers (which I like). I would recommend meeting with him for each paper assignment because he gives excellent feedback!

Entertaining professor and gets really into his lectures. Pop quizzes are super easy. Nice guy who always helps out at his office hours. He's really picky with his essays though, will take off points for minor things.
He's a good guy but he is pretty inconsistent with his grading.

Most amazing teacher I ever had! Had class at 8 am but it was a pleasure to come, he makes everything very interesting, and the classes are just discussions around ethical concepts. All exams are take home, and as he gives great feedback it pushes us to give our best. Plus he gives extra credit if you wanna give a presentation. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! I took Intro to Philosophy with him and his lectures really made me think. The readings are always interesting and he always pushes you to be the best writer/thinker you can be! I would definitely take his class again.

I absolutely loved this class! He was amazing. He is very passionate about this subject and you can tell. He is NOT boring at all. No exams, just papers and a few pop quizzes. If you do the readings though they are really easy. Honestly best professor I have ever had. We talked after almost every class and I wish he could be my best friend lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I got cooked in both midterms but he is still the goat

If you attend lectures regularly and ask for help on homework questions, you will do well in Professor Jin's class. He is friendly and always willing to answer questions on Piazza or in person. Tests can be challenging, but final letter grades may be curved to compensate for that. Participation can also boost your grade. Overall, great professor!
The esteemed gentleman in question endeavours to take meticulous care that the entirety of one's comprehension be satisfactorily addressed.

This class in my opinion was amazing... Professor Jin is by far one of the best professors I've had - his passion with respect to theory makes learning enjoyable. I would recommend that if you do not enjoy proofs as much, potentially stay away from this class but overall Professor Jin makes it manageable and bearable. 10/10 if I could

Tests are fair and the grading was very fair in my experience. Lectures are dry but Prof Jin was a nice guy and would take all the time you need to understand things. I think this was his second semester teaching and from what I heard previously he really has gotten his stuff together and is great now. A lot of time on HW though. Would take again!
His voice makes you sleepy in class. He's always immersed in his own world, you cannot not learn anything from him in class.

Very cool prof! If you want a deep understanding of the mathematical side of Machine Learning, take his class. He focuses heavily on the theoretical aspects, which is rare and valuable. Despite the rigor, he is extremely understanding and patient and is always willing to go the extra mile to explain things during office hours.
Sometimes he UNSURE of what hes trying to say. Poor communication skills.

had him for cs4100 but that wasnt an option. Freest A of my life. Midterm was takehome, attendance wasn't mandatory, and homework assignments had so much starter code I was basically just uncommenting lines and submitting. Learned absolutely nothing though.
He is a highly approachable professor with a wealth of knowledge. As long as you complete the homework and put effort into a strong final project, achieving a high grade is very manageable!

This course covers conventional machine learning materials. I have taken cs6140 under another professor, which actually covered similar topics compared to this course. But that one is more profound and interesting, I guess it's due to the teaching style. This course could be more solid and easy-to-understand for whom just got into this area
Course itself is great, I have learnt quite a lot. However, I wouldn't recommend the professor to take his session on. He is great, but not good at teaching.

I learned a lot from Professor Zhang's lectures. Each presentation/class had a well-structured flow and the content was relevant and useful. He is also very well-versed in the topic which meant that additional comments were typically insightful. He also cares about students and wants to help them in any way he can.
It's ok class. Prof knows a lot in his area, but he's not a good teacher.

Professor Zhang is clearly very knowledgeable in the field of machine learning, and did an amazing job explaining difficult theoretical concepts during lectures. His class includes a reasonable mix of machine learning theory (underlying mechanisms of machine learning algorithms/techniques) and opportunities to apply them to practical datasets.

Professor Zhang is approachable and encourages students to ask questions. Office hours are well-utilized, we often go to his office after class to ask questions, and he was always patient and happy to answer.

Professor Zhang displayed exceptional knowledge and passion for machine learning, making complex topics understandable and engaging. Also, feedback was always constructive and insightful, significantly aiding in our learning process. Besides that, I love how the final project was laid out and presented which gave students many free discussions.

A must-take class if you want to claim that you understand why deep learning works. He comprehends and complements the difficult-to-self-learn textbooks very well so that the large topics fit within a semester. Through the project, he trains you how to read, critique, and build on the latest literature. He is very considerate and accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take other courses if you have chance. The grade is fair, but if you really wanted to learn something from the course, probably NO. You won't feel any passion from the instructor at all.

Professor Zhang taught this course very well and I have learned a lot from this course.

If you are going to do research, please this course. This course will prepare you very well for research.

Professor Zhang is a nice person and answers students' questions patiently.

The course is tough with often unclear lectures. Grading is fair, but a foundation knowledge is recommended. Prof focuses on theory, lacking practical examples. Would recommend other courses at Khoury unless you don't have any other choices.

Prof Zhang's class was a good mix of applied and theoretical ML techniques and was a fair grader. He involves the students in his teaching a lot which was engaging and conducive to learning, so would recommend this class! It helped me with foundations for my ML research and I think others would benefit too.

CS7140 is a challenging course, but you will learn a lot if you dive into it. Please take CS6140 machine learning before you pick this one, or you will feel lost for the entire semester. Professor Zhang is knowledgeable about the mathematical theory of ML. The classroom atmosphere is relaxed. Feel free to ask any questions when you confuse!

I found this class to be incredibly difficult and lectures/materials hard to follow. Homework required a lot of research on my own and slides weren't helpful. However, I thought the grading was fair and the TAs/professor tried their very best to ensure everyone performs well. As long as you show that you put in effort, you should be fine.

He is the best lecturer if you want to learn machine learning. He teaches tough topics effectively using his own words that makes us much easier to learn the topics by reading texts. He has clear instructions and offers support as needed on assignments so that each student can learn through these assignments.

If you have no experience with ML,take cs6140 or NLP,before taking this course. Prof. Zhang didn't provide any solid examples for each theory. I personally just learnt the topic from textbooks/online sources,and used the lectures for review.Northeastern should hire some professors who know how to teach and convey their knowledge to the students

Prof Zhang's 7140 class was focused mostly on mathematical deep learning theory. The materials were in-depth, and I learned a lot from the lectures and the assignments. The class is challenging and can get quite technical, so I can see why some students struggled with it. Be sure to allocate enough time for his class as it can be quite demanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang is extremely knowledgeable in the mathematical and theoretical aspects of ML and he managed to teach the core ideas very well in this course. He was very accessible outside class (also responds to emails in minutes) and provided excellent guidance throughout the course and in picking up research topics after the course as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is an amazing class. Prof. Zhang is very approachable. His brilliance and extensive knowledge of the field of machine learning are obvious. You can study a lot from this class, especially for the theoretical and mathematical parts. He is always available to help and efficiently explains every lesson!

If you want to learn deep learning, look at some free edX/MIT classes; if you're taking this for PhD, I'd recommend taking other sessions other than his. The lectures are super dry, often skipping showing how to solve actual problems. He didn't did do well explaining the concepts. We had to check lectures on the internet to fully understand them.
Excellent course. Prof Zhang is very polite, accessible and extremely knowledgeable in his area. Anyone pursing machine learning/deep learning will gain a lot from this course.

Took his course last year. He's probably good at his field but the course is poorly designed. Just read off the slides which just copy&paste from other universities' slides. He didn't organize them well and plan beforehand. Often changed the assignment's requirements at the last mins. Very little passion for teaching. Doesn't care about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (Physics) His passion, adaptability, and genuine care for students creates an engaging learning environment. He adjusts his teaching to meet us where we are. His willingness to listen and reflect makes him stand out. He's transformed me into an active participant when I typically don't speak in class. I wish professors adopted his teaching style!

If you are a continuing education student who is decades past your last math class and not in a mathematical field you will have difficulty passing this class. Feed back on final paper was belittling to say the least but I did get an apology. Many in class dropped by third week. Professor makes the assumption math is all anyone should do. I MO

Took his class during the summer. He let you know from day one what was expected. LOT'S of homework (mostly bc it was a summer course and we had to crunch so much in). However, always there to help. Also, if something came up he was reasonable for extensions, etc. Great guy.
Very good at teaching the material. Highly recommend taking the class with him as you will learns lot

Possibly one of the best professors I've had so far. He knows his stuff and is genuinely interested in the performance of his students. He's also pretty funny. Best guy to have for Mechanics, hands down.
Best professor so far

The most engaging professor I had this term, and overall one of the 3 best professors I've ever had at Northeastern. He challenges students. Also, as a STEM education expert, he does research in how students best learn these topics, which means he is super good at teaching them.

FINA is a difficult subject, in general, but I feel like he made it more difficult than it was. My class is often chapters ahead for no reason. Dr. Acharya knows what he is talking about and will help you outside of class. He talks quickly, so barely anyone is able to focus in class. Tests (4) are 75% of your final grade...
