Disorganized slides and theory-focused lecture make it difficult to learn anything. Learned more from Google than her after I stopped going to lectures a month in.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked this class and felt I actually learned a lot for once. Some of the homeworks were a little difficult but there was usually extra credit on the assignment to make up.

I wish to learn more about how to actually use and apply ML, but basically all the lecture is about theory and math. The homework is heavy, especially the coding part is barely taught in class. Her voice is so small and with a heavy accent. Instead of wasting two hours, you could just learn the lecture yourself online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Thick accent and can not understand the first thing she taught. The type of professor to push the midterm 4 days ahead with less than a 24 hour notice. Lots of homework and not understanding at all. Do not take her and I doubt northeastern is going to keep her much longer

I was hoping I would love this class and learn a lot about implementing cool machine learning algorithms on cool datasets. The course material is bad(only have done GD after a month) and she is so boring that its impossible to pay attention. I genuinely hope she reads this and tries to do better.

Lectures are unreasonably complex, spends the whole class proving formulas rather than showing us how to use them which is what is actually on the homework assignments/quizzes. I learn more about the material from a google search. Gives random pop quizzes at the beginning of class and calls out students who are even two minutes late.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Oprea is incredibly knowledgeable in her field. The material can be dry at times, but is in depth and thorough. The homework can be very long, but she and the TA's are easily accessible. She listens to students requests and wants us to succeed. Most of the grade is a Final and Final Project.

ALMA IS THE BEST! Her ASL class is completely immersive, so you get the best learning experience. She is funny, kind, and adorable; you genuinely learn so much in one semester. The complete immersion takes a bit to get used to, but it's great. Homework is pretty easy, but be prepared to record yourself. I only have good things to say about Alma!

Alma is an incredible professor! If you had her for ASL 1 I HIGHLY recommend taking her classes again. She is very serious about deaf culture-- no talking in class, no phones, practice your signing-- but she is also quite understanding and really cares about all of her students

Alma was the best professor I have ever had! She would always take extra time to repeat something even if only one person didn't fully understand. The last day of class she went around and gave everyone hugs which made me start tearing up. I would 100% recommend taking Alma's class! ALMA IS THE BEST and you will have the best time!

Alma is a great professor! Her class is structured in a way you can fully immerse yourself in Deaf culture, and you have no other choice but to learn. It's a great learning environment, and it's a class that you must show up to. She is also very funny and wants you to learn and understand!

Alma is one of the best professors I have ever had. She has a great sense of humor and is an awesome professor. Do the work assigned and you should get an A, I recommend taking her because she really immerses you into learning the language, as she is Deaf and the whole class is taught in ASL. Don't be fooled by some of the older reviews.

Alma is great! She may come across as intimidating at first, but once you get deeper into the semester she is quite fun and caring about her students. As long as you attend class and complete all the homework, the class is relatively easy. She makes sure to adapt to students who may not catch on as quickly, and will repeat things.

Professor Bournazian is a really great ASL teacher. She is patient with beginners and always tries to make the class entertaining and fun. She is very sweet and cares a lot about her students. Attending class and doing all the assignments will have this course be a breeze. She will hold you accountable for your work and for how much you practice.

Professor Alma is the best. I read some reviews of her (on here) prior to taking her class and was a little skeptical, but she turned out to be one of the best professors I've ever had. She's very caring and genuinely wants you to learn about Deaf culture. She uses immersion which is the best technique for learning. Definitely recommend her class!

Alma is deaf so for ASL there is complete immersion but she would make sure we understood what was said. She does favor those who put effort in and are direct (as is deaf culture) and will get a translator if needed.

She was very very funny as well, and ASL was the one class that I never zoned out in as it was always engaging.
Shes amazing so sweet and funny. Yeah the class is hard but the subject itself is hard.

the deaf community as a whole are a very blunt group that is based on honesty and this can be shocking and come as harsh to hearing students. alma is a great professor who wants you to succeed and be ready for the next level. she will explain something 15 different ways until you understand and always is understanding. get out what you put in

Alma is awesome! She is adorable, really funny, and really nice. She is a great example of Deaf culture and genuinely cares about her students. It's a little tough because the entire class is in sign language and written English, but if you pay attention and go to class, you'll definitely pick up about 95% of what she says.

She is ADORABLE. I really dont agree with any of the comments.. She is very clear with all the material, I just think that ASL is hard in itself. It gets harder in higher levels, but asl 1 is WAY better with her than with anyone else. Go to class, do your work and will get an A.
Fantastic for those who care about ASL;  not so great for those who don't.  Get ready for a hard class, get ready to apply yourself, get ready to learn.

Fantastic!  She's a little bit hard, but very funny.  Always willing to answer questions and always appreciates honesty and the desire to learn.  The class isn't easy, though:  it's all in ASL.  If you're not going to try, don't take it.  You'd probably fail as well as end up on her bad side.  DO NOT TRY TO CHEAT OR TEXT UNDERNEATH THE TABLE.
Very funny, likes to tell stories but itsn't very clear. Signs fast and moves quickly. No clear order to the class or standard for the homework. Hard grader.

She is one of the worst teachers I ever had, she gives no hand outs no explanations. She is an fair grader and will make fun of  students.  Now that I am an ASL teacher and I strive to be the opposite of her.  She can be a very nasty person.
worst professor i've ever had
Very bad class. If you are interested in actually learning ASL do not take this class. Highest grade given on assignments was a B. Often explained assignments incorrectly and was not accessible

Prior to this class, I had earned and 3.93 GPA in my five years at NU.  During the class, I quickly realized I should aim for a "C." This class is HARD. Here are my tips: don't skip; study your ASL vocab; and do ALL assignments. If I had followed my own advice, I *might* have pulled an "A."  Ah well.  Alma is funny and nice but ASL is NOT easy!

Entire class is in ASL, pretty much understands you as well as you understand her...which is not so much. Sets extremely high standards for students, which are rarely met by anyone in the class. Generally nice, and funny teacher who makes class enjoyable, but very much an unfair grader. One of the toughest classes ive ever taken.
She's a very strict and fair grader but very funny and helpful.
No Comments

Alma is a great person but a tough teacher. She is deaf and rarely writes anything on the bored so be prepared to pay full attention all class long because it is entirely in ASL. This is NOT an easy class, don't take it if you plan on slacking off or you'll be adding an F to your GPA.
I really like Alma, despite her being a hard grader. She's a lot of fun, otherwise. Just as long as you don't blow the class off.
Very hard, not understanding, time comsuming, not very fair.

she was unresponsible...she didn't come to class at least 3 times and i asked her for a recommendation and she agreed to it and the day before the recommendation was due she said she wasn't going to write it..very tough grader..not very understanding or approachable

Alma is a tough but fair teacher. She expects you to work and you end up learning a lot from her. She's spunky and when you get to know her she's nice. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU WANT TO SLACK OFF.
I loved Alma!  Just take a little time to get to know her.  She really is a fun person!
No Comments

Very tough, especially at first. Funny once you get to know her, but still intimidating, especially if she thinks you are not serious. A harsh grader. Class is taught entirely in ASL, so if you don't get it at the beginning, you become lost very quickly.

One of the best lecturers I've taken. Kitagawa is SO smart and will workshop any idea with you. But my experience with her TA has been different. TA graded everything and seemed out of touch with both the class and the material which made the experience of this class stressful
The prof is amazing and so so interesting and fun but all work is graded by a TA who could not care less about the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: CLASS IS SO BORING OMLLLLLLLL RUN RUN RUN RUN RUN SO BORING

Almost all her classes involve heavy group work. Lots of readings due before class, so be ready to read. She encourages discussion and is extremely caring. My only small gripe is that she is slow to grade, which doesn't allow feedback for the final paper in time. Despite this, she is an amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of my favorite POLS profs at NEU. The depth of her knowledge is incredible, she leads thought-provoking discussions, and every lecture is helpful. She gets so excited for questions, and as excited when people volunteer answers, class was always fun and good energy. Lots of readings, but they're skimmable and she goes over them in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Kitagawa is an amazing lecturer, her classes are incredibly engaging, and is one of the sweetest people I've ever had the pleasure of working with at Northeastern. She'll pose thought-provoking questions to get through the sometimes mundane readings, and grades fairly while giving thorough feedback. Take any class you can with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Kitagawa is clearly very passionate about her subject, and her lectures are incredibly interesting. The class itself was pretty easy, but I feel like I gained a lot from the topics she covered, and the discussions we had in class. Definitely get assigned huge readings, but the tests are super straightforward and you barely get any hw
she is an incredibly organized and thoughtful to students. clear communicated expectations on exams and assignments. thorough feedback. lectures and informative

Professor Kitagawa is an amazing professor. Her lectures are incredibly engaging and helpful while dealing with sometimes long and boring readings. She also encourages collaboration through turn and talks as well as group projects. She also posts all her lectures online and Canvas is very nicely organized. Plus she's an easy grader.

A teacher who actually cares about students and what she's teaching. Every class, she asks for you to turn to your neighbor and talk to them, which might seem intimidating, but you end up with a ton of people that you know in the class. If you get the opp to take a class with her, go for it. She's also rated one of the best in CSSH.

Professor's lectures are very monotone but she's a good teacher. Assigns lots of readings and its up to you to do them but you can get by class without doing them. There are only a few assignments per semester. Professor is very caring and nice and loves when her students stop by office hours. Would 100% take her again for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Kitagawa is a very knowledgeable and friendly professor. For Comparative Politics, she outlined the class well, gave us articles and documents to read which matched our lectures, and provided great feedback on our assignments. While there were only four assignments throughout the year, a midterm, and a final, I thought her class was great
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kitagawa was by far my favorite professor this semester, taken for Globalization and International Affairs. She assigns a fair amount of readings, and the class is lecture heavy, but she's very engaging and encourages participation. If you show up and take good notes, you should have no problem doing well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Best one I've had so far at Northeastern. She cares about her students and is great at facilitating discussions. Knows when she needs to go into more depth with certain readings that the class may not grasp as much. I would suggest taking notes during classes since they cover exactly what'll be on exams.

She's a great professor who is not only an easy A but really engages the subject facilitating great group discussion. I learned a lot in this class and had a lot of fun. While you can get away with skipping the mandatory readings sometimes, I recommend reading them and taking notes if you want to get a lot out of the class.

Professor Kitagawa's class was one of the most interesting and rewarding experiences I have had at Northeastern. Even in the online setting, she has been super helpful. She is also the best lecturer that I have ever had. Would definitely recommend taking a class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: i absolutely loved her!!!! she really cares about her students and takes the time to learn everyone's names, even if you don't talk in class a lot. she has really cool experiences in the field, so she is a great ia professor, could not reccomend her more highly. exams are based on the class readings but if you just cram before you will be fine

Dr. Kitagawa is brilliant She has helped me learn a lot in her Civil War class. However the lecture heaviness and unavailability of slides online (so you will go to class) made it a full note taking class. Student participation is important, and the class is only papers due throughout the semester. Semester-long case studies were interesting to do!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kitagawa is an incredible professor. Shes insanely smart and articulate. Kindest person, and great to talk to. There is a lot of reading assigned, but you just have to get the gist of it. Grading is generous. The class isnt too challenging but you will learn A LOT. Just how a class should be.

reviews.comment: very interesting and fun professor! tons of reading and its necessary for class. lots of group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is the only reason I understood discrete and everything was explained really well. She is super sweet and cares for all her students that show up.
She is super helpful and caring and makes sure we understand each topic. I enjoyed showing up every time, and left knowing a lot more than when I came in. Definitely recommend!!

My favorite recitation was the one for Discrete Structures taught by Professor Ghita. She has the power to make concepts digestible for someone learning them for the first time. Additionally, she always took the time to clarify even as after the section ended. Finally, she gives you just enough to let still reach that "aha" moment. Thank you Ghita!

so nice and so ineffective. there were many typos on the shared materials (notes shared, etc.) throughout her teaching, with not enough support to resolve them, making understanding concepts frustrating. explanations were ambiguous and missed the mark. poor teaching quality. highly suggest avoiding if you can. some things just don't change.

Had her for recitation for Discrete Strucutres (CS1800). She was amazing! Not many people went to the recitations, so you are able to have very small group discussions with her and get personalized help. She knew the content very well and did extra practice problems to make sure that we understood the material.

Said that "for computer science" natural numbers start at 0 in the lecture, did an induction example with said assumption, took points off in homework because "natural numbers start at 1". A must take if you enjoy casual gaslighting :)

A terrific professor. Dr. Amor was always ready to answer questions and she explains concepts super well. I got an A in discrete because of her. She provided so much help and kindness. My advise is to show up to recitation - no one does, so she'll spend as much time as you want on your questions. I cannot stress enough how nice and helpful she is.
Gives good recitation lectures. Seems to care if students understand content or not
For CS 1802 (CS 1800's lab), pretty good, although sometimes the explanations may be a little difficult to follow, if you just ask for clarification, she will happily oblige. Very caring and nice.
I didn't like the attitude or teaching style very much

She is nice but she got mad at me once during office hours because I didnt understand a question, like???? Oh and be prepared to take a very important exam the Monday after thanksgiving break very early in the morning. Your end of semester results will be delayed as well.

Just watch the lectures and you can pretty much figure it out. Go to TA office hours/clinic hours!!!!! They will help you with all the assignments they literally were the reason I did so well! Prof is super sweet and caring!

Extremely hard, weekly homework that takes hours to complete, final exams are so important. Very useful information but avoid if not necessary. Prof was available and helpful. Hardest and one of the most demanding classes I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The online lectures are done by a variety of teachers and are comprehensive. Professor does a good job of explaining in class. TAs are very accessible during "clinic hours" to help with homework. They are the reason I did so well. The homework and quizzes can be challenging without help. Tests are a big percentage, but they are the same as the HW

She is a very easy professor to get an A grade under. It does make it unfair for students who are willing to work for the course since she frequently gives extensions, allows late submissions and entertains any sort of regrading if you just ask for it. Take it to get points, do not try to work hard for the course since you'll just be disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Everything you do is online. Attendance is 4%, but CS, in general, is a very intense and time-demanding class. Long assignments every week + quizzes. The grades add up fast. Don't risk your grade unless you're a CS major. Take an online class somewhere else if you want to learn the skills (especially for co-op) but this class is not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is based on watching tutorials online before class, and then practicing the material during class. There are a lot of homework, which are a pain, however it is the only way you are going to learn the material. The things you learn are also extremely applicable to what you may be doing at coop.

reviews.comment: Easily the worst class I've taken in my 3 semesters at NEU. TA is AWFUL. If you sit in the front, maybe you can understand a bit more. But regardless of who I've talked to, they struggle. Unless this class is absolutely required for your major, take it with another prof. She doesn't know much of the material, she needs to look stuff up in office hr

I was on Professor Aldrich's dialogue this past summer and it was one of the most transformative experiences of my life. Even though I had little background doing research, he made the work approachable and interesting. Professor Aldrich's combination of in class and experiential learning made the dialogue one of my favorites at northeastern.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Aldrich is hands down one of the best professors I had at Northeastern. Such an inspirational lecturer who genuinely cares about his students. He is up front with his expectations of students, and makes the course material accessible and interesting through his engaging lectures and genuine passion for the subject. Highly recommend!

His workload was at times difficult but it's clear he has high expectations for his students and will do anything in his power to help them achieve success. I learned invaluable knowledge on my DOC with him I'm thankful to have had him as a professor.

Professor Aldrich expects a lot of his students, but you'll get back what you give tenfold. His lived experiences and research are fascinating and genuinely influence the way I see the world three years later. I wish I had the chance to take more of his courses!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Aldrich does an excellent job of making himself accessible to students at all times. His email responses never take more than 30 minutes, and his advice and recommendations are always insightful. Throughout our trip, he maintained a good balance of academics while also encouraging fun. I highly recommend him and the Japan DOC.

I really enjoyed the class! The main grade came from participation and the main research paper that we worked on over the course of the semester. He was very helpful and helped us throughout the entire research process. It was very educational and an amazing experience overall! Would really recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Aldrich was surprisingly fun. I found it weird at first that students had to lead classes throughout the semester, but I appreciate it in hindsight. You really become an expert on topics you lead and he assists while you lead by shedding more lights on topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Aldrich is a very chill guy. Definitely knows his stuff and what he's talking about. Not a very tough grader, but also a fair grader. Do not miss class, as he gives a lot of valuable insights.

I really enjoyed my class with Professor Aldrich. The workload and grading were fair and it is obvious that he makes an extra effort to provide a variety of interesting course materials. He cares a lot about his students and was available outside of class for extra help. This was my first master's course and I hope to take another with him again.

He is truly such a great professor, and despite this class being online completely, he was always available to talk to. Whenever I did talk to him he always gave great feedback and inspired me to do better on every subsequent assignment. I'm even taking a class again with him next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed the class was a cool strcuture. Lots of reading but he makes it easy with reading questions. One paper which is worked on throughout the semester. Had 2 tests (if you pay attention you will get a good grade). Brought a lot of professional work into the classroom which was awesome! You should take the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is possibly one of the kindest, most caring professors I have had the pleasure of knowing. He is a truly phenomenal person, down-to-earth, super smart, and inspirational. I think everyone who meets him can instantly tell that he is a gem of a human. He is fair in grading, realistic in coursework, and gives GREAT feedback. A wonderful man.

Aldrich is an incredibly effective professor who knows exactly how to make the topics of the class as engaging as possible. While most of the classes are seminar-based, he gets very involved with discussions and is always open to questions. Quizzes and tests are very straight forward, and he gives ample opportunity for feedback on the final paper.

reviews.comment: I was on his disaster and recovery dialogue and can't recommend it enough! reviews.comment: Prof. Aldrich was one of those professors who reminded me why I chose to go to college and why I chose Northeastern. Truly inspirational, knowledgable, and invested in his students education. You can tell he pours his heart into the DOC program and into Northeastern in general. I cannot recommend him enough.

reviews.comment: I did a Dialogue with Prof. Aldrich and I absolutely loved it. He is incredibly intelligent and knows so much about the topics we learn. Great professor!!

reviews.comment: Great professor, can not recommend his classes enough. Class was socratic based upon readings which caused discussions to go wherever the interests of the class lies. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: one of the best choices I made at NEU and changed the trajectory of my masters. Challenging, but rewarding - do all the readings. I can't recommend this class enough, all discussions were so interesting and fun.

reviews.comment: Aldrich is so passionate about his subject matter that he makes it exciting and applicable. I've never met such an accomplished academic who is also a fantastic professor- he is an amazing lecturer although he mostly does discussions led by students which helps with the engagement. Great character too.

Great professor. Each day a student is assigned a chapter of his book which you had to buy to lead class, and it was pretty easy to do if you read. He overall made it an easy workload, and mostly focuses on learning through travelling

reviews.comment: The majority of lectures are seminar style, meaning they are taught through questioning of the audience of students. Also, the majority are taught by students themselves. Readings are challenging and gripping, but plentiful - you must carve out time during your week in order to keep up. There are no written exams as long as you can prove you have read through in-class discussion.

Class introduces many interesting topics, does have a focus on nuclear power and disaster recovery, as that is focus of his research. Graded on attendance/participation, he sometimes cold calls so make sure you've done the readings. Inclusive classroom, everyone has nametags. Grading is sometimes confusing, points taken off but not explained why

reviews.comment: Prof Aldrich is one of the best academic instructors I've ever had. He is passionate about resiliency and the course itself. Decent amt of reading each week but was interesting material

I took POLS7341 online. There was a lot of reading each week but not difficult. Do the readings and you will do well. Expectations and grading are made clear in the syllabus. Enjoyable class. Really made you think and view things from a different perspective.

reviews.comment: I found this particular class easy to do well in, but it definitely has something to do with the professor choosing gripping topics and bite-sized material so the class work is interesting, and not a chore. He is engaging, personable, extremely intelligent, and highly understanding. I enjoyed the work; I would take his courses again if possible.

Prof. Aldrich is my program director and has been extremely helpful since day 1 of admissions. He is responsive to emails and a fair grader. He lays out all expectations and is very enthusiastic about the course. Highly recommend!!

Excellent professor. Big emphasis on class discussions rather than lectures. Worked out very well for this course (6 students). The discussions are engaging and force you to interact deeper with the material. Weekly reading quizzes were straightforward as long as you did the reading.

Professor Aldrich is an incredible professor that I would recommend to everyone! He is really passionate about the topic of disasters and has had incredible experiences that make his class fascinating. The classes are very interactive and focused on student-led discussions.

reviews.comment: Prof. Aldrich is one of the best professors at Northeastern. The Security and Resilience Policy course has (literally) defined the remainder of my college degrees, and my future professional prospects. This course was incredibly engaging and interesting thanks to Dr Aldrich's pristine lectures and modules. I would 100% recommend him and the course.

Professor Aldrich is knowledgable, encouraging, and caring. When our Dialogue to Japan was cancelled due to COVID-19, he did an excellent job of adapting a virtual version (I really appreciated this!). He was readily available to meet outside of class time, and structured the course so it was engaging and fun to learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took East Asian Politics from professor Aldrich, and thoroughly enjoyed it. Hes an amazing professor, one of my favorites Ive had. He strikes a fantastic balance between leading classes himself, and allowing students to lead discussions. The end result is an environment where its extremely easy and fun to absorb the information presented.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Aldrich is incredibly engaging and caring about his students. It was a pleasure to learn about Aldrich's research about disasters and recovery during my Dialogue in Japan. Aldrich was always willing to help students outside of the classroom to give them feedback. I loved going to his lectures and thoroughly enjoyed his Dialogue!

Truly an amazing professor, quite a celebrity in Japan. I had him for diaglogue and it was the best class I have ever taken at Northeastern hands down. The dad jokes are never ending and he loves student drama lmao. The dialogue is very manageable but hectic at the same time. 100% would take again if I could!

Professor Aldrich is a very insightful professor! I had him for a dialogue to Japan, and trust me he knows what's he's talking about. I learned so much and enjoyed the lessons and freedom of exploration given to us by Professor Aldrich. He's also such a dad, with constant dad jokes, so I mean give and take.

This was one of my favorite courses at NU. I learned a lot from the carefully curated readings and the discussions during class helped me retain what I learned . This made studying for exams easy. The one assigned paper was flexible allowing each student to choose a different topic of interest. Overall, I would highly recommend Professor Aldrich.

While at first glance the course may seem intimidating with pop quizzes, mandatory lecture presentations by students, etc. It's one of the best classes to take because a) you get excellent feedback from a really dedicated professor and b) you learn a lot and have the opportunity to apply what you learn to topics of your choice.

Prof. Aldrich's East Asian Politics course was a lot of work - run like a graduate seminar with us leading - but I learned a lot.

Hands down best professor I had. He teaches you how to code properly and did a great job reviewing all necessary requirements to do the HWs. Professor Amini was an amazing professor who clearly cared about his students. Don't take the negative reviews on here seriously. Professor Silvio is a solid professor and clearly well-informed in the field of NLP. Grading criteria was clear & there is no final. This was my first time coding and I think he was understandable. I am glad he actually did the notes with the class because as ds classes go on it is just like presentation rather than working it out.
Please button up your shirt, there was like 5 buttons unbuttoned.

Honestly, every time you go to class you will leave feeling more confused than you previously did going into class. If you are new to coding you will definitely need to buckle up for one hell of a ride, he drops the lowest grade for homework. I once asked for help after lecture and it was useless.

Not good at explaining things. Not accommodating in large lectures for students who sit in the back and cannot see the board. Unhelpful or "idk" answers to questions. Poor, inefficient use of class time. Was supposed to be an introductory DS course but he made me feel so lost and completely steered me away from future DS/coding courses.

Amir is a decent man with a wry sense of humor that comes in spontaneous "sparks" which can brighten otherwise mundane lectures. Lectures are hard to follow and useless. If you don't read the textbook it's impossible to understand anything in the lecture. The lectures have no structure at all and I felt lost in every lecture. Professor cannot explain things very well. This class kinda killed my interest in NLP.

This class pushed me to think outside the box further than I've ever gone before, and bring those big ideas to life in a way where I was constantly engaged and having fun with it. reviews.comment: For MKTG 3720: Professor Butler is a great guy who really cares about his students. The class is structured very loosely, and can be kind of abstract at times. A lot of this class can be boiled down to if you have a good group that's willing to put in work to create a good final product. However, the class is interesting and you can learn a lot.

Great Professor who cares about each student. Case every week and 2 presentations during the semester with some lectures. you don't know your grade until the end of the semester but he really emphasizes participation and being engaged in class. Great class if you want to go into marketing but, it is a lot of work. Couldn't recommend enough!
great guy, had him in spring 2025

Best professor ever. He makes the class the easiest thing ever, tells you what's on the test beforehand down to the question number, attendance isn't mandatory. Just make sure to be personable with him, and everything will be served to you on a silver platter.

Really funny guy, loves to crack jokes. I looked forward to his class. Would highly recommend. Do read the textbook chapters before he goes over them in class. Tests were pretty easy and the homeworks had unlimited attempts. Still have to put in some effort in the class, but workload wasn't bad for such a challenging class.

Classes were lecture-style w/ him reading from a slide show, and the following class, he would walk the class through practice problems from the textbook. He does cold calling. Overall, very kind & caring professor. Very helpful during office hours. He also told us what exact topics were on the exams & 3 quizzes were online. Def recommend him!

Amazing accounting professor. ACCT 1201 is a lot of work and memorizing rules, but Tony makes learning enjoyable. Unlimited homework attempts. Tony often tells some good personal stories that relate to the topic we are going over. Lots of work you have to do on your own when it comes to the readings and homework. Best accounting professor out there

Super laid back and chill guy. Has really good experience as he was a CPA for like 30 years. The lectures got a bit boring at times but he always engaged the class and made us laugh. Most the the accounting department is regulated grade wise, and Tony does a great job preparing you for the final.

Best ACCT Prof . He's not as strict as the other professors but show up to his classes, they might be boring, but he tries to make it fun by telling his stories and getting the class engaged. Doesn't show the total grade on canvas but it can be easily calculated. Unlimited attempts on the homework, one midterm, one paper final, and group project.
I love this professor, but the course itself is a lot of work. You'll have to be very proactive about asking questions and attending his office hours for guidance.

reviews.comment: He's a solid professor with an excellent background in accounting. He knows managerial can be tedious, but he made the class enjoyable with his fun accounting and off-topic stories. He's super reliable and has so many opportunities for office hours, and if you're scared about what's on the tests, just ask him. He's super transparent about it.

Tony is one of the kindest professors I have had. He always made time to meet after class and answered emails QUICKLY. I found the tests to be difficult, but he told us exactly what it would cover and was very fair. Participation isn't mandatory, but he will have favorites and they are the ones who participate and joke around with him.

Tony is a good professor. Overall, the course was fairly easy up until the final. The final was next to impossible. However, I feel like he is the lesser of the evils when it comes to the managerial accounting profs.
Great professor, best I've had so far in terms of explaining the subject. The lectures were very engaging, and he did not hesitate to answer questions.

Solid professor who does try his best to teach students whatever he can. Attendance is not mandatory and students are expected to read the textbook and class time is used to go over problems. Tony has years of experience as a CPA and is very knowledgable in the subject, but he often goes on tangents about his dislike of the use of gender neutral pronouns and shifts the conversation from accounting to politics and commentary on the challenges of being a man. The subject is hard. However, if you have a good teacher that can teach and helps you'll be fine. Tony is none of this. Professor Shesh is an extremely good professor, he teaches from the heart, he's very strict and professional but one of the most reasonable professors I've ever seen. His lectures are nice but his assignment grading is weird. More than for design flaws, points were mostly deducted for not including certain things in submission. Sometimes he expects you to have done some things without explicitly mentioning in assignments.
TAs are not supervised properly.

He has designed the course in such a way that you make a lot of mistakes but also end up learning well from them. The problem is that the grading scheme has been designed to have minimal room for error. Those same mistakes will bring your grade down a lot. For a design course, this course isn't designed very well.

Lectures were AMAZING, sometimes droned on but most of the time was very interesting to follow. OOD over summer 1 (2024) was A LOT of homework, like 20-40 hours a week after assignment 3. Grading was a bit harsh but not bad, and regrade requests are very much respected (not always fulfilled tho, obviously). Overall great prof for a hard course.

Prof Shesh is one of my favorite CS profs! I was initially worried to take OOD but lectures were incredibly helpful. He used lots of analogies and code examples making material easy to understand. Homework was not too bad (time consuming though!), and exams were mostly on code reuse. Grading was fair. Overall enjoyed OOD much more than fundies 2.

reviews.comment: Grading rubrics were not always clear, and assignments sometimes had needlessly difficult language. Homeworks are graded very easily, but on exams even small issues things can lead to very large deductions. He has a good sense of humor, and makes himself available outside of class a lot. He is very quick to respond on Piazza/Microsoft Teams.

Initially I was daunted by how difficult and strict Amit was when I asked peers about how his lecture was. My point of view changed. His teaching is lively, I could totally feel his passion about algorithm. There is one thing to keep in mind, his lab make attendance mandatory since you need to explain your codes to TA and mark your scores.

Great for teaching Design Patterns, but assignments are vague and confusing. TAs sometimes contradict the professor. Tough grader, no grade curve. Despite challenges, the course improves development skills.
I loved his classes.
Professor Shesh is an incredible lecturer. His classes are full of life and keep you awake and tentative. The material is not easy but if you put in effort you'll have a great experience.

reviews.comment: He rounds your letter grade down, instead of up. So, a 92.69 is rounded down to an A-, as opposed to rounded up to an A, and so on, apparently under the guise of some absolutist model of mathematical fairness. Real life, however, is random, and the implication of branding the cheap end of the accident onto a students' GPA is ultimately unsavory...

the best and most responsible professor i never met, he teaches python so clearly, and cares about students.  his class is always so funny hahaha, there are always good stories and i cant stop laughing, so i can def focus more on it. i dont like python, but i like his python stories at class haahahahaha.

Best of Luck :-)

Great lectures! I am still waiting for one of his lectures to be boring so I can fall asleep in a class. Prof. Shesh has amazing teaching skills. He can explain the concepts very well by using real-world examples.

might be one of my fav cs profs. the way he explained concepts made things so easy to understand, and if you care enough to show up to class, he will reciprocate and thoroughly clarify any questions you have. he's also pretty funny at times. the other reviews mention harsh grading/taking too long which is true but tbh a lot of that is on the TAs

Shesh is a good lecturer and always encourages questions. However, sometimes he lacks empathy and students will be greatly impacted by that throughout the whole course. Great and considerate professor. Does a solid job at teaching the class and selecting TAs. Professor is a bit too harsh when it comes to grading hw assignments. Overall, a great professor.

Professor Shesh is a harsh grader and gives tons of work. If you miss even a minute of his lecture, you will be completely lost for the rest of class. He is a decent lecturer and not super boring. Shesh was too focused on preparing us for the "real world" which made assignments and exams harder.
He might seem like a nice guy but if anything bad happens to you he won't have an ounce of sympathy. Computer bricked? Death in the family? Panic attack on a final exam? He won't lift a finger.

Class wasn't too helpful. He used OneNote for all lectures instead of code and sometimes used pseudocode. He knows what he is doing but, I don't like how he writes code instead of typing it

Professor Shesh is a great lecturer. He makes hard concepts easy to understand and is willing to answer student questions. Tests can be difficult in his class but Homeworks weighs more in CS3500.

reviews.comment: Shesh is the GOAT. Knows computer science like the back of his hand. Great lecturer, funny and caring guy too. Take a class with him, you won't regret it.

With Shesh, go through the lecture notes on the ccs website to understand what's going on
Amit is a great professor and really helps his students succeed
His teaching skills are excellent. His office hours are helpful. But he is tough grader. He gives lot of homework. Extremely stressful class. But you learn a lot in this class.

Prof. Shesh is a really good lecturer - he knows how to get the point across without just reading slides, and he can always think of examples or analogies to help someone understand in a different way. He's always willing to answer questions and really wants his students to succeed.
Best programing class ever taken. The prof has a good knowledge of the subject and he has the ability to impart it as well.
Do not hesitate to go to his office hours. He is a very helpful professor and wants to see you succeed.

I haven't had Prof. Shesh before this, but it seems he spends a lot of time moderating the class. Seems to be constantly moderating Piazza even long into the evening and on holidays, and is very reciprocating to student jokes/memes, which is nice.
Professor Shesh is fairly quick with responses and grading. His class is difficult and lectures can be hard to follow.

reviews.comment: I had the opportunity to take PDP under him, which is one of the tougher courses. The course is well structured, and the assignments are well designed.

Good person. Very eloquent. Considers your valid requests. Well thought assignments. And always prepared for the class. He handles situations pretty well. Explains thing very well and makes sure they're communicated well. I love his classes. I just wish there were more lecturers like him!

Shesh likes to teach! He's an excellent orator, but don't bring a pen to class: he teaches the wrong way to do things first and then corrects it in the middle of the lesson. The first time you encode stuff to memory, it should NOT be the wrong way. The directions on the exams are more difficult than the questions.

The course has a stupid notion of self-eval with dumb questions in them. The code walks are worse. It is about some specific design patterns but those seem impractical and are okay only from a certain standpoint. The course needs an overhaul and the grading structure is horrible. Yeah there are no extra credits no useful help to make up your losses

Super caring. Echoing all previous reviews. Take him if you can! I look forward to his lectures!! I wish i was able to have him for every class. He makes you feel calm and puts you in the mood to learn.
He is a real gem. Awesome lectures and if you follow all instructions and focus on all his assignments you will learn a lot from his course.
tough grader but awesome teacher, useful assignments and hard test. You have to spend lots of time on his class. Students can learn many valuable knowledge and stuff through the course.
He is just amazing. Makes you love the course. If you just pay attention to his lectures you are good for the concepts. Best course. Best professor.

reviews.comment: The best professor I've ever had as far as teaching is concerned. Good sense of humor and always keeps the class lively. So lively that the class is more entertaining and engaging than half the stuff on Netflix. The professor has a knack of itching out the solutions from the students instead of outright explaining it. Grading is tough though.

Professor Shesh's class was among the most difficult I've taken, but I'm much better as a student and as a programmer for having taken his class. You will really need to be able to think on your feet to be able to do well on exams. But you will learn so much that the hard work pays off. Prof. Shesh also clearly cares about students! Take his class!
Class starts at 11:45 and she sent an email that it was delayed 15 minutes at 11:47. Heavy accent but her lectures are decent.

The exams are wayyy harder than the quizzes and in class assignments. Despite many students failing, she still refuses the curve the grades. She does not care if you fail. Made many students cry after final. DO NOT TAKE HER EVER!!!

Everything seems good until you take the exams. The exams are stupidly harder than weekly quizes or in class assignments or examples in lecture slides. Idk if this is her fault or the department but yea

She wasn't a great lecturer since she really only had one speed which made the content heavy slides impossible to read through completely and the easy slides super drawn out and boring. Nice lady though. My advice: skip the lectures and look at the slides instead.

Sarkar did a great job explaining the topics, even if the lectures were a bit dry and repetitive. She clearly explained what is needed on all the quizzes and exams in the class. Would take her again if I needed another physics course. She is very organized and communicates what is needed well.

reviews.comment: Great professor. Highly recommend having her if you did in 1151. Lectures may be boring, but as long as you pay attention in class, you will do great on the quizzes. Follow her lead, and you will do great, even though the class is slightly harder than 1151.

Great professor. Lectures may be a bit boring at times, but she is very clear on what you need to know for the quizzes. I took the honors section, and I barely studied outside of class because we did so many problems in class. Follow her lead, and you will get a great grade.

Professor Sarkar is an engaging professor who is always available for office hours. Taking the honors section for Physics 1 significantly reduced the amount of time I had to study outside of class because of how many problems were done in class. Student participation is rewarded. Would 100% take again.

She's an average lecturer; definitely wasn't as engaging as other professors I've had at the University. Had a hard time explaining some concepts, and got visibly flustered when asked to explain things in more detail; was lucky I had notes from other sections bc I was lost during certain parts of the course, and we moved very quickly (summer)
She takes questions well, responds timely to emails, and communicates well with the lab and the recitation (ILS). Good professor overall

Prof. Sarkar is always enthusiastic, approachable, has good humor. Covered all medical imaging modalities w perfect pace. Ensures everyone is on track with check-ins during lectures; willing to answer questions. Invited a guest lecturer (made lectures more diverse), and helped every student with preparing our research-presentations. All went great!

reviews.comment: Professor was amazing. She used time effectively and lectures were easy to follow. I definitely recommend taking her Honors Physics 1 for Engineers course. Tough class but great professor. Stay focused and you can do well. Here's my advice: complete every homework, but totally disregard the questions - focus on in-class examples and textbook problems instead. Reading the textbook helps a ton. Lock in for quizzes and the final exams will feel easy.

Honestly a very good professor for Physics, especially in the summer. She gives a ton of extra credit opportunities, and wants to see her students succeed. The exams are not that difficult, alongside the quizzes. Just study and make sure you fully understand the concept as the class is very fast paced.
She was honestly okay as a professor, not the best I've had but far from the worst. Her exams in my opinion are a lot harder than the weekly quizzes which I would definitely take into account.

I loved taking Physics 1 with Prof. Sarkar. She is very funny and understanding, and offers a lot of extra credit, as she is aware that Physics is a challenging class, especially in the summer. There are weekly quizzes and one midterm, + she drops the lowest quiz score, but she gives you a lot of practice to learn. Would retake her in a heartbeat!

Professor Sarkar is an engaging lecturer who is clearly passionate about physics. The honors section of the course is longer in terms of lecture time and there are a few extra assignments / questions on reports but it minimizes the time needed to study for quizzes. I'd recommend the honors section if you're ok spending a bit of extra time in class.

Professor Sarkar knows what she is talking about and is very good at her subject. She isn't always super engaging but is very good at explaining things individually if you do not understand. Overall, she is an average professor, she isn't great or terrible, but she is a nice person.

Professor Cai is incredible. Her humor and energy turned a difficult language into something I genuinely loved practicing. Teaching Chinese songs was a brilliant touch that made the culture feel alive. It's safe to make mistakes, you gain real confidence, take her course. It's more than just a language class; it's a career-defining experience.

I took 2102. Fast-paced and lots of online homework in the beginning but slows down towards the end of semester. Two projects. Very lenient with grading and cares more about your effort. Accepting of every question and very kind & funny. Explains thoroughly. Many opportunities to practice and improve. Great class atmosphere. My favorite teacher!

Would definitely recommend Cai Lao Shi. She's genuinely wants you to learn and wants what's best for you. As long as you do the work and try, you will get a good grade. Very enthusiastic about your learning and creates a great class vibe.

An amazing teacher for Chinese Language, especially if you're learning for the first time! She's very understanding and is pretty lenient with grading. The classroom experience isn't intimidating at all, but there is a lot of speaking and daily vocab dictations, so be prepared to be prepared!

This is the BEST professor I've ever met at Northeastern! You can definitely take his course if it meets your credit standards. He is humorous and helpful to students. He also provides good feedback and shows caring to students. His lectures are not difficult to understand. The assignments are also interesting.

Had Tony for Fundamentals of Music Theory. Class is graded on 8 chapter tests, many quizzes, a midterm, a final, and 3 performances quizzes. It can be a lot, but if you go to class, participate, and show him that you actually care, you'll do well. He's a very understanding guy and a great lecturer.

Listen. Prof. Deritis can be a lot of things. He's encourageable, stubborn, and a bit of a theory snob. Yes I've cried in his class. Sometimes he makes you feel dumb. BUT. This man has had my back unlike any other professor at Northeastern. He doesn't sugarcoat who he is as a person and he doesn't lie to you. If you put in the effort, he will see.

Tony is by far the best professor ive had a northeastern. If you put in the effort to do well, youll get an easy A and hes very passionate about what he teaches. I wasnt positive music was the career for me until I took Tonys class where he made me want to learn more. Hes a great guy and is very confident in what he does.
Tony is dope, straight up. Also described as "problematic fav", because you'll really like him but not learn much about Music Theory 1 itself.

Took Design Thinking course under him. Does not use any PPT or anything to teach. Does not teach anything. He has a instruction and tell students to work on it. Entire course is based on just one project and you can do that project by your own if you have instruction sheet or if you just do any random course on Design Thinking.

took him for music comp seminar 2. an insufferable politicker who has little interest in music and more concerned with his image and ego. he clearly grew bored of the class and gave less and less effort until he stopped showing up at all. no syllabus or grading rubric, class time quickly devolved into talking about himself without fail

An absolutely pointless and horribly designed class. Tony, believing he could not teach the class himself, brought in other professors to do the work for him. Our poor TA nearly graded everything. His use of take home assignments indicated to me had grown bored of teaching the class. His ego is high and he dresses like he just woke up.

Extremely difficult (read: impossible) to do decently without prior music experience.  The guest lectures range from a chance to catch up on sleep to extremely engaging.  Be prepared for ridiculous amounts of work.  Not as easy as a typical arts appreciation class.

Awful class. Described as a basic arts appreciation class, but the readings require a lot of knowledge of music/painting/poetry etc. Tony is very into himself and will spend most of the class listing his accomplishments or his desire for the students to fail his midterm. Brings in guest lecturers too often. Also ridiculous amounts of work.
Tony is into himself, sometimes late to class, and often difficult to find -- but if he sees that you mean business, that your serious about getting ahead, he will go extra miles for you...

Anthony is the most self-rightious member of the music department. And if you get close enough to any of the faculty members, you'll learn they don't like him either. Nice, right? Thinks everyone is levels below him.

Excellent professor.  I had him as a composition instructor for several years and he was always friendly and open, and was very helpful with advising for my classes.  He was always available for office appointments.  A great musician as well.

Oh Tony is FULL of himself. You'll hear all about the fact he did the music for the 1997 Macworld Game of the Year. He'll walk away from you when you're talking to him. Needs to be more amiable, being the freaking CHAIR of the music department.

head of the dept. thinks he's god...he's not. never in his office for office hours, thinks most students are wasting his time and sends them away from him to their department advisor. needs some new people skills.
Midterms every 2 weeks, no curve and final exam is cumilative of 15 chapters and is 40% of the grade. Good luck.

96% of the grade is just quizzes and exams. 4% is participation. Good person at heart but does not budge to even the most genuine requests. Tests are in class on lockdown. If he is your last resort, trust me and please skip to take this class next semester. Not worth getting a C.

Great and knowledgeable professor. Had 4 tests, but all were manageable.

BEWARE! The tests are stupid and too specific. reviews.comment: Great teacher for genetics. lectures in person and on zoom which is great because I find it easier to pay attention on Zoom. All the tests are online open-book but need studying to do well. He is very passionate about his content and seems to love teaching. does tophat questions for attendance credit in class, but gives 75% credit even if wrong.

He is the nicest professor ever and extremely leniant with late assignments and absences. He really cares about the subject and preparing his students for the real world. I would definitely reccomend taking him if you want to learn useful skills in a low stakes environment.

Javier was a wonderful professor and truly passionate about his students learning in class & out (service learning). Classes are small group discussions based on a variety of aging papers. There are no exams and he is flexible with assignment deadlines. I would definitely recommend taking this course!

Dr. Apfeld is an extremely caring and kind professor, and is very understanding about personal issues and willing to be flexible with deadlines. The class itself is a lot of reading, but very discussion based and helpful in learning how to approach reading research papers. He is very passionate about this topic and cares about his students.
Dr. Apfeld is so kind, flexible, and passionate about the content.

Dr.Apfeld isn't the best lecturer, but it's easy to succeed if you review lectures, teach yourself, and complete all homework and review materials. Tests are online, open book, and not hard with a good understanding of the material. He drops the lowest of 3 exams (each 25%) and the final is cumulative (35%). He is not so great at lecture/oral presentation skill, but he is a GREAT teacher, he cares about you and gives you good grade and a lots of extra credits, he is always there if u want to reach out outside of class. I had to admit that he so far the only prof who actually cared about their student and their grades after high school.

For starters, he is an amazing guy who is very caring. I had a lot of family stuff going on during the semester and he was supportive and would excuse me when I missed class. Apfeld was a good guy, however, I never understood his lectures because he would mumble. His exams were hard, but open note. He was a caring guy, but I never got much out of his class and therefore wouldn't take him again.

reviews.comment: Such a sweet guy but unfortunately a bad lecturer. I tried to follow his train of thoughts until I realized he gets lost in his own logic, and I stopped paying attention. Uses Tophat for in-class questions, quizzes, and exams. Not hard to get an A, but you won't learn anything unless you study all the materials yourself.

Professor Apfeld is very kind and actually quite funny at times. His fatal flaw is that he tends to mumble his way through lectures and it is quite impossible to stay engaged in class. With that said, all of the tests are online and open note so it is easy to get a good grade.

Good guy, and not the hardest class, but a few things: do the hw at the end of lectures and be prepared to pull out ones from past lectures for his quizzes, lecturing skills are mid so printing out the slides and jotting ideas down for review afterward might help more than full blown notes, and tests do have problems that require a lotta practice.

There's tophat questions every class. You can look at the lectures ahead of time on canvas and find the answers on quizlet. None of the tophat questions are on the exams. Exam 1 and 3 are easy, 2 and the final were not as easy. The tophat questions are required. He just reads off slides and can't answer questions.

reviews.comment: I love Professor Apfeld so much!! He really cares about his students and takes your feedback on the class into serious consideration. He always emphasizes going to office hours and he really tries hard to make sure students are doing well. He makes the classroom a safe and inclusive place--overall a very kind man and great professor

Personality wise professor apfeld is so understanding and actually cares about your mental health Quizzes and Tophat questions were easy Exams were somewhat confusing but fair- please do the practice exams Hes open to any questions in office hours but doesnt really answer them well during lectures Mediocre lecturer, reads off slides a lot

Dr. Apfeld doesn't really go too in depth with the material, and usually reads off of powerpoint slides. Not too helpful when in need of some clarification for some material. Generally a nice man, but does not make things clear enough for his students.

Professor Apfeld is a PowerPoint reader. He gives HW from the textbook and doesnt know how to answer them. His test questions are weirdly worded. He loves to talk about worms, but they get extremely annoying. His office hours are useless, get ready to self teach yourself. Only good thing about the class was that the man is nice and the cat memes.
Just a ppt reader, boring.
Loves talking about his c. elegans. Sweet, funny guy but unfortunately a terrible professor. Class was based on tophats, three exams, and a final :/
good!

Certainly knowledgeable but struggles to explain information in an understandable way. The same goes for his feedback. Critical to get off to a good start in his class as this will change the way he views your work. Also, he values the final product more than your iterations, which was annoying.

reviews.comment: Overall really good teacher. Sometimes his explanations didnt make sense and I needed to teach myself a concept myself. I learned a lot about myself and how to fight on in this class.

reviews.comment: Very boring lecturer who is very unclear during class. Often makes simple concepts much more difficult to understand. It is wise to not go to lectures and just show up for discussion sessions with the TA, which is actually helpful. Definitely would not recommend this professor to anyone.
calc is a hard class. professor appel makes it much easier. put in the work and pay attention to her lecture and do every homework problem and the tests will be a breeze for you.
Do the work and homework and the tests will be a breeze. Paying attention in class is essential and you will get an A in the class. Very good math 118 teacher. Recommend class
Very confusing lectures; often not relevent to the course and out of syllabus. Can be a little condescending sometimes but if you ask specific questions, he will help.

Took Calc 1 with him at USC. I was surprised I got an A because I found his material very confusing because he focused on proofs and theory.  He's one of those teachers that thinks hard math is simple for everyone. However, he is helpful and willing to work with you. Language barrier was sometimes an issue with both him and the TA.

Actually teaches CALC I at University of Southern California now. I've taken Calculus before, but this was infinitely harder. Hates calculators, loves proofs. Italian accent can be an issue if you've never heard one before. Overall, I hated this class immensely. If stuck with  Andrea, just follow along with the text book in class.

Average Instructor. Has an Italian accent and uses strange terms sometimes but is overall understandable. Attendance is pretty important for the weekly quizzes, but he only uses 6 of 10 of them for your grade. He likes it when students really participate. HW is online and incredible easy. This class has a low demand for studying outside of class.

I personally thought he was a great professor. He taught throw lecture slides that you would fill in as you went through the material. He emphasized patterns that have helped me through Orgo 2. He wasn't there to be your friend, but he was so helpful at office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Aparece is by far one of the best teachers I've had in my life. His lectures helped me learn a lot, and he repeated certain key words and color coded his notes to really reinforce our learning. He teaches Orgo like a puzzle, which made it enjoyable to learn. Office hours were practice sessions for exams, and I highly recommend going to them.

Very inspirational and caring Professor. Orgo 2 is already hard enough but he makes it interesting and accommodates all the students. Very accessible outside of class and the tests are not hard if you just study and do everything he tells you to do outside of class. Lots of office hours.

Super accessible outside of class. 3-6 office hours/ week where he practically gives away test answers. People worry that his tests are open response, DONT! He is super liberal w/ partial credit, if you answer everything youll get a good grade. Hes consistent and fair, not tryna trick you. Truly cares for his students & wants them to love orgo

Prof Aparece was thorough and very passionate about Orgo Chem. He works hard to try and explain concepts to students and assist them in understanding them. He truly made the stress and difficulties of orgo chem slightly easier. His exams were definitely hard, but his office hours cleared any confusion.

Aparece is by far the best professor I've had in the science department. He is so knowledgable, funny, and personable. He has a lot of office hours throughout the week where you can meet other students in the class and do practice problems. His tests are open response, which requires you to truly understand the content. Would definitely recommend.

I took chemistry before professor Aparece but he really helped me understand the topics I was confused about. He held office hours in chem central and made himself super accessible. I would definitely take him again.
I actually enjoyed Organic chemistry by the end of his class. Never thought that would happen

reviews.comment: Pick another professor if you can. The homework is very difficult and doesn't help you on the tests. When you ask him a question, he gets mad if you don't know it.

Professor Aparece is a great chemistry instructor and is always accessible for office hours. If you show up to class, follow along with the slides, and go to office hours to do work if you're confused, it's not hard to get an A. His tests always align with lecture and he lays out the covered content very well.

Although I barely got an A in orgo 1, I felt like I didn't really KNOW the material. In Orgo 2, Professor Aparece helped me really understand the concepts in organic chemistry, allowing me to solve the problems rather than just memorize reactions. Using the Office hours was crucial and doing practice problems is key Frq tests are hard but not bad

Aparece is a great professor. He's so nice and it's easy to reach him with questions outside of class. If you have to take orgo, take his class.

Aparece was one of the best professors I've had. He explains things in a very clear way and he always prepares for his lectures. Holds lots of office hours.

reviews.comment: What a great guy. Aparace made me actually like organic chemistry. His classes are fun, interesting, and comprehensive. To get a good grade in the class, really try to put in the work at the beginning so you understand the mechanisms/patterns. He gives you all the study materials necessary to get an A. Use them!!!!

Dr. Aparece was a great teacher for General Chemistry at Northeastern. Although his 100 minute lectures can drag on, his tests are very fairmostly multiple choice and a couple short answers. Not only that but he's pretty funny, tries to relate to students, and gives free points by PollEv. If I could have him again next semester I definitely would.

An amazing professor who really cares about his students. I took orgo 2 in the summer, and he continuously adjusted the syllabus to our tight schedule. reviews.comment: Cool Teacher. She knows a lot. Gave some hard assignments and assigned several readings but proved helpful with my writing and analytical skills.

Horrible teacher. She comes to class fifteen minutes late all the time and is never prepared. She reads essays aloud in class and will only give you comments on your paper then, making people sit there for an entire hour and a half of class time just listening to her drone on.
Horrible teacher poor communication never thought a class could be so bad

Really nice teacher teaching an incredibly easy class. You'll watch a lot of movies and if you suggest any movie and have a reason for suggesting it, chances are she'll let the class watch it. Extremely approachable, by far my favorite first semester professor.

Interesting professor.  Classes can be boring to sit through and sometimes she tries creating ideas just so there is more to talk about.  But she will help you improve your essays, and shes a fairly easy grader.  More essays than most professors, but easier as well.  Attendance is mandatory though, but overall, good professor.

She was unclear...her assignments are unclear and she changes it constantly, but she is a pushover...ask her to watch a movie to relate to the essay and thats all you will do in class...will make classes a whole lot easier...she grades easily...but is a stickler for grammar (if you go to the writing center she will give you an extension for sho)
she knew her stuff-very intelligent. and helpful.

It was always difficult to understand what was going on. He would rush, stutter, and make mistakes often which made it difficult to follow along with the lecture. Mr. Gomez's teaching style is not effective at all. His teaching style was really effective and the way he words his questions were confusing as times. He is willing to help out but once again the way he explains things is difficult. He is a strict grader.
I feel like his teaching style isn't really affective
He's very strict and his class is confusing

Joke of a professor, though not a bad person himself.
I'm still baffled that's he extensively used AI for his course.
Uses AI instead of own knowledge and time to prepare their lectures.  Yet doesnt want you utilizing tools. I guess its great for teaching the greedy and hypocritical side of business instead

Worst instructor I've had. Grades were based on flattery, not work quality. Sloppy, AI-generated lecture slides and notes were the least of his many shortcomings. Fire him.
Using too much AI.

Rick might be the worst ever. He spends all the class time on an egotistical rant or creating useless activities and then gives extremely difficult quizzes on lecture notes that he has never discussed. Attending class is a waste of time, though attendance is mandatory, and he never wastes an opportunity to put you down personally and embarassingly.
Very fun professor, super memorable!

Arrowood is a fine professor and this class was not particularly challenging, the content was even interesting. His teaching style was objectively bad. He mostly attempted to actively recall course material aloud in a way that was very difficult to follow. Double standards. Extremely arrogant and disrespectful towards his students. Authoritarian.

(Boston College) Professor Arrowood is charismatic and he tries to make his classes funny and engaging but ends up embarrassing students and himself a lot of the time. He is very unserious during class only for his assignments to be unexpectedly more complicated than they ever should be. Disorganized. Would not take again.

Truly dedicated to his craft great atmosphere & students encouraged to joke & contribute Teaching style not for everyone Went on tangents w/ lectures & interrupted students to embarrass/correct them in front of class Little criteria given - fun at times but expected to know what he wants &  answer how he likes Fun class but introverts be warned!
Amazing gave my group a straight A on the project

Very disorganized and confusing professor. You have to pay for a case study that he wrote which has tons of mistakes and is poorly written. And then he's ironically tough when grading. Asked for feedback on a quiz multiple times and never got it. Discussions are fun but he interrupts frequently and can be disrespectful. Charismatic guy, though.

My second class with Rick and if I could take him again I absolutely would. He truly wants students to learn things through experience rather than from a textbook so the class was very entertaining. Consisted of lighthearted and interesting discussions on EVERYTHING and fun activities. Provided that you match his enthusiasm, you will get an A.

My favourite professor at northeastern. He is the only option to take for ORGB in my opinion. Provided that you go into this course with an open mind about what you normally expect from a class then you will enjoy it. To do well you must participate but all classes are very casual discussions which I loved

One of the most enjoyable classes that I've had at Northeastern so far despite it being a 3 hour long class once a week. 

Professor is nice, funny and fair. Takes a very different approach to classes which involved constant discussion which was a very effective way to learn for me. If you have no trouble participating then this class is for you.

We rarely went over the necessary and applicable materials for this class, and if we did, Arrowwood would only do half of it and ask us to look at it on our own time. Most of the classes were discussions about a topic he chose that was somewhat related to the class. one time he graded my essay with a grammarly screenshot

This class was probably my favorite of all the classes I've ever taken! Though the class was lecture-heavy, it sets you up very well for the exams and weekly homework assignments.
