Lowkey the tests were just super hard imo LOL, I did well on every homework but pretty bad on midterms + final, maybe just me. Ariel as a person is great, she's very accessible outside of class but if tests are hard for you (like me) it may not be the best so go to class because her lectures are very in depth.

Professor Hamlin cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The class is lecture only which is fine, some lectures are better than others. The first exam was relatively difficult, second was extremely easy and just like her guide. The weekly problem sets become increasingly annoying and are worth 40% of your ENTIRE grade, so put in effort.

Incredible engaging and clear lectures, is very knowledgable of the content, and makes you learn it so easy. A bit ackward and cringey. Attendance is not mandatory but I would highly recommend going to class, subject is very interesting too. One of the best professors I've had.
Super nice professor and also very chill. Homework can be time-consuming but will prepare you for the exam. Probably the nicest professor in all of Khoury.

I went to the other professor because i didnt like her she tries to be funny and im just bored of her lectures so i never paid attention. even tho i did the practice exam, i didnt do good on the exams but for some reason i ended with a B+ lolll so ig it chill.

Professor was very warm and welcoming and its hard not to like her. Be prepared to type homework, including tedious mathematical operations, but you get used to it. She teaches really well, grading is fair, and you can really tell she cares about her students. Easy 5!

Very well-explained lectures; knows how to make students understand a completely new topic. Transitions from content is very smooth and easygoing; if you attend all lectures and ask questions, she will make this complicated class way easier. *Be sure to go over formatting for hw since the first day cause you might get deducted some points.
Very good professor, knows a lot about the content and makes the lectures simple to follow and understand.

Tough Professor who wasn't able to provide a lot of support within the classroom. Also notes are horrible, so try to attend the TA Office Hours to understand what happened in class but beware, there are no zooms to check the lecture again so be careful as this professor's notes were bad and there was no zoom to look back at.
Nice professor, easy to follow and understand during classes. Notes aren't great; stay focused during classes.

Great! Will talk about her cats at any given opportunity. HW can get a little heavy, but its not too much work, and the tests are easy. However, do not miss class, there is no textbook and her notes aren't great.
The class is not hard, and you can easily skip classes based on the topic of the class. It's not hard to get an A as long as you go to class and pay attention

Good teacher tbh. Made content that wasn't super straightforward rather easy. I just wish she didn't try to be funny or get the class to participate because no one gives her energy back and it was really hard to watch.

Had very good energy during class. Grading was extremely lenient and fair. Lectures were very clear and easy to follow, she used class time efficiently. Questions on homeworks, quizzes, and the final did not contain material not taught and were very doable if you paid attention in class.

Instructor grading is pretty lenient and they curve the exams if needed. Instructor makes a lot of mistakes during lecture which can hinder your learning experience, but they do correct themselves. Professor would be unprepared and unorganized at times with their notes which can get pretty difficult in understanding material in a timely manner.

Prof. Hamlin is smart, and while the class is lecture heavy, I like her lecture style. She's great at answering questions during lecture, makes herself available outside of class, and is incredibly kind. It's absurd to expect an instructor teaching abstract math to never make a mistake in lecture; she's a great teacher sensitive to students' needs

Often gets confused by her own notes, messes up in lectures, and gets corrected by students. I honestly think she is confused on the topics herself, making it impossible to learn. Homework often includes problems we spoke about in class for 2 minutes. I think if she went over questions that paralleled the homework I would learn much better.
AWESOME

Professor Hamlin is by FAR the best option for CS1800. Attend her lectures even if you aren't placed into her section. The class itself kinda sucks but she does the best job out of any professor of explaining the material in lecture. She's really nice and a bit awkward but that's just part of her charm.

One of the best professors I've had! Professor Guha is very kind and approachable which was huge for me as a freshman in my first semester. He's very knowledgable and is always willing to help. Also a great lecturer. Coursework wasn't so bad but did require a decent amount of work
Arjun is a good guy who cares a lot about what he's teaching and the students' success. His lectures can be somewhat shaky at times. He's very fair and considerate and wants his students to succeed.

Professor Guha was great at dealing with issues in this class. I had an issue with a lab partner and he resolved it quickly. Though the homework and exams were graded pretty toughly, that was due to the rubric of this class more so than Guha himself. Though his lectures left something to be desired, he was definitely the best option for fundies1.

Arjun is a god. He gives paper practice exam problems all the time in class (often they are harder than the exam itself so don't stress too much if one is particularly hard to understand) and he loves to answer questions. Hilariously sassy too.

Professor Arjun has possibly become my favorite professor at Northeastern, so far. He's very engaging in his lectures; he's funny, attentive,  and caring. If someone has a question, he does his best to answer it in a way they understand, and he actually gives enough time for people to ask questions, unlike some other professors. Highly recommend.
The Best professor in CS 2500 for 23 Fall!

Stopped going to Patterson's lectures to go here and learned so much. Loves how he literally gives practice questions during lectures and gives students time to work w/ each other on the code he wrote. Very interactive space and he's very engaging to listen to.
Very caring professor, the explanations of each concept is clear and understandable.

Arjun was one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern so far. His lectures were funny and I always went to them, even though attendance wasn't required. His lectures can seem unrelated to the homework at times, but you will appreciate them at the end of the course. Will often explicitly write code during office hours --  extremely helpful!

His lectures were good, but if you didn't review the material beforehand it could be very difficult. But yes, it's also a weeder intro CS class, so don't expect it to be easy. He was amazing considering the difficulty of the class. Still, many students didn't come to class and used the recorded lectures (that were great) made by Prof. Derbinsky.
Such a good teacher, class also had recorded video lectures which were helpful. However, even if you learn a lot you can still end with a less than amazing grade.

Arjun is awesome. He is so knowledgeable (granted you are willing to go beyond the topics covered in class) and will help you solve any issues. He has a very good humor that gets you engaged into the lecture. Also, He responds to email in minutes. Would take him again in any class.
Loved taking fundies 1 with Arjun. I feel that regardless of your level of comp sci knowledge before the class, you can come out confident about the material.
Great guy. Has a great sense of humor and cared about his student's success. His live coding style was helpful. He is responsive to feedback and a fair grader.
Online class with her was a light workload and she is very generous with grading! Responds quickly to emails and is willing to meet with you if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If Cheryl is your co-op advisor, you are in good hands. She's very supportive, and I wouldn't have wound up in this great situation without her.
Lectures could be a bit slow but the class was run well overall. Fair grader and always willing to help.

The professor is very fair, great at teaching, and assigns weekly homework with coding reviews conducted by TAs. He is caring, understanding, and professional. He answers all questions, but midterm questions are not directly from slides; they are based on lecture content. I would highly recommend taking his class.
Very good teacher, my concepts are clear because of him
Thoroughly Enjoyed his Class!

Dr. Shields is super kind and you can tell she really loves teaching. I honestly have 0 complaints about her or the class. The class is very easy and she is very understanding. Quizzes are all open note, no exams or final. Takes attendance for participation grade.
One of the best professors, so kind… and actually takes the time to interact with her students.

reviews.comment: Honestly an amazing professor! She was super sweet and bubbly, open to extensions on assignments, and responds to emails super quick. Also not a harsh grader which was great since we had presentations.
Very energetic and uplifting! Grading criteria is clear, and feedback is thorough. She cares a lot about her students, and makes the content interesting. Take her for Health Comm!

HAD HER FOR COMM3230 INTERPERSONAL COMM (it wasnt listed here)-- Best professor I've ever had in the comms department as a 5th year. She is bubbly, very personable, caring, understanding and flexible for the student needs. She makes it very easy to do well and breaks down the material in a fun, modern way. Highly recommend.
Great professor, super passionate, and very real!

literally one of the kindest profs I've had! She's extremely understanding about her student's circumstances. She's a really engaging professor b/c you can tell she cares about her work. Her course is pretty chill+ she provides rubrics for her assignments. She made public speaking very comfortable so imo i definitely got better at presenting.

Professor Shields is an awesome professor who definitely knows what she is teaching, she also brings crazy energy to the classroom no matter what time the class is. in terms of grading she's pretty chill, she gives rubrics that clearly outline the scope of the assignments and there is no final exam! super sweet, understanding and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ashleigh is one of the most enthusiastic and passionate teachers I have had so far. She is an engaging lecturer and really cares about her students. She made public speaking seem not as frightening.
Professor Shields is so nice, caring, and kind. She is super enthusiastic everyday in class and is very understanding. She's an easy grader and a great person. Definitely take her for PHTH 2300.
Dr. Shields is great! Very humble, kind, and wants to see her students do well.  She makes class fun.

Professor Shields is one of the best instructors I've ever had in my life. She cares so much about what she is doing and teaching, as well as each student. She is very understanding of life outside her class, and will always be accommodating. A good mixture of assignments and the course is very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Shields is a very genuine and kind person, you can truly tell that she cares for all her students. She's a super easy grader and all of the quizzes are pretty easy too.

Prof Shields is full of energy and is super sweet. She makes lectures entertaining and keeps you engaged. She's very lenient about grades/deadlines/etc. I loved the projects and graded assignments she gave us.

She makes lecture engaging by asking questions about your thoughts. For presentations, public speaking is evaluated and she does exercises during class to prepare for that. She's so nice and energetic. Gives feedback and cares about her students. Projects back to back because it was a summer class.

Professor Shields is wonderful and caring! For those who are scared to speak in front of people, she won't judge you ever. Make sure to read assigned chapters bc she does give pop quizzes where one has to summarize in front of the class. She is so nice and understanding!!! TAKE HER CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

Even you speak more than 3 times on the class she still gives you a B- on your class participation, even you tried very hard to make your final paper perfect you may still eventually receive a very low score. Her classes are all very hard.

Worst professor I've ever had at Northeastern. Never came to class, boring lectures, and holier than thou attitude. Take this course with literally anyone else
Just not a good teacher overall and his grading policy is awful. Would never take his class again if I had the opportunity as well as he is very difficult to understand because of his broken english.
Trust me i work hard this is the only withdrawal on my transcript for a reason

tests are NOTHING like the homework. passionate professor, but unable to teach effectively/doesn't prepare you for the exams. don't get too close with your classmates, they'll probably drop. take that as a sign and join them while you're ahead makes an alr difficult course even more unbearable. horrible, HORRIBLE prof.
helll nawww, to the naw naw naww (hell to the naw)

DO NOT TAKE IT WITH ASSAD. I had Assad last Spring for Diff Eqs and his communication was just absolutely atrocious. All around good professor. reviews.comment: Sweetest professor I've ever had. We had quizzes two times a week but if you paid attention in class they weren't bad at all. Most of the time the quiz questions were exact copies of problems we did in class. We also got to bring a cheat sheet for every quiz and test. The tests were harder than the quizzes, but you should do fine if you study.

He is a very good professor. The class was graded only on tests which made it more difficult but he dropped the two lowest quizzes. The in-class midterms were nowhere near as difficult of the final. I had a 97 going into the final but ended with a B because of the final even when I got 10% above the average so study A LOT for the final.

Great Professor, this was my second time taking Diff Eq's and he was so much better than my first professor. For Diff Eq's if you can't get loopi, Assad's the second best professor. Is a physics guy so if you're into that, you'll love Assad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is a funny professor but tests are way too harsh and the class average was extremely low. Average on the final was a 67, so get ready for this class to tank your GPA. Only graded from 6 exams and the final with no extra credit or anything

Assad is such a sweet guy; he is very understanding and truly wants you to succeed. 
I only took pre-calc in high school so this class was def challenging for me, but he gave us extra credit to keep our grades as high as possible before the final, which is 40% of ur grade. He drops ur lowest test grade too, which helped my grade a lot. I recommend!

Really kind and caring professor. I thought he did an amazing job explaining the concepts. His quizzes and tests were quite easy and homework was optional. He does teach a bit slow and get behind, he doesn't always cover everything and the final is harder than his tests. If you want an easier semester but more work during finals, take Assad.

Doesn't know how to work canvas at all and won't ever respond emails. Takes favorites. I was heavily disliked by him so therefore he would single me out and dock me test points he didn't do for others. Grade calculated is done poorly because there's only 6 things + the final. You have to do well on everything. No calculator, everything on paper.

Super kind, teaches through examples. You honestly don't even have to go to class to succeed. Gives practice quizzes/exams that are just like the actual thing. He confuses himself a little sometimes but nothing crazy. Definitely would take him again

love the man. Just go to class, take notes (he writes everything down on the board you don't even have to listen to him), do the practice tests and quiz a day before your tests or quizzes and you're set. Super easy. HW is fun but not necessary as long as you're able to solve the problems you've taken in your notes, you're good. Just go to class!

reviews.comment: Had him for Calc 1 & Physics 1 ILS, reasonable grader but confuses himself at times. semester 1 vs semester 2 his teaching has declined. He made calc 1 a more confusing than it should have been tbh. ALWAYS late, funny & cool guy though. Calc 1 is a lot of lecture and examples w little explanation of actual concepts, but ILS lectures aren't helpful.

Very nice professor, but his lectures aren't great. He doesn't explain the topics you are learning he just does example problems on the board. So be ready to teach yourself the topics outside of class. Exams can be tricky as well.

Very nice and funny guy but your graded entirely on test scores which kinda sucks, participation isn't mandatory but he did start taking participation near the end of the semester because if you attend class he says he will bump your grade up a bit

Overall not a bad professor, he drops 1 out of 6 quizzes during the semester. He doesn't require homework but in return your whole grade is based on your quizzes/tests/final. Does a lot of examples in class for things on the quizzes/tests/final. He also gives out practice tests for everything which is the same questions just different numbers.

Took Calc 1 in Fall 2024. 6 quizzes, and only the top 5 are graded. 2 midterms, 1 final worth 40% of the grade. Class was alright, very lecture-heavy, and he is NOT tech savvy, lol. Everything (syllabus, practice tests, etc) was just posted into the 'Files' tab on Canvas. Also he never has slideshows, he just writes stuff on the board. He is funny.

He seemed like a genuinely nice guy but very forgetful. I did not have him for the physics class but for physics ILS. While I got along with him well, his explanations at the beginning were a bit confusing, and he kept forgetting to grade the quizzes of students who went to the DRC for test taking. I received my quizzes back RIGHT before exams.

MATH 1241- love love love! Definitely recommend having him as a professor. Everything is super straight forward. If you go to class, pay attention, and do the practice exams, you will do well. 6 tests that are each 10%, final is 40%. Attendance isn't mandatory and neither is buying a textbook, but I would recommend doing so.

Best professor I've had so far! As long as you go to class and do the homeworks this class isn't bad at all. Lot's of the examples that he does in class are really similar to the questions on the exam and you get a cheat sheet for the exam. He's super funny and I would really recommend going to his office hours. Final was hard compared to midterms.
The Group problem is hard and he hardly ever explain it.

Physics 2 with Assad was a cakewalk over Summer 1. Super easy exams, similar in difficulty to the practice exams. Some questions on the homeworks and quizzes can be challenging, but the most challenging questions won't be on exams. Lectures are great but are very long and slow paced. Physics II Lab isn't hard, but is a time sink; some bad TAs.

Assad is a great professor. His lectures are very clear and goes through many practice problems in class. The practice quizzes and tests were exact representations of the tests and quizzes given in class. He cracks jokes throughout lecture and is very kind.

Assad is the best professor I've ever had! He makes class funny and enjoyable and explains difficult concepts really well. Outside of class I really recommend going to office hours  he is very kind and is always willing to help.
This is by far the best profession I have had at Northeastern. His study guides laid out clearly what was going to be tested on the 6 exams we had before the final.

Assad is the best. His lecture are very clear and he tells you exactly what you need to know for quizzes and exams. He does tons of practice problems that are similar to assessments. He is so sweet, I recommend going to his office hours whether you have questions or just to chat. I wish I had him for physics 2, he's truly the best!

Assad was great. He derives formulas and does primarily practice problems. He's often late to class. Has an accent, but easy to understand. He gives notes on common mistakes and drops the lowest quiz. The practice exams he posts are exactly like his actual exams. Just find the textbook online for free. Easy if you took BC and just need refreshers.

He provided the notes online and his practice quizzes closely resembled the real ones. However, your grade is entirely made of quizzes/tests -homework/participation has no impact. No extra credit was offered. He mainly wrote on the board, rarely explaining the material. He was often late to class. The average class attendance rate was about 50%.

reviews.comment: This guy does not know how to teach and at 10pm the night before final gave 2 more topics to learn

Assad was the best math professor I've ever had throughout my school life. He made everything so clear and his practice tests were very similar to the real ones which prepared me very well. I 100% recommend taking his class

Assad is a very caring and funny professor. I had him for Calculus for Business which is a very easy class especially if you've taken calculus before. If you haven't taken calculus before, the way he explains concepts may be very confusing. He is very knowledgable though and will take the time to explain something to you.

AWFUL prof. His lectures are terrible, not clear, and all over the place. Easy A tho.

Assad is a good guy. Really funny and clearly knows the subject. He's very receptive to feedback when a student points out an error in his work. For his calculus one class, if you show up to class, take notes, and spend maybe 30 minutes after every lecture studying, there's no reason you shouldn't get at least a B.

Prof. Fotovatian is a great professor. He is funny and clearly loves physics. Grades are from homework, biweekly quizzes, and the midterm and final exams, but there is a ton of extra credit on the homework and he is always willing to help. The difficult part of the class is the lab reports since they are worth 15% of the lecture course grade.

The lectures mainly consist of learning through examples, which is helpful if you take notes. He is also very clear about what is on exams, making studying streamlined and less stressful. 

Great professor- I recommend you take him for Calculus 2, Physics 1, and Physics 2. He often tells funny stories which help make the class interesting.

I had this prof for physics 1 and this course was much less well taught. It felt like the lectures were poorly planned and I had trouble following the content. There would be questions on the hw and quizzes that we hadn't learned yet. The material was pretty easy so it wasn't that bad and he's a really nice guy, just very diff than physics 1.
Great professor. Lecture interesting

Lecture heavy, homework is completely optional, and if you have taken calc before, it is an easy A. Grade is based off of 6 exams and the final. Practice exams are super similar to the actual exams, and he is very understanding. He can get distracted during class, so sometimes he is hard to follow. I personally loved him!

Professor Fotovatian is definitely a safe option for Calculus. Not going to lie, sometimes he would make me super mad cuz a lot of times his lecture examples had a lot of mistakes. But overall, he's a super fair grader and super nice, so still a really good professor. Way better than some other calculus professor that I hear of.

Grade is entirely based on tests but there is sometimes bonus and he drops the lowest one. Not the clearest teaching and sometimes class feels all over the place. You'll be fine if you've taken calc before. Practice exams are super useful and he gives optional homework.
best teacher i've ever had at Northeastern!!!!!
i love him. BEST PROF i've ever had at northeastern. he makes physics seem simple compared to other professors. homework can be a bit challenging but exams are straight from his lectures.

He was a very good lecturer and gave practice problems that were exactly like the tests and quizzes. The homework took awhile but was worth getting good grades on the midterm and final. Would recommend studying the reviews and the in-class problems, don't waste time or money on the textbook. Overall, would recommend for this class.

He doesn't engage much with students but seems like a great guy and gives very clear lectures. Gives practice quizzes and exams that are exactly like the actual thing. Not very accessible outside of class but the class is pretty self-explanatory. Don't have to come to lectures but it's best to bc then you don't have to look in the textbook.

Showed up to class late and never explained the concept; he only teaches the concept and not the application. You could probably do well if you've taken calc 2 before, but as someone who didn't, he didn't explain enough for me to understand completely. He also barely went to his office hours (at 8 am), and his lectures can be hard to follow.

He may be a better physics than calc teacher, but for calc 2 I can't recommend him. He is okay, but very often late and disorganized. He doesn't explain concepts as thoroughly as he could, but I don't think he's awful. Definitely an okay option if you're good at calculus or have taken it before.

This class feels like my dad taught me Calc II... in the best way. From the subtle dad jokes to the comprehensive variety of examples to the warm way he teaches during office hours, I enjoyed it. 40% of your grade is a final, and another 40% are two midterms, so beware, but the rest are quizzes (and the lowest two are dropped!). Class is fast.

reviews.comment: Stay away if you can. He's a great guy and is really nice but doesn't explain what he's doing. The whole class consists of him writing on the board and you copying it rather than actually learning.

The only physics professor who actually knows how to teach! He actually makes me not hate physics. He explains and derives the equations carefully so that you actually understand the questions instead of *just* plugging in numbers. He can go a little fast, but if you spend time with the material or go to office hours to ask, u'll do great.

Professor Fotovatian was such a professor. For Fall 2020 semester he only graded quizzes (9 and dropped your lowest grade), the final, and midterm. He is a very fair grader and even gives you his number to reach out
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, however I did feel better when I went for tutoring sessions outside of class to help me prep for exams. As long as you understand the problems on the boards and on quizzes, you'll be ready for the exams. Weekly quizzes.

Gives quizzes about every two weeks which are straightforward, and provides practice exams which are basically the same as the actual exams. Lectures can be boring, but he explains everything clearly and prepares you well. Won't need textbook at all.

He is a good professor and clearly knows what he is talking about. He gives good explanations. However, sometimes he would stray from the material or show up to class late and not leave us enough time to do work. So, you just need to be patient. But overall, really great professor!

I took Calculus I with Professor Fotovatian and his lectures were always enjoyable. Not only did he explain the important concepts in detail but he also made them easy to understand. He is a great teacher and he tends to be pretty funny as well. I am happy to say that I am taking Professor Fotovatian's section of Calculus II next semester.

Really Nice guy - Dad Jokes and innocently funny anecdotes litter his class. Uses loads of colorful chalk, has all his notes on blackboard, does lots of examples in class. Tests are super easy if you listen in class, reading not necessary.

I'm so glad I took physics with professor Assad! He is AWESOME! He is so helpful and always available after class for help. He even provide his students with his personal phone number so we can text him with any questions about problems. Exams are based on the lecture and the quizzes! Quizzes are from lectures and he will drop the 2 lowest grades

He's super funny and nice, if you pay attention, show up, and do the homework, it's a very straightforward class. He loves his job and thinks he's hilarious (which he is). Very generous with partial credit but also teaches very well so you actually know what's going on

He has a great personality to lecture. He sometimes doesn't finish his sentences, but he'll always make sure you have what you need for the quiz/test if you're paying attention. I suck at algebra and Physics, and I regret not going to his office hours. I can't stress enough to go to his office hours. Overall one of my favorite professors.

Literally the nicest professor ever. Very understanding and is always wiling to look over grading for quizzes and tests. Very good at giving partial credit, has lot's of opportunities to boost your grade. Available to reach outside of class. Very funny during the lectures. Would take him again and recommend to other students.

Assad cares about his students and wants all of them to do well. His lectures can be chaotic, but some light textbook reading before class will help you keep track of his direction. He makes an effort to actually explain the application and relevance of different concepts, and he's available outside of class for help. He even gave us his number.

He was the nicest professor! I would recommend him in the future! Grading was very clear, 10 quizzes with 2 dropped. Lab grades are factored in which helps. You can bring a cheat sheet to the midterm and final but everything is clear as to what will be on the exams.
The professor goes out of his way to make the class fun and makes jokes along the lectures. He is a very kind person and is accessible to students when they have doubts.

He is extremely specific about what will be on the weekly quizzes, midterm, and final. He even gives examples of the exact problems during lectures! If you just go to the lectures and take notes, it's an easy class to pass, even during the harder units. Also gives cheat sheets during all quizzes and tests :)

reviews.comment: Prof. Fotovatian was really nice and caring of his students needs. He grades homework and weekly quizzes fairly. He is a bit disorganized when providing the notes, so paying attention is key.

The grading was really clear and when we had a problem or uncertainty about the grading, the professor well explained and fixed the grade. He gives the quiz and the test based on the class material so it is best to not skip the classes.

Professor has a great personality and is very helpful when answering individual questions. During Lecture, it may be hard to follow what he is writing since he writes all over the blackboard. If you pay attention, you'll be able to understand what he is teaching. Stay on top of weekly quizzes and homeworks.
Great!

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Prof. Nabil's class, so much that I enrolled in another course he teaches. His teaching style combines lectures with hands-on practice, which makes the material very easy to understand. He is also understanding and fair with grading.

Professor Atallah is one of the best instructors I've ever had. He has a rare ability to turn complex topics into clear, engaging stories that actually make sense, rather than material you're forced to memorize. His class never felt overwhelming, because the teaching was thoughtful, structured, and genuinely focused on student learning.
Very good professor

Nabil's class was not just smart, it was current, and bioinformatics was accessible, human and relevant. I felt intellectually alive, safe to ask questions and show up as my full self.  More of this in STEM, please.

As a software developer, Dr Nabil didn't just teach tools but thinking patterns. I learned how to design for high-stakes production environments, and how to integrate automation from the very beginning. I moved beyond simply writing functional code and I began thinking in terms of architecture, systems, and clean, elegant engineering practices.

I'm beyond grateful to Professor Nabil Atallah. Every piece of advice he gave me stayed with me, and during a highly competitive job interview, his exact words guided my answers. I got the job at a top bioinformatics company, and HR told me it was because of how I answered. I couldn't have done it without his mentorship! Best Professor ever!

He is a thoughtful and exceptional professor, clearly passionate about Bioinformatics and made the course material very interesting. He consistently goes the extra mile to help students understand complex material and creates a supportive learning environment. If I get the chance, I'm definitely signing up for more of his classes!

Hi I usually don't write comments, but I have to make an exception. Dr. Nabil Atallah class is sharp, engaging, and makes Bioinformatics easy and exciting. Tbh I never thought I'd enjoy it this much. I hope to take another course with him.

I am taking currently his course on Computational Methods in Bioinformatics (BINF6310). Professor Nabil Atallah brings passion and expertise to his teaching. The class is enjoyable and fun, making challenging subjects more approachable and interesting. I highly recommend.

Nabil is one of the best professors I have had the pleasure of learning under. He is knowledgable, understanding, and more than happy to help when asked. I had him for both 6310 and 6420 (I'm not sure if he's still teaching them) but there is a reason I took 2 classes with him he makes concepts feel easier to grasp without it feeling overwhelming.
An outstanding professor! Incredibly knowledgeable and always eager to support and guide students.

Absolutely incredible teaching! The way Dr Atallah break down complex topics into easily understandable pieces is truly impressive. Great passion for the subject shines through, and it's clear how much you care about your students' success. Every lesson feels engaging and informative.

Most of the homework are discussion posts and discovery-related homework. He does NOT teach these components during the lecture. You will spend time learning how to code to do homework.

The lecture material is undergrad biology that could be taught in

Group projects are hard but we taught ourselves a lot.

hands down best professor

he can't teach for more than 10 students, and he always goes out of subject , but is helpful when we need him

Weak professor.  His homework assignments are okay, his tests are often confusing and subjective, and his lectures are almost completely useless.  He makes no effort to engage the students.  He lectures as if it is only a secondary or tertiary responsibility of his as a university professor.

Obviously all the students above had a class average below 60.I think he is great if you actually follow along with the book. You can't expect to sit down and relax wishing that everything will come and take a sit in your head.

I really like him as a professor. I've had him for several classes and he gives challenging work that makes me work hard, but I like the challenge.  He most definitely does NOT qualify as the "worst teacher ever" or anything like that. He knows his material.
Horrible teacher ... doesnt care about the students, never shows up to office hours, all over the place when lecturing. For the amount of money you are paying for this school we deserve much better.

knows his stuff, very tough time explaining class material to students.  tries to be helpful...but just leads to more confuzion. i'd give him a c+

reviews.comment: Gives a good chunk of reading from textbooks that are referenced heavily in class but pretty irrelevant if you have any background knowledge. Group projects for days too, and she doesn't want to be told who's the one guy not doing anything. Assessments are self-reflections, so if you already understand material, good luck showing progress.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Had Polly for many ed courses. Although her class entails lots of reading, she may be the best professor in the ed dept. All you really need to do to get an A is show up to class, and offer opinions on the regular class discussions. She is incredibly supportive, and will continue to help even when you finish taking her class.
Polly is a great teacher. Although the class has a lot of required reading, it was interesting and I didn't mind doing the work. Come to class prepared and ready to participate; easy A.

talk about having your cake and eating it too. this serbian professional  enlightened me to all aspects of education and what it takes to be an independent teacher (like not dependent at all). I give this class a V for Viciously Vigorous
great teacher, great experience. too many repetitive books

Very interesting class and professor, thought provoking.  Assigns A LOT of reading material and not much else, which becomes the basis of class discussion.  Very much a participation based class and it is essential to do the readings.

Great professor, very interesting. She really cares about her subject, and really wants to help students become as passionate about teaching as she is. EDUC1111 requires a good amount of reading, but the class discussions that are a huge part of the class are very interesting and a great way to learn to widen your perspectives. Highly recommend her
why is the final paper 10 pages? ridiculous. she is alright. alot of unnecessary and repetitive work. BLAHHHHH

The ratings on here do not do justice to Polly Attwood as a Professor. The class is a lot of work, but it is worthwhile and you truly leave it with an understand of the subject. She is supportive, passionate, and generally there to help you succeed. Very genuine and fair.

Be ready to read and overanalyze everything. If you put in the work and actually do the critical readings, you'll be fine. Polly knows a lot about kids and teaching and is very passionate about it in class. She is also passionate about her personal beliefs, though, so try not to oppose them too often...

One of the worst professors I have had at northeastern. Gives enough work to accumulate at least three courses. Seems to think her class takes priority over any other class. Readings are redundant and mostly unnecessary. Very strong on her beliefs so dont dare to disagree because you wont get anywhere.
She gives a lot of work but she's really not as bad as these reviews say. Occasionally confusing but she always makes herself available for any help you need

I had to laugh while I was reading the other comments. While they are aggressive, they're definitely true. Polly made me second guess majoring in Education at Northeastern until I read about her days at Lesley (as mentioned in one of the other reviews). She would be better suited teaching at a disciplinary high school lol

Polly loves to teach n no one can argue against that. unfortunately, she has a "benefit of the doubt" view on the world; the same one among politicians that has created more and more horrible poverty and racial tension in this country. b/c of this u have to have about 10 sources to back up every statement u make. she is helpful but get out if u can

Really nice woman with a sort of hippy-sh spin on education. Very supportive and helpful. The class itself is really repetitive, but she does her best to draw on her own and your personal experiences as well as various media to make it interesting. Easy A.

Very little clarity in what he wants, need to ask multiple times and still do not get a clear answer. READ THE SYLLABUS, he will not warn you when things are due. Also, the lectures are pointless, he goes off on tangents of his own life and never quite gets into the material. I honestly cannot tell you what I learned in this course.
Prof was good. I found him interesting because of his accent. He is knowledgable about International Business.
Not helpful and will not even respond

Class is very boring, the professor is absorbed in "cultural" awareness - but I personally find the topics in the course promote more stereotypes than remove. The prof. also is not suitable to teach part time, adult students - treats all students like young undergrads or first year grad students.
can't "decenter" from his cultural background
Very experienced and knowledgable professor in the field. He uses the book and his personal accounts to teach the class. Answers any questions asked and is a very friendly person!

He turns every class discussion into an irrelevant story about himself.  He also makes the students teach the class, having each class session consist of a presentation of a reading or book.  Certain groups have to do case studies, others have to do 5 page articles, and others have to do 300 page books.
Very experienced in international business.  Very interesting to listen to in a 2 hour class.

I said my idea for my project and he jus said it was a bad idea.I stayed after class to ask y but he got defensive and did not clearly explain why it was bad, he jus said if u think its a good idea then do it. some1 asked to ellaborate on the details and he jus told us to read the syllabus

Though seemingly well versed in the subject Dr. Charles was completely disengaged with the class. Not a single email reply, carelessly sparse feedback, apparent random assignment of grades outside of the rubric (even though I personally scored high). Very unfortunate that NEU has allowed this from a teacher in the ED.d program.

Course and subject matter was very interesting. Dr. C was not active in discussion boards, however, she graded according to the rubric. I had no issues with her or the coursework. I do wish she was more engaging as this was a six week course on a subject matter I was very interested in. Overall a good experience and material was useful in my work.

No feedback on assignments, discussions, or grades until last week of class, despite repeated attempts to engage via e-mail. Grades were not calculated according to the standards in the rubric. And she repeatedly submitted incorrect grades, so watch out! Make sure to challenge it if your grades seem unusually low; it's probably her mistake again.
Best. Professor. Ever. Literally nothing bad to say about him. Funny, makes classes interesting and is the nicest person ever
Best professor I have had to this day. Amazing guy who really cares about his students. Stay in contact with him!
THE BEST TEACHER EVER!!!!! George is the man If you never have him as a professor then you are missing out
An amazing professor. Hands down my favorite.

He's a great instructor, tries to be funny which is entertaining. Breaks the class up into different parts making a two hour class fly by. Def suggest choosing him if possible. Great guy, book is easy reading.
good professor

Prof. Awatef is one of the nicest professors at Northeastern. She is really helpful outside class, she is an easy grader, and she gives easy exams. Don't expect the best teaching. However, if you do the HWs and go to class you will get an A.

Prof. Awatef is a very nice person. She teaches really good. Even though she has a little problem with communication, she tries her best to teach the subject properly. If you attend classes regularly and pay attention, then you don't face any difficulty in exams. She takes a lot of examples in the class for practice. She is very caring.

This is the single worst professor Ive ever had the displeasure of having. She cannot hold the attention of the class.  When asked a question she never provides an answer that makes sense. Her examples aren't helpful. She'll spend 20 minutes on problems that only need a minute. When she is going over in class examples her explanations are all over.

Very nice person, not a good teacher. Had a lot of difficulty keeping the attention of the class. Read off of powerpoints for her lectures. IE4516 very similar to a Probs & Stats course but she rarely provided practice problems. Students will most likely get a good grade but will have a hard time learning much.

Dr. Avalon is extremely approachable and passionate about helping to support the next generation of healthcare leaders. She serves almost like a mentor as well as a professor. I encourage all of her students to make a connection with her and rally engage in the classroom discussions. She offers so much more than just the syllabus. great person.

There is weekly discussion boards, readings and articles to read. There will be a midterm paper which is easy. The final paper was a little difficult because Ive never done a grant proposal writing. Be sure to ask and questions or things that may seem unclear. The professor will provide good feedback and clarity. Great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Avalon is a great teacher and very understanding. If an assignment is unclear she will communicate with you by email or phone. I love her she wants to see all her students succeed and is available outside of her class. This class is based on choosing an internship so there will be writing assignments based on that and discussion boards .
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher.  Mrs.  Avci  made the class fun in and out of class with interesting  readings and class discussions.  She is also very clear with what she expects and grades based on effort.  Overall a very understanding and nice instructor.
Very easy to work with and understand. Just show up to class, do the assignment, turn it on time and you're good.
Very sweet. Shes young, so she understands her students. Knows what shes teaching well. Very easy to talk to. Definitely recommend

Talks a lot about current events, which is a good time waster. Likes to name drop, but it just gets humorous after awhile. She's very friendly with students and really does know a lot about the industry. Teaches very well and is really nice.
I don't agree with the majority here. She was super informative, helpful, and a real sweetheart. She went out of her way to help me out in the industry. For that she gains my love and respect.

i had her last semester and she was basically the thorn of my semester. she's kind of like the mean middle school teacher everybody hated. her class is not enjoyable by any means and i didn't learn a thing i couldn't have learned by sitting down and reading the book for like an hour. she also holds grudges.

Lawrence was very boring and I didn't learn much from the class at all. Usually ended up wasting half the class with current events chat. She worked at a record label once and likes to mention that a lot. Not much teaching, lots of browsing web sites and videos.

Ava Lawrence is a horrible professor. She is incredibly boring and being in her class i a waste of time! She does not have a clue on how to teach and is incompetent. I strongly suggest switching teachers if you can!
DO NOT TAKE MUSIC INDUSTRY WITH LAWRENCE. PERIOD.

Without a doubt the worst teacher I've ever had in all my years of schooling.  How this woman got a teaching job (or any paid employment) is beyond me.  Sitting in this class made me feel guilty that my parents were actually spending their money on this.  Did you know she worked at TVT records?  She should mention that more in class.
name dropper.  not a good teacher.  "i worked at tvt records" yeah good for you.  i just hated her.

I feel bad that eva thinks she's *still* a hot shot in the business. tells lots of stories about herself, her career, very boring class. take Prof. Strasser instead, i took him for music industry 2 and it was SO much better

She's really nice and knows what she's talking about, but perhaps not the best at actually TEACHING it to others. She lets you know what's on the final a few days before so that helps and it's easy enough, as well as her projects. Perhaps not the most engaging class but still fun.
this class was a waste of my time.  i expected a lot more out of this class and this major in general...this professor was one of the reasons i dropped out.
This class was a waste of time. Take another professor.

Not good if you want to learn computer programs you don't already know how to use(ie.ms-word)Projects are vague without clear explanation of conceptsShe'll try to help you,but sometimes it's hard to get beyond the condescending attitude&name dropping every.005seconds.I think she misses the industry.
The class was straightforward and easy...she tells you directly what will be on the midterm and final but overall it is very boring.

She's a nice and helpful professor, especially with scheduling and stupid NU paperwork crap. I think she's still getting used to how to add entertaining things into class and still make them relevant. SHe'll get better I'm sure... as long as she stops saying "When I was at TVT..." everyday.

I didnt like her at all.  she constantly talks in circles, so its hard to take notes because everything is so disorganized.  the papers are easy, tests even easier.  she also likes to name drop:  "when i worked at TVT records where the ying yang twins and ja rule are signed...blah blah blah..."
Has a good attitude and a high tolerance for people not understanding every step of the projects. She is willing to explain the steps numerous times and is very helpful.
prof. lawrence is a great professor. she is always there if you need answers and will work her hardest to help find you a co-op come dec.2nd and you still have no job.
No Comments

honestly, i can't stand her as a person, as she can be extremely condescending at times (pretty much all the time actually).  but, the class is really easy and most people just surf the internet the entire time and completely ignore her...a good throwaway music industry class.
makes you wanna switch majors....

She has no idea how to do math. Taking 10% and then 30% is not the same as taking 40%, but it is to her. (idiot) However, I am biased, went into the class not liking her. Janikian is easier and better, so if you have the oppurtunity take Janikian's class.

Anderson-sensei is my favorite professor I've taken so far. She is extremely caring, understanding, and is always smiling. Her class was also very tough, with lots of homework to varying levels of difficulty. It is certainly not an easy A. As long as you put effort into this class and actively stay engaged, you will love it!

She is a super nice and caring professor (very motherly like). Classes are really engaging and all material to study given prior to the assessment (most if not all on quizlet). Will say its not an easy A course you will have to work for your grade!

Anderson Sensei is so sweet and is an excellent professor. I got so much better at reading, writing, and speaking this semester and you are given chances to practice vocab, kanji, and sentence structure in and out of class. The only downside is the amount of homework. While easy there are multiple videos each week which leads to a lot of busywork.

Such an organized professor like Canvas was chef's kiss. Kind and caring, very motherly. Accessible outside of class and very understanding. She's not tough, but she's not an easy A. I loved this class. She'll match each student's pace. Every class was fun.

Professor Yildirim is a great professor in class and cares a lot about what she teaches. The grading is a bit off and can be confusing, but the material is typically fun and interesting. She is great for communicating and engaging in a fun class environment. The workload can get a bit much at times but overall great class.

So you see, the class itself is quite interesting. You may be thinking hmm I like this! That is until... you get a paper every week that is at least 9 pages. Argh. However, she tries her best and is very nice in class. The lectures are fun and all, but don't necessarily teach too much. I would recommend going tho bc it means a lot to her and is fun
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Genuinely cares about what she teaches and rewards effort.
Good energy

Professor Yildirim was really great. Her class is always super interesting and I never found myself board in lectures. She gives 3 "pop quizzes" randomly throughout the semester to basically make sure you are in attendance. Attendance isn't mandatory but it does help you on tests. Her exams went along with the lectures and the work is pretty easy

Professor Bilge was okay as a teacher. Her class was super easy but her grading is a little strange. Her tests are easy and there is a final project but that is also easy. To be honest, she did not really teach anything new or different from psych1011 so I wouldn't take her for a subject I actually wanted to learn something new in. Overall, nice.

I love Dr. Y. Classes are definitely lecture-heavy, but she records them. And sometimes lecture won't be interesting, but lock in & you'll do fine on every exam. She has lots of resources and will always help you. + She clearly loves teaching.
4 exams, one of which is dropped; take-home quizzes (2 tries); sometimes extra credit + test corrections!

Dr Y is a sweetie! Her class is interesting and the poster project is a semester long effort and not bad at all. Her tests are a bit tricky, but not that heavily weighted. Her lectures are crucial for details on exams, so review daily because content builds up. Make sure you follow rubrics to get full credit on classwork grades and it's an easy A.

This class was interesting and Professor Y was very funny, but her teaching style was often hard to follow. There were a few exams and open note quizzes, but they weighed very lightly in terms of your grade. There were slideshows shown in class, but they weren't very helpful so make sure your attendance is good.

I thought Professor Yesilatay was really nice and caring of her students, but her lectures were often confusing. You have to attend class to know what will actually be on tests because the lecture slides are not helpful. There were few assignments, but they were all pretty lengthy. She is very understanding and lenient though!

Dr Y was an engaging lecturer and explained material clearly. Lecture heavy, so attending class was necessary since slides were not comprehensive and most content on quizzes/exams was only taught in class. Grade was determined by many small assignments. She gave detailed rubrics and lots of feedback. Exams were not weighted heavily and fairly easy.

I took A&P 2 with Professor Yesilaltay and I don't regret it at all. She's super caring and wants her students to succeed. There are 4 exams (lowest one gets dropped) and a final. She also allows for test corrections which gets added to your test grade. There's a lot of content but that's to be expected.

I had Dr.Yesilaltay for both A&P 1 and 2, she is amazing! It is a lecture heavy course but lectures are recorded so you can always go back and rewatch. There is test corrections after each exam and your lowest exam grade gets dropped. She is very enthusiastic about teaching and was an overall great professor! I would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: she's awesome!! makes great analogies and answers questions well, and she's honest when she doesn't know an answer. lecture-heavy but she is funny and gives breaks so i've never found a lecture boring.

She is a very nice lady and cares a lot about what she is talking about. However the way she explains things is not straightforward at all and her lectures are very hard to follow. Luckily her exams are pretty easy, as long as you get the big concepts you'll be fine. Lectures are not recorded and slides are not helpful.

By far the best professor I have this semester! Definitely recommend if you want a professor who will bring enthusiasm and inspiration to both yours and her own work. Very intelligent individual. Love this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She makes stuff really detailed and deep more than what we are learning in class during the test. She also walks around so much during the test. I personally wouldn't take her class again since she not really teaching us anything, she just copy and pasting things from the text book that's not really related to A&P and not really teaching us things

Organized, learned a lot, fair exams, exam corrections, and she is really nice and answers all questions. We had online quizzes with multiple attempts and a page of notes for our exams. The lab is the hard part. Great professor and I got an A!

She rambles and goes off topic a lot during lectures but you can tell she's really passionate about her job. Slides are not helpful at all to study with so make sure to attend lectures to catch key points here and there she'll test you on. Amazing lady and so caring as a person. She tries and really wants her students to do well
Very charismatic personality, truly wants her students to succeed! Also very understanding, did well with explaining more difficult concepts whenever prompted.

take-home quizzes every week, poll ev for attendance, and exams that are completely fair/not too difficult, it is manageable to pass this daunting class. she is super sweet and answers emails so fast. if anything the lab was the hardest part and i mean its HARD, so time consuming for a 1 credit course but the lecture is more than fine honestly.

Dr. Y is the sweetest person ever. It is very feasible to get an A in this class. The tests only make up a small part of your grade and there are no curveballs. A lot of the grade is based on a poster project which she does not grade harshly. The lectures can feel long and monotonous, but that's really the only negative thing I can think of.

she is such a sweetheart and i absolutely loved this class. she truly cares about her students and i've maintained a relationship with her afterwards. if you can, take this class, especially if you're new to northeastern.

LOVE HER OMG. she has a funny personality and was very good at answering questions. she had 3 EC assignments and all exams were open note (hand written) and final was online. she also does corrections so not hard to pass her class.

Prof Ayce genuinely cares about her students and goes above and beyond to support their success. She's kind, and approachable, and provides helpful resources like exam corrections and others to help you. Her engaging teaching style makes class enjoyable. Having her for Anatomy 2 was amazing, and she made the challenging material fun!!!

I absolutely loved Dr. Y. She is so so kind and her course was interesting. She allowed us to write a paper for the final instead of a final exam, and she is very reasonable with grades. All exams had corrections as well. She really cares about your education and well-being, and I would take any class she offers just to have her again as my prof.

Dr. Yesilaltay really cares about her students and wants them to do well. If you go to class and do the assignments, you cannot get a bad grade. You can tell she really knows what she is talking about. She is very sweet, funny, and approachable. There was sometimes busy work but it did help boost your grade. She also offered test corrections.

The lectures are a bit hard to follow. She often goes on tangents that are unrelated and the slides are not very helpful in explaining the content. The test questions are often more detailed and difficult then the lecture slides or what is covered in class.  She does give extra credit which I really appreciated.

Literally nothing bad to say about her, impossible to get lower than an A in her class and would make up extra credit if you needed it. So funny and cared about all her students, her class was so easy and even if you failed the exams, they were barely worth anything, she also gave corrections. Wish I could take her forever.

Dr. Y is super nice and always there to help. If you have any questions she has no problem helping you and making sure you're all caught up. Super accommodating. I would take all my classes with her if I could.

Dr. Y is the best professor out there she is so kind and caring. She responds to emails quickly and is always willing to help. Her lectures are engaging and she genuinely cares about all of her students. She wants to see everyone succeed and engage with each other in class.

I LOVE DR Y!!!! She is both passionate about what she teaches and helping her students succeed. Some homework is time consuming and a bit difficult, but she is kind with grading and often moved due dates back to give us more time. Dr Y is also very fun. I was never bored in her class. Take her if you can!

My favorite professor at Northeastern! She made the content engaging, and I feel like I truly learned something from her class. She is very accessible outside of class and genuinely cares about her students. There is a poster project and a lot of reading, but everything is manageable and easy. Exams are done online and at home. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Y knows how to make class engaging. She is constantly coming up with little rhymes or songs to help you remember concepts. She is also the most caring professor I've ever had. She recognized me from her BIOL1000 session the semester prior and emailed me to check in on how I was doing. Genuinely the sweetest.

Prof Y was amazing! I took her cholesterol section of this class, she gives great lectures, gets to know everyone, barely any out-of-class work, and an easy grader. Loved her class, was never confused and found the material interesting. Highly recommend :)

Dr. Y is great! She's so caring about her students. The class has many articles and you can easily fall begin if you don't take notes. There are 2 exams and the final one. She gives opportunities for corrections for the exams. There are also quizzes taken only for completion grades. There's also a big project poster about an article of your choice.

Prof. Y is a great teacher and is extremely passionate about biology. She will take as much time as she needs to explain a topic if someone is confused. 2 exams and a final. Some long homework assignments here and there but its all very doable. She offers points back on exams, and for the quizzes, we got 2 attempts and discussed answers in class.
walking dub

Professor Y was all I could have hoped for in a biology teacher. She had weekly "figure facts" that were really straight forward from research papers we read in class, was extremely time consuming though. All tests and quizzes were online, quizzes had multiple attempts and there were test corrections. She was extremely caring and knew everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at Northeastern. Her lectures are always involving and interesting but doesn't pressure those who don't want to participate. All quizzes and tests are online, and she offers the ability to correct your mistakes to earn some of your points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Y was a joy of a professor. She really emphasized engagement within the class and tried to make everything as stress-free as possible. She wanted her students to enjoy lectures by making them interactive and was always accessible in case you had questions on anything. Exams and quizzes are all online and she provides corrections.

Professor Yesilaltay has been my favorite professor at Northeastern so far. She is so caring and understanding and just genuinely wants you to learn the material. Grades aren't really stressed, but trying to understand the material is. I was not even interested in cholesterol before taking her inquiries but I thoroughly enjoyed the class.

Prof Y is the nicest and actually teaches you. She is the best professor I have had at NEU. She cares about you and understands when something is difficult. She encourages asking questions and explains things well. The class is very project bases with two major exams. Most things have the opportunity to do corrections that can help your grade!

One of the best professors I've ever had. She's so sweet and really does want everyone to succeed, and lets you do corrections on all quizzes/exams to earn points back. Great at explaining concepts and super helpful if you have questions, I would highly recommend her class

Professor Yesilaltay is the type of professor who truly cares about you and wants you to succeed. I loved being in her class as she made lectures interesting. There were some online quizzes which were open note, and she did offer corrections on them. There were a couple midterm exams which she also allowed corrections for. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Yesilaltay is the most caring, helpful professor. She will help you if you need something, and make sure you get concepts, and her lectures are fun, collaborative, and not just the professor speaking to the students. There isn't a ton of reading, and if you pay attention and stay engaged during class you'll do good.

Dr Yesilaltay is an extremely knowledgeable and all around great professor. If you are taking inquiries, you want this teacher. She is understanding with grades, keeps lectures engaging and interesting, and cares about both what she teaches and her students. HW load is a bit lighter than other classes, if you pay attention its a pretty easy A.

Dr. Yesilaltay is an incredible professor who deeply cares about her students. The cholesterol class can be a little intimidating, but you learn so much more than that in a fun and inviting setting. I'd definitely take Bio Inquiries with her if you get the chance!

She is an amazing proffesor!! She cares a lot about her students and provides lots of support. The content was engaging and easy to follow. You can tell she cares a lot about what she is teaching. The workload isn't high so it is great to take as an elective.

Prof Ayanna was very kind and knowledgeable, which made her class engaging. She was also very flexible with due dates, gave mental health days off, and was open to feedback. If you complete assignments with effort, you will get an A. Class was enjoyable, and I would love to take from her again if possible
So nice. taught super interesting material but also wanted us all to succeed. Lots of chances to get extra credit or points.

She is really nice. You don't NEED to go to class but the material is interesting and she ends early sometimes. Tests are online and open note. She is very understanding with late assignments. Cares about the topic and the students.
really chill, readings aren't too necessary to do, easy work, engaging lectures, no exams

She is very knowledgable about the Criminal Legal System and will do her best to answer any questions. She is fair when considering due dates and will use student feedback. However, she would sometimes assign long, technical readings. Despite this, I learned a lot and found the textbook extremely useful.

Ayanna was amazing! Her lectures follow the required textbook but also follow very current events in our society. She facilitates great discussion in class and is very accepting and open. Take this class even if you aren't going into criminal justice! You will learn so much with an awesome professor!

Professor Ayanna was amazing and understood the content to teach it. She cares about the class and is passionate about what she does. She is an easy grader and will offer you room for improvement. She is very reasonable and understands. This is your class if you are looking for a good introduction class to see if you like criminal justice.

He's super chill and gets the work done. He made me enjoy reading and writing and has a very laid back demeanor. Class isn't hard, just do the assigned work (not bad at all). If possible I would 110% take him for first year writing.
Such a nice and helpful professor, definitely recommend. He's really funny and the assignments consist of a few projects and writing assignments.

really good teacher. Ends up having a good relationship and gets very connected to all his students. At the end of the day he just trying to make you a better writer. He doesn't use textbooks and makes the class fun and engaging. Homework wise its not bad at all, he gives like project essays every once in a while and somehow you want to do them.

The best teacher you will ever have understands how to make a class that is supposed to be easy, be easy. Shows you the most important errors you have to improve your writing. Is the funniest teacher I've ever had, fun projects, fun class videos and documentaries, overall the GOAT.

Amazing prof and such a funny and cool guy! Gives helpful writing tips, but the more you give the more you get out of it. If you do the assignments you will do well. Def take this class cuz he makes it fun and is caring towards students!

Prof. Ayala is so nice! He does not assign homework but there are some very small presentations here and there (you choose the topic). He is very flexible and understanding. Also an easy grader. Definitely recommend!!!
I do not recommend to take this course. This course is not hard to understand, but it is hard to get a high grade in the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: my arch nemesis. once a class she'll tell us we shouldn't be on our laptops and we should be asking more questions, but will absolutely clown us if we get something "wrong" in a discussion that doesn't fit her narrative. her slides are wordy and she doesn't have one cohesive thought. you will be jumpscared by rubric criteria she never communicated

There's a lot of readings that can be very boring unless you're into agriculture. As a professor, she is super sweet and a good teacher. Lectures can be boring at times, but she does her best to make it interesting. Brings in guest lecturers and even brought food for the class to try.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Ayers is an outstanding educator; however, this course poses significant challenges. The exams demand hours of reading and studying the material. Particularly, the Neurocreation paper is quite formidable and needs to be worked on ahead of time. Many students opt for an Incomplete grade (I) and submit the paper later in the year.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No longer using flipped classroom as he did in Fall 2020. 3 exams, 1 paper. Take this class if: - You are extremely interested in comparative neurobiology - All the other classes you are taking this semester are easy - You are being legally forced to take this class - Your mental health is stable enough for you to have weekly mental breakdowns

Professor Ayers teaches via a flipped classroom, which is just his way of being able to include as much information as possible into at home work and class lectures. They are extremely dense lectures that take about 2 hours to get through (minimum) and class time is spent reviewing the lectures.

By far the hardest class I've taken in the BNS program. He's an absolutely brilliant professor who will teach you an insane amount of cool info about nervous systems, but his presentation skills are lacking. His slides are incredibly dense, and he gives no hints on what we're supposed to know. Take it if you're brave.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You know those professors who are VERY knowledgeable in their field - yet, they just do not know how to convey the information to others? Yea, that's Dr. Ayers. He's a really nice person, but his lectures are all over the place. His exams are incredibly detailed and the Neurocreation paper was the death of us all. I learned a lot in the end though.

This is class is extremely difficult, it requires a massive amount of work, especially the paper. While i learned alot in this class, i would not recommend taking it in less you are looking to go into neuroscience.  If you take this class make sure the rest of your course load is light because this is a very time consuming class.

Wow! This class is crazy hard.  Only take it unless you are honestly interested in going into comparative neuroscience.  He asks ridiculous detail on tests, refuses to answer e-mails or meet with you, and when you ask questions, he says, I think it is very clear.  I learned a lot, but REALLY hard class

He is an extremely smart guy and the class is interesting. But it was amoung the hardest I have ever taken. You have to read ever thing because he test on the smallest details The test are difficult TF and MC but if he gives you the option  to give short essays I would take it. The paper is difficult but he grades it really easy.You will learn alot

This was the most difficult class I've ever taken.  His tests are very difficult, and the averages were always around 70.  The paper is a beast and will consume your life.  Don't procrastinate on it.  You'll learn a lot, but sometimes he contradicts himself.  The book is useful only about 1/2 the time.  Read the PDF's.  I wish I had had more time.

Definitely the best teacher I've had in college. The subject matter is quite complex and can be overwhelming at times. BUT if you are interested in neuroscience this class is definitely worth taking. The tests are mul. choice, t/f, short answer and essays. You have to write a paper that composes a nervous system. Highly recommended teacher & class.
Joe is awesome, but be sure to pay attention, cause he tests you on EVERYTHING you never thought you'd need to know.

Ayers is the man. Awesome professor and he's got some great stories and does interesting research. Who couldn't love a prof. who makes robotic lobsters?!  Seriously, if you want to know how nervous systems give rise to behaving organisms, he is the man to talk to. Never saw anyone bored in class.

My favorite professor I've had at Northeaster so far. He clearly knows what he's talking about. He's super passionate about what he teaches and it's contagious. Can get sidetracked sometimes but it's almost always informative or entertaining. I highly recommend taking a class with him!

This man is a genius. He talks really fast, but everything he says is amazing. He doesn't put the slides on blackboard, so type the notes. It's an interesting class. Tests are online and easier than they look. The final paper is a breeze. There are readings but really only need to use 2 for your paper and some are on blackboard.

One of my favorite profs I've had.  He's clearly really into his field so he knows what he's talking about, and probably knows what you're talking.  Even if you don't know what you're trying to ask, he probably knows what you mean.  A bit difficult to connect with in class but really opened up in office hours.  Also, super cute.

Professor Ayers is one of my favorite teachers I've ever had at Northeastern. He's not only incredibly smart and humble, but is incredibly understanding about individual schedules and is open to all ideas. Promotes very interesting discussion and encourages students to be confident in their ideas. Definitely recommend!
Excellent professor. Provides great feedback, is extremely helpful, and is not difficult. Allows you to research your own ideas with application. Highly recommended.

Professor Larson is great! She's exactly what a professor should be. You need to participate in her class, but she is an entertaining lecturer and cares about her students and helping them learn the content. The midterm and final are written answer but you get a cheat sheet.

Harsh grader and gives tight deadlines on essays. Her tests are very long and all open response and fill-in-the-blank, no multiple choice, but you do get one cheat sheet. The course is very content-heavy.

Professor Larson is a phenomenal ORGB professor. Although the content is a bit boring, she truly does care about her students and makes her lectures engaging. The exams are all short answer but you get a one page cheat sheet that helps. Out of all the ORGB profs, she is probably the best choice!

Passionate about teaching and knows her material very well, but is a very tough grader. Class is usually engaging, but ~23% of grade comes from participation, so be on your game from day one. Attendance is very important for doing well in this class - if you pay attention and do your readings you will be just fine.

reviews.comment: OrgB shouldn't be a required class to begin with, but it is, and do not take it with her. So unclear with grading, its so objective. Too many assignments towards the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Caring towards her students - most memorable professor I've had. Lectures are engaging with group activities/discussions. Participation matters and she gives enough opportunities to participate. You get a 2-page cheat sheet for exams and textbook is free. Exams are SAQ but you'll do well if you write a good cheat sheet and have attended class.

Very difficult class because of the way she chooses to grade, we clearly understand concepts, but so that everyone doesn't get A she grades very tough, which is also heavily specific/even at times opinionated.

reviews.comment: Way too opinionated grading. Dont take puts off for not explaining the answer when the question doesn't say explain(Especially when you dont for other questions!).
