reviews.comment:
*MSCR 2895 REVIEW*
Professor Blake is extremely passionate and knowledgeable.  As someone who took this credit purely out of interest, he made the class far more than what it was on the surface.  There's a lot of reading and writing assignments are pretty detailed, but he is a fair grader and is transparent about what he's looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Blake is a nice guy. Even though this class is honestly a lot of work because you have to keep up with the readings and watch all the films, he makes it interesting. He goes a fast in lecture but he posts everything online so you don't really need to go to class. The quizzes and exams are online which is nice and there are only 2 papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I got turned off of the class quickly due to how much work was required outside of class time. I spent more time working on this class more than my actual required classes for my major. It just felt a bit unnecessary. To his credit, the tests and quizzes were online, so it was fairly easy to get good grades on them, though they are timed.

Nathan is caring, passionate, knowledgable and attentive! This class is asynchronous this semester which can be hard at times but he is devoted to making it as easy to manage as possible. The course is still well thought out and grading is clear and easy to understand. He really cares about students thoughts on films and gives insightful feedback.

Really thoughtful and kind professor. Genuinely super passionate about what he teaches and it is sad that not many people participate in class over zoom as much as they should. Great guy, it's a difficult class in terms of concepts but he makes it accessible.

Nathan outlines exactly what he wants, with very clear percentages. He tells you exactly what you need to do to get an A, and if you are engaged in class he will bump you up to the next letter grade if you're on the cusp.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Courseload is heavy but tolerable. He is very nice, saved my grade. Replies fast and very helpful and caring. He'll help you learn a lot about film.
Such a nice guy. Honestly my grade saver.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading for the midterm and quizzes, but the class is well balanced with a great selection of films. Professor Blake is very nice and caring who cares about his students and is always accessible outside of class. The class is mostly lectures which can get boring.

Professor Blake is incredibly intelligent and kind to students. I love our conversations in class and he makes some abstract film theories very accessible, which everyone appreciates. I'd love to take another one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Nathan is a great professor. He's very patient and he treats everyone's work seriously. He gives a lot of feedback in details. He replies email very fast. Overall, if you really want to learn about film, he is a great choice. Workload is kind of heavy so it depends on your choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: You will learn a lot from this course, but I don't recommend co-op student to take this course because there are just so many readings, lecture recordings and movie clips each week. And you won't get a good grade if you skip any of these. Not an easy A- class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Gave good feedback. Great in-class discussions. No 2 classes were the same. Students helped each other w/possible sources for their individual research projects. Classroom felt like a community. Didn't always understand students' perspectives. Banned computers by saying that he would look things up on his computer,  but never did.

Blessington was the worst professor I have had in my time at Northeastern. I took his class because I was interested in poetry and he basically destroyed any chance of me ever pursuing that interest again. He was extremely rude and never responded to emails. He made fun of students and faculty repeatedly and was incapable of using online resources.

Created a classroom environment that made students fearful of reading their work because of his abnormally harsh criticism. Was incredibly unsympathetic and did not care about his students in the slightest. Ruined poetry for me and he clearly has no idea what a subjective writing course is supposed to be about as he was very objective when grading.

Course was called "Origins of Genres," and was part of a PhD program. I have no idea if attendance was mandatory because I wanted to go. I didn't mind putting work into it because I was there to learn and develop.  He was thoroughly prepared, hugely literate and immensely interesting. One of the top profs I've had, and I've had some good ones.

In a class about self-expression he promoted a critical, toxic environment. He made bigot comments on pieces outside of his own perspective and students felt uncomfortable/anxious about contributing to the discussion because of his scrutiny. If you want your self-confidence shredded then I recommend this class.
Professor Blessington ruined poetry for me. Never take a class with him.

I took Greek Tragedy so we were assigned mini reports for each play we read. It was fun, no pressure because of how short they were, and helped you dive into the material. Vague about what he wants from your assignments. He is more lecture based and he really knows what he's talking about, though sometimes class questions go right over his head.

Best teacher I have ever had.  I was at NU from 99-01, so it's been a while.  I am now an Eng. teacher, and I can honestly say that interest started in his class.  He is probably the smartest person I've ever met, but doesn't live in an ivory tower.  He's spent summers farming and Spain and just seems to know everything about everything.

Blessington is the best.  Wish he was my grandfather.  He is brilliant, hilarious and nice.  I was doing horribly in the class, probably because I never went during the first half, and he helped me get back on track and completely turn my grade around.  Makes the material interesting and fun, and I would recommend him to anyone.

Best professor I've yet come across. This man is a genius, and it's almost impossible to believe the extent of his knowledge of literature. He has translated Greek plays to English, is avid about Milton, can point you probably to any precise line in Homer or Virgil. Just the best, I want another class with this guy. Smart, funny, memorable for sure

He is brilliant and hilarious. I enjoy listening to what he has to say in lectures. He makes material fun and helps you to understand. I would recommend him to anyone. He's a bit of a hard grader, but it pushes you to work harder. I learned so much from this class.

AMAZING! He has seen and done it all. His knowledge of literature is astounding. His lectures are clear and while he does veer away from the topic at times, his stories/antecdotes are witty and interesting.

The readings were at times overwhelming, and much of the assignments I never finished.  His lectures were amazing, however, and made the class worthwhile.  The man really knows his stuff, and is HILARIOUS.  There are too many Blessington quotes to count.. and too many aren't acceptable for younger readers to see! ;)
Definitely intense reading, I would recommend keeping up with it. Other than that he is extremely knowledgable and impassioned about the subject.

The reading is INTENSE.  I'm an English major and I had difficulty keeping up.  Pay attention to the readings in class - they WILL be on the midterm/final!!!  But beside that, he is an incredibly intelligent guy and keeps a fairly uninteresting topic somewhat interesting.
Blessington is extremely intelligent. He makes a few jokes, and has some interesting things to talk about. He is a fairly tough grader but if you do the work you will do well.
One of the best professors I've had in NU.
No Comments

Blessington is the man. He knows his**** inside out and if you ask him a question on what you don't understand, he *will* clarify it and be direct. He's funny too, at random moments. Quite quirky and definitely the biggest character out of all my teachers
professor blessington is very brilliant although can be a bit boring

Blessington is the best professor I have come across at this school. Some how he made paradise lost and a**** load of poetry about god interesting. Extremly intelligent, a fair grader and, he's actully kind of funny. This guy could teach "the evolution and science of tax reform policies" and somehow make it captivating

One of the most intelligent people you will ever have the good fortune to meet in your life.  Honestly, such a great professor. His comments  anecdotes are also quite funny at times.  Although he might as well be the most knowledgeable professor at NU, he doesnt seem conceited.  Good Guy.

This guy has so much knowledge over such a variety of literature, it's unbelievable. One of the few professors I really feel I learned something from. A bit tough sometimes, but stick with it and you'll do fine.

He is obviously very intelligent, but the class was BORING.  Lectures very dry, I wanted to sleep through all of them...  Don't worry about going to class, most of the material on tests is from the reading assignments

Probably the best prof. I have ever had.  Made me want to become a teacher of literature myself.  The reading requirement isn't that bad if you stay on top of it.  Besides, by the time you get to college you should have read most of those texts anyway.
very very smart man.

The best teacher I've had at Northeastern. There is usually a good amount of reading and lengthy lectures, but I've never known a teacher who gives as interesting and informative of lectures. Recommended more for English majors or those who really love Literature.

although the course content is somewhat dry and a lot of reading is required in a fairly short amount of semester time he does make it as interesting as possible. And though he is a relatively tough grader he is always willing to help when you need him. He also really knows what he's talking about.

A smart man...but doesn't know how to teach. His lectures are full of tangents, and he doesn't really explain text very well. He's nice enough, though, and every now and then makes a good point, but overall...I'd say you had to be really into the subject matter to put up with this class.

Loads of reading--a novel each week, sometimes more.  And Blessington is something of an elitist--he belittles popular fiction, or anything that isn't considered "literary"--but he's a thorough marker, and smart as hell.  Recommended course.

Be prepared for a****load of reading.  Illiad, Odyssey, Aeneid, Bible, Bacchae and some other plays in a VERY short period.  Seems like a nice guy, very knowledgeable, but the material can just get boring I guess..

Very interesting course but look forward to a lot of reading. Blessington is a really smart person so that makes the class interesting as well. Only two papers and a midterm and a final besides the reading. I learned a lot though.
Appreciate the effort put into the syllabus and the structure. I do think she makes things unnecessarily hard though
wouldn't really recommend. Enjoy the guest lectures but the regular classes themselves are not exciting. a lot to read as well which can be tiring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Currently in a class taught by Professor Boeckeler and I strongly vote against taking her as your professor. She gives an unnecessary amount of busy work and both her and the TA are looking for ways to ding you and deduct points. It's not a good environment, I don't feel supported at all. It is disheartening and stressful

Prof. Boeckeler is super nice and it's clear she has a true passion for Shakespeare and teaching. She's always fangirling over his writing and it's super wholesome. She's a tough grader, but her feedback is well thought out and she wants her students to do well. I highly recommend meeting with her (office hours) so she can help with your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I actually took Global Lit 1 (ENGL1700), but that wasn't an option listed on this site. Anyway, she was great. I'm not an English Major, so coming from someone without an English background, I think she is a really fair teacher, and her class is absolutely manageable if you actually show up and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Boeckeler is NOT an easy grader, but nothing unusual for an English prof., her feedback is okay. She truly wants to make connections with her students and knew all of us by name relatively quick. Boeckeler is a really nice as a person with really interesting stories to share, you can tell she's passionate and excited to teach each lesson!

Difficult to get an A in this class. Good feedback is hard to come by. Wouldn't take this class or this professor again. The only plus is that she is passionate and knowledgeable in the Shakespeare topic.

I enjoyed Prof. Boeckeler's class, although it wasn't easy for an intro. class. She's a hard grader -- don't think you can get an A on a sloppy paper. She can be intimidating at times, but email her/go to her office hours and you'll feel more comfortable about class. You do a variety of readings, and it's a good class to see if ENGL is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Boeckeler is great. I took her Shakespeare class, and her clear passion for the subject was really contagious. She was very considerate about being easy on students because of the pandemic, not as in assigning zero homework, but that she was very open to working with students who were having a hard time with the class. Very sweet, fun.
she really just makes things harder than it has to be. wants students to learn, and therefore makes grading hard. it's really annoying. if you already like shakespeare, don't take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Wayyyyy too much homework for a 2 credit course. the lectures are also very long and boring. dont take unless you live and breathe sketching and drawing. please take a different class if you just need a art elective. weekly sketches are graded too harshly.

reviews.comment: dont take.

reviews.comment: Class is long, repetitive, and truly made to be boring. Do NOT take if you've had any previous art training.

Don't take this as an elective unless you're great at drawing and willing to put the time in.

reviews.comment: Skylar Borgstrom is an awful instructor. She forces everyone to draw only her way, ignores prior experience, and grades you unfairly. Class is just two hours of mindless still lifes with zero teaching. She falsely accused me of copying photos and handed out C- and D- grades despite accurate work. This class ruined drawing for me. avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The HW for this class is 5 30-min drawings every week without exceptions for holidays. She claims that a 30 minute drawing every day isn't time consuming, but this simply isn't true. I took this class as one of my general electives because I thought it would fit well with my very busy schedule, but that was not the case.

She takes this class far too seriously and does not accept absences even if excused or wellness days. It is an introductory drawing class but she grades harshly. There was no final/final project which was nice, but the outside of class homework and writing just got so tedious and it is difficult to know whether she is happy with your work or not.

Class was less drawing-focused than expected. There were readings, weekly sketchbook assignments, weekly self-evaluations, etc. She gives good advice but only if you seek it out, otherwise she won't speak to you. It felt like I had to do the learning myself and she was just giving work. Workload exceeded what you'd want from a 2 credit class.

this class made me not like drawing anymore. assignments are repetitive & the sketchbook homework was time-consuming & did not teach me much. she prides herself on giving feedback, but most of the time her suggestions are so vague and not helpful, and when grading homework she will often give a low grade with few words instructing on how to improve

I just graduated and am looking back at the worst professors I ever had, and no doubt this guy was it. I'll never forget when he wouldn't let us use the restroom and someone in the class had a disability. Straight up bad person and an even more impossible teacher who would give out bad grades just to give them out. Cant stand him, don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst professor Ive had so far at Northeastern. Ill never forget the time they just graded my question wrong when it was correct and he wouldnt give me the point back because he wouldnt work the problem out himself to see the answer. Save yourself the trouble

Definitely an unorthodox teacher, but you can tell he knows a lot about the subject he is teaching. Beware that he customizes his own syllabus and the topics covered are very difficult to find examples of online. Also, the only grades we have are quizzes and the final and there are fewer quizzes in the honors sections.

FYI. In the canvas, in the quizzes, there were all of last year's bi-weekly quizzes and the final exam there. I found that out a bit late. It's not enough though; many of his quizzes are unpredictable. Just make sure you understand what he covers in class. Don't worry about unfamiliar things in recitation, since those won't be on quizzes.

As a person he is probably a good guy but he is a horrible professor. Very condescending and his course does not make sense. Impossible to find practice tests and exams, unpredictable and makes up his own way of teaching the material. You have to show up to classes to understand the way he does things. Office hours are weird sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: "Old SAT" grading only occurs for matching questions or MCQ, and quizzes rarely had those. While explanations of concepts can be kind of convoluted, he explains HW problems very well. If you are cannot switch out don't fret. An A is very possible. Do your due diligence of doing ALL the HW and going to office hours, and AP AB Calc was easier too.

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible professor. He is so rude to students and fails to explain concepts. Absolutely avoid taking his class at all costs.

I'll never forget when he wouldn't let us go to the bathroom, and a girl got her time of the month and yelled at him that she had to go. Mean person, mean grader, dropped this class and preferred to take it with anyone else. AVOID. Absolutely terrible person. Miss class? Good luck. Have to go to bathroom? Hold it. 0 empathy here

He does go over questions before the quiz which can help
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have a choice, do not take his class at an honors level. He makes the quizzes much more difficult by putting questions that related to topics we never learned in class. Also, his grading criteria for the honors section is much more harsh than his regular section, for example, an A in honors is anything above a 94.5. I would not recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't seem to know how to teach. He's clearly very knowledgeable, yet he holds us to a higher standard on quizzes than even he is able to perform during class. Your grade is exclusively based on quizzes and tests, and if you make even a minor mistake on a quiz that can bump your quiz grade down to the 70s. Overall extremely difficult.

Professor Blank is extremely condescending to his students and laughs at "dumb" questions. He frequently makes mistakes on the board while teaching and students often correct him. Regardless, he is extremely smart and knows a lot about what he teaches. If you cannot keep up with him, you will not be able to excel in the class. D- required to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: sandy blank is by far the worst professor at northeastern university. he does not care for his students' success at all and in fact, enjoys when students do not perform well. He puts in minimal effort to explain topics to us and even purposely gives us incorrect problem solutions to work on at home. I promise that you will regret taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sandy is not a great teacher. He doesn't respect the learning process. If you don't get it, he fails to explain the concept in simpler terms (or at all). His tests were graded in such a way that partial credit is nonexistent, and you could only miss about 3 problems (over quizzes and the final) to still secure an A. His grading style is "old-SAT".

Hes willing to answer hw questions but spends too much time on hw and not enough on new lessons. Final is harder than quizzes and half the grade. Quizzes are the other half. Theres lots of pressure on the end of the semester because quizzes are weighted progressively more. Also grades no. right minus half times wrong , so a pretty hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 40% of the class is based on the final and 60% is based on quizzes. He talks in a very quiet voice that can hardly be heard in the classroom so lectures are difficult to follow. This class is meant to be Calc 1 and Differential Equations, but he skims all of Calc 1 in the first week and skips through to linear algebra by the last month.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the strangest men I have ever met. Spends a large portion of the class giving background information on topics instead of teaching them. Quiz difficulties fluctuate. Would not take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As much as I love Sandy as an individual, he expects his students to be able to understand complicated math theorems after doing one problem together in class. Be prepared to have to teach yourself the concepts through doing your homework. Attendance isn't necessary, but if you miss a class you'll fall behind and it can be hard to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you already took AP calc AB, then itll be an easy A

I personally love Sandy and would recommend his class. He is exceptionally smart and likes to teach. His content is difficult but if you attend class and do the assigned homework problems/ask questions, you should have no problem getting an A. I have always loved math and Sandy is one of my favorite professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sandy is a very smart man but he taught so students were supposed to learn how and why certain formulas/strategies work without him explicitly explaining it. This would work if the subject matter weren't already confusing enough. He does his best to answer all Qs but he's often hard to follow and makes a TON of mistakes. Harsh grader as well. Avoid

He won't be a good teacher for everyone. I personally did very well in the class but many people struggled especially if they hadn't taken calculus before. He can come off as condescending at times but if you just ignore it and ask your questions regardless you'll get a clear and helpful explanation. Show up and study hard and you'll be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Must have a general understanding of Calc 1 BEFORE taking this class. Very heavy on differential equations. Don't recommend if you're not a good self-study. Grade is 50% quizzes, 50% final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awful teacher. If you did not have calculus in high school do not take his class. He uses his own methods to teach and your grade is solely based on tests designed by him. Awful.

Not very helpful outside of class &doesn't offer extra credit. Came in with 3 yrs of Calc experience &knew all the material but performed poorly because of my test anxiety and he wasn't helpful at all. Makes everything more complicated than it needs to be, and tells you to learn things his way when there's and easier way. Quizzes  50%, final  50%
Awesome professor. Very clear, helpful, straightforward. Very clear homework and quizzes. I learned a lot and it was no easy, but he gives homework every night to help you keep up.

Took him in my first college semester and thought I was going to pass with a B but got a C+ after the final. Try to take a different professor. I practiced and participated, and even went to his office hours a few times. He's a cool guy but I would not have taken his class if I had the choice. But don't fret if you have to; just practice.
Sandy Blank makes up math terms, teaches you things in round about ways, and then lets you know you were learning derivatives etc. all along.

I personally didn't struggle in his class. I had a great calc teacher in high school so my foundations in the subject were very strong. However, if math isn't your strong point I wouldn't recommend Blank. He barely teaches in class, you basically teach yourself the material by struggling through the hw. But if you can do that the class is fine.

Blank does not know how to effectively teach calculus. He often gets example problems wrong, and his students are forced to correct his math multiple times per class. You're better off just reading the textbook and teaching yourself. As lon as you can do the practice problems, though, the quizzes are a breeze.

Sandy is not a helpful person. He is very disrespectful and generally not approachable. Usually spends the first 20 min of class on attendance the next 30 doing hw problems and then crams a whole lecture into the last 10 min. His quizzes aren't bad as long as you can do the assigned problems. If you cant teach yourself math it wont be an easy class

To get an A in this course you MUST do the homework and do it well. Take your time on the homework, and then the quizzes should be fine. The quizzes are pretty easy and its fairly easy to get an A for the class. The final is much harder than the quizzes, but doable if you know your stuff. If you are in honors and can take non-honors I recommend it
Awful. Doesn't care. Doesn't know how to explain. Takes joy in tricking and deceiving.

Prof. Blank is a really funny and nice guy, and extremely helpful when asked.  This does not mean his class is easy.. his quizzes are difficult and are 50% of the grade, with each quiz worth more than the last.  The final is the other 50%.  He makes the material clear and is always willing to explain things as many times as you want.
Though the material was difficult, Professor Blank was a good teacher. For someone who has trouble understanding math, he made the topics clear and easy to understand. Overall, a very good teacher.
Prof Blank is funny and really nice. His quizzes are pretty difficult, but bearable. Stay on top of the things and it's not that bad of a class.

I loved Sandy! The comments on here scared me at first and the first day of class he even acknowledged that people thought he was mean. His jokes are funny, and he's a really nice guy. He doesn't mind joking around during class. While his quizzes are hard, he's always available in his office. Sandy's one of my favorite teachers at NU :)

I had Prof. Blank for Calc&Diff Eq for Bio 1 and 2 my freshman year. He is definitely the hardest of the teachers for this class, but you will actually learn the material. Go to class and do the homework because the quizzes come directly from these two things. He is actually pretty funny and his hats were always entertaining.

Hated him in calc 1 but loved him in calc 2 since finally understood how to excel in the class: DO ALL HW in time for every class and ASK QUESTIONS for EVERY problem you don't understand. Uses hw for his VERY HARD quizzes and bases midterm/final off these quizzes. He's glad to go over problems and is helpful if you take initiative to ask questions.

ok teacher, not so great of a personality.. although there are only a few quizzes, they are hard -- STUDY for them!  don't be intimidated by the material covered the first day, it's not so bad.. the whole semester builds on basically the same stuff

Prof. Blank was a pretty good teacher. He knew what he was talking about. The online notes are really helpful, but overall he's kind of strict and condescending. He can be a jerk sometimes but when it comes down to it, he's a decent guy. Kinda funny, also will count good quizzes twice as much as quizzes you do poorly on. He's a pretty good guy.

Not to bad.  He is boring in class and moves pretty fast.  He quizes are on exactly what you do in class so if you study you will be fine.  The overall subject is very easy anyway and he is very fair with his grading.  Never uses the book though all the hw is on blackboard.  dont waste your money like i did on a book.
this is the best teacher ever. he look s great funnnyy, just the perfect genes. SOOOO U GUY BETTER STAYYY COOOLLLLLLLLL OORRRRR..... yeah just stay cooll

He was extremely rude to use if we didn't get something. One time he even said to us "It's not rocket science." If you pay attention in class then the tests aren't that hard and he'll replace you're average with what you get on the final if you get a better grade on the final. He had annoying mannerisms that bothered me the entire semester.

i once missed a quiz because my flight got delayed. i showed him my ticket as proof and he wouldnt excuse me saying it was my fault for not scheduling an earlier flight to be safe. but he excused my friend and she had the exact same situation and proof. his quizzes and tests are very fair if you listen and do the hw, but he's just a mean person.
Doesn't explain well.  He's also a little bit rude.  Enjoyed my other calc profs much more

I usually like math a lot but I did not enjoy this class. He trys to trick you on the quizzes. Will replace your quiz average with you final grade though which helps. Do good on the final and that is your grade for the class!
i had him for calc 1. do your hw and ask q's on which ones u dont get, and ull do fine. quizes usually have no surprises, and final is very fair. hes a fair guy, i thought he was easy
would take off lots of points when you only got one question wrong on the test. does not explain very well.
Pretty good class.  Quizzes are easy if you do all the homework and ask questions in class.  The final had no surprises.
This guy is great!!  Tries to be funny and makes classes interesting...not bad lookin' either

This is the worst teacher I've ever had. Class average was below 60%, and he refused to do anything about it. His explanation: "Well two of you are doing well and I'm teaching to them. You should all withdraw." Waste of my time and money.

He acts like you're an idiot if you don't understand something on the first explanation, or tells you to drop down to lower level math courses.  Who the hell wants to do that, and then have to take your class all over again dick.

I don't know why everyone gives this guy such a bad rating. Lectures are VERY helpful, problems are clearly explained, as long as you keep up with the material the tests are fairly easy. You want a bad math prof? Take one of Braverman's classes. <s
worst math teacher i've ever had. .  makes fun of your mistakes, talks to you directly in class - embarassing.  mean.  incompassionate. BAD TEACHER
pretty easy class, very helpful. knows when you dont understand and will try to re-explain

worst professor i've ever had!  very intimidating! loved to ridicule students and display their mistakes!  this is college!  he is the reason so many kids grow up fearing math!  teachers like him are why our country is behind the rest of the world in math
No Comments
Great professor, she grades well as long as you contribute to class and demonstrate engagement!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Monica was a great professor throughout the semester! She was caring, attentive, and really easy to reach outside of class. She genuinely just wants to see that you're trying and participating (definitely participate a LOT). The textbook doesn't matter until you get to the midterm/final, and even then, just look up chapter quizlets.

Professor Borgida is a wonderful Professor. She is quick to answer emails and provide clarification and help at any time. This was a harder class, but that goes with the territory of accounting. The homework and discussion boards tied in with the weekly text and facilitated learning the topic. I would take another class with her. She's wonderful.

She is very kind and always willing to talk, but her feedback is never clear. She often assigns very clear, short assignments, but grades them like her life depends on it. I am constantly emailing her trying to find out what I am not getting and she tells me to refer to a rubric (which I have been unable to find.)

One of the most understanding Professors you'll have. Super accommodating and really cares about her students. The class itself is very reliant on participation but as long as you speak 1-2 times each week you can get a good grade. There's a lot of group projects but this class is very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This will probably be the easiest class you take at Northeastern. Participation is 30% and she gives 100's on almost all presentations. It is unfortunate that she dumbs the class down so much as she is extremely accredited in the field. However, if you really try to get the most out of the case studies, you will walk away having learned something

Sweet and caring, but her train of thought can't be followed and grading has no clear criteria. You could probably submit the same project twice, but she'll give them different grades. Tests are heavily based on the textbook, which isn't gone over in class. I would tell you to skip class, but participation is a huge chunk of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Borgida is awesome. She is a very passionate and respected in the field of international business. The textbook is utilized only on the midterm and final which are very easy if you read and study. Participation is a huge part of your grade so you need to show up and speak at least once a class if you want an A. Projects are fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Borgida enjoys speaking for the majority of class. Going on seemingly unrelated tangents to the topic, it's impossible to follow her train of thought. She also accepts incorrect answers from students and ultimately contradicts her lecture/misinforms the rest of the class.

She is a great professor and a really caring person. The class overall, is really easy and you can easily get an A in this course. Class participation is an important component of her grading criteria along with group projects.

This professor's class is really unclear. You're not sure how you're graded at any point. It might as well be random. Doesn't try that hard when it comes to making or grading assignments, expect surprises on grades and test. Don't expect to learn a thing. One of the most negative classes in my 4 years at Northeastern. Get a different Professor.

This professor is a very kind person. With that being said, you will not understand the structure of the course at any point during the semester. Grading criteria changes every class and youll have no understanding of how youre being scored. All grades other than quizzes are provided in the last week of the semester. Nothing but uncertainty.

He's my FNCE 623 prof in UCW. He doesn't teach visually, only verbally, so lectures are very hard to understand. But his class is very chill and sometimes dismisses us early. Pop quizzes, but only for participation and not graded. 1 individual assignment, 1 group assignment, & 2 exams. Advice: REALLY STUDY HIS SAMPLE TESTS.

Amazing prof, amazing lectures. He is always happy to help students. There are quite a lot pop-up quizzes, but if you show up and listen carefully, quizzes are easy. He wants everyone to have good grades by giving easy quizzes and easy midterms. But for final exam, if you don't study hard for it, you won't be able to finish it.

Professor Drissi is one of the nicest professors i have had at Northeastern, take part in class and he will remember you and like you. He does pop quizzes but is very lenient in grading them. He really wants each student to get a good grade. Go to his office hours if you need help! He will be extremely happy you made the effort.

Terrible instructor. Easy Midterm, ridiculously hard final. Those are the only two tests of the year, the rest is pop quizzes that happen approximately once a week and are so frustrating to deal with. Does not articulate speech well and he has no ability to teach others whatsoever. AVOID.

Interesting ML course and material. Exams are very hard and will need to be massively curved. Homeworks are easy. Kind of an odd guy, he is very worried about people recording the class or distributing his lecture slides online among other things.

The class consistently runs 20+ minutes overtime despite already being 3.5 hours. Homework is straightforward, but exams are closed-book, closed-note, no cheat-sheet allowed. No practice exam or study guidance for exams beyond “just review the slides.” Lectures aren't recorded, and slides are uploaded days after class.

I enjoyed Professor Braun classes, the material is up to date and provides great NLP basis. The books he refers to are great and he takes time to explain concepts in the class. His exams are difficult but he applies curving to the grades. His classes are theoretical and his homeworks and project require to apply the concepts using python.

great professor, gives insightful lectures to help prepare data scientists for industry. the material was useful and informative. easy class as there were no exams and only homeworks/"take home exams" that were basically homeworks. TAs were excellent as well and always graded on time

The lectures were quite scattered and had to learn the materials myself. The piazza questions were almost never answered. The project was brought up extremely last minute so everything had to be rushed. We werent even informed what score we got on the project. Would have dropped out but the course was mandatory for me and no other prof taught it.

No clear grading criteria, never responds to emails (including his TAs), is not at all accessible outside class hours, does not grade assignments on time (assignments from January were graded right before the semester ended), cannot receive timely feedback on your work.

This guy's "office hours" were just him answering questions after class for like 15 min. Before the midterm there were about 20 people lined up and he just goes "dont have time for this today" and leaves. The midterm had almost nothing to do with the class material and was just advanced probability screwed if you didn't have enough prior knowledge.

Honestly this class was like the twilight zone in the worst ways. I would go in to office hours and he would not be there. He would show up late and cancel class randomly. You only get feedback on things you do well and never seem to see quizzes you do badly on. In addition we were graded on 3 quizzes worth more than 3/4 of the entire class grade.

David Brady runs a very lecture heavy class for EECE2540. He goes over the text book material from slides provided by the textbook's publisher. The homeworks are spaced out, so there's not too much, but the problems are from the text book, so expect to pay for it (or find it via alternative methods). You could easily not show up and still pass.
No Comments
One of the best brains I have ever met
Only professor in ECE with biceps and brains.
It is a lecture heavy class, but informal in nature. She spends class time sharing her knowledge about phonetics and it feels natural to ask questions and participate. I enjoy her a lot!

excellent professor. very passionate about the course and actively tries to include every student in the class before and during the lecture. if you participate in class and take the time to do the readings you will do very well

She's an amazing teacher, and really cares about her students/wants to get to know them. She's super willing to help one-on-one and is accessible outside of class. Her class has lots of in class worksheets to practice concepts and she keeps a fun atmosphere. She tries to make her students laugh a lot, and lectures are never boring because of it.

Alejna is a very good linguistics professor, she is clearly very knowledgeable about the topic. Outside of class she is easy to reach and responsive to emails. Super understanding, you just have to communicate things beforehand. No in class tests, just like 5 homeworks where she accepts corrections, a project, and a take home midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is lecture-heavy, but as long as you show up and pay attention, the midterms and finals are easy. She is very understanding about extensions. The rubric for the final project is not very clear, but she is a lenient grader. I really liked her as a professor, and her lectures were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professors Brothers is an amazing professor that has a deep passion for architecture and that was evident in her course. While her Canvas page is not the greatest and her organization could be better, she compensates her digital ability with her information packed lecture slides. I would recommend this class to anyone!

There was technically a lot to read for this class, however I did not find them all necessary. The class is lecture heavy, but I found them engaging and she gave us a break in the middle of class. She is not always the most clear with what she wants but she is very flexible and understanding. I loved this class and would take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Brothers makes lectures into dialogues which help to digest the content. She cares deeply for the success of her students and also has a great sense of humor. This class does need good study habits for the final/midterm, but it is manageable because, across the board, she sets very clear expectations for tests/projects. I loved this class!

Cammy brothers was a fantastic lecturer her talks truly derive inspiration, she speaks with a genuine passion and interest in her content. She is sweet and kind and genuinely only wants the best for her students. Her grading is kind and the criteria is very straight forward. Thank you!

Canny brothers was the best professor to ever exist ever. Nobody could ever top the lectures that she gave. I would go to bed dreaming about the churches of lalibela because of the absolutely thrilling lectures. Thank you cammy for enlightening my academic journey.

Professor Brothers seems passionate about her work and the history but she also doesn't seem to do much work as she has 3 TA's for her class and I notice they do most of the work such as the grading and etc... besides the lecturing. 3 different TAs had separate grading styles and who knows what you'll get for your grades back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: In the beginning of the semester, there were only 4 assignments on canvas. In the end of the semester, she added to 8 assignments, including attendance, paper, exams, weekly responds, note taking, and recitation performance. She left all works to TA and forgot to upload our final grade before the deadline of the semester. No clear criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really wanted to like this class. The material was so interesting especially as a stem major. Professor Brothers was just highly disorganized and oftentimes rude, and assignments instructions and grading was incredibly unclear. She lacked communication skills outside of class and it ended up being a frustrating experience.
Grading criteria is not clear. All works are graded by TA and sometimes they give C or EVEN WORSE.

Professor Brothers  is a grate professor and although she is a little unclear about the instructions on when the homework assignments are due this is because she is flexible. Some people are saying that she gives long lectures which is true but they are really interesting if you participate, if you take this class you will definitely learn a lot
Professor Brothers was great at teaching us the vast and diverse architecture styles of the world. She made every lecture fun and engaging, and I came out learning a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brothers is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about architecture history. As long as you come to class, pay attention, and participate in discussion questions (which are usually stemmed from inclass activities and discussion), you'll have a great time. The grading criteria may seem vague, but actually is extremely reasonable.

She did a great job at keeping long lectures very interesting. She provided a multitude of ways to learn through slideshows, documentaries, and museum visits. It is clear she is very knowledgeable and passionate about architectural history and I have recommended her to other classmates!

Took Spanish and Islamic Renaissance Architecture in spring 2022 in person. Was a very good class, the biggest portion of the grade was the final paper but the work was spread over the whole semester. She is a very understanding professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brothers definitely was enthusiastic about what we learned about so I found the long lectures to be quite interesting. However, her grading criteria was very vague and reaching her outside of class was nearly impossible. The homework for this class absorbed most of my effort as weekly readings were upwards to a hundred pages a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Disappointing! She doesn't really teach and passes you off to the TA. Minimal feedback. Boring lectures, too!
Unclear grading criteria (no rubric), doesn't grade homework personally

The actual time spent in class is fine, she just lectures the entire class about historical architecture. There are no words on the slides, and all notes are up to you to take. It is a lottt of information to take in, and the class is very long. The grades are, like others have said, pretty unclear. Not much instruction on papers given. Hw not bad

Looking at all of her negative reviews, I want to put some respect on Cammy's name! I think everyone is being overdramatic--given she doesn't always give clear details about assignments and due dates, it's more that she's flexible about everything. Although many complain about a lack of clear instructions, it translates to less harsh grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible. Her lectures are pretty interesting but she has HORRIBLE organization of everything. Directions and expectations for tests and paper rubrics are SO vague, unhelpful, and confusing! Cannot answer students concerns and questions at all regarding grades/clarifications for assignments because she just likes to brush it off and laugh at you!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I dont know how to say this nicely but she is not a good teacher. Shes a fine lecturer and clearly cares about the topics we discuss, but when it comes to caring about her students and communicating expectations, she is terrible. She constantly condescends her students and says that if we want our assignments to be graded, /we/ need to ask her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gives very vague feedback on exams and assignments. When students ask clarifying questions it's like pulling teeth to get a clear answer. The only way to get feedback is to set up a meeting outside of class, but good luck in getting a quick response as they never check their email. Lots of "it's only worth 10%" responses to student concerns
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives very vague feedback on exams and assignments, and there are very limited options for knowing what your grade is, as it's only based mostly on two exams and a paper. On the plus side, we got 5 minute breaks in the middle of our 100 minute lectures.

He was super caring and really easy to talk to. If you ever have any concerns, you can talk to him right after class or send him an email and he'll respond quickly (within a day). His grading is different from high school English, but he outlines his grading system within the first week and I honestly preferred it over traditional grading.

Genuinely one of the best professors Ive had, I really hope I get him again for more advanced courses. Sometimes Id head to the classroom early to use the empty space to study, and on days when he'd arrive early as well we would talk about all sorts of funny and interesting stuff. He's awesome, please take him, pay attention and you'll learn tons.

Literally such a caring professor who just wants everyone to enjoy the class and succeed. If you show up and participate (even in little ways) you will do just fine (obviously also complete the assignments). I loved going to this class because no two classes were ever the same from different discussions to new takes on writing. TAKE THIS CLASS!

I highly recommend taking Prof. Bushnell's class! Not only is he a passionate and caring teacher, but his grading criteria is clear from day one. He is helpful and accessible outside of class, and the material discussed in class is engaging. I learned more from this writing class than any other Writing/English class I've taken.
Take Jeremy! He really cares about you and cares about your grades. It's hard to do badly in his classes. Just show up, participate and you'll be fine.

Bushnell was the most caring and sweet professor -- honestly a life saver with his grading policy. As long as you do the work assigned and participate in class you will do well. Highly recommend taking first year writing with him!

Bushnell is super nice and cares about his students. The criteria to get an A is to literally do the work. As long as you submit the papers you get an A. There was a decent amount of time to write each paper and the class never felt like a burden. Would definitely take him if you have the chance.
Professor Bushnell is an awesome. He will give you an A if you participate in class and put effort into your work. He was a real life-saver this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor was very nice and understanding. Made class somewhat enjoyable. Clear grading criteria, so pretty easy to get an A in the class. Only three big papers in the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Bushnell is a super cool guy. He's passionate about his field and he really wants students to succeed in their writing. The class is based on students attempting to get their work published and he takes a realistic approach to the publishing world. We workshop a piece written by everyone and explore other writers works. would recommend

Professor Bushnell is not worth taking for advanced writing within the disciplines. He is not knowledgeable in the business field and has you work on assignments that are not relevant in the business field. He is nice but can be a jerk. He is not clear about what he wants from students at all - take with someone else or take the class online.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He appears to care about his students, but if your interest do not overlap with his you will struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bushnell is a great english professor who teaches well and is also not a harsh grader. His assignments aren't boring and tedious since you get to choose your own topic to research and write about. As long as you follow the guidelines for the major assignments, you'll do well. He also gives good feedback so you can improve as a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I didn't learn anything from his class, but he is incredibly clear about what he wants in your papers. It came down to a formula, and once you figure that out, it's easy to get a 100 on every one. Didn't enjoy the class, but you could choose most of your essay topics which was nice. My writing suffered, but give him what he wants & get a good grade

Seemed to know what he was doing, was clear in teaching and his standards, but was a pretty tough grader and it seemed a bit rigged at times. Didn't really take away much from the class. Not a bad teacher, just very forgettable and if you want a flat A you will need to both do the busy work and really know what he's exactly looking for on papers.

He is a nice teacher but I personally felt that he did not give the appropriate amount of feedback for the grades he would give. He tells you that you are doing good but keeps giving you a grade that does not reflect that.

Professor Bushnell is great! He is always looking to help you and if you go to his office hours he definitely will help you a ton! Participate in class a lot, keep up with the minimal readings he assigns, and hand  in the three papers on time following the rubric and you'll be fine. He is my fave english teacher ever and is super fair! Love him!

Jeremy is a great professor and super nice guy, really funny. The class itself is interesting, as well as helpful (if you're looking to get into publishing or be a writer). His assignments are pretty straight forward, not hard if you do them... The classroom vibe is really chill. I highly suggest taking Pub. Arts with Jeremy if you can!

Ngl this is a test-heavy class, taking up a big portion of your grade. But I personally found his lectures engaging and interesting. He does repeat stuff, but it reinforces stuff you need to know and makes the material stick. He's also super nice, so if you reach out to him with any questions, he will really help you and give you good guidance.
Even when you think you studied enough. It's never enough.

He knows his stuff, but his lectures are extremely boring and dry. He also has zero leniency in his syllabus, so if you get sick for more than three days or have a family emergency, your participation grade is tanked. Tests are difficult and he doesn't answer any clarifying questions during the test. Not the worst professor, but avoid if you can.

Bunce is overall not a bad teacher, but his lectures are so boring. He is redundant while lecturing, and I honestly learned better just watching the videos he recorded. Tests are all 50 MC questions and were not too bad. The class isn't that difficult, but I wouldn't take this class with him if your teacher being engaging is important to you.

Prof. Bunce is kind, caring and very knowledgeable who genuinely wants students to succeed. The course has 3 open response exams (lowest weighted less), 6 reflection articles (lowest dropped) and poll everywhere attendance with 2 drops. If you put in the work, you'll do well.

My complaint with Dr. Bunce was that his lectures were boring and very slow paced. All of his lectures are recorded which was really helpful. There are 3 exams, the lowest scoring of the 3 he weighs the lowest, he drops one quiz grade, and gives 1% extra credit at the end for trace. This gives you plenty of opportunities to get a good grade.
He is a great guy, and the class is easy enough if you are a behavioral neuroscience major. But im sorry, the lecture are a bunch of repeated information that makes me disengage.

A lot of materials in a semester, but exams were okay as long as u put in adequate effort. He also gave out 1% boost for your overall grade for completing the trace evaluatio,n which I think is very generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't encourage people to take this class unless necessary. Lectures are uninformative but mandatory. I had to teach myself the content before each exam. Incredibly harsh grader and gives no extra credit. Grade is 3 exams and 6 reflections. He's a nice guy, but this class was unnecessarily hard. @BNS students: take a different BNS core.

Theres so much content to learn esp. if you havent taken and bns classes before. Bunce is super passionate but I couldnt keep up with him and there was so much to memorize. Your grade is only composed of quizzes and exams so theres not a lot you can do to raise your grade. Attendance is also mandatory. Great guy but a lot of content to learn.

Professor Bunce is very understanding and an excellent lecturer. Getting an A is attainable if you're willing to put in a lot of work. He films all his lectures on Panopto (very helpful), and all of the questions on the Test can be found in the lectures. However, you will need to rewatch every lecture before an exam to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce is super passionate about what he teaches. His exams are based on lecture material and he is a very fair grader. Your effort in this class corresponds to your grade. Bunce is supportive, kind and accessible outside of class. Wants the best for his students. Material can be complicated, so go to class. Great for BNS students.

Dr. Bunce is honestly too disliked, he's great. Tries so hard to make class engaging even with dense material. Wants students to do well. You have to actually come to class to succeed, but if you pay attention and study the exams should be pretty fair. Weekly quizzes and poll everywhere help buffer grade so it's not just exams.

If you don't memorize each slide (and each midterm is about 80-90 slides each) you are cooked. All of his questions are so specific and he gives no other opportunities to raise your grade, even when half the class (I'm not joking) get below a D.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce is a great professor. He explains things clearly and thoroughly and welcomes questions. Exam questions are heavily borrowed from weekly quizzes and PollEverywhere. Your grade is almost entirely based on exams, but he weights your lowest one the least. Attendance is via PollEverywhere, you can miss 3. Lectures are recorded.

Dr. Bunce is great! Exams are extremely fair; mostly all content comes from lectures, and pay attention to what he says (and not just the words on the slides). You don't really need the textbook content for the exams, maybe 1 or 2 questions (I would still skim it though). I personally enjoyed his lectures. Learned lots of useful information.

Professor Bunce is wonderful. His neuroanatomy course is moderately fast-paced, but he always reemphasizes important concepts. He is encouraging, and he provides you with everything you need to succeed (like recording all the lectures!). He is also helpful during office hours, and his tests are very fair. I hope to take another class with him soon.
He is really fun and a generous grader. He tends to go on tangents during lecture but they are usually pretty interesting. His office hours are super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce reads from a slidedeck, resulting in boring, monotonous lectures. On the bright side, his tests are an easy 50 MCQs that are pulled straight from the slides. I would take him again for the class, even if it is a little boring.

This man talks A LOT. Sometimes it does also feel like he grades based off of a set grade he decides to give you (I've lost points on tests and gone to office hours and he has said that I got the right answer but didn't answer it how he wanted me to even though he says we can answer it however). He does seem interested in what he teaches though.
He looks evil. PPT not designed for self-study-iers, class good, not boring

- lectures can sometimes be boring and material is made more complicated than necessary 
- exams are not too hard if you put in the effort and study (taken from slides and lecture)
- material is interesting and he is very clear when communicating the material 
- Good prof. and if your willing to put in some effort you will do in the class
professor bunce literally bombards students with information

He is a great professor thats passionate about what he teaches. Sometimes his explanations of pathways are a little rocky but then again they aren't easy so its not his fault. Can get caught up in tangential discussions which is good if you are curious but can be boring for some.

Bunce is probably the nicest person I have ever met. He clearly cares about all of his students and wants them to do well. Sometimes his lectures feel like a lot, and he can be monotone at times, but all lectures are recorded, so you can review anything you did not catch in class. The tests are multiple-choice, and no textbook is needed.

Nice teacher, lectures can be monotone and dry, but its valuable information condensed and made easier to understand. Lectures are recorded so it's easy to go back to if you miss class. Exam questions are pretty straight forward if you study the material. If you go to his office hours, he is very supportive and will answer any questions.

Professor Bunce is clearly a very knowledgable and passionate member of his field. His lectures can be pretty dry, but he's always excited to answer questions. I would say to make sure you are actively listening, because his tests often have material that he doesn't put in the notes. Despite that, tests were very fair, not necessarily easy though.

Professor Bunce is great! While his lectures themselves can be a little dry at times overall the course material was interesting and his exams are super fair as long as you study. He is really accessible both at office hours and via email and overall is just a really nice guy!

He makes a lot of mistakes in lecture, but does not tolerate your mistakees on tests! Grade are typically scaled.. A lot.
He's a brilliant teacher. Always willing to help. Had a great time in his class. Highly recommended.
Overall, he is a decent professor yet fails to explain  the lesson easily. He isn't a very grader, and he isn't fair with exams but if you work hard in his class you ought to be ok

He is a brilliant guy who struggles from a language difference. I took Structural Analysis 1 which wasn't easy. He definitely knows his stuff, but has a hard time communicating concepts. However, if you don't understand something, he'll give you 110% to help you out. You just have to be patient with him. He's a great guy.
Very passionate about what she teaches. Lectures are informative and content is engaging.

Prof. Pereira was a great professor! You can tell she cares deeply about the topic and is experienced within the field, yet she's still lighthearted, approachable, and easily accessible.There are two bigger group assignments (with the same people), so it really depends on who you get paired with, but she has a system for ranking effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super sweet! So much reading to do tho, you will most likely not even try to do it at the end of the semester. Weekly discussion posts but only like 20 mins, but you have to pay for the program. Two group projects with assigned groups, but relatively light is you have a good group. She's very easy to talk to and passionate about the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's super nice and understanding, but lots of group projects with the same pre-assigned group, so cross your fingers you get a good one. Leanient grading, but there is a discussion board every week.

Prof Pereira was sweet, but I'm not sure I would take her again. I liked this course, and you were assigned a group to work throughout semester which I found valuable -- very project-based and several weekly readings.

I would rather be taught organic chemistry by a degenerate camel with schizophrenia rather than suzie. i didnt think it was possible to be so mis-informed in a subject you are required to have a PhD to teach...
THE WORST TEACHER ON NORTHEASTERN"S CAMPUS BY FAR. PLEASEEEEEEE TAKE ANOTHER TEACHER IF U CAN. She is the WORST and I'm a very good student.
Most horrible teacher. Not helpful, book cannot be used to study because she doesn't teach from it. Memorization of the study guides is the only way to get a good grade.

By far worst teacher I have ever had. My life was miserable during this class. It was so bad a tutor couldn't even save you. I am pretty positive she got fired so no worries anymore. BU can have her back!

During the semester, 2 kids (or the same kid twice) got a question right on the blackboard. Both times resulted in the whole class applauding. I understand Orgo isn't supposed to be easy but unfortunately her lectures make things worse which is frustrating. You'd think that her tests would somehow be related to her lectures but they're far from it

Suzie is crazy.  Her tests are ridiculously hard and don't cover the material she covered in class.  She relies too heavily on her slide shows and doesn't actually teach us the material.  If asked a question she stumbles and she is constantly referring to her notes throughout lecture.  Avoid her if you can!

Made the mistake of concentrating on the lectures for the first Orgo test. She'll cover the basics but will throw curveball questions. The second test, I ignored her lectures and used soley the textbook and had a much better understanding of the material. However, if you have a friend who already took this class, cling onto them and don't let go.

Definitely not a good teacher. If youre looking to be taught organic chemistry, don't take Byun. Everyday I question how she managed to get a PhD in Chemistry, because she has the hardest time answering the simplest questions and frequently gets confused by her notes. Its like she doesn't understand what she's doing. Reading the book is necessary.

I respect the fact that Prof. Byun is new, however I feel that her incompetence, at any level of education, is unacceptable. Her nose is buried in her notes throughout class, writing and talking at the same time, as if she were talking herself through the material and not us.  Students did exams in pencil and changed answers for a re-grade.

If you are smart this class is easy.  I got a 100 on almost every test.  You have to read the book and notes and learn her test style and you should do fine, as her tests cover only a small fraction of the total material.  Yes, overall she's a pretty bad teacher and I didn't learn much, but if you put in the work you'll get an A.
If you can, avoid her.  Warner is even better.  She doesn't know the subject.  If you ask a question, she won't be able to answer it.  AHHHHHHHHHH!

You can't just rely on your lecture notes. She is very unclear with her teaching, and going to her office hours and asking questions is useless because her answer most of the time is, "You just gotta know" or she'll give you a page number. She makes it hard to establish a student-teacher relationship. She's always rushy in class and office hours.

The WORST teacher I've ever had here.  Suzie sucks.  She's just awful in every regard- she doesn't understand the material and is constantly corrected by students.  She goes through notes at a rapid-fire pace but doesn't explain them nearly enough, and asking her a question is a flat out waste of your time.

Okay, so byun is hard but so is orgo. She is no worse then warnner and i might say she is easier. She lectures and if you can keep up with her she makes sense out of all the concepts. Her grading is harsh but all averages for orgo are low. overall she wasn't that bad.
horrible teacher... can't even speak english!! in the second semester, she started using powerpoints and pointless!! practice exams are not helpful AT ALL!!

Class notes don't prepare you well for class, if you can even understand your notes because she goes unreasonably fast and without much clarity.  Test were too hard and had problems she never covered in class. constantly needed correction.  Avoid her if you can.

Byun makes orgo harder than it already is. Her lectures are usually fast and unclear. Her last test was incredibly hard and far off from the difficulty of the practice test. Not to mention the keys for the practice tests usually have mistakes on them. One plus- due to the complaints, she did a better job of telling us how the final was gonna be.

Terrible.  Lecture is useless as she usually doesn't know what she is talking about.  Gives practice exams that are usually wrong.  Also, make sure you check your returned exams because she usually makes mistakes while correcting or uses the wrong answers.  Avoid at all costs.  She thinks a class avg below 50 is decent and laughed about it in class

Worst teacher ever.  She has no clue how to teach and does not know what she is talking about in lecture.  She puts material on exams that was not covered in class or the text.  Going to class is pretty much useless as all learning is done through the text.  Gives practice exams but most of the questions on them are incorrectly answered on the key.

Terrible teacher.  Do what ever you can to get another teacher.  Her lectures are incomprehensible and tend to be all over the place.  She tends to speed through topics in class while everyone falls behind, not to mention she does not know what she is talking about.  Her tests are very difficult and often include material not covered in class.

She thinks a class average on an exam of below 50% is "healthy." I pray to God that she gets fired ASAP not only for my sake but for the entire student population. It is a shame that we have to pay around $50,000 a year and have it wasted in a class where you will learn NOTHING and your GPA will suffer, no matter what you try to do.

Please, if you can avoid it, take orgo with someone other than Prof. Byun! The average on the last exam was ridiculously low, and she thought it was funny! If you do end up with her, I guarantee you will be teaching yourself because she doesn't know how. As someone else said, she really should not be responsible for teaching anyone this subject.

It seems unfair to have a horrendous professor for Organic Chemistry. I mean, the class is hard enough without a teacher who comes to class every day like she stumbled in by accident, but Byun's level of complete incompetence in all matters organic chem is really the iceberg to the proverbial Titanic that is my gpa.

Going to class is completely pointless. She reads off her notes the entire time and cannot answer a question if her life depends on it. Students are constantly correcting her. Tests are not that hard but she doesn't write them herself and will not tell you what they are going to be on. all and all, a completely waste of my time.
her tests are hard (b/c she doesnt make them up)but she also doesnt teach the material at all..horrible teacher... avoid at all costs
WORST TEACHER I'VE EVER HAD..she doesnt understand the subject, and can definatly not teach it

Terrible teacher,constantly needs correcting by students, extremely unclear about how she will determine your grade, makes an already hard subject nearly impossible to understand, does not make up her own tests, i had to completely teach my self orgo
She is useless! Extremely hard grader and is clueless in class!

nicest professor I've had. This class wasn't hard to get a good grade in, but it was difficult to actually learn/understand the material. She sometimes got confused by her notes during her lectures and then assigned homework that she didn't know how to do. Let us correct quizzes and get extensions when needed.

Prof. Carrier is amazing. Her lectures and homework prepare you perfectly for the four quizzes she gives for the semester (no tests/final). She cares deeply about her students and is definitely one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern (especially in the cheme department).

The nicest prof. I've ever had. Her lectures are pretty clear and the homework prepares you well for tests. Only con was that she was extremely disorganized, but she is a very sweet person and understanding with extensions, which made up for it. Allowed test corrections for half credit, which I know helped a lot of people.

Professor Cetin is truly one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. He is super smart, relaxed and encourages participation that really helps us learn. I came into class liking Micro Economics, but three months in and I love that stuff. Definitely recommend!

He's so great and nice! His lecture is relaxing, and he explains everything clearly. He always asks us if we follow him and give a lot of actual examples to help us understand. One more thing here, people complain about his accent a lot. I don't think it 's a problem. English is not my first langue, and I can't understand what he says.
Tamer is the GOAT of Econ. I would like nothing more than to kick back and smoke with him. Chill guy, great flow, class isn't too hard.
You can't really understand him, but all in all not a horrible guy and pretty easy course.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Teaches from PowerPoints, hard to get much out of them. Tests are easy, based off the 1-2 hw assignments (MC and a few short answers) per unit, and the recitation class right before the test. Super chill, doesn't care if you come to class, very nice guy. Super accessible by email/office hours, v understanding. From Turkey, so his English is ehh.
this guy has no idea about anything in the subject. he copies the stuff he teaches from other books. he is sooo bad, if you want to understand try to avoid him.
The guy is sooooo bad. he has no idea about the subject and he doesn't know how to teach or anything. avoid him because you will not learn anything and you will spend money for nothing.
I don't know how northeastern university hired him as a teacher. The guy has know idea about the subject and has know idea about anything in IE.
Easily the worst teacher i've ever had to deal with. nice enough guy, means well, but NOT knowledgeable in area of study. always blames the TA, is very unprofessional, and CANNOT TEACH.
No Comments

Had him for Digital Simulation.  One of the useless professors I've ever had.  I'm still not sure what I even learned from that class.  Very unclear, and not an easy class.  Nice guy, pretty awful teacher for this subject.

Definitely not an easy A, you have to put in the work to get your grade, but if you complete all assignments she guarantees you get a B. Other than that, she is very sweet and listens to her students. I can tell she really cares about our mental health and success. She's always available for extra help if you reach out.

I loved Dr. Musselman! She is more than willing to take you under her wing if you show interest. Her essays and projects are made to pull you out of your comfort zone while still being simple. Grading is confusing and vague at times so be sure to ask questions! If you follow her guidelines and listen to her feedback you will do well. Super sweet!
Great women and professor,  available if you need extra help. Gives constructive feedback in each paper to help you improve.

Great Professor. Dr. Musselman will make you appreciate writing and you will enjoy writing about 3 essays and 1 video project/graphic novel. With enough effort and re-writes, you will be able to receive a good grade.

Great professor, really keeps class interesting. A tough grader, but really helps you to improve. She was very willing to meet with you outside of class to help you. I was in her honors section of College Writing, and class was always a lot of fun. She brought in food for us several times, and overall was my favorite professor this semester.

I was in her Honors section of College Writing. She's an interesting person, but will not give you a good grade if you don'r write what she wants to hear, which is sometimes hard to determine. Her written feedback is often vague and unhelpful, but if you go to her office hours and ask a lot of questions you can sometimes get the idea.

I took the honors section of Advanced Writing in the Disciplines. She is available to help you if you need it, but I found the class and the assignments really stupid and uninteresting. If you put in effort, you will do fine, but she thinks writing is the most important subject when Pharmacy majors have more important things to worry about.

Always ready to help. Well informed and enthusiastic. Accepts other opinions -- people who say otherwise couldn't defend their position well enough or didn't have the motivation or confidence to do it anyway. I got an A and I disagreed frequently -- maybe not with subject matter, but sbout writing styles and sentence structure.
Nice lady and passionate about her work. The history of english course is difficult to grasp, but she is a very kind and fair grader.
