Great professor! Loved the homework. Very creative. Funny guy. Don't believe the haters!

Lectures are not related to coursework. Homework is only doable if you have prior experience with the programs. He grades based on how much he likes you so dont get on his bad side. He doesnt know how to write a homework assignment and will give you the most convoluted instructions. Id write more if I had the space; do NOT take him.

As stated on my other review, he isn't a great professor. Although he is passionate in what he does, his teaching skills are subpar. He gives hours of unnecessary homework and doesn't explain his assignments very well. There's also lots of filler, as he generally doesn't cut to the point. Great person, bad teacher.

Overall, Professor Mukasa was a difficult teacher. Although his class was fine itself, he was convoluted in giving instructions and on more than one assignment, I had no confidence I was completing it correctly. He is a great person, but his teaching skills are questionable. The class isn't hard, but he wasn't confident of the content.

He is enthusiastic, yes. Otherwise really confusing to learn from. We kept telling each other to "interpret the assignments how you want" because they were not clear that we would all do them differently. My only saving grace was having previous experience.
Convoluted Instructions for all assignments. Difficult grader. English not first language.
Extremely incompetent. Doesn't know what is happening

Nice person to approach but has no idea what he is doing. His lectures are disorganized and when you ask questions, he doesn't know the answer most of the time. Homework is much harder than what is gone over in class, so expect to be in extra help a lot.

Mukasa is a nice guy, but the man can't teach. He's really bad at communicating effectively to students and oftentimes gets confused with his own course material. There's WAY too much homework and it's all busywork. Even though it's easy, it's so annoying to complete. Again, super nice, and he means well, but he's so out of touch with his students.
awful professor, great human

This dude was absolute garbo. He never explained assignments and his homework was so hard. Also anytime you ask a question, he gets mad that you didn't pay attention. I should have dropped when I had the chance. 1/10 would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Mukasa was incredibly nice, and clearly cared about his students. I learned a lot, and made friends due to his group work. However, assignments were often confusing, and things disorganized. Many of my classmates were very rude to him, but he took criticism well, and improved throughout my two semesters.

There was SO much homework for this class, especially compared to other cornerstone professors. Be prepared to hear about how everyone else's cornerstone classes are a breeze while you suffer through hours of c++ and random ethics research "assignments" (they're basically essays). If you don't go to class you will have no idea what is going on.

Mukasa gives a ton of busy work w unclear instructions which means random points off for dumb things. He really wants to help students and get feedback but there is a just a disconnect and he doesn't understand how to. No one ever had their camera on or participated but lots of extra credit means its a super easy A and content is sorta interesting

Horribly organized and a ton of assignments. He clearly doesn't know what he's doing for most of what we do, and is very condescending and rude. Though it's an easy A, it's really not worth the grade.

I had him 1st and now 2nd semester. During Cornerstone 1, he was unclear about all instructions. Apparently he was an EE major, but you could not tell. His only redeeming quality is the sheer amount of extra credit, which he doesn't do anymore in Cornerstone 2. I got an A+, didn't go to class or take the final. Avoid this class or collaborate.

His homework assignments have confusing instructions. when he asks students for feedback, and they give it, he gets mad and says they are wrong. There's also so much work every week, and he doesn't make it very clear when stuffs assigned. He marked me for plagarism for turning in the same thing as a group member on a GROUP project.

Mukasa is a decent professor some of the time, but he is extremely unclear about his expectations for assignments and group projects, with the latter making up a huge portion of your grade. He is quite frustrating to talk to, and puts emphasis on participation and pointless busywork in the form of endless feedback and memos. I would stay away.

You can tell Mukasa really cares about his students, but he is new to teaching and this shows. He is not very good at lecturing and his instructions for assignments, as well as the grading criteria, is very unclear but he gives so much extra credit that as long as you do the work (which there is a lot of) it's virtually impossible to not get an A.

Very very difficult person and grader. Would not recommend. I really depended on my peers for help with assignments, which while a nice way to make friends freshman year, should not have been their responsibility. For reference, I had no experience coding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's organizationally a mess. You never know what's due or when, or how what you're doing connects to the curriculum. He focuses primarily on mechE projects in a general engineering course. Anything you learn will be from peers or self-taught, but he is an extremely easy grader and gives loads of extra credit. It's not worth the A though.

Mukasa is a very nice guy who cares about the input he receives from students. While there was a fair amount of busywork, I didn't find that it took up too much of my time. There are plenty of opportunities for extra credit, so getting a good grade is no problem. Mukasa has room for growth teaching-wise, but I wouldn't say he was a bad teacher.

Overall the professor is passionate about the topics and cares about his students. He gives many difficult assignments. You definitely have to work hard for a good grade in his class, but he is a generally fair grader and offers extra credit opportunities.

Overall, Professor Mukasa is a pretty good professor. He gives interesting assignments and is available for feedback. He structures his classes well. However, there is a ton of work and he is a difficult grader. His grading criteria is also not very specific or easy to understand, which is frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's ok. He gives alot of work, but he's flexible. I submitted an assignment 1 week late and he waived the late penalty because it was my first time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very unclear instructions. Assigns so much busywork. Grading is confusing. Be prepared to do the assignments with classmates, because they're pretty much impossible by yourself.

Professor Mukasa is extremely unclear about what he wants when he assigns work. Most of the coding homework was just busywork, and if you want to learn to program, find another teacher. He was extremely unforgiving with the group project amidst the COVID-19 pandemic and is the worst professor in the department.

Gives unnecessary busy work compared to other profs. Grading criteria is unclear and you lose points for things you weren't even aware you were being graded on. Takes more time to figure out what what needs to be done for an assignment than it take to do it. Mukasa refuses to give straightforward answers to questions even when necessary.
Very fast paced class, poor teaching of coding unit so get ready to teach yourself. Lots of homework that takes a long time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a new professor, so he changes his plans alot based on student feedback. The homework is not hard, but it does take up alot of time. Pay super close attention to the rubric if you don't want to lose points. He gives extra credit sometimes too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Doesn't give clear instruction or will give 3 different rubrics for one project and expect you to know which one to follow, resulting in a loss of points for which the reason remains unclear. Friendly person. If you haven't coded previously, get ready to teach yourself and be in FYELIC constantly because he did a terrible job teaching that.

Good at taking student feedback and adjusting his teaching style. Very difficult homework. A lot of time spent outside of class. Pace was too fast at first and material was not clearly explained but he got better after taking student feedback. Lectures weren't boring.

He is a very nice guy and genuinely wants to help his students. However, as he's new his teaching skills are a bit lacking. He isn't good at explaining things, which with the heavy homework load and his tough grading policy mean that you often lose points due to misunderstanding directions. He is forgiving with late work though.

I dont know why Codesso has 2.6 rating, hes amazing! He genuinely cares for his students by always doing hands on problems which has really helped me and Ive learned the most from this class than any other. Just do the pre-class assignments. Ppl who rated him bad js didnt do well. Hes super caring!

He is kind, lenient, available, and thoughtful. You have three big projects and he grades easily. The class is what you make of it-- can learn a lot or easy A. He also dresses up for Halloween. Take his class!!

Best profesor ever. Very caring about his students and wants everyone to do well. If you show up to class, do the worksheets before exams, you will get an A. Codesso is the goat. One of the Best profesor I ever had.

He forgot to post assignments halfway through the semester. Didn't really learn much at all during his class, and I never felt challenged or inspired by anything we discussed. Lots of 'code' in our projects was just his that he told us to copy. Easy A if you want to waste 4 credits.

Mauricio is really a detriment to both the accounting and data analytics programs at the school. I feel like if anything, my data skills suffered as a result of atrophying over a semester with him, and I wish had the opportunity to have literally anyone else teach me coding and databasing.

There are three exams for this course and one case study (group project-20%), midterm 1 (10%), midterm 2 (15%), and the final exam (25%), so this course is EXAM HEAVY. The case study took so much time and was overly complicated, and at least he gave everyone an A on that case study.

Mauricio is an awful professor and a detriment to Northeastern's accounting/data analytics dept as a whole. He's required for a lot of programs, which is tough for students who genuinely wanted to learn coding and data analytics. If you have any option in the matter and genuinely want to learn, avoid this professor AT ALL COSTS.

Professor Codesso doesn't spend much time on just lecturing during his classes but stresses a lot of hands on practice that he then goes over. All of his tests were multiple choice, including the final, so as long as you pay attention in class, you will be able to ace any test he puts in front of you.

The worst professor I've ever had!!!!! He assigns many assignments while failing to teach all the essential things. I did not learn ANYTHING also BEWARE of the final project because it will screw you up. He will not give any shit no matter how much you struggle or even if there is an error in the assignment directions.

Was genuinely excited to learn coding for my grad program, and this man completed ruined any ambition for that. Absolutely no useful class instruction, he never responds to emails, and his class consists of copying and pasting premade code he often writes incorrectly anyways

Hands down the worst professor in the business school. If you want to learn python, go to youtube or datacamp for free, since that's what you end up doing in his class anyways. He's never prepared for class, and has absolutely no clue how to explain tech heavy ideas to relative novices. Avoid him at all costs if you can.
Codesso is the goat. Take him if you can

He is not a bad guy at all. Most of the hws are on Connect, which almost serves as the lecture. If you really put effort into the hws on connect, the lecture will be easy. By lecture I mean some talking but mostly example problems. He is a pretty funny guy, responds to emails fast outside the class, and his tests are pretty easy.

He regularly made us download add-ons and programs via a remote server that regularly crashed our computers, which was problematic in a Zoom class. Then he begged for good reviews on this site and other surveys, so this guy is really just a complete unprofessional mess. Dont take him, hes terrible.

It is highway robbery that this guy's class is mandatory. The skills learned don't translate at all to the workplace, and any skills you do learn will be entirely through Datacamp because this guy STINKS at teaching. I spent 5 hours each week in class, and I honestly cannot tell you one thing that he taught me, not the online assignments.

I took Prof. Codesso through NUFlex online. He does a solid job at times of outlining the course and knows the material; however, English is not his first language, so his written materials can be confusing and his lectures border on unintelligible at times over Zoom. His communication skills are unfortunately not at an acceptable level.

Prof Codesso is super easy going. I had him during NUFlex fall 2020 and he was considerate of student needs in terms of extensions and extra help. He answers emails pretty quickly (usually within a couple hours). A lot of assignments on Connect but are manageable and also worth most of the grade. He is a great guy and wants his students to do well

I loved having Professor Collins as a professor and I found her classes to be very interesting. I would just be aware of the amount of reading that is required as well as the fact that some of her instructions were not clear when it came to the presentations that we had to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Collins was amazing and super nice. Going in I didn't expect to learn this much, especially as a non-criminal justice major. But it broadened my perspective for a lot of current issues we have. The course itself was a lot of reading and writing every week based on three books. But you do learn a lot from all of them along with the discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Collins is a great professor and extremely knowledgeable. The course was a bit disorganized but the actual class content was really good. It's discussion-based through most of the course based on 3 books you read. The class is not hard and is an average amount of writing, the best part is the guest lectures she brings in and her own input.

Dr. Collins is the most amazing professor I've ever had. Attendance is mandatory but the class is so interesting I would never even consider skipping. You have multiple required readings but all the texts are interesting and none read like a textbook. Grades are based on group presentations, discussion posts, and attendance. EC is an option!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of guest speakers (which are super interesting), very smart professor. However, for this class, while she is not a hard grader, there is a lot of work. There are 5 2-3 page papers, a final, and a ton of reading every week. There is also one group discussion you and a few classmates lead. Also unnecessarily rigid and rude to her students.

Dr. Collins is very sweet and I enjoyed the course material, but be warned that there were around 200 pages of reading per week that were required to participate. There were also papers close to ever week that had to be checked by the writing center for credit. The class is not necessarily hard but it is a pretty good amount of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: DJ is one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures are super informative, and all lectures are recorded live on zoom if you cannot make it to class. He genuinely cares about every single student in his class, and helping them succeed in becoming an EMT.

Jolliest prof ever. He is so enthusiastic about teaching EMS that you just naturally succeed in his class. If you show up to lectures and put in the work, you will 1) be jolly af and 2) succeed in the class. The course lowkey has the most work I've ever had in my life but it was SOOO worth it bc both DJ and Ben really want you to succeed.

DJ is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so caring and makes every lecture enjoyable with his enthusiasm and kindness. The two exams are a little tricky, and there is a skills practical, but he works with students during lab to ensure everyone can master the content. Truly one of the nicest people I have ever met.

He's genuinely one of the best professors that I've ever had. I love his lecture style, and he gives amazing feedback in simulation labs and class. He is so clearly experienced in his field and loves everything about it. He's very passionate, which makes him such a great teacher.

Took Basic Clinical Skills with DJ, both the class itself and DJ were great! Definitely learned skills that were extremely helpful for co-op interviews. It's a easy class with a majority of online assignments and a practical exam at the end. To do well show up, participate and actually learn the skills for the practical exam at the end.

This has been by far my favorite class at Northeastern, and DJ is the main reason! He and the other instructors for the course are so knowledgeable and really want you to succeed. Course is, by nature, lots of textbook reading but you learn so much from him. He's a quick responder to emails and is eager able to help.

DJ is so awesome!  Great professor with a passion for all things EMS. He responds quickly and is strict, but not in an unreasonable way. If you utilize all of the tools he gives you, it is basically impossible to not succeed. 10/10 DJ is the best.

Basic Clinical Skills was one of my favorite classes that I've taken so far. You get CPR certified in this class and learn a lot of useful skills for coop. He is very quick with emails and extremely knowledgable. There are online quizzes every week but theres only one hour of lecture and one 2 hour lab. 10/10 would recommend!

One of the most interesting courses I've taken at NEU. Classes are open discussion based, always corresponding to the assigned readings. The readings are ~25-35 pages and very interesting -- the language is not technical either so it's easy to follow. Creel is so genuine and passionate so it is easy to do well in her class!
Extremely nice and respecting of her students and the work and quizzes are not bad at all. I found this class to be very interesting and highly recommend taking it.

She's super sweet and caring. The class itself is mainly based on in-class activity worksheets, homework, and two exams. It is mainly subjective, so my advice is just enjoy the class activities because she really does make it an amazing experience. Hoping to get another class with Prof. Creel.
He takes the time to get to know his students and will put in the effort to ensure their success.
eccentric guy! but good at supporting you throughout your coop process
Richard is simultaneously a professor and a therapist for all his students. He is so knowledgeable, helpful, hilarious, and approachable. My favorite!!
Best Professor in NEU. Simple as that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Richard is an incredible advisor. He is clearly passionate about his job and his students. Attendance is mandatory and he does have a weekly assignment but the assignment is a breeze.
Richard is hilarious. Had a fantastic time each and every class. He really cares about getting you placed in a co-op. As long as you show that you're doing your part, he'll be there to help.
Great guy and funny! Makes classes interesting and helpful. Cuts straight to the point.

The funniest professor I have ever had i was rolling on the ground laughing every class and actually wished class was more often. Also by far the most helpful coop advisor because he's there everyday and does so much work to get you a good job. He is the only professor i keep in touch with. Like mentioned before this guy is the man.
Very hilarious guy in class. Quirky and weird in the beginning, but you get to wish every professor was like him. Will have you laughing most of class, just hope your not the butt of his jokes.
WORLD CLASS HOTTIE

conley makes the class interesting, and gives you absolutely everything you need to know about interviewing and getting a great co-op.  i specifically scheduled myself into his class for my next co-op class because his class is just that entertaining and informative.  all hail, richard el magnifico
Great

Richard Conley is the best coop adviser at Northeastern University. A friendly, patient, and caring person who goes out extra miles of his way to help students. I highly recommend students to change their last name to have him as coop adviser.
Richard is awesome!  He is most definitely the best co-op coordinator there is at Northeastern.
No Comments

Conley is probably the funniest teacher at northeastern. Take his co-op class! It consists of him basically talking/making fun out of the whole class, and he is absolutely hysterical. ALWAYS willing to help you out at anytime, and will definitely help you get a good co-op job. Simply stated, he is the man.
Richard is awesome. Very easy class with a hilariously inappropriate guy. TAKE THE CLASS.

Very funny guy. If you want some serious strict professor, don't have him. He gets everything he needs to get done but in a fun way. This is not your typical class but it was one of my favorites. If you're sensitive, don't take his class. If you have a good sense of humor, you'll love it. He definitely doesn't mind helping you out.
funny guy.
Good class, it's easy and he's helpful.
Conley is a great professor, don't know if he actually follows any sort of agenda for his class, but it's a lot of fun for something school related.   P.S. say he's hot....he's a little insecure
I'm very disapointed he didn't write any quotes.
No Comments
No Comments

Although the class was a little disorganized, we talked about a lot of interesting things and brought up a lot of topics that make you think.  It's hard to tell if you're doing well in the class or not, but I'd still recommend people to take this class.

Rather unstructured style of teaching (doesn't give deadlines, expectations in advance, etc.) can be frustrating for students who like to stay organized. Easily strays from the topic at hand. Acts chummy but probably won't do you any favors.
Cool guy, very helpful.
By far the BEST teacher I have had at NU. Take this class and take any class. She is so funny and so sweet. Love her
She was awesome! I took cultural history of Spain with her and even though the material was boring she made the class so fun
Very knowledgeable about the subject matter, I watched movies that I would have never seen unless I took this class. Super inclusive and understanding.

Cristina was such a fun and engaging professor for an otherwise potentially boring class. She took time to go over grammar which not everyone does. She is very forgiving with late work and partial credit and her class was a great experience overall. The class (SP 2102) itself can be a lot of extraneous work at times but she made it more fun!

One of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. She makes class so fun and engaging and treats everyone with so much respect. She is super understanding with late assignments and is always available to talk. There is a lot of work but she makes it manageable and is always willing to help.

Cristina is the absolute best. She knows that SPAN 2101 is a class most kids take only because it's required, but she manages to make it so fun. You never know what to expect with her making each class very interesting. A lot of work but that's not her fault. She really cares about her students and does everything in her power to help them suceed

She is amazing so funny and every class is very interesting. She is also very understanding with turning things in late or missing class. She teaches like a drama and you learn the important cultural things not just dates and names.

SPAN 2101 is a very dense class, with lots of homework and quizzes, but Cristina makes the class as fun and interesting as possible. She is incredibly understanding and flexible when it comes to grades and due dates, and does weekly check-ins with everyone to make sure they are doing ok, would 100% take Cristina's class again

Truly one of the kindest people I've ever met. I can't speak highly enough of him. If you reach out for help or need an extension, he's incredibly understanding and willing to work with you. I highly recommend taking any of his classes, he's genuinely supportive and accommodating.

I absolutely LOVED Craig. He is such a gem and deserves so much more attention than he's given. His lectures can be boring, but he loves to expand on topics and really help students understand. He's accommodating for his students and really cares about his students. He's the sweetest man ever.
Professor Roberston is so funny, gives great content and lectures. His class definitely isn't an easy A, it's kind of a lot of work but not super hard work.
This guy is the best. Inspirational. Really just living his best life writing unintelligably on the chalkboard. If you do the readings and go to class an A- is practically guarenteed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very passionate about his subjects, but he gets it if you aren't. Very clear about expectations and genuinely just wants everyone to learn something from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Craig is awesome! He makes class super interesting and has the best sense of humor. Would highly recommend his classes.

Robertson is one of my favorite professors I've had here.  He's funny and engaging in his lectures, and he is very passionate about his subject and wants you to get excited about it too.  He's very accommodating and understanding if you speak to him.  It's a lot of reading, but nothing too bad.  I highly recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I am not a fan. Craig is extremely biased and I never once was given an article to read that provided a viewpoint that wasn't his. This class was dull, useless and had no educational value. Also regardless of if I spent 1 or 20 hours on a paper I always got a B. If you want an easy useless class go ahead, but not if you want to learn anything.
Amazing professor with awesome teaching style. He is very clear. Do the readings and be open to understand what you may not have thought about before this class. can't stress enough how amazing.

Robertson is very smart guy when it comes to media and cultural theories. The class is an absolute ****, as the topics are really abstract, but Robertson manages to pull you in with his unique teaching style. He has a great sense of humor. You must read, and do not BS the essays, he'll see right through it. He also gives a ton of comments on work.

While this class had a dry topic, Professor Robertson made it pretty exciting and interesting.  The classes were dicussions rather than lectures and he valued participation.  Grades were based on 2 long and 4 short essays. He's also very funny.

Very interesting class with a fun teacher.  The class is discussion based and Robertson did a good job of keeping the class going.  He is also pretty funny with a dry sense of humor in an annoying briton kinda way.  He's also got a funny New Zeland accent.  Craig Robertson rocks hard and often.  He's got a black belt in keeping it real.

Shilli is a fantastic professor!!!! His classes are very straightforward (Geo, Materials, ect.). However, if you do not like learning from a slideshow then you will kinda struggle in his class. His exams every year have a similar structure and he's very accessible outside of class to answer questions.
Beware, comments on Shillaber are very subjective. He tends to have inconsistent and unprofessional attitudes towards different people and students. Very tough grader over minor issues.

i recommend attending lectures, but all of the information on the slides is found in the textbook. the textbook is necessary for the course. assigns a lot of work, but it was not too difficult. exams were hard, he gives some practice which gives you a general idea of the exam, but they are a bit harder. do the textbook problems and you'll do fine

Shillaber is a reasonable professor. He does not throw any curveballs on exams, so if you study the material from lectures and do the homework, you'll do well. His lectures are very thorough and you learn a lot. Labs can be long, but split amongst group members so they're not too bad. Not the nicest guy, but the longer you know him, the better.
Assigns way too much work. Would never recommend

Craig Shillaber seems to assign way too much work. We had a bunch of homework, up to 20 page lab reports, a semester-long project, and difficult exams. The exam practice that he posts are not similar to the actual exams that you take. He also is co-author of the textbook that you use, so if you must take the course, find the book online.

Craig is one of the best lecturers at Northeastern. There is never a dull moment, even in a 9am class. He is very knowledgable about the course content and clearly very passionate about the subject matter. Exams are very straightforward and fairly graded.
Professor Shillaber is very knowledgeable and cares so much about the subject material. Very fair on exams, and homework, although sometimes long, is always useful.

I didn't really get much out of lectures because he just read off the slides. He's also kind of picky about random things like formatting on homework/assignments which is annoying but as long as you follow his instructions your fine. Tests are fair and very similar to homework/class example problems.

Shillaber has super organized lecture note packs that make it easy to follow/revisit content from class. Tests are generally very fair and while there are quite a lot of homework assignments, they end up helping later on/save you time studying. Super accessible outside of class and genuinely enjoys the content he teaches.
Mostly read PowerPoints and looked down on us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems like he's gotten a bad rep from previous years. As off 2022, fantastic professor. Homework is due digitally, and although there are frequent assignments they are usually pretty short and can be done in 1-2 hours. Lectures were helpful and not mandatory. Grades VERY fairly. I have no complaints from his Materials class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: homework take a while. craig has very clear expectations and they can be annoying but he is good at teaching and very fair at grading. go to office hours. love craig,
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: very fair. Great at answering students' questions. He is smart
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You should ignore previous bad reviews. Craig is a very good professor. He is incredibly passionate about what he teaches and very caring for students. Exams are always fair. He clearly loves geotechnical engineering and made me like it a lot too. HW is difficult and long but helps a ton with preparing for exams

Past comments are basically irrelevant. If they are true, then that goes to show how much an effort Professor Shillaber goes to improve his class and he takes feedback very seriously. His homework policy is strict but it is one of the only things he asks of you. The class itself is A LOT but he very meticulously outlines everything that is excepted

i thought he was a great teacher and I would take his class again. I think a lot of people are mad about the homework policy. That makes sense, but it is a lot easier to adhere to now because everything is on Canvas. Lays out all the rules, and if you follow them you do well. HW's are about 2X a week and take about 45 minutes each.

While 2260 is a hard class, Shillaber does a pretty good job cramming in all the content he's expected to teach. His lectures are organized and his grading has gotten much more lenient than past years. Lots of weekly homework but if you benefit from structure and smaller, spaced-out assignments it's not so bad. Tests are relatively straightforward.

So. Much. Homework. Extremely annoying with the formatting of all assignments and he is a VERY tough grader on exams. He was knowledgeable about the course material though and his lectures were decent. Thats it though. He is the most condescending and arrogant professor Ive had so far though, hope to never take any class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Craig gives good lectures and is organized, and that's where his pros end. He gives an insane amount of homework, and is extremely unhelpful if you don't understand problems. He doesn't post homework solutions ever, and exams are tough. Super strict grading criteria for exams and homework. Doesn't post annotated lecture slides.

Was scared by these reviews going into this class, but Craig was a pretty good professor. Did not experience the concerns other students who rated him did. I thought his exams were fair. reviews.comment: She's so kind and caring of her students. Her enthusiasm for bio makes the lectures more interesting. She really prepares you for the exams by providing study guide questions and practice exams; grading for the exams is also fair. Highly recommend!

reviews.comment: Shes an amazingly professor. Her lectures are engaging and the coursework is very meaningful. But she cant keep track of time!

reviews.comment: The best teacher I e ever had! She is extremely helpful. Her lectures provide you with great notes and reflect her exams. She also gives you past exams as study tools. She wants you to succeed and understand her subject. Honestly take her if you can she's amazing and extremely helpful! I wish all teachers could be like her.

Dr. Cram was by far the best professor I have had during my 3 years at Northeastern. She made the class fun, applied real life concepts, and always had a great attitude. Clicker points during lectures were an easy grade booster and made the lectures interactive which made paying attention easier. Her exams were fair, and helpful in office hours.
Very enthusiastic. Keeps it simple but ensures that she conveys everything that she wanted to. Not too taxing.Would love to take another of Erin's classes

Cram is so genuinely nice, and really wants you to do well. She dumbs down the information and holds your hand through the class. Seriously, on several occasions I felt like I was back in Kindergarden. The lab for this class is horrendous, but her lecture is excellent.

Relatively easy class. Prof. Cram knows all about topics relating to her research - meaning some other topics difficult for her to teach. Overall a good class, however the lab is another story with a couple of long scientific papers to write.

I loved Cram. Some people complained that she just reads off the slides, but I liked going to lecture and thought she did a good job organizing the material. I could tell she really knows her stuff and loves genetics. Just know everything in the slides and on the practice exam and you'll do well.
Pretty easy to understand. Powerpoints give most of the information that you need to know so it is easy to catch up if you miss class.

A little different teaching style.  You will have to write a couple short papers and read some literature.  We gave a presentation as well.  Overall it was pretty good though, exams are hard but fair.  I would recommend taking this class with her the other proffesors arent that great compared to her.
No Comments
If you are looking to be a geneticist and get your bases in this class... you probably won't.  Cram is very easily flustered, but she means well...
Classes were boring overall. Weekly quizzes and homework were fine, but midterm & final were graded like she has a vendetta against every single person. 56% class average for the final & no curve.

This class was not great. The labs, ILS, and in-class polls were perfectly easy, but the Homeworks took 4+ hours, and the midterm and final were horrific, not to mention that they were graded like I personally offended her. The lectures did not help at all, and it might have gone better for me if I had just skipped class and taught myself.

She's very boring and each lecture is hard to follow. The class is clearly organized and you can get an A for both physics 1 and 2. Personally she doesn't work well for me, but I can see how other students may enjoy her teaching. She definitely knows what she is teaching though.

Don't get all the bad reviews. Has so many good examples and practice problems in class and truly cares about her students and that they understand it all. The ICAs are easy and free points, and you can miss up to 12. That being said, it is still Physics 2, so it is a hard class, but she makes going to class fun and helps you learn well.

I really liked Professor Di Credico. Her quizzes were very reasonable and we had in class activities that would help us prepare for the quiz. The exams were also very reasonable, with the grading being generous. The class to finally help me understand physics. I took her class in the summer so it might not be the same during the normal terms.

People are right that the lectures are not super useful. Homework can be tough but the book is free and has basically all of the theory and equations you need to ace it. Plus cheat sheets are allowed on quizzes and exams so if you can write it down you should have an easy time.

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring, don't prepare you for the homework and there's an in-class question for participation. Use your time better and just read the textbook. As a professor she is really not great. Her lectures feel like hour long yap sessions where she really only covers the topics at the most surface level, not as deep as the homework or tests take them. reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Genuinely such a mediocre professor. The lectures will give you general concepts but do nothing to actually help you solves problems or develop a real understanding. Completing homework's will get you infinitely more knowledge than lectures. If you struggle with non-physical application this class will be a major challenge.

She's pretty good considering how hard Physics 2 is to explain, but her lectures are too vague/conceptual and don't prepare you to actually solve questions with numbers. The midterm and final are rough and there is a lot of homework, but it balances in your grade overall.

she is an okay professor for a difficult course with a big lecture section. however, the slides were super vague and lectures were fast and confusing. the ILS professors are better for actually preparing for the quizzes and tests. i didn't feel like i missed anything if i missed a lecture

This teacher is genuinely terrible. If I never went to class I would be in the same spot as if I came. Also she is very hard to communicate with as she is very rude and has a rather large ego. I would rather pick any other teacher.

I took Physics I over the summer, and she let us know it moved at a much faster pace since it was compacted into 2 months. Had 2 homework assignments a week, which was time consuming but helped a lot. Lectures were confusing at times but she was willing to answer questions and provided examples. Had a quiz every week and she graded fairly.
She is unprofessional and made unfair assumptions about her students.

I took Energy, Env. and Soc. Fall '23. The workload is light, with a simple weekly homework and 3 in class assessments. Before each assessment there was a detailed review which it made it easy to get an A. Prof. Di Credico has a good sense of humor and I would definitely recommend the class if you are interested in energy or need an easy SI credit.

Grading boundaries are generous. Grading of midterms and homework is extremely fair. The homework is equal to (and sometimes harder than) the midterms which makes it good practice before tests. If you are struggling she is happy to help. Let us redo a midterm problem because the wording was a little confusing. Makes the hard topics seem possible.

Professor Di Credico takes an accelerated physics class and transforms it into digestible homework chunks.  Her grading curve is insane, where an 85 is an A-.  She is accessible outside of class and responds quickly to emails.  As long as you understand the homework, the class she teaches should be no trouble.

She is all over the place. The lecture slides make no sense if you want to re-read, she barely does practice problems and rambles a lot. If you get a good TA for ILS you will be fine, but if you don't you will have to teach yourself everything. Then again, I haven't heard great things about any of the other physics 1 professors.

She is very kind and knowledgeable, but she goes very fast in her lectures so you must pay attention. No matter what teacher you have for physics you will have to do pearson hw twice a week but she often gives examples similar to the problems.

I loved Professor Di Credico! I never really understood physics before her class, but she lectures so clearly that everything makes sense. She is very good at explaining, is passionate about physics, and offers so much help during office hours.

Physics is difficult. Luckily, Prof. Di Credico understands this and does everything she possibly can to effectively teach the material. I found her lectures to be the most engaging across my courseload. She tries to prepare her students for the weekly ILS quizzes and course exams with tricky practice problems.

I took PHYS1132. She was a very passionate lecturer, funny, and very chill. She gave very in depth study guides, and gave full freedom on the final project. The class was informative and she tailored the topics to your interests.

Physics 2 is already a really hard course and Prof. Di Credico makes it even harder, it is hard to fully grasp concepts from lectures and the homework is sometimed too hard. However, she is very understanding with students and easy to talk to.

I took PHYS1151 over Summer 1. The double acceleration proved very difficult, but Professor Di Credico was very aware of how difficult this made an already difficult course. Prof. Di Credico is super attentive and wants to get to know all of her students, very understanding and open to provide help. Took it during the summer so very fast paced and lots of homework but if you do all the homeworks and go through the quizzes the midterm and final are very straightforward.

Her teaching style is amazing! I love her comical real world examples. I'm really glad she breaks down the different sections of physics and tells us where certain topics go. She also writes (and keeps!) all the equations on the board.
Professor DiCredico is an amazing professor at the Physics I ILS. She gives a great review of the week's lectures, which makes quizzes seem easy.

The lecture is just a way for the profs to give you the equations you need.  Other than that, you'll learn absolutely nothing.  She does not go over examples and does not teach anything related to the quizzes or homework.

The main problem with her is that her lectures really are unrelated to the physics homework as well as the ILS course and lab. Very nice and helpful! She might be difficult to understand sometimes, but she does her best and her class is super easy. Take any physics class with her!
Really a bad teacher ever!!!! never give us a study guide before text. the classes is not clearly. moreover, no drop the lowest and no curve over the semester!! do not take her class!!

Great ILS teacher! Get her if you can!  Much better than the lecturers and actually goes over examples.  She summarizes the material well and makes sure everyone understands before moving on.  She provided an extra review session for the exam as well which turned out to be extremely useful.

DiCredico was the best ILS teacher I could have asked for. BEST ILS TEACHER EVER!  Seriously, if you have her for Physics 2 ILS, she is extremely helpful.  My lecture teacher (George Alverson) taught me nothing but she explains everything very well and happily answers all your questions.
she doesn't teach you what you need to pass the course. you don't have to show up to class to end up with a good grade..

The material is not the hardest but she cannot explain any of the concepts and she provides no examples, she makes the class more difficult than it has to be. Horrible, horrible teacher. She does not know how to explain concepts, even though she does understand it. Do not take this class.

Physics 2: lecture with allessandra is worthless. she only derives formulas and attempts to explain theory. She never uses examples or actual problems to explain anything...   However, she would be probably be good in any teaching format that DID have such examples. Like ILS or Office Hours. but maybe its just cause shes pregnant.

The material itself is not hard, however sometimes she is difficult to understand.  Has a tendency to "improvise" on the board, which is a good teaching technique, until you're midway into a problem and realized you messed the entire thing up.  My advice is to go to class, take notes at the beginning, but don't follow the examples on the board.

At first I thought she was just an okay, nice, average professor.  As time went on, I grew to really like her teaching style.  She is very good at introducing new concepts and making the class as painless as possible.  She covered everything we needed to know for the exams.  She was also very friendly and approachable.
He mostly bases his teaching in talking to the class rather than slides. There were many many readings.

reviews.comment: Great professor and person. Loves teaching and cares deeply about both his students and the material

Professor Cross is so passionate about the subject of Of Princes and Utopias, making lectures extremely interesting. Only take this course if you love to read and write, the reading assignments are pretty lengthy but definitely manageable. This course is a great way to study philosophy.

Prof. Cross provided the tools to succeed while being flexible in times of need. He relates to his students as human beings, which made this process, though painful, much more enjoyable. Prof. Cross is skilled in his academic writing, and as a witty historian, "retired musician," and photography hobbyist, his knowledge spans multiple IA disciplines

This was easily one of my favorite classes I've taken so far due to Professor Cross' passion for the subject and his interesting lectures. If you're at all into history beyond what he discusses, he will have a detailed answer for your questions. Highly recommend this course and this professor.

I am so glad that I took this class. Professor Cross is easily accessible outside of class, incredibly easy to talk to, and his lectures are genuinely very interesting. His lectures are fascinating, informative, and they consist of theories from both Western and non-Western authors. Overall, if you have a chance to take this class, do so. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very nice person! Talkative and inspiring.

Cross is one of the smartest people I have ever had the privilege of learning from. He is incredibly passionate and well-researched, and truly cares about the success of his students. His lectures are engaging and thought provoking, though are often fast-paced. He holds his students to a high standard and grades you as such, but it's worth it.

Took 2 HIST courses to round out my minor. Assigns too many readings, the content of which is not necessarily tested on exams nor required to write the papers. (You do not NEED to read everything, but should get a good sense of what the course is about.) I struggled to keep up (Econ major.) Great lecturer and kind man; +readings shld be optional.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Can't lie this was the most work I put in for any class last semester. It's really reading intensive especially at the beginning. Plenty of room for discussion and really interesting class.

Overall, Prof. Cross's lectures were very interesting. It was often a combination of him teaching the historical context of each reading and a discussion about the readings. Course graded only on two papers, a midterm, and final. It is evident that he is passionate about the topic!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and reasonable grader. If you attend class frequently and do the readings you will be well prepared for the papers and tests. Even though I didn't receive an amazing grade, I loved his class. It is obvious that he loves teaching and enjoys his own class. The exams and papers were hard for me. However, I would love to have him as a professor again.

a good person but wouldnt take again. too much info info with no time to process & doesnt like questions in class. downplays the need to know dates but makes a good portion of the exam about dates. slides are useless. terrible grading system. I feel like he didn't read our final papers and just put in random grades tbh

reviews.comment: Professor Cross is one of my favorite professors.
