The papers and exams are difficult, but if you put in the work, you'll be fine.
Very enthusiastic when lecturing and flexible for all students.
I love him, would highly recommend taking his class! One time I got sick and he sent me all the lecture slides, he really cares about his students.

He's lovely. Really nice man who genuinely cares about his students. I took Latin American Film with him. He assigns really interesting films to watch, and offers great discussion questions that make analyzing the movies fun and informative. He's really optimistic and funny. Def take him!

Prof. Cuenca is an amazing teacher; he's so bubbly, keeps class fun, and ensures you really understand what he's talking about. He is always willing to be available outside of class and is one of the kindest professors here. He really has a passion for the language, and it shows through his teaching.

Cuenca is the sweetest professor I've ever had. He is so genuinely passionate about what he teaches and is extremely knowledgeable on levels past what is expected. He wants only the best for his students and is supportive by nature. My class loved him so much that we planned a dinner for him at the end of the semester altogether! No final exam :)

Dr. Cuenca is an amazing professor! He's knowledgeable, kind, and truly cares about his students. I've studied Spanish since 3rd grade, and his grammar teaching is the most effective I've experienced. The homework is thorough and reinforces learning, which is why I rated the difficulty 3—it's time-consuming but worth it. Highly recommend his class!

INCREDIBLE professor who truly loves teaching and is super knowledgeable. Cares about all his students and only wants them to succeed in Spanish. Grades based on realistic expectations and is always transparent and helpful with any problems/questions. 100% worth taking! I left everyday in awe of how much I learned and eager to continue with Spanish

Profe Cuenca is my favorite professor of my 4 years at Northeastern! I've taken his SPNS3101and CLTR1240 classes and loved them both. He teaches in such an original, passionate, and inspirational way and is excited to help every student do the best they can. You'll get back what you put in to his classes, and doing the work is always worth it.

I love this professor. He is one of the best lecturers and teachers I have ever had. The passion he has for the spanish language and language in general is unmatched. He walks through very interesting linguistic examples. His homework, tests, and projects are all very interesting but still easy to get a good grade on.  I LOVE HIM SO MUCH!!!!!!!!!!!

Easily the best and most passionate professor I have ever had. Extremely knowledgable about linguistics. For lectures, he will make many more slides than necessary and show certain slides depending on how the class is going. 100% would take this class again.
Professor Cuenca is incredible. He really cares about all of his students and really wants you to learn. Every class was engaging. I can't recommend him enough. My favorite class I've taken so far!

Profe Cuenca is the best! He taught me Spanish in a way that I had never thought of before. He essentially goes back and teaches you everything you have learned in Spanish before, and then explains it a million times better. He is brilliant and definitely knows so much about linguistics and teaching Spanish!! Could not recommend his class more.

Prof. Cuenca is the kindest professor I have ever had. He really wants you to succeed. If you aren't the best at Spanish and want to get better, he gives you all the resources to do so. He starts with very easy content. There's a weekly module that seems like a lot of work, but isn't too bad and can definitely be done in one setting.

Profe Cuenca is a great teacher.  He is very passionate about his subject and clearly cares about his students.  It's not too difficult but you can get some good Spanish practice out of it, and he is not a harsh grader.
THE KINDEST PROFESSOR. So understanding, flexible and wants students to succeed. Super knowledgable and engaging, even in the asynchronous learning model.

An AMAZING professor! He is so understanding/kind/patient especially in the online environment. Assigns weekly modules that seem like a lot of work but aren't really that bad. Emphasis on watching Spanish films/videos and discussing them in the class. Expect breakout rooms during lecture and adding work/thoughts to the Padlet.

Cullen is a good prof, there are 3 tests which you don't really even have to study for, if you just paid attention to class you can get an A on every test, There are a lot of readings for homework but they aren't that bad, theres also some anime episodes/movies and other movies for homework which was cool. She is a nice person overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really nice, grades fairly, interesting, and offers good feedback.

Prof Cullen is very knowledgeable and her passion is infectious. The course consists of a few papers and 3 exams, all of them were very straightforward. Be aware that you don't watch the films in class and therefore have to watch them on your own time.

Professor Cullen is so considerate and easy to talk to. She really knows her stuff and makes lectures very interesting and relevant to students' interests. Fairly easy course with short-answer HW questions and a few papers, but you definitely learn a lot.

Professor Cullen is truly a great professor! The class is quite easy but very informative and I enjoyed every assignment we did. The homework consisted of watching anime, reading manga, and other pieces related to Japanese culture. I can confidently say I was excited to come to class every time and really took away a lot in the end!

She's an amazing teacher. I loved the class (Japanese pop culture) so much, we focused on many issues and interpretations in japanese history and modern culture. There's two short papers (2 pages ish) and two question sets (10-questions each, but you have to be concise), and one final research paper (5-6 pages). Classes are interesting

Professor Cullen is great! For CLTR1700, Cullen really knows her stuff and makes class engaging. Sometimes lectures are tied to hw assignments, but hw is really not much work. Even the question sets and essays were kind of fun! If you want an interesting, low-work class, take CLTR1700 w Cullen! Highly recommend.

Prof Cullen is very nice and she really enjoys what she teaches. The lectures and homework are super interesting, I wasn't familiar with Japan's pop culture before taking the class. She made us watch anime and read manga which was a completely new experience for me. Very interesting class with engaging papers and no exams.

She's nice, class has some really cool discussions. Tests are fair (especially since they are take home). I spent a couple hours on each paper and did well. The open-ended research paper was cool, great class to learn more about modern japan//recent history.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I got 100% on this course, very easy if you put in the effort. I don't know how difficult it usually is, but during the pandemic where exams are take-home I got 100% on both midterm and finals, although I did spend quite a bit of time on it. If you spend around 5-6 hours for each assignment you are pretty much guaranteed an A.

Prof Cullen is respected, knowledgeable, and kind-hearted. Her lectures are clear and very interesting, and I love her use of videos and real-life examples. Some of Japanese culture is weird but she handles everything very well. Her class inspired me to take a dialogue to Japan, and I felt well informed thanks to her class.

Professor Cullen gives off a "mom" vibe. She's clearly very knowledgeable about the content and going to lecture is required, but she always discusses things in a kind and interesting way. This class was interesting (I even found myself enjoying the readings we had for homework), and the exams weren't bad either. Would definitely take her again.

Prof Cullen's class was so fun and unique. I learned so much about Japan that I didn't know before, and she was so knowledgable and clearly loves what she teaches. Her tests are fair and the final presentation and paper was so fun! Keep an open mind about some of the stranger parts of Japanese culture and you'll get a lot out of this class!

The curriculum lacked clarity, especially around the paid online simulation. We were expected to “figure it out” without foundational instruction, and questions about how it worked were not clearly answered. Lectures felt disconnected from Canvas and the Sim. The 5 weeks of intense group work were challenging, and overall the course felt disjointed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer. That is about the only positive thing about him. I would say "avoid," but he is the only one teaching this required class, so "good luck." He is not reasonable. When he admits to mistakes on grading he still won't change the score. He is not rationale. Has a god-like complex and thinks he just has higher standards than others.

Dr. Odom is awesome!! Super knowledgeable in consulting and shares a lot of his personal experience. He's really down to earth and treats his students as equals. Class is very discussion and activity heavy. Few things make up your grade like the simulation and a couple presentations, so try to do good in that. 10/10 recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Odom's class. Throughout the semester, the professor uniquely integrated AI, and students learned how to write clearer prompts. To be transparent, the simulation is a significant portion of your grade, so I would try to get comfortable with it and ask questions earlier on.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have a bad group in this class you will have a very difficult semester. The amount of work you put in does not reflect your grade. Unless this class is require I would not recommend.

I really enjoyed Professor Odom's class this semester and would say he is one of my favorite professors in DMSB! He recently restructured the course to include AI and is extremely receptive to feedback. The group airline simulation project is a lot of work, and it rewards detailed analysis and group decision-making. I recommend Prof. Odom

Professor Odom is genuinely one of the best DMSB professors! He really embraced the use of AI during class, gave really engaging lectures, and he is very passionate about what he teaches. The group simulation is a fair amount of work but so worthwhile, and he was always checking in on our progress throughout the semester. 100% recommend taking!

Professor Curtis cares, knows what he is talking about, and is passionate. He has experience and has been in the industry which provides stories, lessons and advice throughout the course. Heavily weighted on an airplane simulation & presentations that if not done well, can impact grade severely with minimal individual grades to make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Odom is easily one of my favorite professors I have had at Northeastern. He has completely restructured this course to remove exams and papers. It is heavy group project based and he has very clear grading criteria and a clear syllabus. He integrates AI into the course well and really wants student input into making the course better.

Professor Odom is awesome. The course is well-run, with a clear focus on preparing you for your professional life. There is an emphasis on AI as well. The course requires thought and organization more than it is difficult, so stay on top of things. There aren't any exams; it is all presentations and the airline simulation. Highly recommend.

Professor Odom is an amazing professor! His teaching style is structured very well and there are many opportunities to ask questions and learn from his real world experiences. He is very pro AI usage and always willing to meet with students outside the classroom setting to talk about consulting or give career advice. Everyone should take his class!

Professor Odom is great. You can really tell he has practical consulting knowledge through his own hands on work in consulting and previous work experiences. The course is not necessarily hard but there are many weekly timelines/deadlines. Be ready to organize yourself and work ith a team to successfully address simulation and presentations.

Enjoyable class. Professor Odom is upbeat, interesting, and treats students like adults. Forward on AI.

Class curates an authentic experience by putting students into groups to work through a realistic simulation. Students are graded on their team's simulation performance and several client presentations, rather than papers/tests.

I mean he really is a good Professor. Yeah it's a lot of work, but if you come to him for help, he'll work with you. He is also very receptive to feedback. Would take again, I would just recommend taking the class during a lighter semester

Professor Odom's humor and personality made the class enjoyable, and I always looked forward to it. He treats students like adults and values feedback. He can be inflexible on grades and seeing alternative perspectives on assignments, but he is consistent with his expectations. It was a fun, challenging class and a good way to end my last semester.

Although he can be pretty hard to reason with at times, he's genuinely a good professor. He has a lot of experience and he is a good person to ask about anything regarding post-grad plans. If you don't communicate or reach out to him, you most likely won't do good. Just talk to him regularly and you will be fine, don't worry.

This professor and this class are by far one of my favorite classes at Northeastern. This class is tough, and it isn't going to be easy, but it's gratifying if you attend class and pay attention. I recommend this class to everyone that I know, and I wish that this professor would teach more classes because I would take a class with him again.

EXTREMELY harsh grader - avoid if you care about GPA. Going forward this class has a lot of proposed changes that will make it even harder. He treats you like an adult, but is really inflexible with grades and deadlines. His class had a lot of potential to be more enjoyable, he's a fun lecturer. Wish my grade reflected the time and effort I put in.

Typically felt like meaningless busy work. Would NOT recommend.The whole semester you are working with the same group, and he offers no peer evaluations so if you get a bad group, you're screwed.I was hoping to get some real consulting experience in this course, but instead, I left with nothing but a lower GPA to show for it. RUN.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
One of the least understanding professors. Very tough grader and doesn't ever give partial credit on any of the assignments. 
Don't listen to the comments saying he provides ACTUAL consulting experience since this semester he switched to the simulation which has nothing to do with real consulting. 
Overall it was a useless class that tanked my GPA

Professor Odom creates a collaborative and dynamic work environment that enables students to absorb the material long-term. He will challenge you as a professional while providing support and autonomy throughout the semester (Make sure to take detailed notes and try not to miss class lectures, the info will be important for your deliverables).

Professor Odom makes his lectures very interesting and gives students a lot of autonomy throughout the semester. The course is extremely back heavy so it is important to keep up to date with assignments and manage your time properly. Tip: make sure to take notes during class (especially things Professor says 2x) and make sure to include in papers.

Prof. Odom is an engaging lecturer that prioritizes how useful the class is for students. We had "reading days" to work on our group project or written assignments, which were helpful in balancing this class with other responsibilities. Working with real clients is also a great experience! Grading is tough at first, but gets better.

Professor Odom was always available outside of class to meet and provide any support needed for the client project. He is very passionate about the class and has a lot of previous knowledge from his experiences. I felt like I learned a lot because of his teaching style and his deep experience in the field. His lectures are worth coming to class.

Amazing Professor! Professor Odom is a great lecturer and makes each class not only educational but also very fun to listen to and participate in. There are a few papers in this course, but he gives plenty of time to prepare, I would advise starting each paper a week in advance though so you're not rushing at the end.
Would not recommend this class. Gives no instructions when you meet him one on one to ask what he expects on the paper says just follow rubric. All the other comments about him are completely true
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I met in NEU. His feedback to your papers totally useless (use same comments to students have the same grade). It's great that you can engage with real-world clients. However, it has nothing to do with the professor. Without the knowledge you learned from the course, you can still perform well in client project. No curve.
Opportunity to work directly with organizations as consultants!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't get why people claim he's a bad professor. The class offers a lot to apply to real world, the podcasts really get you thinking about how you choose your career, both as a consultant and otherwise. I feel like if you really pay attention to what he says and the things assigned, you learn a lot more and find this class is absolutely great.

Curtis is a disrespectful professor that acts like he cares about his students but won't even take the time to meet and discuss grading issues. Very unclear with his grading and is unreasonable when you challenge his feedback. Overall, one of my worst class experiences, and I regret taking this class. This class makes me not want to do consulting.

He really cares about the course and is able to bring relevant real world experience to his lectures. The grade is heavily weighted in a few large assignments (a paper and the final exam being worth 60% of the grade). He is in interesting and engaging lecturer, but the grading criteria isn't always clear. Pretty easy B but definitely not an easy A.

Professor Odom is a smart, professional professor who also runs/works for a consulting firm in Boston. For that reason, I highly recommend taking Consulting in Orgs with him. You get real experience with real clients and he is super helpful throughout the entire semester. Its not an easy class, but its one of the best ive taken here
Talked a lot how amazing his course is but grading is so confusingly unreasonable. Not an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AMAZING - super nice guy who knows how to teach. He also has some amazing work experience that he shares, infused with Ted talks, which makes the classes overall interesting. No need to read the textbook - tests are an in class paper on a case study which is kindly graded. Super inspirational too!

One of my favorite classes and professors at NU and even better guy. Decent work load, but topics are interesting. He will change it up if the class is feeling stressed. 5 stars all the way. You have to take him at some point, very interesting, gets to use his real life experience in lecture

Horrible, unprepared lectures, and so obsessed with in-person attendance (huge irl lecture). Developed traps to trick students about attendance (is it really that deep..) very sassy as well...10% off your grade for every absence, but attendance is also worth 10% of your grade overall ARTG 2262

Derek is really good at balancing lectures with hands-on classwork. He's not a tough grader so putting effort into your work will always yield good results. He has a lot of experience in game design so he gives very thorough feedback for projects and is really good to talk through ideas with. Overall I recommend you take a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class bc it was a requirement so it wasn't all that interesting for me. Derek is a good prof and definitely willing to help out. relatively easy grader if you just show some effort and do the assignments. I found the class a bit boring but it honestly just wasn't my thing. not his fault though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This Professor made me fall in love with game design. He was clear and if you didn't understand you could submit the wrong thing and he will let you redo it for no credit off. You either get a 100% or a 0% you just have to do the homework to get an A. It was really fun too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He taught way to slow and focused on material that was not important to tests. He never posted grades on Canvas so you never knew what your grade was. Everything he went over on review days were on the test, so that was great.

Took Stats online with Professor Curry and he was super helpful. He provides slides and his syllabus is pretty clear. Textbook/problem sets were all accessible online through Cengage and the layout was very easy to navigate. He's lenient with due dates if he knows you're actually trying.
He makes calculas fun and easy. I really enjoy his teaching methods.  He is very helpful and convenient.

The sweetest professor ever! He breaks down material very well, tests are pretty fair just make sure you study the slides he provides on the study guide! Class is graded on 3 tests, simulation game, and some homework assignments which are straight-forward.
Great professor truly cares about each one of his students

The sweetest professor ever and really cares about his students. He shows funny videos at the beginning of each class and is always willing to offer extra help. There was little homework and grades were based on a few assignments and tests. Tests are pretty much all memorization and a bit of math. He's the best I def recommend!!
Literally the sweetest prof. Barely any HW, three exams that make up most of your grade. Going to class is good because some info is only mentioned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I ended up dropping this class bc I'm awful at supply chain but this man is amazing. He's the sweetest and most wholesome prof I've had at NEU. He genuinely, truly cares about his students and is always encouraging. If you like supply chain, pls take his class.

Sweetest man ever. You definitely have to go to class to do well on the exams since he verbally relays a lot of info that is not on the slides. He also definitely will like you a lot more if you attend because my grade fully got bumped up from a B+ to an A-.

Professor is a really caring guy and treats all of his students like his kids. the class is determined on three tests which is just memorizing the slides presented in class. barely any homework and its not weighted anything, definitely recommend this prof. he plays a cat video before every class its so cute
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: your grade in this class is based off of 3 tests, so don't mess one up (like I did). Other than that, it is not work heavy at all, just be sure to study hard when assessed.
Absolutely best professor! Easy, caring, flexible on deadlines. Sweetest man!

Tests are pretty much all rote memorization but pretty easy to study for since he provides the specific slides. He allows unlimited attempts on the simulation modules and there are a few extra credit opportunities. Lectures are kinda dry. It's an easy class + nice professor but I didn't learn much of anything.

Great prof OAT. Gives extra credit, only has tests + HW. Extremely kind and understanding if you talk to him outside of class he will happily help. His tests require lots of memorization but he gives you the slides to study.

Super caring, but if you're not good at memorizing I wouldn't take his class. However, he gives you unlimited attempts on the stimulation, has his own videos to help with excel problems and has review videos to follow for test days. Highly recommend going to review sessions. I feel a lot more confident with excel after taking his class.

He is the sweetest professor who wants to see everyone do well. Hes so flexible and very understanding. Tests are based on slides he provides which you have to memorize the tests are all about memorization. Homework on connect was annoying and the 4 assignments he gives are so easy on excel. Textbook was not needed. Really sweet guy I recommend

Professor Eroglu is one of the most caring, kindhearted professors I've had at Northeastern. He teaches in a lecture format and explains everything very clearly with good examples. He gives humane breaks for my 3-hour class period, during which he usually plays funny cat videos. His class was very interesting and he will be missed next semester!

Such a wholesome professor. Started off each lecture with a cat video, and was an extremely fair grader. The only issue I have with him is he was useless in office hours when I went to review my exams he didnt really explain what I was struggling with and told me to look at his slides at home. But class time with him was good.

Such a sweet man! Provided daily cat videos, super flexible on deadlines & will work with you to make anything better for you and your schedule. I would 100% take him again. The assignments are designed to help you learn excel & the sims are hard but after enough attempts you can def get them! overall love him!
The absolute sweetest man. So helpful and genuinely wants you to succeed. Would 100% take him again.
So easy to follow along. He explains absolutely everything. Very flexible with deadlines!
He is the best professer
Not too much work, but the Connect assignments are time consuming. Detailed lectures, but spends too much time explaining one concept. There are 2 midterms and 1 exam, which were all 30 minutes long.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most caring/nicest professor at NEU and genuinely wants the best for everyone. The test are very multiple choice heavy, which is not my thing but I was able to do alright by just making flashcards of the slides he told us to study. Very accessible outside of class and would recommend going to his office hours before exams. Would def recommend

I took this class only to fulfill my business course requirements but was blown away with the Professor's way of teaching and caring for his students! I highly recommend to take him in all possible supply chain-related classes. Professor Eroglu wants you to succeed so if you put enough effort and seek help you will have a good grade!

Cuneyt Eroglu is a very kind and helpful professor. He genuinely wants students to get a high grade. The course is by itself very heavy on memorizing definitions and concepts. Be aware you will have to memorize and know lots fo concepts. Final exam was not cumulative. I would recommend taking the Supply chain with him!

Cuneyt is one of the kindest, most caring professor I've ever met. He uploads all the slides and lets you know exactly what slides are going to be on the exam. His lectures can be a bit boring and it's not the easiest class at Northeastern, but I've never met a professor who cares more about his students than Cuneyt. Take his class, it's worth it!!
Cuneyt is a great professor! goes over relevant material on exams and the course material itself isnt too hard either so I definitely had an enjoyable experience in supply chain.

Follows the syllabus given. Teaches very well. Very kind and helpful to students. Always accessible and gives feedback. Brings in distinguished speakers from the industry to interact with. Lightens up the mood by playing a silly youtube video. Emphasizes on real-trend, practical metrics happening in supply chain industries. Tools: SAS, Excel

The BEST nicest professor out there he is so cute he always plays little youtube videos at the start of class and is an all around nice guy! the class itself was pretty hard but he is very helpful and understanding. best professor at neu.
He is the nicest prof in the class. He will help you if you need.

Professor Eroglu is the sweetest guy I've ever been taught by. By far the easiest SCHM class at NEU. No need to come to class, just memorize the powerpoint slides he gives you and you'll ace the exams. 4 easy assignments, 5 easy simulations and 3 exams (final not cumulative). 10/10 recommend!

I took him for transportation. But the reason you do well or not isn't because of attendance or how much you actually learn about supply chain its because the test's are more like random trivia then what he actually tells you is on the test or is covered in the pointless classes. I've gotten A's in all other supply chain classes but his.

Nicest Prof in Northeastern, absolutely recommended. Make sure to study the slides  well and you'll be more than fine for the exams. NO: group projects, mandatory attendance, or participation! A few out-class assign and game simulation. Also, buying the book is a waste of money.

Extremely helpful and nice guy always started class off with a youtube video to brighten up an 8am class.  Really is accommodating when it comes to making up a test would really recommend him as a professor.

I love this professor! He is hilarious and charismatic, and truly helps students if they don't want help. He's not a very hard teacher either. I would definitely recommend him if you love the topic. SCHM is naturally boring, but he really made it so much more interesting.
One of the best professors! So passionate and makes the topic exciting (for supply chain management). Recommended!

Prof Eroglu is passionate about the subject and has a great deal of experience. He is also committed to his students and truly wants everyone to succeed. If you are struggling, he will help you. This class is NOT boring! It is designed to teach the fundamentals of the subject and it does just that. Prof. Eroglu makes it very fun & interactive!
Seriously THE nicest guy ever. So understanding and passionate about his teaching. Would definitely reccommend him!
Nice guy, easy grader.  Two homework assignments and three exams.  Exams composed of about 50 mc and a few short answers. Class is mostly taught by powerpoint and through videos.

Funny professor, tries to make a boring class interesting. He has the worst grades distribution, 40% on MT & 60% on the final, THAT'S IT!! He gives some extra credit points for classes with low attendance.
Very easy class. Very nice guy. Relies heavily on power points for in-class lectures. Attendance is not mandatory. If you study the slides closely before each exam, you will do fine.
Talks about a lot of things but the course. Appears to be nice but grades poorly. Gives poor advices that leads to bad grades. Shows a funny video before every class. Very boring otherwise.

Supply Chain Mgmt/ Logistics. Knows A LOT and talks A LOT about what he knows. Fair enough. The class is fun if you participate otherwise it's a lot of listening. Easy class but pay attention when it comes to Excel. Ask exactly what he expects and this will be a successful class for you.

Hes an easy teacher, a "nice guy", but classes are boring. He relies way too much on powerpoint (google death by powerpoint) He should include less stuff in his powerpoints and try to use the chalkboard more. Other than that, hes really easy.

Easy class - great teacher! He knows that operations is an easy class and he sets up the course in that way. Quizzes are easy, final is a mash of all quizzes, but be careuful on the assignment (tricky). Gives 100% on participation. If you want to get an A,definitely take him!

Great professor and amazing lecturer. She made class very enjoyable and if you study for the tests and follow the guides everything is made easy, even the final paper and exam were ridiculously easy. Makes you want to participate more in class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Cury is the person who solidified my decision to switch from a pscyh major to international affairs. She's incredibly helpful in office hours, especially nearing exams. She loves participation, so try and speak up in class! Although there is a lot of reading for this class, she breaks it down in powerpoints. Her accent is awesome too.

Professor Cury is an excellent professor. Her enthusiasm for international affairs could not be more evident when she lectures.  Her exams aren't too bad, just study and you'll be fine. She also really encourages classroom discussion so come to class ready to participate and do the readings!!  She assigns reading quizzes throughout the semester.

This was an online course for me, and I still can say she is horrible. She is VERY rude, petty, not willing to help struggling students. Her grading has no rubric and seems like she hands out grades based on how she's feeling. Does not keep her politics out of class. Made us buy a textbook, yet never uses it. Also says "so forth and so on"- What?

I really enjoyed the class. There are quizzes every week based on the lecture from the week before but don't worry, as long as you paid attention, the quizzes are easy. She gives the midterm and final but if you paid attention, attended, class, and took notes you'll do fine. She does give several extra credit opportunities over the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I am an A student. Rarely have I had issues with professors. However, this class and teacher had me pulling out my hair. First of all her grading system as it's setup is confusing and leaves no room for error. I would expect a teacher to sympathize with her students, rather she is apethetic. She is very petty.

Veronica was definitely interested in her students and the subject matter (Comparative Politics). She was well prepared for all classes and clearly put time into her lessons. The only drawback of her class would be her grading. Exam style needs some revision and she doesn't provide much help with preparation for the exams (no study guides!)

Veronica is very smart and knowledgable but she expects a lot out of her students, sometimes a little too much. She is great to deal with one on one however, so highly suggest going to her office hours. Take notes during class because she gives no study guide and does not make ppts available. She is a great person, tough grader. Overall she is good

Research Methods:Terrible course. It should be understood that this course is rather dry and can feel a bit redundant. She did not help with this. Extremely rude and condescending. She could not have cared less about our concerns. She instead would use class time to recruit for her dialogue and occasionally redefine terms she had previously defined
She is a hard grader, sarcastic and condescending TA. She laughs at every bad joke Prof. Urman says in class. Yelled at a student because he was using his phone.
I really liked Veronica! She was really funny and relatable, and was very well-informed. I enjoyed having her as my TA.
Definitely very nice and very helpful!  She made things much clearer, and was always willing to talk and explain topics.

TA/Recitation for Comp Politics. Very nice & helpful w/ papers. Opinionated, but entertaining and open-minded. Helped clarify lectures & gave additional information through article readings. Gives little handouts at the end of recitation w/a bunch of random info - so funny! I fully recommend her!
Very petty, she will take points off of your average for any silly reason.  She will never admit that she is wrong even if she directly contradicts the book.

He is very enthusiastic about math. He explains content very well and also gives visual explanations of concepts. His exams are very similar to the practice problems he gives, so it's easy to get a good grade. Attendance is mandatory but his lectures are very good and helpful.

I can definitely understand the bad reviews he gets, but for me personally he was a great professor. It was funny asf when he yells at people when they're on their phones during class or when he gets passionate about the material, but otherwise his grading structure of 4 tests + the final was really good as someone who's strong with tests.

Professor Lang is definitely enthusiastic about math but I feel that most would say his teaching style was not effective. He doesn't come across as approachable and often complains about students in class. He spends way to much time on proofs and things you don't need to know, but if you understand the practice exams you'll be fine.

He shouts at us like we're misbehaving children, and very frequently complains about students in general mid-lecture. He yells at us for answering, not answering, or asking questions. He will scoff if someone enters late or leaves on time (if he goes over time). He shouts about anything and everything, like he's trying to teach through a hurricane.

Professor Lang really cares about math, and is very enthusiastic in his pedagogy. However, this tends to come across as him being quite loud and dry, drilling in basic concepts for an excessive amount of time.

I would not recommend this professor at all for MATH 1215. I did not learn anything from his lectures, and he overcomplicated everything, I had to get a tutor who was my saving grace this semester. He answers questions very condescendingly in class. The only good thing is that the quiz reviews typically match the quiz format.

Prof. Lang is a pretty good teacher and is ready to teach. Attendance is mandatory. If you're a bad test taker, I wouldn't recommend this class, because 88% of your grade is composed of the finals and tests, the rest being attendance. He teaches super quick, so missing just one lecture will leave you behind.

He has a loud voice and yells a lot!

He's always dripped out with his suit and tie and also loves proofs (that you do not need to know, but proofs are important, so go to class and watch him ramble). Get ready for mental math because no calculator is allowed. Pay attention when he does examples and you'll do fine.

Professor Lang is crazy to the point where you'll either really excel or fail with him as a professor. His boisterous personality makes it extremely challenging for classes to be productive. Asking him to explain an idea will always either end in further confusion, or him berating the person who asked, or both.

reviews.comment: Do not take this course if you are looking for a considerate professor. Lang will belittle anyone who asks questions and is completely condescending in emails. This is an easy course, with practice tests modeling actual midterms. He just isn't kind!

David Lang is the worst professor I have ever had. He is condescending and rude, berating students for asking questions. His policies/grade weighting make it difficult to do well in his class. I highly recommend you find another professor if you are not extremely gifted in math and can follow along with convoluted explanations of complex topics.
Will race through lectures, but his tests are very similar to the practice ones he posts. Might get upset about a dumb question, but is very willing to help at office office hours.

reviews.comment: His tests are pretty fair. He will yell at you if you ask him a ‘stupid' question. Someone literally asked him what the test was on and he yelled at them for not listening during class. Also, trigger warning, he randomly emphasizes words throughout his sentences (low key keeps me awake). Other than that, he scares me a little.
The best teacher I ever met.
He's the best teacher who taught calculus, he's extremely knowledgeable and care about his stundets.

Professor Lang is overly passionate about math to the point where he refuses to slow down and explain concepts to people who are struggling. In fact he has no issues yelling at and berating you for simply asking for clarification on often time confusing topics. Save yourself ghe headache and never take any of his classes.

Professor Lang is very passionate about the content that he teaches, and because of that, he tends to overcomplicate the course material, leaving many students confused. He moves at a very fast pace. If you ask questions, he will berate you. If you understand the examples he covers in the lecture, you will do well on the exams. There are no tricks.

Professor Lang is great. His quizzes are just like what he goes over in class. He moves pretty quickly and what he covers in class isn't exactly like what's in the textbook or on the exam. He's hilarious without meaning to be.

Overall a great professor, you may need to spend more time after class on this course. The only issue is that the concepts taught in class were not so sufficient for the final exam and it made me feel a bit worried.

Prof Lang's lecturing style is clear and fast-paced. He tends to scream with excitement and loves to talk about how important math is. I think if he just lectured and gave homework the course would be great. Sadly, the tests were insanely difficult and graded harshly. He won't be everybody's favorite prof, but you will probably learn a lot!

Prof. Lang's lectures are unhelpful and he will yell or talk down to you if you ask questions. I spent his lectures frantically copying down his notes, not absorbing the information. His communication style is ineffective and if you dare to ask a question, he will not reframe the idea but will reiterate what he said. Worst professor I've had.

Prof. Lang was very passionate about his studies in math theory and this was evident in his lectures. While I hated taking Math Reasoning, as a professor, Lang had multiple office hours and was always eager to explain math to anyone. I wouldn't take him again because he's very intense but that isn't necessarily a bad thing for everybody.

Prof. Lang is amazing. Although he sometimes gets a little too passionate about his work, he always explains everything clearly and gives plenty of examples to help him understand the material. Tests are always straight to the point and if you do the homework and review problems, you will do amazing. Great professor overall.

Lectures are very fast and you're given very little time to actually understand what he is saying. He is very passionate about math but it isn't easy to keep up with his pace. Also, the screen he uses for lectures tends to be blurry more times than not.
L professor
don't take it if you don't have to, he makes class difficult because he gets to passionate and doesn't really answer questions well.

Everything you need to know you will learn in lectures so go to class. In class examples are similar to his test questions so just know how to do the in class examples. Grade is based off of 6 tests and a final that's worth 40% of your grade so if you don't test well good luck. He likes to teach and you can tell and is willing to answer questions.

reviews.comment: Prof Lang is extremely passionate about his job. He will not dumb down any concepts for you, and will rather tend to berate you for not understanding. He gets extremely passionate and loud during online lectures, which makes it difficult to focus on the content being taught.

Lang is an awesome teacher. Had him for calc two, the class was 4 tests and a final. Its kind of scary since each test is 15% of your grade and the final is worth 40. But honestly, his practice exams are just like the real test, and the examples he does in class are also extremely useful and similar. Crazy enthusiastic and loves math.

Professor Lang is very passionate about math and wants to share it with his students. His lectures are fast paced an in-depth, but he gives the opportunity to ask questions. He gives plenty of optional hw. His test review sheets are almost identical to exams. He is a fair professor - did horrible on my first exam, but Lang did everything to help.

reviews.comment: Lang is the best professor I have had at Northeastern so far. He prepares students very well for midterms and provides separate canvas PDF homework problems that are very helpful. I would highly recommend Lang to anyone.

reviews.comment: This guy lives and breaths math. I don't know if you'll find a professor more into his material than Professor Lang. Definitely recommend him for Diff. Eq

He preaches as he teaches. Really helpful outside of class, will give extra problems for you to do if you need some extra help. Quizzes every week like other calculus classes but the questions are related to the homework. Prof Lang keeps it straight forward, but don't expect the tests to be easy though! GREAT PROFESSOR!

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the more interesting calc 2 teachers. You can tell he wants everyone to succeed and provides all the means to do so. He can get a little lost in his own explanations and derivations, but there's always a joke in there.

reviews.comment: Lang prepares you well for assessments and wants you to do well. He's eccentric, but once you get past it, he's a good professor. Explains things thoroughly. The final comes out of nowhere, but it's doable.

David Lang was by far the best maths teacher I have had. After struggling in maths through high school, I grew a disliking towards maths. However, after the first few weeks with Prof. Lang, I have significantly improved and regained my liking for math. He is very clear and precise with the work and quiz/test schedule.

On the first day of class, I have to admit, I was a little intimidated. But David is a great professor. He knows really his stuff. If you pay attention in class and do a little bit of homework, it shouldn't be very difficult to get an A. He's also a nice guy, and will occasionally crack a calculus joke here an there. He loves math.

I had him for clac 1 and he was a good very clear professor. He goes fast in the lectures so if you have no calc experience the class will probably be hard but if you have some then it will be easy. The quiz's are really easy and he gives one every week and he drops the lowest two. If you have a question in class he'll answer it.

Great professor. Loves math but is not a people person (although he is willing and available to help). He talks really quickly and the class is fast-paced. You should have a background in calc and be decent in basic algebra. Would definitely take again for a math course.

He never collects homework, which is a huge benefit, but it is fairly necessary to really understand what's going on.  He can be hard to take seriously because of his ill-fitting suits and very thick accent.  A solid background in calculus is also really important.
Good

Excellent guy. Knows his stuff. Just make sure you take notes and do the homework.

Great professor for Differential Equations. Very clear, very knowledgeable. I've never seen anyone so passionate about math.  Hands out review sheets before each quiz.  I never felt under prepared for the tests.  Highly recommend.

Massey's lectures were incredibly effective. He is funny and laidback, which removes any stress a student may feel. He might be intimidating but is helpful when approached. Quizzes, homework, and tests are normal.

Sure he wrote the textbook, quizzes are homework questions. His classes don't feel like a welcoming enviroment. reviews.comment: Was terrified at first to be taking Calc 3 with the guy who wrote the textbook but that makes him THE BEST professor. His book is wordy but his class is super clear. Quizzes each week are taken directly from homework problems so if you put in the work you are golden. However homework is not mandatory!

Weekly quizzes are straight out of the textbook (which he wrote btw), classes are organized, he writes out clearly on the board what you need to know. He's extremely sarcastic and likes to poke fun at people, however, it's never personal, just who he is as a person. Very lenient grader and makes calc 3 easy to understand.

Amazing Professor. Course is well organized. Professor is funny and teach diffcult concepts clearly. Even though HW are not mandatory but they are helpful for quizzes. Three exams make up most grades, but there are tons of pratice exam to prepare with.

Professor Massey was very organized and clear with his lectures. He made it easy for me to understand complex topics. He's sarcastic and funny. I knew what to expect with the two tests and final, and he had a lot of materials posted for review.

We get it, you are smart. He is not a good professor. I like being organized and his lectures were all over the place. He is a smart guy but he was very condescending all class, no one would answer his questions because he was straight up rude to people when they got it wrong.

He can be a little intimidating at first, but he is an incredible professor who is hilarious and really sets his students up for success. His lectures are easy to follow, and he explains every concept clearly along with many examples. Quizzes are on problems directly from the homework, so do your homework!!

Go to the lectures and you will learn everything you need to know. Quiz problems are taken DIRECTLY from homework problems and he will tell you which pool of problems could be on a quiz. He might seem arrogant and condescending at first, but hes just joking, go to his office hours and talk to him and you will see, hes chill. Dont let him scare you.

The best possible math professor you can get. Makes calc 3 seem like second grade addition by explaining each section with such simplicity. If you want to understand calc 3 while getting an A, take Massey. Great dude, very down to earth and has great humor. Always at office hours with his TA Jason, who is also very helpful.

Professor Massey is an amazing lecturer who also wrote the textbook. He explains concepts really well, provides clear examples and is happy to clarify misunderstandings or go over questions you have. His homework and exams are also very straightforward, and he really cares about students doing well. His sarcastic sense of humor is a bonus!

Massey is the goat. He wrote the textbook you use for class so he is super knowledgeable on the subject. Everything is concise and to the point, homework is optional but pivotal to doing well. His quizzes are an easy 100 if you do the HW and his midterms are very reasonable. Make him your top priority for courses.

The only reason I gave Prof. Massey a 4 and not a 5 is that he can be arrogant which can make him feel unapproachable & can dissuade students from asking questions but if you can get over that he is an amazing professor. Breaks down hard material well & cares about his students doing well. Also, his funny comments can make dense calc lecture lively

Massey is great. Like others have said: great teacher, but condescending dude. He is really great at teaching material, but he can be snarky and arrogant. He is a tough and annoying grader, but overall he is a great prof. Take if you can.

Massey is a great professor, but definitely also a hard grader on tests and quizzes. Like other people have said, he is sometimes condescending, especially when asking questions. Best Lecturer I've had even outside of Math. You'd be a fool to miss this one.
very good

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgeable about Calc3. Wrote the textbook you use during the course. Consistently challenges his students to go further. I took the same class in highschool but with pretty poor instruction and the difference is night and day, this time I really learned the material.

He is a great guy, overtly sarcastic, but he knows his stuff (he wrote the textbook). At a deep level, he cares about math and teaching, but his ways are a bit condescending. However, he makes the math class bearable and, to an extent, fun. His quizzes are just hw problems, and the tests are a bit hard.
Great guy, sarcastic, knows his stuff for sure.

He is so arrogant and makes his students seem inferior. His textbook is literally his lectures in text format. Watching his videos only helps to a certain extent. Try using tutoring cause his office hours only helps a bit. If you want a challenge take his class.

strict grader, decent lecturer, horrible person. He can lecture on and on but he's a worse teacher than the ones from high school. He's a very strict grader but that's not his worst quality. Acts like everyone should just know what he knows within a second of him explaining an entirely new concept. In any case, keep away from this guy.

He is a condescending jerk and is on a power trip because he wrote the textbook for the course and went to duke. They are convoluted and worthless, pick up another book. He is not helpful at office hours and tries to act like a bro when you really just want a teacher. He caters to kids who already had calculus. Take intensive if never had calc b4
I've never met a more knowledgable math teacher. The man is a freaking calculator, he wrote the textbook that you use in class. Extremely committed to helping his students understand the material.
Had Dave for Differential Equations, and he was by far the best math professor I have ever had.  Great communicator, clear instructor, and very helpful and professional both in class and one on one.
He makes you feel inferior and expects you to know a lot. He knows 1/2 the kids in calc 1 had calc, but 1/2 did not at the same time... he does not take this into account.

Excellent teacher.  Fair grader and tends to give high grades.  Weekly quizzes are really easy, but the exams can be tricky.  It is important to learn the concepts, not specific examples.  He can come across as cocky, but he is a good guy over all and pretty funny too.

Little bit sarcastic at times but a great professor. He teaches the material really well and is a very fair grader. At the end of the course he goes through and individually adjust the grades so you can get a boost if you go to class and he knows who you are.

Expects you to truly understand the material and be able to apply it to anything, quizzes are wicked easy but tests not so much. Walked out of all three tests thinking I did REALLY well and got 56 (mid), 74(mid), and 87 (final). Intimidates you when you ask questions sometimes.
He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is not an easy grader, but knows the material very well and knows how to teach it. Take with him.

I did not do so well in this course, but really has nothing to do with the professor.  He can come off as extremely arrogant, but go to his office hours and he'll help ya out.  Funny guy, some might find it too sarcastic.  He has easy quizzes (picks exactly from a set of homework problems), labs are not as easy (but only worth 4% overall).

Extremely good professor.  One of the few that can actually teach math within the department.  Is a little arrogant, but will be enjoyable if you are not easily offended.  If you can get him, take his course... you will not regret it.

I found this professor to be very arrogant and not as helpful as other comments would suggest. He at times can interject sarcasm and a bully-ness when asking him questions in class which makes it awkward and makes him less engaging. I didn't doubt he was a smart professor, I'll give him that, but he knew it and was cocky about it.

Multivariable Calculus isn't an easy course.  Massey will do a VERY good job of conveying the material clearly.  His humor is like no other professor I have ever had.  To the class, he may appear extremely arrogant, but if you go to his office hours, you'll find he really wants to help. Quizzes are based on homework problems.  Exams are difficult.

One of the best teachers I have ever had, hands down. Just read the reviews. Even the people that can't stand him, just can't bring themselves to say hes a bad teacher...Because he may be the best that is out there. Smartest person I've ever met. I personally think he's a great guy ,too.

So far Massey's 343 was probably the best class I've taken. It's a hard class, but he is very clear in his teaching. Some apparently think he is cocky, but he's just not a robot. Who else writes LOL on a student's exam when they grade it? (And for the record it was tasteful, not degrading)
Overall, not a bad prof. However, he is very arrogant. He thinks he owns the world. It's especially been that way since he became a full professor.
very clear -- plenty of examples. easy to approach. funny as hell. willing to go the extra mile.

Massey is the man, but he knows it, which makes him laughably cocky in an endearing way. Ha. He is very clear when teaching, and easy to find outside of class.  Massey's 343 is an outstanding class. Highly recommended.

Best teacher ever. Period. Besides being extremely adept at teaching mathematics he is an awesome guy who actually tries to get to know some of his students. He is very helpful and his lectures are extremely clear. People say he is arrogant and he is. Doesn't change that he's a great guy. Also has a great sense of humor and is very intelligent.
best teacher ever. take his class if you want to pass and know the material.  Teaches like a mathematics god, and his clarity is unbeatable. take Massey if you know whats good for you
EXTREMELY arrogant, but knows it himself.  Knows the material extremely well, and gives good examples. As long as you can stand a LOT of sarcasm, he's the best...
Had him for all 3 calc classes several years ago when I was a frosh. He and I still maintain a good friendly relationship.  My favorite professor by far.

Ahh, massey, a mac zealot that you can't bring yourself to hate.  He makes sense, and that's something you can't say about lots of math professors.  Funny too.  He once told the class about this girl who walked up to him after a class and said she was majoring in math, but didn't quite understand what those "letter things" were.

This is a god among math teachers.  David Massey is gifted with a Feynman-like ability to explain anything so that you get it.  But take notes, because it's easy to think that just because he can make it look easy that it is.  Not so.

This guys is awesome. Very clear and very helpful. Keeps it humourous as well.  He will go the extra mile. He let me sit through a whole semester of calc 3 to refresh myself since i missed the final and had an incomplete.
What a great guy, though it's a little creepy that he has a 'kept' student all the time...

Massey is the best math teacher at NU.  He makes the class, which can be really tough, into something easy.  Very thorough, very helpful, and very personable.  I aced this one in a walk.  If you have the chance to take one of his classes, do it.  Also, go to his review sessions.  They're worth their weight.

I've taken several of Massey's classes,people aren't kidding with calling him the MOST helpful prof. always available and he's so cool about it. he's respectful of people but if you ask the lamest question in the world he will make fun of you,and everyone will laugh at you cuz you are lame. so don't be lame. seriously though, one of the top 3 profs

Massey is BY FAR the best professor at Northeastern. He truly cares about his students. Not only did I learn the most in this class out of any other classes I have taken, but I got an A with flying colors. Go to class, respect him, and he'll go to the end of the world to help you.TAKE MASSEY'S CLASS
By far one of the best math professor at this school.  As long as you show up to his class and pay attention you will get an A.
The material isnt that easy, but he is so clear and to the point.  This guy is a math genius AND he knows how to teach.  Definitely one of the best professors I have ever had

he is by far the best math teacher at NU.HE ACTUALLY KNOWS HOW TO TEACH.his gives good notes,do the hw and u will do fine on the quizzes & tests.hes always willing 2 help if u need it and very flexible.jokes around with u,has fun in class,ive had him twice and would take his class again in a second.

He may seem cocky and arogant but thats because he is. BUT he is definitely one of the best math professors at NU...very clear and helpful, he is the type of professor who can provide a challenge and in the end help you learn a lot more..
A great calc teacher.  I hate math, but I enjoyed his class.
Massey is really good. He knows everything and will answer your questin but will give you serious attitude. Web cam on website, foxy!
seems haughty and stuck up but by far one of the most thorough and clear teachers i've seen at northeastern...if you come to class and pay attention, you should have no problems.
Presents topics ideas and material clearly. Is more than willing to help outside of class. Good sense of humor. Even helped me with math classes that I wasn't taking with him.

The best teacher I've ever had.  Great personality and wicked smart.  Tests and exams are only as hard as the material is.  Goes over tons of problems in class. He can teach a blind dog to see.  I arranged my schedule around this guy and you should too.

By far one of the best teachers I have had, in math or out. Great sense of humor, plenty of patience, and he treats you as an equal and with respect. Willing to help however, he stands out as one of the good teachers here. Better than my others this year.
good teacher but made the third midterm and the final way to hard...but he is still the best math teacher i have had at this schoo though

Great professor, but goes a little overboard going over homework and examples in too much detail, causeing classes to be extremely slow. No point in doing homework because he spends half of every class going over it anyways.

I've taken all sorts of maths my entire life, even got a 700 something on my SAT and this man is the best math teacher I've ever had. Expect a very very fast paced class and hard tricky quizzes though.
Really a great guy. Lives near campus (Gainsboro Street). Funny and really teaches well. Anyone who suffers in this class doesn't deserve to be in college.
Terrific teacher, fun guy.  Very intelligent and clear speaker.  He makes jokes about problems and keeps things moving at a fast pace.  If you don't have him, you're missing out.

this class is agonizing. class is boring if it isn't confusing. He introduces topics by giving layered problems and expects you to already know the material. I have already taken the class before and I still get confused when he introduces a new topic. He might be the most condescending teacher he creates a culture where questions are bad.

if you've never taken calc before, RUN. he basically just takes notes on the book and then just writes them on the board with little to no explanation/teaching. if you go to office hours and display an ounce too much of misunderstanding he quickly gets condescending. just a bad teacher overall, your better off switching

How tf does he still have a job. In class he just copies worksheets onto the whiteboard and expects you to make sense of it- gives NO explanations . Its better to show up for the weekly quizzes than for class. This guy faces the board the whole time, copying things from the textbook. He doesn't make sure we're following and skip steps. reviews.comment: The class is much harder than I expected, but it was quite rewarding. I love space and everything astronomy so doing the work didn't feel like a chore. reviews.comment: skibidi toilet

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy, but rarely ever spends time to actually make sure we understand what's going on in class. doesnt speak to students, only gives quizzes with few questions, extremely boring, does not care.

Great professor who likes physics. Very funny and has good conversations. Lectures heavily and don't skip class because he gives pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Hudon is clearly very enthusiastic about his subject. However, that does not translate in teaching or how he treats students. He was not very understanding or caring when it came to any of the students in class and had the tendency to be sort of mean.

Professor Hudon is very inaccessible, does not answer emails, and overall is not a good teacher. He does not explain the topics and with a midterm average of 68%, refused to curve or scale it even though a majority of the class had not been able to complete the exam. Also does not explain topics or WEAR HIS MASK IN CLASS!!

This professor is pretty bad at actually teaching concepts. He usually briefly explains the material and then does a few examples that he does not explain well. It's hard to follow along what he teaches in class, but he always offers extra help outside of class. Some homework is graded and there are weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very very poor instructor. All he does is write problems on the board, solve them, and say does everyone agree? He also takes off full credit on exams even if you show work, and a small mistake will cost 8/10 points. Learned nothing from his mandatory lectures. Got through the class via textbook and online videos. Never take him if you can.

Lectures can be a bit boring at times but he is a really nice man who does plenty of example problems to make sure you know how to apply a certain concept. Homework isn't graded and as long as you understand the material presented in lecture you don't really need to do it.

In class lectures covered no content and were honestly kind of fun if you didn't think about how much you were paying for a 0 content class. She didn't really cover content & treated class time like a joke but you have way more essays/in class presentations than other ORG B sections and her grading on that extra work is harsh and not transparent.

She asks students to do a lot of stuff  but seldom provides any feedback of value. Unfortunately I did not learn one single thing from her. Often times, you can clearly tell she has no ideas what she is talking about...

Terrible class. Definitely different than any other section of it because she prides herself on her "innovative ideas." The class is basically funraising 101. You have to form a class organization, develop a hierarchy, and do a bunch of fundraisers. Papers are lengthy, attendence is mandatory..it's just too much for HRM 201. Don't take it with her!
