We eve get a wacky wednesday last class he brought in his action figure collection,I tried on his light up batman mask. Luh this guy fr

He thinks it's okay to give a student a 89.9876 on an exam and not round. He gave one student in the class a 6.99 for participation. He is on a high horse, and you don't learn a thing, saying you'll probably fail.

I wish I read RMP earlier. The entire class is just memorizing jargon. I'm convinced that he designed the introductory MIS course to steer students away from the department. Good for him, because I'm never taking such a course again, especially when he's teaching. Avoid at all costs.

Just back to remind everyone that he designed MISM 2301. Yes, all the 10 odd sections who take this class every semester learn the same outdated jargon filled stuff because he does not care to change anything about it. He needs to go.
Honestly, he shouldnt be that bad for you, if you actually put in some work.

I hope he stops teaching. Spending a third of each class “revising” the previous class while skipping slides in the current class is ridiculous. Easy material made unnecessarily hard. Pointless jargon, outdated class materials… I could go on. Avoid this class at all costs.

I have no words. I have learned nothing from this course, and I got an A with 95% attendance. I found out today that his professor is responsible for the course being designed in this manner. Hundreds of students learn nothing in this class every semester due to him. I hope NEU changes something because this should not fly with the amount we pay.

Pros: Excel, Figma, group work doesn't trash your grade, professor Dias is lively and has (dry) humor, theme Thursdays are fun, provides feedback even for hw, literally tells you "this will be good for your notes..."
Cons: 1> hw due per week, required textbook ($$), some topics felt less necessary than others, lectures can get boring, grading
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Frustrating course. Slides have little to no text. Prof spends 20 minutes talking about the previous lecture which can easily be avoided. Then he skims through the current lecture while going off on tangents at every turn. Case studies are graded pretty randomly. Exams are weird, and require you to spew out the same jargon he said in class.  Avoid!

I got a good grade in this class, but let me make this very clear - every lecture is boring. This professor cannot talk for 5 minutes without going on tangents, and it feels intentional because there is nothing worth talking. As others have mentioned, you may do well in the class depending on your notes, but you are guaranteed to learn nothing.
Enjoyed having Professor Dias this semester. The tests were online, open-book.  Assignments and tests weren't too difficult as they were all based on how well you could take notes.

If style over substance were a professor, you've got your guy. If you think positively of him, it's likely that you got a good grade. But if you care about learning, you can't help but be disgusted because you'll learn absolutely nothing that's useful. It blows my mind that this is a mandatory class for me. Makes me pity the MIS folks.

legit one of my favorite profs ever. the class is a lot of work but he does his best to really help students do well and feel comfortable with the class. tbh if you do badly it's kinda ur own fault cuz he has so many good resources and office hours are super helpful. as long as you do the reading and put effort into work you should be just fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is a weird class. The professor talks a lot, and yet when you leave the class you don't feel like you've learned anything. The class materials seem terribly outdated. It's a shame that he is the one who's in charge of this course at the university and is largely responsible for how bad this is. Busy work with no learning.

He's mostly fair, there are a lot of case studies, exams are a bit hard. He definitely cares about his students. I feel like there wasn't a lot of learning in the class, but there also is, it's a really weird class. MAKE SURE TO TAKE NOTES when he says "You might want to write this down." He is a good a person, but I didn't really like the class.

Subpar professor that teaches with enthusiasm, however is overly critical of work. Wastes 20 minutes every class engaging students and covering the previous classes material. The rest of class is spent covering slideshows that are visually incredibly difficult to understand.

I honestly don't even know what this course was about. I would participate in class but not even know what I was saying. I'm think he sometimes doesn't even know what he's saying either. He goes off on many tangents which don't help and won't ever answer a question directly. Really weird course and I'm still just as confused as I was at the start.

A submitted assignment that's complete & accurate won't get a 100; thorough case study submissions will get a 3.6 out of 4 unless they go above and beyond. Because of this and the fact that every point of the assignments count to a total of 100, I found it hard to get above a B+/A-. Still, he def cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

Professor Dias's class is definitely more difficult than other MISM courses but you will learn so much from him. The class is based on weekly case studies and he gives very detailed feedback on them. Class participation is weighed very heavily, participation every class is expected. Hard but definitely worth it, Professor Dias is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Extremely professional. sometimes felt like an etiquette-esque class. Focus on the main ideas, I found that its one thing then 4 little things and that was primarily it. Exams are online slightly difficult but are just how and why you would implement certain things. Case studies are short yet you have to be clean and extremely precise and detailed.

If you take MISM2301 with Martin Dias, you will need to put a lot of effort into this class to get a good grade. He grades your participation on each class session (which was intentionally kept secret as far as I could tell) so if you don't go to class you're kind of screwed. But if you put in the effort you realize he's a dope professor.

Professor Dias was great. As long as your participate and you put in effort into the case studies, you will do fine. I personally got an A- because I did not participate in class discussions as much as I should, so I could have gotten a higher score if I did.. MISM 2301 is a hard course, but Prof. Dias is the best one there is so take it as u will.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The only reason that people wouldn't get an A in mism is because they don't participate. Graded on case studies, at home quizzes, at home (REALLY HARD. but graded leniently) exams, and participation. Case studies were definitely time consuming (not hard to get a good grade if you read rubric). Sit in the front row and participate and you are fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: My favorite professor! He's passionate about teaching! His class can be daunting since it requires high engagement and performance, but he is really understanding. He has an uppity personality that some people may be taken aback by, but his being himself is part of what makes his teaching great. Assessments are 100% fair. Don't be disorganized.

as far as professors go for MISM, Dias is pretty good. He's a really nice guy who cares about students and is available outside of class. The assignments are pretty tough and exams are the hardest I've taken at NU. Still, I think he is one of the better professors for information systems and an overall good choice!
Amazing professor , bad course

Passionate about the course, but grades very harshly considering he skims over concepts for the test in class that are not even explained on the slides or the textboo. Emphasizes participation, but students are less inclined to participate because of his tangents and his extra obnoxious personality. If you want an A don't take this course

I think Dias is a great professor, but I hated the course. The course is just simple concepts stretched so thin like a trojan on a gourd. I don't know why this course is a must for CSBA students who take courses from both colleges. I really hope Dias gets to teach a higher-level course. He's passionate and knowledgeable and I think he'd be great.

Prof Dias is super enthusiastic about the course. The course itself is honestly pretty hard to understand if you aren't tech inclined and he made it as easy to understand as he could. If you constantly participate, really focus on textbook readings, and are able to keep up in lectures, you'll do well. Assigns 1-2 cases a week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dias is great, if you're willing to work hard. He is very clear about his expectations and expects you to bring 100% to everything you do. If you aren't willing to work hard or learn, don't take his class. He LOVES what he does and is always willing to meet outside of class to go more in depth. He can get carried away on tangents during lectures.

Smart guy, terrible teacher. He is knowledgeable about MIS but can’t get the concepts across to students in a meaningful manner. Its obvious from his feedback that he only glances over homework and grades them based on how many buzzwords you throw around. As other students have said he is incredibly condescending

All of the reviews here are entirely correct. Made the mistake of reading these reviews and still taking the course. Don't make the same mistake. The class makes no sense, and he throws around meaningless buzz words that he rarely ever takes time to explain. Sometimes it feels like he does not even know what he's saying.

MISM just makes no sense in general. Idk why they teach it, everyone I talked to says the same. Given that this course makes no sense, this guy goes out of his way to be a tough grader. To get an A- or an A, you have to tryhard every single class and schedule a meeting in the beginning of the semester on "how to get a superior grade" :/

Its not even the confusing instruction that bothers me (use technical word salad in assignments and your solid). Professor Dias is just an obnoxious dude, something I sensed from the first day of class. Ive observed on more than one occasion him embarrassing well-intentioned students for no good reason. Hands down the worst professor Ive had.

Prof. Dias is passionate about MISM2301. He assigns 2 cases studies a week along with take home quizzes that both rack up to be a large portion of your grade. 3 exams, first one is very difficult while the last 2 are very similar, but you get used to his "style." PARTICIPATE -- it will help you stay engaged in the class because it can get boring

Unless youre 100% focused the whole class you cant pass. His grading is horrible, even if you try so hard you can never get a full grade. The class is the hardest class that I ever took, my friends took the same class but different professor, and it was much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don'. Take. Him. I'm a CS kid and his class is harder than my cs classes. Easy concepts are twisted and forced into irrelevant case studies for the exam. He rounds grades to the 20th decimal place just to increase your anxiety. The slides barely cover the textbook. Atleast 2 quizzes and case studies are due every week. He makes it hard on purpose.

Professor Dias' lectures are very hard to understand. A lot of the information within the textbook and lectures isn't applicable to the case studies. He grades case studies strictly and tests (there are 3) more leniently. It's pretty hard to get an A in this class so if you're trying to protect your 4.0, you probably shouldn't take this professor.

Literal hardo for no reason. Dias thinks that his class is the center of the universe and assigns a ton of work, however his feedback sucks and his lectures are hard to understand. He also grades participation for each individual class, something he didn't make clear at the start. Worst prof I have ever had, stay away.

Dias is definitely passionate about MIS which really shines through his lectures, not many professors are as enthusiastic as him about a base level course. On the other hand, he is very unclear when giving feedback and is a very strict grader even about simple hw assignments. He also makes tests unnecessarily difficult and quizzes 1-2 times a week.

Person below me is the teacher's pet, go figure. Dias holds a high standard for his students and none for himself He waited until the last month to grade everything and is extremely condescending and unhelpful with all of his feedback. I can confidently say I didn't learn a thing in his class and was a total waste of time. Never again.

Dias is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable, I guarantee anyone who rated him poorly wasn't really paying attention. It is difficult to get an A, but if you have any remote interest in the topic and aren't just taking it for a grade-booster, I would definitely recommend. Amazing lectures and you NEED to go to class to understand the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Extremely clear lecturer, very passionate and a great guy. The class content is not the most interesting, but he definitely explains the topics clearly (you will learn!). Difficult to get an A, but very easy to get a B/B+ w/ minimal effort. Due to the amount of work due, grading was handed back fairly late. If you're a serious student, take him!

The topics are fairly straightforward, but he makes them much more confusing. He is very disorganized but has rigid structure for what you can/cannot say and do. He goes on lots of tangents and gets distracted easily. He is very unclear about his tests. No clarity into how he grades or assesses you. Has high expectations for you but not himself.

Professor Dias is very knowledgeable and clearly knows what he is talking about when it comes to MISM. With that said, his case studies can be difficult at times, but his tests are graded more leniently and are open note. Overall a really great guy who is amazing at teaching and connecting with his students. Not an easy A though so be ready to work
The most awful professor I have met. He does not lecture in a logical way and his presentation slides are nonsense. Plus you never know what grade you will receive.

Of the harder MIS teachers. Easy grader for tests. Hard grader for case studies. Participation and preparation matters a lot to him. The textbook is useless. His lectures are boring, but if you don't actively pay attention, the slides make no sense. Its hard to apply his lectures to case studies. This class was hard for no reason compared to others
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dias is super passionate about MIS but makes the class more difficult than it should be. Lectures are often hard to follow, exams are challenging and stressful but graded leniently, and case studies take a long time to do them right. If you're looking for an easy class, avoid Dias, but if you want to work hard he will teach you a lot!

This class was one of the biggest wastes of time and money I have ever experienced. This dude is really fired up about the class which is cool, but I learned absolutely nothing. The grading makes no sense, and he gives almost no feedback. He sets deadlines but can't keep any himself. Overall just a really bad class with a really mediocre prof.

One of the more difficult professors I've had. Definitely a smart man, and he's engaging. However, his grading is not straightforward and very ambiguous. Its very easy to get a B or B+ with adequate participation, but getting an A is very very hard (94+). Participation is HUGE and his slides are incomprehensible if you don't follow along in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Only take him if you're serious about the class. Absolutely phenomenal lecturer. Has extensive knowledge in his field, and committed to students' success. Class material needs careful work, participation is a huge deal, but everything positively compounds on each other if you work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: if you do not answer questions in class, your participation will be 4/10 even you come up every class. 10 minutes quiz before each session, 1 case study every week, 3 exams, no final.

Loved his classes! So engaging and keeps MIS material exciting (and funny too). Exams are pretty challenging but he's definitely worth it! His depth of knowledge in MIS and technology is overwhelming! Although I'm probably going to end up with a B+ in his class and I'm typically a straight A student, I don't regret taking his class.

If you don't want to participate daily in this class, do not try and get an A. If you want a B, then this class is an easy B regardless of how hungover you are. Case studies are all on course hero, its worth the $15 a month for an easy B+ or A-

Dias was one of the most life changing professors I've had in my life. So passionate about MIS, his lectures force you to listen to him and furthered my fascination in MIS. Tests are rather difficult (open book, but notes didn't personally help that much) so he makes you work for it. In office hours, he is more than willing to help you do well.

Dias is a very passionate, very great teacher. He reiterates the most important topics to assure everyone understands the foundation and is very energetic. He really cares to make sure students learn, regardless of major or even if no-one wants to be there. Participate and you'll be his best friend. He really appreciates participation.
tough grader!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: DiasBEST professor ever. I'm NOT naturally smart (never a 4.0 student) & didn't have prior MIS knowledge but took MIS in Summer 1 (2x faster than Fall/Spring) & got an A. If you're willing to put MANY HOURS into case studies & studying you'll succeed. Dias will prepare you for coop like no other by challenging you & make $60k tuition worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Dias is exactly what I look for in a Professor. He is knowledgeable, fair, and he treats students as his equals. The class requires effort, and is probably more difficult than the same course taught by other professors, but Professor Dias will ensure each student receives the grade they earned. He is a role model to future educators.
Makes boring material exciting and interesting, I enjoyed his class and found him to be a fair and clear grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: MGSC 6204 Managing Information Resources was a require MBA course focused on IT systems. This class had very little value to me and a heavy workload for a 1.5 credit class. The only positive experience I had was with Prof Dias. He kept us engaged every class and was a joy to listen to. Great professor! Boring subject that had very little value!

Dias is a great professor. So passionate and enthusiastic that he makes a dull subject interesting. He's also one of the most articulate guys I've ever met. The course will challenge you and class participation is a big part of your grade, but his teaching style facilitates discussion so the participation is natural. If you want to learn, take Dias
he's good but he wont just give you a grade

Dias is an amazing teacher and one of the best I've had at NU. Im not a "tech" person and he was able to actually get me engaged in this dry MIS class material. You need to participate and do the HW! FYI you can google online quiz q's for answers. Definitely need to study for tests and read the grading criteria, it really helps to score higher.

He is great! One of the best professors I have had a NU. He makes the dry material of MISM interesting and engages all the students in class. You have to come to class to learn/pass the class. But if you work hard he will notice and he's willing to help anyone who asks for it.

Professor Dias is awesome- the topic is not the most interesting business class but he makes it practical in terms of being a business person. He is one of the most intelligent and insightful teachers I have had at Northeastern and is the only teacher one should consider when taking MIS.

He is very passionate about MIS. He makes a boring subject kind of exciting. He has a good sense of humor. He will always try to do something different to keep your attention. Go to office hours and participate and you will see a difference. Grading is fair. Tests and Cases are challenging but they are the same for all MIS classes.

He is the only prof. teaching the MIS class that changed the way things are done, making students think "outside the box". I personally found that i wasnt falling asleep in his class, but subject is not interesting. All exams are heavy on analysis and absolutely no memory.

DIas is very passionate about teaching and keeps classes interesting. He gives his own version of the material, which seemed good at first, but by the end caused the class to be really hard. Avoid if you don't want the hardest tests ever.
so boring and mandatory attendance, everything was kinda guessable and easy?

Professor Youly is really nice and genuinely cares about her students. Overall, her class is very straightforward and easy, as a lot of the content is common sense. Just be aware that attendance does impact your grade and she also doesn't let you use computers.

Great professor. Super chill. 100% recommend. Homework is very manageable. Exams are easy if you focus in class. Very kind and respects all students--also remembers everyone's names and backgrounds :) Never cold calls and ensures a safe space! Also extremely understanding!

Youly is very sweet and understanding of her students' needs. The class is very lecture heavy when I've heard that other teachers make it much more interactive. The class utilizes a lot of group work that lasts throughout the semester.

Youly is a great professor and she truly cares about her students. She is always inviting people to utilize office hours and frequently offers opportunities for students to expand their learning beyond the classroom. It was a great course to get an overview of related topics, and exams are straightforward. I highly reccomend her course!

She's a great person, cares about her students and I found her lectures to be pretty interesting. Class structure is super weird - 3 essays, 7 pages all about the exact same topic. She is not a super easy grader, but I would still recommend as I did look forward to hearing her lectures every day.

Definitely an easy grader and the class is easy to pass if you pay slight attention and study a bit for the midterm and final. Her lectures are incredibly boring and she forces students to take handwritten notes but a lot of it is common sense. She does allow students to do class via zoom which is very nice.

I took her as an elective and this class was great. I learned alot tbh.  She is flexible on zoom. To be honest easy A ,study lecture slides and you will be fine for the exams . Theirs alot of discussions board but its straight forward. She is accessible through her emails and office hours. she so nice.

A really kind professor, an easy grader, and flexible with extensions or anything you have going on outside of class. I wouldn't say that I learned much in the class but I don't think there is much more to learn in IAF after foundational courses so I don't think that is her fault. I would recommend taking her if you have to take and IAF class.

She is an incredibly kind and understanding professor. I enjoyed her class a lot, even though it did get a bit dry sometimes. I really liked that she brought in many guest speakers who had amazing stories to tell. If you put in the work, it's an easy A. Many discussion boards, midterm and final, and a few papers. Overall, not a very hard class.
Would totally take her again. Papers are easy and the exams are based on the slides. Easy A if you put in the work. Shes super kind too.

This professor is super nice and invested. The class consisted in a semester-long group project. It wasn't an easy one but very rewarding when you got it right. Not super homework-intensive and lectures are interesting. She also set up very interesting talks with international speakers. Would recommend!

Took her intl conflict & negotiation class, honestly loved it!! Lectures might not be the most interesting if you aren't invested in the topic, but she's the sweetest and most caring lady! Sometimes she has funky opinions but oh well. I would 100% take another class with her! If u have to take INTL2400, make sure you take it with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Youly's INTL 1101 course online. She is so so so so nice and caring. You're going to have to read a lot, watch her lectures, and write papers. Her class can be boring at times, but also very interesting. It depends on the student's personal interest. There is a lot of critical thinking and research, but she is very willing to help anyone!

Youly is very nice and clearly cares about her students. She is more than willing to help inside and outside of class and always wants students to share their opinions. Sometimes discussions are long, boring, and off-topic. The class is a little dry at times and mainly informational but expected for an introductory class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Youly is a really nice professor! She lectures from slides and posts them online so you don't have to worry about missing things. Her assignment instructions were sometimes unclear but she is very approachable and always willing to help. She was also a pretty fair grader imo. My only complaint is she sometimes lets students go on off topic tangents

Took the honors section of this course. Straightforward professor who clearly knows what she is talking about. Lectures every class, questions on quizzes are basically straight off the powerpoint slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Saha is new but I have not found a Professor who cares more. He makes a real effort to make sure that his students understand and will go over topics again if asked. He's a fair grader who gives really good feedback. It's a hard class but I would be surprised if there was a better Professor teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He explains clearly and really tries to help in office hours. He doesn't give answers outright but asks guiding questions that make you think and understand the material better. A patient and highly effective professor.

Professor Saha is an amazing lecturer, he is very approachable and super helpful. He goes in-depth with concepts during class, and explains thoroughly when asked a question. Also, he responds to emails quickly, and is transparent with how grading works. The content in the class was hard, but taking the course with him made it much more bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is the first time the professor has offered a course. Despite its even graduate students take it and assignments being entirely programming-based, the professor never teaches programming in class. You must rely solely on AI and textbooks to acquire knowledge. You won't want to be at 3 a.m.still debugging code with mounting errors.

If u want to go to therapy to undergo the depression you endured from taking a class w this guy be my guest. Total complete as. Doesnt grade consistently. If u ever slightly make him upset he takes off points for no reason. This guy should not be teaching if he hat es his students so much
Extremely unfair grader, left a failing class average for all exams. Did not respond to any communications asking for help or clarification.

Terrible! RUN at any cost. Same as the other grader points out. Terrible at grading. Delete Canvas right after the final exam. Very strict in answers and have very limited time in quizzes and exams. Outside knowledge will be considered 0 points. The slides are not easy to understand, and there are no extra resources at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really felt like I genuinely learnt a lot in class. Encourages participation, and classes are conducted just the way they are supposed to. Agreed, the grading is tough, don't believe all the negative comments, make sure that if you take this class, to balance this with scoring subjects!!

His grading criteria are very difficult to understand. He reduces marks for not writing enough and not writing too much if you don't write your full name for the assignment submission. You must write the answer exactly as he wants it, or else he will give you a zero!
I got my points taken away because I said "A is equal to B" and he said I should instead say "A is same as B". Now you see why everybody complains about his grading.

I've had him for two courses: BIOT5120 and BIOT6214. Avoid him at all costs. He's a terrible grader and nitpicks the smallest things to tank your grade. No remorse. I'm convinced he does it for fun. Feedback on why points were taken off is obscure or not even available. Went from an A to a C in just 2 weeks. Choose. Another. Professor.

Grading is pathetic. Biostats is about data and numbers but he grades for English. He takes away points for wording and doesn't care if you get the answer right. We use Excel to calculate but he would ask you to break down the Excel formula into 15 sentences. He gave 8 assay-type questions for a quiz and only allowed 20 minutes to finish.

He's horrible. Threated to fail me if I didn't use resources from his material for my assignments and homework's. This isn't specified anywhere in the syllabus fyi. His quizzes are lengthy and time given isn't adequate for you to finish them on time.

The worst professor I've ever had. Grading scheme is arbitrary, and he will knock off points for wording when you actually had the correct answer and processes. Questions in assignments are vague, and it is never clear what is expected of you. He stresses not using any outside resources for assignments except the lectures which makes no sense.

Honestly the most confusing professor I've ever taken. Tests and assignments have points taken off for small wording choices, which is odd, since he doesn't know how to use most words correctly.
Enjoys reminding everyone how he has worked in agriculture, government, biotech, though he should scratch professor from that since he's not a good one.
Extremely tough professor. please never take this person to teach you Biostats. you will regret definitely. he cut marks for even a minute mistake.

He once stumbled into class, some 15 minutes late, with an uncomfortable expression on his face. It was clear he had pooped his pants. He sits down for quite some time, not saying a word, but gradually growing more and more uncomfortable and fidgety. Then, about 10 minutes later, he shot up from his chair and said, "Class! I have pooped my pants!".
Horrible experience. Very unfair grading with vague questions almost designed to make you lose marks.
He is awful. He is an unfair grader. His classes are assignment heavy. Exams are lengthy and questions are very vague. I would never take him again.

There are many assignments for this class like discussion posts, proposal paper, presentations, quiz, midterm and final. His exams are extremely lengthy and has lot of short answers. module content doesn't match his lectures. lectures are too basic compared to module readings. he is a tough grader

Wish I could have more than 350 characters to describe how bad my experience was. Absolutely do not take any classes with this Professor - lot of reading, lots of assignments (weekly quizzes, midterm, group presentation, group paper, discussion posts, final). Assignment questions are based on one-off comments that weren't in the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Kurt is a nice teacher who assigns light hw. Tests aren't bad and very similar to practice material & the group project can be interesting if in a good group. Participation is light as long as you try. There is also very little feedback given for literally anything turned in? Still would recommend, but not a life changing class by any means.

Too much content, flew through slides, missing information on slides / slides were vague and she spoke most of the content which was hard to keep up. Two group projects which were very annoying to complete, needed a special software, didn't provide time in class to connect which made it difficult. Tests were only multiple choice but difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing prof! If you do the readings and actually are interested in learning about consumer behavior, this class is pretty easy. Prof Kurt is super nice, but make sure to actually attend class and do the readings!
Dont take her class, cannot learn anything
No feedback for everything, everyone get same grades Give the score casually, all depends on the luck
Don't listen to the bad reviews. She is a great teacher and her class isn't that work intensive. Highliy recommend having her.

Worst professor. Grades super easily until the final project. Went into the final project with a 98, left with an 86. She doesnt give clear expectations and is simply wrong about a lot of things. Idk if it had to do with faculty politics and her realizing not everyone can get As, but she clearly doesnt care about her students. Avoid.
The best prof never met in neu. Professional, kindly and helpful for every student  only if you are concentrated.
Great prof.  I am a physical science guy and I learned a lot from his mol bio class.
I liked the class. the subject matter was hard so had to study a lot.
He knows his subject well but not his students.
he is versatile.
Very helpful professor. Really works to help students understand. Class is not easy but def doable. You will have to work hard to get a good grade.
excellent person with love for yeast...

Great professor, will tell you exactly how to do well.  But do not take that as an indication of being an easy course.  Exams still test how well you studied, and especially on the last exam, you need to study well.  Book is really helpful.  I just attended the review sessions and read the book to do well.

Good professor who likes to use the figures from the text.  He posts powerpoints but if you go to class and listen to his explinations you will do fine.  Definatly a doable class.  Great guy and a great professor.  Three exams 50 questions multiple choice he lays everything out for you to do well in biochemistry.
No Comments
No Comments
Easy A. It's an extremely watered-down form of the ENGL classes I took in hs so it's a waste of time.

Lynn is a little crazy but she means the best. There is not much homework but there are three papers and none of them are hard you just have to put in effort. She is a fun time and I always enjoyed going to her class. You can't miss more than 3 classes but she is very understanding.

Such a sweet professor, her assignments aren't very interesting but it's easy to understand what she expects from you and if you do exactly that you're fine. She's very understanding and will respond kindly if you ask any type of questions online. Not what I expected from this course but I was definitely pleasantly surprised. Go for it, she's good!
She was super nice. You will do well in this class if she likes you and you put in time with her. Would recomend though.

She is a nice professor, however, can be extremely condescending during class. You have to write the papers exactly how she wants them and provides no constructive feedback. I do not recommend this professor.
Loved her for connections and decisions. I haven't had her for english, though.

This professor is the worst. Constantly assigns first drafts to be submitted but won't ever give criticism or corrections until after the final draft has to be submitted. Harshest grader who only likes one writing style. I am not an English major for a reason and SHE made my experience that much more unenjoyable. AVOID AT ALL COST!!

Professor Dornink was really great. I did learn anything in this class but it was a good way to get a break from the stress of other classes. It is extremely easy to do well. She really cares about her students and occasionally brings in treats for special days. A very nice lady.

Lynn doesn't know how to do math, but her enthusiasm nearly makes up for it. She is sweet and means well, but feels more like "The Crazy Aunt". If you really need something, ask the TA. But in general, it is an entertaining class.
She is definitely tough. The hardest in the department but you will definitely learn a lot! She is helpful and available... Overall Great!
Attend class and you will be fine.

She is a very easy professor! But to get an A you must definitely ALL of the assignments which definitely are NOT hard and are NOT many. Her essays could be very fun if you are into creative writing and learning new writing styles. Ask her to check your essays (only 3) so that you can know what she wants and what to change to get an A!!
She is little bit challenging Don't expect an easy A AT ALL!! Always willing to help. Remember to show effort, and you'll do just fine...

Really great class.  Although she is a bit challenging its definitely doable.  ITs really rewarding when you finish that class, you really feel like you've accomplished something and feel somewhat enlightened.  Shes a really nice teacher and very accomodating to the students needs.  Freshman english sucks but if you need to get though it, go w her.

I really enjoyed her English class. She was always making us do these crazy but helpful things for class. She was very clear on what to do, and was always there for office hours if you needed help with something. One of my favorite classes this year.

I really enjoyed this class. It was challenging, but if you put in the effort and the time you will do well. I think a lot of how well you do depends on how developed your skills were to begin with. She keeps class interesting while challenging you to look for more. She is one of the best teachers I have ever had.

She is a really good teacher and one of the most helpful teachers I have ever had. She is always there for her students and will help you in any way possible. Lots of class discussions and not a lot of work. It's your standard freshmen English class so unless you're interested in English you won't love the class but it is a good class nonetheless.

Ms. Dornick is the best teacher at this school! i had her all of my first year. She is the most helpful and understanding teacher you will have if you participate, and she makes a boring class really interesting. She is so fair and motivating. I would take this class just to have her as my teacher.
although the class might not be that interesting...the assigments and papers are quiete easy to write...she is very helpful and tries her best to meet with students with problems

Class is easy and tests are online. The professor is clearly passionate about teaching, but lectures can be hard to follow and often feel more like him talking through ideas. The term project shows up late in the semester but is manageable and not too difficult.

Dimitrios was not an effective instructor in my experience, and often seemed more confident in his teaching than his delivery supported. The homework was easy, but the written portion of the exams was difficult and bad. Lectures were difficult to follow, and the classroom environment did not feel welcoming overall, a disappointing experience.
Didn't understand anything from lectures, self-study but it's easy

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I've had

His lectures are impossible to follow. Handwriting is illegible, and slides are a complete mess with typos everywhere. Does not convey information clearly. All tests and exams are extremely long, and there isn't enough time to complete them.

Dimitrios doesn't cover content well and doesn't actually answer questions; he reforms the questions and answers the question he pretends you asked. More class time is spent discussing the same "life advice" every lecture than statistics. Also he says the grades on Canvas are "very misleading", so you don't know how you're doing during the course.

Dimitrios is a very nice professor and cares about his students. However, he is an awful teacher. He is all over the place when teaching and his notes make 0 sense. It is so hard to read his little scribbles and somehow his online notes are no better. Self-studying is required because he doesn't efficiently cover test materials.
Professor Fotiadis is very passionate for stats. However, he is not the best teacher. If you want an easy A take his class, but if you want to actually learn avoid his class.

PLS AVOID!!! Class was very hard/lectures made no sense. If you missed 1 class or just went to the bathroom, you would fall VERY behind. Board is just hieroglyphics and impossible to follow/read. All exams even final are very difficult and impossible since you don't learn in his class. People with knowledge of stats could not comprehend anything.

his lectures doesn't make sense because those who understand stats would find his lectures useless due to prior understanding while those who don't understand stats would find his lecture still useless as they can't comprehend his lectures. it is a poor mixture of technicality and accessibility. also attendence is mandatory and that sucks alot

Dimitrios is passionate about teaching; however, he is truly an awful professor. His lectures are just him rambling on to himself without actually teaching us the material and they're impossible to follow along with. Also, he's awful with Canvas and the quizzes are difficult to actually do good on. Plus, he refuses to curve or give extra credit.
He really cannot teach. If you want to learn stats AVOID because trust you won't learn a thing. If you want easy A and online tests, final, and projects, this is the class for you.

He's very kind and all and it's an easy class given a lot of the work is done online, however his lectures are awful. They just look like scribbles and he gets very confused with what he's talking about. Overall, extremely easy, but avoid if you're actually looking to learn.

We use webassign and there are only 2 tries. A good amount of tests but they are all online at home no camera. Final project doesn't make sense and he will only explain it 2 weeks before the due date. It is hard to understand him, but I usually do the homework while he teaches. Very unorganized and you won't learn the material. Take for Easy A.

Participation doesn't matter at all in this class, even though it's part of our grade for the semester. As long as you show up to class, you get credit for attendance. Dimitrios isn't tech savvy at all, so be ready to work out a bunch of your own technical issues by yourself because he won't be able to help you there.
He cares a lot and loves his job but his lectures were confusing and all over the place, same with his canvas, all tests were online including the final and they are worth 90% of ur grade

Great person, but the worst professor I've had. His organization is a disaster. His online notes look like a preschooler wrote them—just random scribbles—and he talks way too fast. In class, it's worse—he scrawls barely legible notes on the board, and by the time you figure them out, you're already behind.
Class was mandatory but all exams are online, even the final.

a horrible teacher in almost every respect. that being said, its not that hard to get a good grade since the exams are take home and very very very similar to the practice questions. 

also, he's difficult to understand, messy, terrible with tech, extremely unorganized, out of touch, and more. 

otherwise, he's a nice man.

DO NOT TAKE! He cares about his students and is easy to get in contact with but trying to learn in class was impossible. The canvas is the most disorganized canvas I have ever seen and the notes are not helpful. Going to class is basically the same as not going to class - you will not learn anything. Attendance was mandatory but was a waste of time

Worst professor I've had. He is a sweet guy but definitely can't teach properly. Don't take this class if you have no prior experience in stats. Goes fast on content and his notes are a mess. He made attendance mandatory to scare his students into coming to class. If I studied on my own and never attended class I would have gotten the same grade.

His handwriting and typos when communicating, seriously needs to be checked on. I wish I could attach examples because its truly atrocious. He changed his syllabus to make attendance mandatory and threatened to drop our grade a LETTER each time we were gone halfway through the course because everyone realized how low quality his lectures are.

Lectures were a waste of time since his teaching style is next to impossible to understand, frequently does not answer questions students pose, saying that they are pointless and that they should be "paying attention to the textbook" if they are confused. Exams are super lengthy and typically have numerous errors in them. Canvas is a mess.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. 90% of your grade is dependent on your tests and the class material does NOT match what he teaches in lecture. His Canvas is unorganized and it's super difficult to find anything. He made our attendance mandatory 8 weeks into the semester and made it that if you miss on class, your grade drops an entire letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor. Grading is a bit annoying because you have to get over a 95 to get an A. The exams make almost all of the grade but if you go to class and pay attention you will be fine. He usually curves all exams.
worst teacher ever. does not follow curriculum.
This is the worst teacher I have ever had.

One of the best courses I've taken at Northeastern. Dimitrios clearly loves teaching stats and puts a lot of effort into teaching every day. Very clear syllabus and he is very understanding. Best professor for business stats.
The absolute man. Is very funny and also passionate about stats. Take this class if you want a good and easy class. Love this guy.

Really nice guy! Sad to hear he is retiring this year, but I thought he was great. Helps guide students in the right direction in this course and outside of it. Despite this, lectures can get a little confusing even if you watch the pre recorded lessons. But all the information he gives, helps so much. Questions from tests can be found on homework.
Went slow through easy topics and then sped up when we got to the tougher material. Very passionate about the course, maybe just not my style.

Why does Dimitrios give ridiculous curves on tests and allows you to drop one of your test grades? He is simply a bad teacher. Sure he cares about his students and is passionate about stats. But if you don't know how to engage your class and organize your notes/lectures in a good manner, it doesn't change the fact that he is a terrible teacher.

Dimitrios is easily, EASILY, the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. He has an awful, slow, boring, mindless teaching style which results in every student in the class is looking at their phone or computer, 80% of the time. The only reason he gets good ratings is his insane (20%) curves, which is just a testament to his teaching abilities.

There is too much workload for one class! Long homework assignments. Quizzes every week. Exams are impossible. Extremely irrelevant to what we learned in class and 10x more difficult. Almost everyone in the class failed before the curve. You need to really understand everything in depth, but there is just too much to learn that its overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Too many documents and readings on the BlackBoard. Very disorganized, good luck finding what you want because you'll have to dig through a million links and even the pdfs are images, so you can't search for keywords. Quizzes Every Week. Some say read the textbook to do well on quizzes, others say look at his articles.. I say read EVERYTHING..!! Bad
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fotiadis is very passionate about statistics. The class material can be a little boring and repetitive but he wants you to learn. He encourages students to push themselves. The tests are hard, but graded on a curve.

Not helpful in office hours and no TA. Off topic often. Would not recommend unless you've taken a stats course in high school or want to just teach yourself. Ended w ok grade in the class bc the curves are huge because nobody understands what is going on (30%+) but felt like it was huge waste and learned nothing helpful. Studied a lot.

This class was tough, but there is a VERY generous curve (usually 30%). I got a 78 on a test and that curved to over 100%. He is hilarious and provides us with great life lessons. He still remembers me and was very friendly when I saw him outside of class.

Excellent professor. I would recommend him to anyone who is willing to put in a lot of work and doesn't mind getting frustrated. He cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed in life. There are a lot of quizzes based on the textbook readings, but they help you to understand the material better.

Take Dimitrios' class. Although his lectures can be a bit confusing at times, he posts very detailed notes online, and tons of practice material before each exam. Also MOST IMPORTANTLY he gives very generous curves on all exams. I got a 67 on one exam which was brought up to a 97. He truly cares about the success of each student.

His lectures are hard to follow since he moves very fast.  Nonetheless, he has extremely detailed notes and an abundance of practice problems and answers on his website which are where I learned everything I know. The tests are very reasonable and large curves are added.   Very easy to do well as a non math person.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dimitrios is a great guy, and clearly loves what he teaches, which made getting to the 8 am a *little* easier. The class is pretty straightforward, but is still difficult. The tests are definitely designed to be extremely challenging, but the curves on them can be very large. Overall, it's a challenging course, but his care for students is better.

A wacky dude, but very nice. Can get off topic but incredibly knowledgable. Goes very fast during lectures but highly encourages  students to stop him when they get lost. Office hours are very helpful. Tests are difficult and study guides aren't incredibly specific, but he usually curves them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic! His tests are difficult and the course is not an easy A. He curves fairly. For example, I could get a 78 on a test and he would curve it to a 104. His tests are EXTREMELY hard. He's a professor who will really push you and recommend have a strong background in math and like a challenge. He gives you the answers to a whole project

Attendance unnecessary. Responsible and respectful professor. Always reach out to students. No need textbook, all of the materials are provided free on blackboard. Could not find a better professor.  The quizzes are actually not hard as long as you study and really understand the materials. Students who say it's hard is probably not that diligent.

Very had to understand, he means well and wants his students to succeed, however his exams are really difficult. He gives a lot of homework that you need to pass in but you are also given the answers.  good luck.
The tests are hard. The average grade on final before curve is like 58%.

His explanations are not great and he makes everything seem x10 times harder than what it actually is. Also, his final is impossible. However, he helps a lot with assignments and the project. Also, the notes he posts on blackboard are enough to get an A.

He's complex in class because he writes out every single step of a problem on the board, so it looks a lot harder than it actually is. Just read the book if he's too hard. If the book is too complicated (like in the later chapters), pay attention in class. Tests aren't particularly difficult, the entire class is just using the formulas he provides.
don't even dare....
Great person, but no such a great professor. Really hard to understand his accent.

His class is no longer easy. The structure has been changed drastically, don't expect to receive free A's like previous years. He had to drop an entire exam (lowest of 3) so students wouldn't get C's and D's. Work hard, and you'll do fine. No need to buy the textbook, he uploads all necessary readings/assignments to blackboard.

He is definitely NOT super easy. It is clear that this semester he changed his methods. He doesn't give study guides or any kind of material to prepare for the test other than his lecture notes. He is in love with stats and he is very helpful and funny but don't expect an A if you don't work hard for it.

His tests are the exact same as the practice quizzes online (different numbers), so as long as you study those you will be fine. Lectures can be confusing, but again you don't really even need them as long as you study the practice quizzes.
Best Professor in NEU

This class was so easy! All of his tests are based directly off of the review packets he gives out. Most of the test questions are exactly the same as the ones in the packet. Go to class, do your homework, and study the review packet, and there's no reason you shouldn't get an A. He is also a very nice guy, and helpful too.
All his review packets and homework questions are very helpful when reviewing for exams. The exam questions come directly from review packets so it is very difficult to not do well in this class
Best professor for this class! Honestly do not think of taking this class with anyone else.

He's a sweet man, very enthusiastic about the material he's teaching.  I found everything he taught easy to grasp, and he would always state that he loves teaching and if anyone ever had any questions feel free to ask.  I enjoyed this class more than many other's, and really appreciated his genuine interest in wanting his students to succeed.

I took Dimitrios for statistics in my freshman year. I usually do very well in school but this class was (NO EXAGGERATION) the most difficult class i have ever taken. The students with other statistics teachers said the course was a breeze. Please dont make the same mistake i did. AVOID THIS CLASS. ps the class avg on the last test was a 45

Took this Fall 2025. Lots of readings. You have reading logs due on Tuesday and Friday. Lectures are basically based on the readings and more in-depth explanations. For the more graded assignments, please ask her about the assignment in full detail. It will help. WARNING: This is not a Republican (Trump MAGA class), be aware! Very liberal class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is amazing. She is not the most tech savvy but if she made a mistake, she would never fault us for it and would give us an extension if needed. In the middle of the semester, she had us sit down and write down what we would like her to change about the class/teachings, and she actually changed everything that we asked her to.

Profe Dominguez is passionate, knowledgeable, and very kind. She can be confusing, but is very helpful and receptive if you ask her questions (plus she's more responsive via email than most profs). She's also super understanding so if you have any issues just communicate! Also very chill grader (almost everyone got 100s) and LGBTQ friendly!
The goat, does not deserve previous bad reviews, could be more tech savvy

She did not put any resources on canvas aside from the required reading.She did not put in any grades during the semester and arbitrarily sent me an email saying I got a B with no explanation of why.She isn't hard? the reading and class lectures aren't hard? apparently grades hard but doesn't give any feedback to why you scored what you did.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shes so confusing. She makes the work given harder than it looks and gives busy work instead of meaningful assignments. Her grading scheme is a mess because she grades things in groups so your grade on Blackboard is not accurate. On top of that she wont even tell you youre actual grade if you ask. Protect your mental health! Dont take it w. her
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took Senior Capstone with this professor and it was horrible. She already has negative reputation in the Sociology department but I had to take this course to graduate. She would guess definitions on the spot. The syllabus was extremely disorganized. She is also no trans friendly and will mess up pronouns and not care if you correct her.

She took 1.8 off my grade for missing a single class and 7 off my grade for participation. She didn't give a single grade back all semester. Doesn't teach and forces students to read about 150 pages a week. Disconnected from students. Worst professor at the university.

Dominguez gives a hell of a lot of reading, and can be biased in her teaching... BUT conceptually this class is one of the most interesting i've taken at University. Despite the quantity of work given ; weekly essays and one 10 page final paper (no midterm or final) if you pay attention and participate you will manage fine. Tip; do the reading!

reviews.comment: Worst professor at this university. I wouldn't wish this professor on my worst enemy. Hard pass on ever taking a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I've ever taken at Northeastern. For an elective you have to write tons of papers, and her biases clearly show in her teaching. I would strongly recommend against taking anything with her unless you absolutely have to.

This is her first time teaching Sociology of Violence (the other professor is retiring). It isn't bad. There's only 8 people in my class so all we do is have a discussion on Tuesdays and watch a movie every Friday. There are no tests! But there is a LOT of writing (a short analysis every week, and three 10 page papers throughout the semester).

WORST TEACHER EVER!  Don't take this course. For an elective you have 8 papers, two presentations and a midterm. If you don't speak more than twice a class your grade will be negatively affected. A class that's about realizing how people are treated unfairly concerning race, she does the same thing with grades.  Save yourself now.  DON'T TAKE IT!

Unclear and vague when teaching and especially on test questions. Often defensive and thinks her students are dumb. Would not recommend the class and be skeptical of most of what she says because she is usually wrong

Do not take this class. She is way too vague in class, prints her quizzes offline and doesn't edit them to what was covered in class, argues with students whenever they go to her with a concern, doesn't practice what she teaches, is not helpful at all, and basically is just an all around terrible professor. The worst I've had at Northeastern.
doug is the GOAT he is so passionate about graphic design and i genuinely think i'll remember this man for the rest of my design career. 10/10 take him

took graphic design history online duirng covid and loved it, he's so knowledgeable and caring for his students and you can always reach him by email/office hours. the course itself is a great foundation for art history/graphic design majors.

He knows everything about design and his class is so enjoyable. The projects were really fun and he gives really good advice and critiques for them. There are quizzes but they're really easy and he isn't a harsh grader and he gives extra credit. Take his class!

this class was really interesting for me and I truly enjoyed all the lectures. doug does a lot of show and tell w/ his personal collection of stuff which is really cool. you have to watch lectures outside of class, but the class is pretty evenly split between studio projects and lecture. he is very passionate and knows literally everything
Very clear lectures and simple grading rubric. Test heavy but the tests are very simple with lots of extra credits rewarded.

Fantastic professor, covers subjects with nuance and in a way that is understandable, plenty of time to ask questions, available outside of class, explains and articulates math concepts well
     \ was late to course by 2 weeks, he helped me get back on track \

fyi went in w/ highschool precalc and calc experience \     

highly recommend course
Pretty chill teacher, provide extra credit on ever quiz.
Super awesome grader, barely did any studying, and still ended with an A.
Amazing professor. Super kind and caring. He will help you do well and increase your confidence in math, no matter your background. Take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class should be relatively easy if you got a background on math. Other than that he gives clear lectures and reviews whats going to be on the quiz and tests. He always make sure his students understand pass the quizzes. He does give extra credit. Occasionally does crack jokes and give students a good laugh. You”ll be in good hands with Kien.

Absolutely great professor. He is super caring and kind, will always answer questions and explain most things clearly. The course is heavily graded on quizzes, midterms, and the final exam (40% of your final grade). I would highly recommend taking him if he offers Calc 1, amazing professor.

He seems to really care about how students are doing and he answers any questions you have. Super patient and kind. Homework isn't required and you get an equation sheet for the first few quizzes which really helps.

Awesome professor, lectures are clear and actually useful, exams are fairly written and grading is pretty generous, hw not required Very down to earth, clearly cares about his students succeeding and actually learning in the class, occasional jokes sympathizing with suffering of his students are pretty funny. Don't miss lectures and you'll be fine.

I wish they would stop doing Service Learning; it's a waste of time every week to go to some random place to practice Chinese. Service Learning, in general, is one of the biggest stresses in this class and simply adds more onto your plate than what's necessary. It's an hour a week, but you have to commute.
Dong Laoshi is the best. She is tough on you but she loves her students like her own children. Give her your best effort and she will give you hers.

I took this class because I am pretty fluent in Chinese and thought it would be a good gpa booster but it wasn't. I feel like she purposely grades me harder than other people because I'm fluent and she also grades so hard on participation. She also gives so much homework and projects that I feel she doesn't give enough time for

I wouldn't say she is really good, but she is not really bad. I had her for 2201, it wouldn't let me choose. This class has the most amount of homework. There are a lot of projects and she calls on people and then makes them say the word/sentence properly over and over again. She is very understanding and brings tea and food for us

Her quizzes are hard, you really have to study and keep up with learning the characters but she is the nicest!! Rlly considerate especially w covid. Fair bit of in-class discussions & group work but there are so many contributing factors to the grade (quiz, hw, mini-essays/final projects for each unit) that you have time to make up for a bad grade.

Prof Dong is a nice person, but her teaching style is not the best. The class is very much lecture heavy and not many class activities, which would make the class much more interesting. Hard tests, even if you study for them and a lot of homework.

I took her class and I can pretty much say that the textbook is your everything. All her powerpoints are material from the book. She's very knowledgable, explains clearly to students, makes sure that at least everyone from the class speaks once during that class and is overall a good teacher. It's hard to get an A though so you need to work hard.

Adorable!!! Such an amazing teacher, and I love how she laughs at her own jokes. its a foreign language class so you get what you put into it, but she's very helpful and friendly, she really cares about her students, wish I had her again.

Professor Dong was one of the best professors I had this semester. Although her teaching style using powerpoint wasn't the most effective for me, she really wants everyone to do well and is genuinely a kind and intelligent person. If you want to learn the language, definitely take her class. She's not an easy A, but working for it really pays off.

Prof. Dong is a very good/funny professor. She laughs a lot at her own jokes which keeps the class lively. She is a really easy grader on hw and her quizzes are usually medium difficulty. She emphasizes real world scenarios to teach the material. Just make sure you spend enough time on the material especially if you didn't pay attention in 1101.

I love professor Dong. She is a really smart woman and very well versed in English, knows how to teach Chinese in an interesting and fun way, she is very contemporary in her approach and will use real world examples to help get the message across, and she's always laughing. Take her if you can! Class is a big jump from CHNS 1101, be prepared.

Dong Laoshi is an excellent teacher! The class is not a walk in the park -- Chinese is not easy. But, Dong Laoshi makes the material fun, and she has a very light and airy spirit. I would recommend her if you want a very thorough teaching in Chinese.

Love Dong Laoshi!!  She is one of the best teachers I've had at NU.  You do a ton of work, but her style makes it easy to understand and retain.  I definitely feel confident in my speaking and writing skills.  She's also so nice and genuinely cares about how well you're doing.

Professor Dong is great! You definitely have to put in a lot of work and studying for this class, but if you do she really appreciates it and your grade will reflect that. She is an extremely nice person and makes learning such a hard language fun! Definitely take her class!!

dong laoshi is super sweet! she wants students to learn and will always help you if you ask for it. students sometimes take advantage of that but she's smart and won't let you get an A unless you've worked in the class and deserve it. def try to take chinese with her if you can!
I don't even have her as a professor but she's hooked me up with so much stuff in China ie. internship, housing. She's got mad guanxi, like tons of it.

had previous chinese experience so the class was easy, but prof dong is the sweetest woman if you try. participate in the class chants like everyone else - she appreciates it. NEED to go to class, not just for attendance reasons, but it will help you tenfold. loves to help kids, just help her by preparing for class
She's a good teacher who helps students get exposed to the language. If you have prior experience with Chinese the class should be a breeze, but you do have to commit a fair amount of time to it.
No Comments

Professor Dong is a wonderful women.  You won't be able to slip by this class without studying, but the work is porportional to the time she gives you.  I get A's on all her quizes and you really retain a lot of vocab in such a short time.  She makes learning a new language extremely simple!!!

Prof. Dong is such an awesome teacher for this difficult, difficult language.  She is enthusiastic, funny, and always pushes us to learn, even when it's clear we'd rather not.  She'll go out of her way to help you, and she is an awesome person.  If you're going to take Chinese, get Prof Dong!

Genuinely nice guy, but he really needs to retire. Taught out of his own textbook that we had to pay for with $30 cash, and most of the vocab are terms he made up. Gen chem here is two semesters fit into one so its a lot of work but the curve is generous.
He is clearly passionate about what he does but he's very demeaning and makes you feel terrible when you ask questions. Hard tests too.

Professor Dransfield works hard for students to understand the material, not to memorize. Exams were very difficult, but he does prepare you well for them. I strongly recommend attending all lectures and his office hours. He is more than happy to go over difficult concepts.

CHEM 1161 is notoriously tough. His exams are challenging, but if you apply yourself it is possible to do well. I'd recommend him as a prof to anyone who asked. He's a great guy. Don't be scared by any low ratings. If you show effort and grit, he'll help you get to the finish line. Best prof I've ever had hands down

He made me hate learning. 10% of your grade is attendance taken off a chemistry problem on the info you just learned. If you get it wrong you only get .5 attendance for the day. It's a hard class. He thinks it's fun to create the most difficult test possible. I could write a paper on how bad he was. If you have the option pick another professor!!

This guy cares and wants you to succeed. That being said, he needs to cram a lot of material into a very short time. It will be tough, but Dransfield knows what he's doing. His PhD is from Harvard in Atmospheric thermochemistry and he also does interesting research. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He loves his scare tactics. Be prepared for him to tell you you should drop the class; honestly, don't listen. With how he curves, it will be easy to get a b- or above if you do all the homework and attend recitation. He can seem harsh, but he cares about what he teaches. His tests are just incredibly hard and hard to prepare for. But he's good

Dransfield didn't make the class difficult, curriculum crams a lot of info into a semester, so we moved fast. Funny, explained topics very well, and ensured frequent office hours, especially closer to exams (I recommend these). Find the textbook online for free. You don't need it to do well if you took AP. Records lectures, so you can review notes.

Funny and engaging lectures, probably the best part of the class. He answers questions, but often runs behind in his plan for the lecture. However, he likes to put ambiguous questions on the multiple-choice section and makes you guess between two answer choices. This is especially annoying since the final exam is entirely multiple-choice questions.

Great lecturer and he cares about what he does, but he can be VERY condescending. Asking questions is a coin toss between getting an actual answer and being made to feel stupid for even asking it. Test averages are usually terrible but he heavily curves
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dransfield didn't make the class difficult, curriculum crams a lot of info into a semester, so we moved fast. Funny, explained topics very well, and ensured frequent office hours, especially closer to exams. Find the textbook online for free because you don't need it to do well if you took AP chem. Records lectures, so you can review notes.

I think Dransfield does a great job making chem interesting. I really liked chem and I attribute that almost entirely to Dransfield himself. That being said, he has a tendency to come off as condescending to students that ask questions that may seem obvious. If you show interest, he is willing to put in time outside of class to ensure you succeed.

If you didn't take AP Chem in hs, prepare to struggle. If you're honors/not ChemE, I would recommend avoiding taking his class for the honors credit. Interesting class, but dented my GPA. He moves fast, covers topics even outside the curriculum, and hw/recitation problems were much (purposefully) easier than the midterms/final. Be cautious.

Professor Dransfield was overall a great professor. I didn't take AP Chem so I was a little nervous. It is great that he curves the exams A LOT (about 10-20%) and the final as well. I had a B for most of the class but after recitation was added and the final, I ended with an A-. I would recommend him. It is not easy but he is ALWAYS eager to help.

While he is a good lecturer and clearly cares about what he teaches, it's impossible to ask questions or get clarification. If you don't already know the concepts don't even ask him. He'll make you feel like the most unintelligent person on the planet when answering them. I kid you not he laughed at me when I asked him a question in class.

Professor Dransfield is so passionate about his field and such a passionate & high energy lecturer. However, the first-year engineering chem class is difficult (he says this the first day). If you're fine with being challenged, Dransfield is a fantastic professor. His research is in climate science, something you will learn a lot about in his class
It's Gen Chem...what can u expect

Dr. Dransfield moves at a very quick pace, and it's really difficult to keep up at times. It's a lot of material for one semester, and he does his best with what he's given. Tests are hard, but he's always available outside of class and is really helpful one on one. Grading is also extremely fair. Showing up to class/recitation is 20% of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is amazing and he aims to challenge the best students in his class, so his exams are a bit tricky, so if you like chemistry and are good at it, go to his class, you'll find him fascinating. If you have questions, don't hesitate to ask him. He loves to answer questions both in and out of class. "Thinking is more important than memorizing."

Chem1151 was honestly the hardest class I've ever taken, but the only reason I still liked it was because of Dr. Dransfield. The content is really fast, there were four exams counting the final, and overall the class was just hard. But Dransfield was always caring, had awesome engaging lectures, and was available outside of the classroom.

Professor Dransfield is very passionate about chemistry and it reflects everyday in class. I took AP chem and decided to retake this course to get an easy A before orgo, but I was mistaken. I did receive an A but this course was very very hard. Overall I thought his lectures were very engaging and his class was my favorite this semester.

Unless you are in love with chemistry and took AP Chem, PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He teaches at such a high level and if you don't already know the concepts you will not understand. If you already took AP chem, you will enjoy his teaching pace. BUT I DID NOT UNDERSTAND A SINGLE LECTURE. Be prepared to put in a lot of effort.

Dransfield is a great guy. He's a little intimidating and blunt, but is super helpful when approached one-on-one. Tests are a little difficult, but definitely manageable. There are lengthy homework assignments each week, but they can really only raise your grade. If you can put in the time to study, you'll do well in the class.

To be honest, if you see yourself as less self-disciplined and "searching for a comfortable" person, just don't take his lecture will be much easier for you. Professor Dransfield's class requires 100% attention in class and 5-6 hours of after-school work to do well. Chemistry is hard, and getting good grades depends on self-studying.

Teaches super fast and teaches harder than the other chemistry classes. Teaches some unnecessary things and got into Orgo topics. 3 midterms and one resurrection final. Homework and participation points to get your grade up. Exams are fairly hard. You can do well in the class if you spend hours a week in the class.

Professor Dransfield is one of the most arrogant people I have come across. Instead of helping a student understand when they have question, he will automatically make you feel lesser without actually explaining anything. He can be unprofessionally aggressive when dealing with students and does not to seem to care about understanding the material.

He's arrogant, passive agressive and intimidating, which makes you not want to ask questions. Not comprehensive and there are no make ups. Even though the midterms are off class hours and online, they are very hard. At least he curves them. His lectures are heavy and he goes in a very fast pace. DO NOT take his class. avoid him at all costs.

This is the worst professor I have had in my life. He is extremely rude and is not understanding. He goes through the material as we were all familiar with it, making it intimidating when we would like to ask questions. For the midterms, they are extremely hard although he curves it at the end. Also, he has no respect for his students at all.

Take this class if you enjoy chemistry and would like a challenge. Do not take this class if you are looking for an easy A. If you take this class carefully balance out your schedule with easier classes if you can. Professor Dransfield can be intimidating and talks highly of his class, but have confidence in yourself that you are able to do well!

He is so passionate about chemistry. You're graded on participation (in-class poll everywhere), three midterm exams, a final (can replace midterm scores), weekly homework, and recitation attendance. He knows he's a hard teacher and offers plenty of extra credit and outside support. You have to engage with and stay on top of the content to do well.

Professor Dransfield works extremely hard to get through all of the material because it is so much stuff. You definitely have to have some discipline and put in hours of work outside of class.
