I definitely recommend a study group! There are 3 midterms but he has a resurrection final! He has office hours and so do the TAs which are extremely helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield's class is the hardest college class I've taken so far. Not having a strong chemistry background, I struggled greatly. He went so fast that I could not keep up at times. His tests are extremely difficult and I barely passed all of them. To pass this class, you must dedicate a few hours a day studying for it.

Professor Dransfield is a great professor but the class goes very fast and is pretty difficult. You should definitely devote time outside of class to studying and making sure you know the material. The tests are hard but extra credit and the weekly homework assignments help your grade. Having a background in chemistry will help you immensely.

Professor Dransfield is an efficient lecturer, he is able to convey his points easily, but he speaks too fast and the class is very difficult. His tests are also very difficult and backtracking is disabled. The only way to be adequately prepared for this class is to have taken AP Chem (I did not, and I struggled, but my friends who did did fine).
He pulls the high school teacher "I'll wait" phrase when students don't know answers to his questions within literally 10 seconds of him asking it.

for the exams and the final you had to answer the question before moving on to the next one. Also, once you submitted answers to questions, you couldn't go back and revisit. Prof thought this would prevent cheating but all it did was waste time and leave you with literally seconds left before the end of the exam.
YOU MUST GO TO CLASS IF YOU WANT TO PASS. This professor is amazing, but it will be difficult to do well if you don't study regularly and show up to all classes.

Professor Dransfield is a great guy and professor, but the course is rough. It moves at a very fast pace that he worsens by adding in unnecessary material. The exams are MUCH harder than any examples he gives. He does offer many opportunities for extra credit, which is much needed. Overall, you will learn a lot in this class but it is hard.

The lectures are so fast and very dense. You can fall behind in notes and in the class very easily. He is very enthusiastic about chemistry, so I had high hopes in the beginning. If you have a good background in chemistry, go for the challenge. But if you are not confident in chemistry, do not take. He is also extremely passive aggressive.
Sometimes when students asked questions, prof Dransfield would literally laugh in their face. He's so pretentious and passive aggressive and his exams were so unbelievably hard.

The lectures went EXTREMELY fast and we were given new material for the final TWO DAYS before the final test. The lectures contained WAY too much information and I walked out extremely confused after every class. Be prepared to do most of the learning on your own outside of class and spend 30+ hours studying for each exam to barely scrape by.

professor dransfield goes extremely fast in every lecture, theres lots of homework and often he comes off a bit pretentious in class. but if youre confused he truly wants you to understand. He really wants you to succeed in his class. keep up with lectures and do practice problems from the textbook!

He the best lecturer I have had so far in college. He is engaging, interesting, and provides helpful ways to help you understand the content. It's a lot of content, but that isn't his fault, and he does everything he can to help you. He is very accessible at office hours, answers questions very well, and will work with you until you understand.

Professor Dransfield is a dedicated professor who loves chemistry and is thorough. However, CHEM1151 is basically 2 semesters of chem in one (fast). Also, while homeworks and quizzes may be straightforward, his exams are EXTREMELY HARD. One of the hardest courses I have ever taken and I only got through with excessive studying. Go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield is so enthusiastic about chemistry, and it's shown throughout the lectures. He goes through units fast so study every unit thoroughly. DO NOT DO LAST MINUTE STUDYING. THE TESTS ARE DIFFICULT SO BE PREPARED. TIPS: Do well on the quizzes and HW to boost your grade. Also find a study group! Resurrection Final is the move!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield is a great professor. He is passionate and occasionally funny, and he really wants you to learn. He is put in a tough position teaching a stacked class, but he manages to get through all of the material and more. I took an honors section of the class and I don't recommend it. The tests are way harder than other sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture is like drinking through a firehose. I had him for honors gen chem, and he will teach the honors section additional topics, so we go insnaely fast.. Very nice teacher, cares about people who works hard, but I think there was too much information.

Professor Dransfield is passionate about Chemistry but goes very quickly. He always says we are behind but added a new chapter to the final that is not even in the curriculum (I would've rather spent the extra 2 days on review). He is not an empathetic professor at all. Prepare to put in lots of work outside of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Dransfield is a good professor, but the amount of material he goes through is insane. Started off not liking him too much, but by the end of the class his dedication to his students really shone through. He tries to make the class as bearable as possible, but he can only do so much. Midterms are tough but bearable. Resurrection final is clutch
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good teacher, class is tough but he makes it as easy as possible. This is my third year of chemistry, so it wasn't too hard for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Had him for an Honors section of Gen Chem for Engineers. Very enthusiastic about all the topics, but he goes through lectures VERY quickly. Homeworks are reasonable. Exams are extremely time-sensitive and fairly difficult, though he curves final grades to compensate. Also, definitely ask him questions about kinetics or global warming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He may talk fast and cover more material in a semester than seems possible, but he's a phenomenal teacher. Midterm averages are low, but mostly because people intentionally bomb them knowing they can make up for the bad grade with the resurrection final. He's a tough professor, but I learned more in this class than any other at Northeastern so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice and funny guy who has a lot of knowledge about the subject, but this class is a CHALLENGE. I study at least 25 hours before each exam and barely scoot by with a B/B- on each. Be prepared to be overwhelmed in lecture, take hours to do homework, & study your butt off. Definitely harder than other chem sections for this course. Learned a lot tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He taught so fast it was impossible to keep up. We where like 5 chapters ahead of the other section. It got to a point where he wouldnt even accept some questions because he wanted to go faster.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class average was generally around a 75 with a curve. He talks like you're watching his lecture on 2x, so get ready to write. He's super lecture heavy, with weekly HW that's about 25 Q's. I studied for 12-15 hrs per test and averaged mid-high 80s, but I'm not naturally great at chem. Wouldn't take him again, but he's a cool dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: First off- This course is VERY difficult. If you aren't already pretty comfortable with high school chemistry, prepare to be confused 90% of the time. Be aware, the professor is not very understanding.

This professor made chemistry very difficult for me to learn and to deal with emotionally. Many tears were shed because of conversations with him. I personally was not receptive to his harsh delivery at times, and I would have preferred a more understanding and compassionate professor. I will say that the homework assignments are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: THIS CLASS IS HARD! If you're taking this class prepare to have the ride of your life. There's a lot of material and the course goes by veerryy fast. Start studying on day one and I recommend watching Organic Chemistry Tutor after every lecture to make sure you understand everything from that video. He's rly nice but pls take this class seriously.

He's an incredible person, but his class is way harder than any of the other profs. Tests are incredibly difficult and not like practice problems. Lectures are great, he's very passionate about chem, and really cares about his students. A good amount of homework, but nothing crazy. Lots of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield was a good professor but his classes and tests were considerably harder than the other chemistry professors. His classes were very fast-paced but he was always in a good mood, ready to teach. Attending classes was definitely a must to do well in the course. There were lots of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield, though new to Northeastern, is by far one of the best professors. His class is not easy, and it won't be easy. However, he is the most caring and passionate man I've met and won't let you fail as long as you put in the effort and the work. Try hard and. you will succeed in his class. Go to his office hours if you need help!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Even though the class might be in person, classes are so big that you don't really have to go. Lectures, homeworks and tests are all online. There is one partner project, but it is easy to complete and quick. She is a good teacher and very knowledgeable. Good at responding to emails.
shes the best
Pretty easy class make sure to do the homework on time, everything is through canvas and cengage, caring professor, attendance not necessarily mandatory, one duo project that isn't too difficult
A very nice lady, teaches effectively & makes learning fun. Material is relatively easy. Take her class!

Professor Dupree is very nice and caring. Her lectures are easy to understand and she makes sure students are really thinking about the material. However, her voice can be a little too good at putting you to sleep. Her lectures are all recorded, so most people skip often, and her test are all take-home and open note. TAKE HER CLASS.
Prof Dupree is super straight-forward with all of her assignments and exams which makes it easy to do well in this class. Very understanding professor and overall a chill class!

Guys at first I was like I'm so scared of economics so I went to every class, but one day the class was freezing and I kept hearing noises so I was like maybe I will stop going a little and I did some work on my own w/ A+. She is very generous with what she gives; open note at home exams, drops lowest grades, etc. Take her she is kind
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exceptionally easy but extremely boring. Lectures are just her reading slides and telling tangential stories with no point, which sucks because she's clearly passionate/knowledgeable. Still recommend though. 1 test is dropped (including final if you don't wanna take it). 3 HWs are also dropped. Textbook is expensive and mandatory for assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I never went to class, attendance wasn't mandatory. She is a very nice person. HW is long but online and so are tests. very easy class take her for sure

Professor Dupree is knowledgeable and excited to teach. Class was overall easy ... tests were all online and considered "open note, open resource, can do it with friends, etc" (her words). Very few people attended lectures, and they were not very engaging, so I felt I didn't learn as much as I wished. Wish she got to know the few who came to class!

Professor Dupree was great. She clearly cares about economics and comes to class prepared and interested. Class was okay, it was hard to learn deeply in such a large lecture hall, and many times I felt myself zoning out. Overall, it was great, and Professor Dupree did a great job teaching a large lecture.

Lectures were extremely dry, she just regurgitated the slide decks provided by the textbook. I got a good grade, but all tests were assigned through Canvas so basically everyone cheated and no one went to lecture. Nice professor and easy class but you don't really learn anything

Very kind professor and great course. Yes, there are quite a few homework assignments and 5 exams, but nothing too hard. Content is very understandable and class is quite easy. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was great. So easy, you literally just have to complete the weekly HW assignments which are all online and ALL of the tests are take home (including midterms and the final). Her lectures are good too you just have to show up and want to learn. I highly recommend taking!
easy class, just do homework and ur chilling, all tests are take home open book but if you need help you can get it very easily, occasional assignments, but hella easy.

Jill is great. The class is easy, don't worry at all. She responds to emails quickly and is very caring, willing to work with you. Doesn't take off points for late assignments. Tests are open-note, asynchronous. I would take this class again. It was a relief to have an easier class like this one.

Lectures were a bit all over the place. Textbook reading is unavoidable as there are quizzes on the reading every class (they're easy though as long as you did the reading). When writing the essays, it's best to attend office hours to make sure you're going in the right direction. Class was really interesting at times but overall a little boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grading seemed random at times - on multiple occasions, it was unclear why I was getting points taken off. She would get somewhat defensive when asked about this. Lectures can be hard to pay attention to as they directly reflect reading we are told to do before class; hearing everything twice was boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: i loved prof dupree's class! the whole semester for american econ history was based on 1 book, and we covered 2 chapters a week. discussions are student-led and very engaging! short reading quizzes every class made by students, and total of 4 papers throughout the sem (1 paper per book section). very understanding and lenient grader!
She is nice professor, but her classes don't really help with tests. She usually grades assignments at long intervals, which makes me confused about grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not the greatest lecturer, she reads of the slides which are not very thorough. There are many unit tests, they are not difficult if you read the textbook and do the homework. You do need to self-teach yourself but the class isn't very difficult.

Second time taking her, have taken Conflict Ec 1916 and now American Econ History 3470. In 3470, we had 3 papers about one long book (800pgs), Ages of American Capitalism by Levy. Late grader. Class is very participation based; you teach a few chapters of the book for a week as a group. Fair grade. She loves what she teaches.

Easy class overall if you aren't interested in economics. Take it asynchronously if you want less work. There is a big group project which takes a lot of time each week, so make sure you have a good group and you get to choose your group in the beginning of the semester.

I don't know why this professor got such bad reviews, she's entertaining, kind, caring, responsive, and easy grader. There are reading, graded outlines and 3-4 test units but the concepts is so easy to understand it's really not stressful at all. I don't think the in person lectures add anything to the textbook but she gives detailed explanations.

So far, definitely the most useless class and professor I've had at Northeastern. Professor sets her things up for 10-15 mins each day while we sit in complete silence and do nothing. Her teaching is poor, takes very long to explain concepts, and doesn't really do any in-class examples to prepare for the test. Would not recommend
Took Conflict Econ 1916. Hard material, not recommended as first econ course. Gave make up exams. IMO lectures too slow for content. Great TA Roy.

As long as you do the homework and readings, you'll be fine. Late homework is accepted with a 10% penalty 3 days after it was due, you'll have 5 tests and the lowest is dropped, and your lowest two lowest homework grades. All in all I think she's pretty fair, not that much interaction bc it's online, but she emails back pretty quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The entire class is asynchronous and relies only on the textbook. You're graded on tests, homework and a group project. It's heavy reading and homework but the project isn't that difficult. She explains how to do the proper steps and as long as you're coordinated with your group you should be fine. Only take this if you're okay with reading online.

Took Professor Dupree asynchronously during Summer II and did not enjoy it in the slightest. She doesn't lecture, just assigns textbook chapters and homework. Overall pretty easy to do well if you put in the work, but not a fun course.
Easy class fully virtual easy A as long as you do the work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is extremely easy to pass and all exams are easy. She drops your two lowest homeworks and your lowest test score. There is a multi-part group project but she gives clear instructions and walks you through it step by step. I did however take this class online and not sure how in person class is.

Took this class online and asynchronously, so barely interacted with the professor at all. Everything is taught through textbook readings and homeworks, no lectures. Basically a self-taught course but easy to get an A if you put in the work. One big group project, easy grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: This is a terrible class to take online. I've never met the professor or directly interacted with her, and I'm pretty sure it's the same for everyone else in the class. There is a ridiculous amount of reading every week, too many exams, and the group project is such a pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her class is pretty okay if you read the textbook, but I barely learned anything. Literally no interaction with the student.. way too much homework sometimes...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Here are something I wish I knew before taking Dupree's ECON1115 class -it's completely asynchronous (besides going to office hours ONCE, I've never met her) -it's all taught through online textbooks (if you don't read you're done) -be ready to schedule yourself. 1 hr of recitation is all you get. I made a time table so that I'd get stuff done
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very nice. I'm not sure what people are on about with her NUstart/online class being difficult. The readings and homeworks each week can be done properly in 3-4 hours just by reading through and comprehending the material before doing the homework problems. Tests are shortish and are no problem if you study a bit - or Google the answers.

ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE. How are these teachers so disconnected from there students? Ridiculous amounts of work for an intro econ class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS ONLINE. The group project is an ABSOLUTE NIGHTMARE and this lazy piece of crap literally doesn't do any work. She makes US grade each other's work. Such a waste of time and money

For an intro online class during a pandemic, it's WAY too much work and a confusing format. 2 homeworks per chapter (20 chapters), discussions, 5 tests, 5 parts to a group project, and peer reviews. Barely any teaching done by prof. I'm so confused where to go for what assignment. This prof was not meant for online teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: The format is absolutely terrible. Apart from one group project the whole class is conducted through Cengage Mindtap, a textbook software. All homework assignments and tests are conducted through this and most of the actual teaching as well. The prof is available outside of class but not super helpful. Overall a waste of time and money.

Like all other reviews, Professor Dupree is highly relaxed in terms of attendance. You cannot show up all semester and still receive an A regardless. There is a presentation at the end of the semester which you will have to go. I gave her a 4/5 because you will not learn in class, all exams and HW are online and in Chegg. The textbook is $100!

Definitely the easiest macro theory class as it is not quantitative heavy at all. Make friends with the smartest kids in the class because she lets you do homeworks and exams together (Exams are take home). Also get a tutor for the exams. Not sure how much I ended up learning through this method but she is a very nice professor and is very caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dupree is a very kind person and professor. She is very accommodating and understanding. The tests and quizzes are online, which makes doing well in the class much easier. One nice thing is that she does actually teach, for those who want to learn. She goes over the presentations and clearly understands and conveys the material. Great professor!

First level of difficulty is called "show up and you'll pass". In this class you don't even have to show up to pass. Test and quizzes are taken online, you can find all the answers and solutions in the internet. Final project she will just take a look at the poster and discuss it with you. If you have a heavy semester - take it, easy A.

Professor Dupree is a great choice if you're looking for a laid back class. Attendance wasn't mandatory, and all the tests and homeworks were online; this makes it very easy to get a good grade. However, with this system, you'll only learn anything if you put the effort in, which is pretty much optional. Overall, she is very nice and accommodating.

Prof. Dupree is great! She's super funny and amusing tbh. She really knows what she's talking about, but might overlook the fact that the students do not so be sure to ask questions. All assignmentsincluding midterm and finalsare online so it's fairly easy to get a good grade. Just read the power points, show up to class, and do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Funny guy and good professor here at northeastern. Homeworks are long and hard, but I guess that's expected when you take Advanced Linear Algebra. Lectures are good and have bits of comedy in them. Responds quickly and thoroughly to all questions on piazza. Overall good stuff!
Incredible professor!

I had Dr. Dummit for MATH3543 and WOW! It was an amazing class! Dr. Dummit was funny when he taught the class and he was a great teacher too! I highly recommend you attend his classes and OHs are a good way to catch up. Overall, the class was amazing and I would take another class with Dr. Dummit again!

*MATH3543. Hands down the best math professor at NEU. The math department here is underfunded and understaffed, but there is a small batch of great professors, and he is definitely one of them. In terms of class, homework can be time-consuming, but it is well thought out and will help you understand the material. If you like math, take his course.

The actual content may be difficult, but the professor explains all concepts in a formulaic and engaging way. The lectures are accessible, but it's very easy to fall behind. The tests are much easier than the homework and the study guides, so as long as you do them well, you can get a good grade. TLDR: content is hard, tests easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a super good teacher, I will be taking his class again simply because of how good the lectures are. Tests count most of the grades, be ready to do a lot of homework, and actually learn the stuff.

Professor Dummit is talented at describing extremely complex mathematical concepts. However, if you miss even a minute, you are at risk of falling behind -- attend all classes, and unless you're ready for a LOT (and I mean a LOT) of homework, don't accelerate the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All around a great professor, and if you haven't found this before, look up ChipsChallenge fandom wiki, and search for Evan_Dummit. The man has his own damn wiki page in this random game I've never heard of. If that ain't qualifications, I don't know what is.

Couldn't have asked for a better math teacher. The kind of guy where attendance isn't mandatory but you still show up to class because he's so good at teaching. Tests are reasonable. Homework might take a few hours but is manageable especially with piazza.
Good prof

Does an excelent job explaining concepts. While his homework does take a really long time to complete, the modterms are pretty easy in comparison and he is a very generous grader -- giving lots of partial credit.
Great lectures and notes, a bit too much homework though. If you put in the work, you'll be able to get a good grade.

His lectures were amazing, as he clearly knows so much about the topic and is always willing to answer further questions. The homework is difficult and pretty much impossible to do if you start day-of, but if you start beforehand you'll be ok, and the tests are much easier than the homework. Overall difficult, but very rewarding class!

Dummit is the most talented math professor at NEU. His lectures and (detailed) notes are extremely easy to follow and interesting. He knows so much about a breadth of topics. His homeworks are extremely long but rewarding, and he is very fair when it comes to grading. I highly recommend taking any of his courses, you'll learn a lot.

This was a pilot version, so I was the lab rat. Professor Dummit knew how to explain his content thoroughly and was good at leaving notes online and was easy to review. That said, he did give intense homework and can assume you have learned a topic before. Good professor overall
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dummit's courses are a fabled right of passage at Northeastern. MATH 4527 was one of the most demanding classes I've taken. Incredibly heavy material is compacted into just 4 months. That being said, the course taught me a lot and was very enjoyable. Time seems to fly when you're having fun or when you're finding reduced quadratic forms.

Evan Dummit is a great professor. His lectures are always so engaging and his homework is usually straightforward. If you read his notes, it usually does not take a long time. Also, there are only 3 exams, which are generally very passable. Overall, you should take his class as it will boost your gpa without having a lot of work.

The homework can be very difficult, the midterms are usually easier. Attendance in lectures isn't mandatory but you won't get by if you try to read the posted notes because they are very dense and can be confusing.

The notes work great to review what you've learned already, but it's still useful to write your own.
Great professor for 3081. Explains in a calm and collected fashion - types out notes on canvas and supplies great review sheets for exams. Would totally take again.

It's only been two weeks but I've already found myself to be a lot more engaged and interested in Professor Dummit's class. His explanations are clear and concise, and the questions he works through are challenging but lead to a deeper understanding of the subject. One of the best teachers you could take 3081 with.
Great teacher, would def take again. Highly recommend.

Evan Dummit was an excellent professor in just about every way. It was clear that he had an enthusiasm for the material and would always provide excellent examples and feedback. He also created a ton of supplementary material that helped immensely with learning any confusing material. I would recommend any math course his name is attached to.

In one word: amazing. Evan is clear during his lectures and manages to make linear algebra intuitive and simple. I have taken another linear algebra course at NEU and the difference between the courses (the content was virtually identical) is insane. Homework is standard, once a week. For tests, he grades super fast so you always know your grade.

An excellent professor. His lectures are excellent and convey really advanced material in a digestible way, and his lecture notes are superbly written. If something comes up and impacts your ability to do well in the course, he'll accommodate. He genuinely cares his students.
I enjoyed his class immensely. Evan Dummit is a brilliant professor and his notes are amazing. I recommend taking any class he lectures at NEU.
Loved this class, expectations were very clear and he gave really good feedback.

Professor Dummit is the best! Knows everything there is to know about the material he is teaching, and gives great lectures. The material and practice problems are exactly like the exams. Has a great sense of humor, too.

Absolutely amazing professor. I guarantee you will not regret taking any course that he teaches. His brilliance and extensive knowledge on all areas of mathematics are obvious. He is a very pleasant guy. He makes every concept so simple and easy to understand and provides proofs for everything. Overall 10000000/10. Take his class fr.

Evan Dummit is a fantastic professor and a great person. He is really funny and I feel bad for him since I would be laughing during class, but my mic was on mute all the time. If you attend lectures and do the online project sets (which were immensely helpful) you will enjoy the class. Plus he writes his own notes that are better than any textbook.

Adjusted very well to COVID struggles and has very informational lectures.  The no questions asked homework extensions are amazing and the default extra time for exams has been very helpful.  Makes these calculus concepts seem effortless.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dummit is one of the best professors I've had at NEU. He made the hardest topics of Probability + Stats straightforward and clear, and he truly cares about his students. He added in policies throughout the semester to help students (midterm drop, final exam percentage choice), and is overall such a cool and funny guy.

I forgot to do my Trace evaluations, so I'm gonna give my brother a bit of love here. In short, Evan is incredibly fair and transparent; he doesn't make you pay for a textbook, he doesn't have pop quizzes, and if you take the time to study, you will get an A. He is also funny. Take his class if you can. Seriously.
Great professor. He's funny and his lecture notes are thorough and easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dummit is one of the best instructors I've ever had. He's an absolute genius and makes extremely hard topics and math seem intuitive and straight forward. His lectures are incredible, and his free notes are better than most math textbooks out there. His grading is super fair, and he cares that you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Duncan is the goat, lenient when grading tests, overall easy homework, amazing guy, amazing energy and enthusiasm, and great at teaching the curriculum especially compared to other cornerstone profs! 6 pages are allowed for every in-person test which is usually more than enough.

He's not bad- kind of a yapper and does a lot of random stuff. Felt like the class was a lot of busy work, but he tries his best. Some things are challenging but you'll be ok, it's an easy A if you put in a little bit of effort.

Great professor with extremely kind grading. He genuinely cares about his students and their wellbeing, offering tons of opportunities for extensions and extra credit. Email responses are extremely quick and he is obviously very well versed in the topics, offering good advice.

One of the best profs I've had. Amazing guy, committed to our best experience possible. I learned a lot from him. The whole class is game themed which was fun and the projects interesting. He knows his stuff and is super reasonable. GE 1502 tests were mostly online 10 attempts. Take cornerstone with Davis if possible, you won't regret it!

Dr. Davis is an amazing professor. Lectures were very helpful and done very well. The group project is well structured and quite fun, try not to get too behind with it though. You will learn in this class if you put even just a little effort in. He is very understanding and always offers free extensions. C++ tests are in person but are manageable.

Great professor that can give you a solid intro to coding, design, and team-oriented projects. All tests and quizzes are very manageable, and he allows you to bring cheat sheets. The C++ exam and quiz were both on paper, not online. Grading for the final project was very lax, even if your project wasn't the best. Very passive aggressive sometimes.
Love him, very fun and engaging classroom. Homework wasn't without challenge but always had some funny theme to it. Encouraged creativity and learning
Very approachable and obviously interested in the material. If you go to class, you will be fine.

Really solid teacher for an intro-level class. you don't need to put in tons of effort to come out with an A, but high effort will be rewarded with bonus points. Just don't use AI on coding until past midterms for HW or on the online exams, only time I've seen this guy get mad.

Professor David is a wonderful person. Lectures are very good! In the first half of the semester you'll have to work a little harder so that the required homework does't have to be done in parallel with projects when semester ends. Don't use ChatGPT for homework&tests, he sees this very clearly and can resort to the measure of C++ tests on paper.
Dr Davis is awesome. He has very clear expectations and is available and willing to help you. He is very accessible via email and is chill with extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very enthusiastic. The tests are well structured. The homework is helpful, but so long that at one point in time it is no longer helpful but just tedious. He has a very hyper- "You're an adult, toughen up" mentality to a point where it's not even an adult thing but just a power trip. The class is also unorganized especially the final project.

Dr. Davis is very enthusiastic about engineering and games. Overall this was a good class, however, there is lots of long homework assignments one every week. Not great at lectures, and explaining the material. Class time felt rushed.  Most learning was done through the homework. Overall though a caring proffesor, who wants you to do well.

GREAT! I took for engineering design and i loved it! hes very entertaining and class is super interactive -- you get out what you put in. quizzes are 10 tries and open note and homework is mostly pretty fun (room to be creative), definitely takes some time though. unique class format and learned a bunch -- built escape room as final project!

A well-designed class that made learning the material a lot easier. There was a lot of homework, but it was created well so that you actually learn the concepts that were taught, and there wasn't any busy work. Dr. Davis is very enthusiastic about teaching and knows the content well. He wants his students to succeed and does not grade too harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, made Cornerstone so fun and really cares about his students. Only class I actually enjoyed this semester tbh

Fantastic experience with this prof. Really cares about making sure you learn all the skills he is teaching. Is willing to change his plan of actions based on feedback. Very knowledgeable and capable to help. I do recommend you try to come into his Cornerstone I class with some coding experience, it will make your life easier. Assignments were fun!

This class is not easy with no experience. The concepts and software, if you are unfamiliar with them, are difficult. However, prof. Davis was a really good professor and was happy to help you out with anything. A good part about his class was that he provided examples for the concepts. There was a lot of homework, but it was necessary. Great dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Could not recommend Dr Davis any higher. He's the highlight of my day every time I get to go to class, he's super caring and genuinely makes an effort to know every student, and he gets you thinking in fun, productive ways about cool topics. Bonus points if you're into games, Dr Davis loves them and includes them in class as much as he can.
Hands down my favorite professor due to his enthusiasm and excitement. Such a goofy guy and was a pleasure to be in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Extremely lively guy with lots to teach and alot of enthusiasm for teaching. Makes his students his #1 priority and is extremely dedicated towards making sure everyone understands new concepts and can apply them effectively.
What a man, dude is a highlight in my day
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Incredibly effective teaching, for me, and very engaging and fun

Fully admits he is terrible at explaining material and writing instructions. Homework is very difficult to follow and seems to take off points randomly. Not usually very helpful when using programs. He's very into puzzles though if you are into that.
Constant lecture - nothing really related to marketing - just a bunch of random stuff for an hour and a half.

Really nice prof but bad grading. You will get a 3.5/4 no matter what you do. Your entire grade is determined by the final project and participation. He says attendance is not mandatory but it counts towards participation and if you get a B in that you will get a B overall. I don't feel like I learned anything I didn't already know.

Take home chapter (30 pages each) quizzes before almost every class. He likes super outgoing students, so SIT IN THE FRONT. He tells everyone "speak up!" "I can't hear you" constantly, makes it hard to participate then harshly grades participation. Lectures are summary of chapters, repetitive. Easy concepts but do not recommend this prof.

JUST SHOW UP AND YOU WILL BE FINE. This class is not difficult as long as you participate in class and show up for daily attendance. He is a nice guy, as you show interest in what he is teaching. Grading can be a little unclear, but overall, it's great. Do not question your grade because it will not change. You get what you get.

Every week we had a quiz based on the last chapter we read and it is open note and at home, basically just homework. Our mid-term and final were the same thing, only he was more strict with grading the final. We had a group project, but we were graded on our presenation and not the project itself. I would recomemnd this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Easiest class I've had at northeastern. Class was cancelled like half the time as well. Only thing that is “hard” is participation but if you speak once a class it's fine. Would recommend to anyone who isn't a marketing major!

Easiest professor. All quizzes are online and open note. Grade is determined by one simulation project. You don't have to do good on the simulation, you just have to have a good presentation. If you participate a LOT in class, he will like you. Sit in the front, and laugh at his jokes. If you actually want to learn marketing, don't take him.

Easy A. Durant wants everyone to do well, and half the time he cancels class or lectures super quickly and lets you out early. Class consists of weekly quizzes (online, not lockdown), a group project, and an easy exam. He is lazy and it is boring, but it's very light and easy. He also seems experienced which is a plus.
Disaster. Cancels any class, whenever he wants to, and provides an unworthy excuse. However, for students, he does not excuse absences and is extremely strict. Not caring

Great professor who knows his stuff and has an infectious personality. I thoroughly enjoyed the majority of his lectures. The class is merely matching deep thinking common sense and buzzwords. Assignments are easy to follow and easy to do. He's a great professor who cares about his students future. Take him, take him, and take him. You won't regret

Graded by a few things for sure. Rob makes this class very easy. There's no taste, but there are home (non lockdown) quizzes on each chapter. Do well on those, understand basic concept, you are going to be just alright. There is one group project, ace that, you don't have to worry.

Professor Durant is one of the most unprofessional professor I've had during my time in Northeastern. He doesn't explain the concepts well in class and seems uninterested in teaching. His motto is "I want you to fail" and he takes that too literally making it impossible to get an A; hard A-. Not a good grader too, very subjective grading.

Thought this would be an easy class at first, but he quickly became passive aggressive as people did not participate/slacked off. Instead of correcting this, he would give very low grades on the few graded assignments (THE CLASS HIGH WOULD BE UNDER 90). It's hard to imagine how anyone could've ended with an A. Did not learn much. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: do not take this professor! his lectures are very boring, and is a harsh grader for participation. the highest participation grade was 85%. easy class in the beginning, but refuses to give full credit on the presentation/paper at the end of the semester. you have no control over your grade

Honestly he was a very lazy professor. He was funny at first, but his lectures are so boring. No one participates and instead of trying to fix the issue, he just has the kids present the slides to each other. Also he doesn't hold students accountable in group projects. I ended up doing all the work for my group but not the grade to reflect my work.
Easiest class in the business school and the best marketing professor. His grading is so light and he wants you to succeed. He is a professor you want to take for marketing no matter what.

Super easy A. Not a very interesting class because he basically just reads the chapter summary during class. To do well in this class, make sure you do well on the weekly online quizes, take the marketplace simulation seriously, and participate in class. You don't really have to ever read the actual chapter, just go to the chapter summary.

At first, I thought this class was going to be the easiest class I ever took at Northeastern and quite frankly it was. But he switched up really fast. His lectures are boring and consist solely of fluff. I didn't learn a thing in his classes. Assignments were pretty easy. But participation and attendance are mandatory.

He's great at the start... don't take him if you actually want to learn marketing. His classes are extremely mandatory, or your grade will drop to a 15%. Little homework and his lecture provided absolutely nothing, but he made the class easy to pass... unless you don't participate or show up. No midterm and the final is a joke (one page paper).

Course was very boring and repetitive.  Did not actually learn anything important and the professor was not understanding.  Put over 80% of the grades in during the last week and the highest participation grade was an 85%.  Do not take if you actually want to learn anything and have actual control over your grade.

Very easy but also very boring. Grades were put in at the end and he was kind of harsh especially with stuff like the presentation and participation. If you're a marketing concentration and looking for an informative and exciting introduction to your major -- this isn't it. If you're looking for an easy A to knock out a requirement -- this is it.
Great class, informative lectures, very passionate. Only negative is attendance is mandatory

I had a great time in Dr. D's class. The lectures were thought-provoking and he cares about his students. Tests are worth a lot but aren't too difficult. Absolutely take the class if transportation even remotely interests you!

Great guy, even better professor. Dr. Dulaski's lectures were incredibly engaging and useful if you're someone interested in multimodal transportation. Keep in mind he's very test-heavy (like 80% of overall grade), but if you go to class and engage with the content you'll have nothing to worry about.

I was so grateful to be in Dr. D's transportation class. I loved starting class with transportation news, keeping the class up to date with current events. Class content was engaging and if you payed attention in class exams, while worth a lot, were not very difficult. Would recommend to anyone interested in transportation!

Amazing guy, AMAZING professor. Keeps you very engaged in class and makes sure that you understand every concept you'd be expected to know. Have him for CIVE4554 and had for Statics, has been fantastic in both and has clear expectations of his students. Only complaint I have is he is very hard to reach via email.

I've taken five classes with Dr. D during my time at Northeastern. Take his classes. They're usually difficult, but you learn a ton. He deeply cares about his students and has unmatched passion for transportation. He is extremely detail-oriented, and accessible outside of class for help (book a meeting or go in-person!). Hands down my favorite prof
Dulaski is the greatest professor of all time. Love this guy
He's the best!
The GOAT. Cannot make statics any easier.

Can't recommend enough. Establishes a friendly, first-name relationship with EVERY student. Wants you to do well and will do everything he can to ensure you do well. Lectures were great, homework is helpful, and exams are very fair. Funny guy too.

Dulaski was such a great statics professor. He was so caring and kind and really wanted his students to be successful. He has been the best professor I have had at Northeastern and I could not recommend him enough. He does in fact call on you during class but it keeps you prepared. He also will not judge if you don't know the answer. Great guy.
Overall a GREAT teacher. Dulaski is a super nice and respectful person. He explains concepts well and encourages questions. I would 100% recommend and would definitely take again.

Professor Dulaski is a great Statics professor. While I took the class in summer so it was an accelerated course, he had reasonable tests and homework. His notes are very clear to follow and he always makes sure everyone understands the material. His tests don't trick you, they just ensure you are grasping the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor

Ran a bit like a high school class, short homework due almost every class, 6 exams throughout semester, calling randomly on students. Very good at communicating topics and helping students who aren't grasping at first. Respects students and commands respect in turn.
Great professor. Prepares you for the real world! More than any other professor. He expects a lot because he gives you a lot to learn.

Highway design was not an easy class, requirements for hw format were pretty strict, final project took time, especially design part in CAD. However, it's been a year since I took this course and I still have all the info left in my brain. Lots of work but it was worth it. Also by the end of the semester the class turns into almost a family.

Talk. If not, he'll call on you. Do practice problems for  midterm and final. There is also a paper due for this class. I recommend do the paper from AWD on transportation and use it again for his class. Homework take forever to do but that's just him. Remember, MEMO formats. His class gets harder each time he teaches it. Highway and Transportation
worst! choose the other professor. she conducts exams completely unrelated to what she taught. The professor seems to not have a clue about what she is saying and her syllabus is outdated.
Great class!

Public School Professor
A Employed person
Never Taking it again

The professor just rushed in the last and we students ended up losing marks in the last homework because she missed out on discussing the possibilities of a specific type. 
The TAs are inconsistent , the grading was unfair.
Especially in the exams too many questions to solve, which made us losing our grades further.

Worst professor I've met in Northeastern University. There are too many homework and tests.Each task requires a substantial amount of time to interpret, as the instructions are often unclear. TAs grade the homework without standard rubric, seem to reflect individual interpretations rather than a standardized approach.
The class was very boring and the professor seemed to agree with any solution brought up by the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not recommend this professor. The material itself is not difficult, however the professor behaves very spitefully towards students when it comes to grading, and generally communicates in very inappropriate condescending manners. Exams have near impossible time limits, and participation points are given however she feels like.

My biggest complaint is her lack of professionalism. She responds to piazza posts in condescending tones (all caps, sounds irritable, etc). Was a no-show for one of her office hours, no explanation given. Her exams are difficult and there are 3 (also a project). Her grading scale is weird (can only get an A with 95%). Lectures are painfully boring.

The content covered in the class can be readily acquired through YouTube tutorials, requiring minimal time and costing nothing. Regrettably, I feel the class did not provide any value for the money and time invested. Moreover, the professor's assistance outside of class was notably lacking.

The professor spent weeks explaining some really simple concepts repeatedly. She doesn't seem to realize she's teaching master students. Sometimes she doesn't seem to like students asking her questions either. The course doesn't include some important database concepts. If you want to take an easy class and don't expect to learn much, take this.
Curriculum seems outdated. Needs update

While the professor is knowledgeable of SQL concepts, she is not commanding enough during the class. She tends to accept solutions during lectures from students which makes it unclear and vague to understand the concepts. The lectures are very boring unless you interact. The exams can get scary if you don't manage time.

Well-structured online course, but lectures are very long and there are so many of them. The tests are 51% of the grade and are based on all the lecture videos. Professor Durant offers study sessions each week to go over the materials, which is helpful though. Definitely not an easy A as it is a 95-100 grading scale, so be ready to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Very lecture heavy, but lectures were boring. The amount of work was overwhelming. For an asynchronous class, there wasn't a good sense of an online community. 

Directions for assignments can be unclear, and if you ask questions on piazza it is also hard to get a clear answer.

The pre-recorded lectures are well structured, so I rarely went to lectures. There is a final group project of 1-3 people which was a great way of applying class knowledge on a domain of interest. The negative part of this class is that your grade depends on 3 exams, each worth 17% of your grade. Prof.'s office hours are great for learning.

Grade distribution is very weird. 1 exam holds almost equal weightage to the other 10 assignments. Very average teaching. Apart from SQL stuff, she isn't able to convey her dbms knowledge to the students.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the professor's lecture. The grading criteria were clear so there wasn't a surprise when the marks came out.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Professor Kathleen is very caring and teach with a lot of passion. You will learn a lot from her lectures. Make sure to read the book before every lecture. Homeworks are easy. 

Exams are long and you have to be very very careful about time management. Practice as much as you can before every exam. There are 3 in total (51% of total grades).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Assignments took hours every single week. Not sure if it was the content being extremely difficult or the teaching but I'm assuming it was a mix of both. Between the weekly videos and the assignments I saw the excel screen more than I saw my own family this semester.

I figured it couldn't be too bad since it was asynchronous, but I was apparently very wrong. professor durant makes just about all the lecture videos which are extremely time consuming (about 3-4 hours worth of videos alone) each week and they are rarely ever helpful for the assignments. instructions are unclear and she is very unhelpful in piazza.

I really enjoyed Professor Durant's class. I thought her lectures were clear and extremely thorough. She also held copious office hours (more than any other professor I have had at NEU), which was truly appreciated. She also looked to give partial credit on exams wherever it was available.

Gives you almost everything you need to succeed in class lecture. Skim the reading before hand, answer a few questions, and you will be set. Start the final project early. Most homework can be completed in about an hour. First 2 tests are hardest. The homework exactly covers the material for tests.

Prof. Durant is a very understanding professor. She is clearly passionate about Databases and would love to give you practical advice from her career experience.

I did find her exams to be tedious - not difficult and found myself not having enough time to complete the Test, but the Prof. was understanding and curved the results.

Professor is a very nice person but can be dry and fairly confusing about material - reading textbook seems to give equal if not better information. She's extremely helpful in OH though. Poor grading scheme, classmates and I would receive different grades on same submission because of TAs. HWs are often unrelated to class or test content.
Nice person, easy material, horrible lectures
Easy homework, tough exams with unreasonable amount of time, unfair exam (students will receive different questions with different difficulty)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Lectures are unclear and hard to follow. I think I could've learned the course material in half the time. As other's have mentioned, she simply reads off of her notes and doesn't seem to really know what she is talking about.
For 80% of the time, her lecture has nothing to do with her homework. Tough tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is often disorganized and confused about her own content. Seems like a nice person but I wouldn't take a class with her again. This class became very confusing very quickly and most students in my class agreed with me on this.

She's definitely making progress, at least as a professor for a remote class on Canvas. She organized logistics very clearly on a separate website, including every week's schedule, readings, assignments, grades... etc. , which made me feel safe remotely. The database course needs many readings prepared for each lecture. Intensive but fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Where do I even begin? She is a very bad teacher. I tried to keep an open mind and not take the negative comments too serious, but I 100% agree. She is the worst teacher. She goes way too fast in class and expects you to follow along. Best advice: just go to class b/c easy points and then go to ALL the TA hours even though some of them are bad too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So Prof. Durant is not a great lecturer, because the lectures are really dry. But she is an incredibly nice person, and if you have an issue, she will do what she can to help you. She knows a lot about databases, and if I went to her office hours with a specific question, she really helped, I just wish she was the same in class. Tests on the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She doesn't know what she's doing at all and mostly reads off the powerpoints for the class. Going to lecture is honestly less important than making sure you know what's on the powerpoints, because that's all the assessments are. The homeworks are for the most part unrelated to class and sometimes don't even factor into the test.

Her lectures are mind-numbing, and you are genuinely better off staying at home teaching yourself. If you ask any questions about the homework, she will rarely if ever give you anything helpful (I'm convinced she just had the TAs create the homework assignments, which are confusing but that's a different matter). Stay at home, read the book, do HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Durant is a terrible lecturer. The way she teaches makes it almost impossible to learn even a small amount of the material in class. I regret showing up to lectures as I think its just a waste of time. The best way to succeed in this course it teaching yourself and preparing yourself for tests using the textbook and the course material
The lecture doesn't help you learn. There are few people left in the classroom at the end of the semester. Homework is not related to what was covered in class, and I taught myself nearly everything.

Prof. Durant is very kind, she cares about her students and wants them all to do well in her class. She is an easy grader in general. The one critique of her is that her lectures are somewhat boring. She talks for a while and sometimes it is difficult to stay concentrated 100% of the time; the good news is you don't need to be at 100% to succeed.

This lady absolutely has no idea what she is doing. I feel like she relies on the the class to solves the problems that she assigns, simply because she does not know how to do them. She is a nice lady, but the class is an incredibly waste of time. Do not recommend.

I took her in the excel and access class and it was the best thing I could have done. She was so helpful and would stay after class ended to help me with things I was struggling with. If you are an econ major, take her ASAP. Half of my classes use Excel and I know what I am doing thanks to her assistance.

You can Ace the class if you get help from the people that have already passed the course. She has 2 huge screens to show us examples and decides to do problems on the board which is so counterproductive. She is very boring to the point that you will probably decide to skip after a few weeks.
Great course covering the important background of advanced machine learning !

Really liked her machine learning class. It's a very tough class, broad and math heavy but if you are attentive you will gain a solid foundation for machine learning. She is both very knowledegable about ML and over the years has mastered the way to teach it. The HW can be a little intense but they are doable. Tough exams too
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is willing to help if you ask.  Not the best explainer.  Class was pretty easy, her slides are straight forward.  Accent is not an issue, just humerous.

Digital Logic is a fairly easy class, her lectures are straight review of the homework so you can pay attention if you want or just teach yourself from the book (most of the class is easy enough to do this).  Very unclear and doesn't have the best command of the english language (though I've seen worse).
A good teacher, passionate about math, but not teaching.

He gave us quizzes that were intended for us to fail. We would ask for examples of how concepts would be applied on the quizzes, and he would scold us for asking, and refuse to give examples. One time, to spite us, he decided not to write on the board the entire class and described a 3D graph to us, using only his hands. So yeah.

Pretty good at explaining the larger concepts behind the math and connecting it to real world applications. It was Calculus 3, so it was still a fairly difficulttough class. Grading is fair. Quiz problems were usually based on text book examples, but tests were hard. Had extra study sessions before final. Generally good teacher.

Dylan is a good professor. He is a very good Mathematician and obviously loves Math. His lectures are generally clear and he is very helpful during office hours. That said, he isn't necessarily easy! Quizzes and assignments do tend to be pretty rough once in a while and he sets high standards of high grading. Overall, a great teacher!

So weird. I am in her class at another college and it's like she doesn't prepare for her lectures at all. There will be pauses that last minutes as she scrambled to find the materials she needs. Seems to me that her expertise is in subjects other than what she's teaching. so so weird.

I appreciated the class structure, with each week building off the previous material. I also enjoyed the peer-review forums. Professor Dygert provided clarity and constructive criticism, responded to my questions, and met with me via Zoom. The work in this class is what's expected from a grad-level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I never write a bad review cause I don't believe in it. As a student, you'll always have areas for improvement. But this is like she is waiting for you to fail her class. She would say that your topic has great materials and well-cited, but it's still weak. Don't give feedback to her feedback, she doesn't take well to it.

She is ridiculous because she won't tell you that your topic does not work, she let you finish it, and then give you really lower grade. If you have any questions about your project, she just tells you your project is great, you should work on it, and other lower grades are not important, you will get a good grade on your final proposal. F end.

Dylan clearly cares about the topics he teaches but his class was not challenging by any means. There were two exams, a presentation, and one paper--all were graded extremely leniently. He attempts to give feedback but it is sometimes lacking in substance. Nice guy, not the best teacher.

Took him for intro to Intl Relations last semester. He's a really tough grader and there is a lot of work for the papers. He's accessible in office hours but has very high expectations and criticism isnt always constructive or helpful. You'll learn a lot though if you can keep up with him.

I took Professor Maguire's International Relations in my freshman year and I wouldn't regret it at all. Sure, theres a lot of reading and he may be a sort of tough grader, but what I learned in his class was absolute superb. I'd never learn what I learned from one class than in any other class I took. This was my first political science class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Dyer was great. He is deeply passionate about the subject matter and really cares that we all understand all the nuances of the origins of economics. His tests are long answer and require some work but his lectures make it worth it. I'm going to miss this class
Awesome.

Dyer was a great History of Econ Thought professor. You will learn about more than raw theory with Dyer. He really appreciates how culture influences on our ideas, and presents the social/religious conventions of various historical time periods, the personal lives of great thinkers, and the actual theories developed in reaction to that environment.

history economic thought. very interesting class with a responsible teacher who doesnt manipulate his students in believing what he believes. all lecturing, extremely boring (u will fall asleep), 2 tests, small project. You learn a lot but do not take his class if u dont have to, it is hard and you will feel like a zombie.

Took this class in 2009 and still have yet to find its equal.  Dyer is the most brilliant, thoughtful, and humble professor I have ever met.  He is one of the few professors you may have that goes against the grain in their field.  This class is an opportunity to significantly expand your worldview, at least it did for me.

I don't like writing a bad review of someone, but I took a class after reading good reviews here, and regretted it. The tests are not hard, and the lectures are not boring. I'm sure you could do worse, by far; but I found myself wishing I could have taken the class with a different prof.
Good professor, but can be a little confusing sometimes. You have a midterm, final, and a project. But he gives you the test questions ahead of time.

Dyer is the best professor I've had. Ever. You can tell he puts a lot of effort into being a good teacher, i.e. planning lectures. Either that or it just comes very easy to him. Very nice guy too. Workload isn't hard with him.

prof. dyer is hands down the best prof. I have had at nu. his lectures r unique and very interesting. u won't fall asleep even in the 100min class! the midterm and the final account for alot of the grade and are fairly hard. u'll need to take very good notes and make sure u ask questions when stuff doesn't make sense, he's always willing to help.

Fantastic instructor. His lectures are clear and insightful, especially in the beginning. Towards the end of semester he started rushing to get more in. His work load is minimal for a 500 level course, but it makes you think a great deal. Take this course if you want to open your mind a little.

Highly recommend this class for any econ majors.  I'm not even an econ major, but I took it for the fun of it because I read about what a great teacher Dyer is, and it's completely true.  He's hard and makes you work, but you get a new appreciation for Economics, so it's worth it.
Professor Dyer is the best professor I have ever had. He is very professional and gives wonderful lectures.  I plan on taking more classes with Dyer.
This guy is the man, often lectures over the alloted time period, but everyone is so focused in you rarely notice.
A great teacher and asset to Northeastern's economics department. Very clear and straitforward when teaching, makes you think beyond the basic ideas.  Highly reccomend for any class.

Probably the single best professor I had at NU. Turned me on to a discipline I never thought I'd like, and was genuinely interested in helping me with post-grad choices. A class act and an asset to the school.
No Comments
OMG, someone get this guy a psychiatrist!  So weird, not a horrible teacher though.

Definately the BEST economics professors at Northeastern.  He really makes you open your eyes and think.  You're definately getting more than you paid for.  If you work hard, you'll do well in his class.  And he treats you with respect and doesn't have a holy than thou attitude.
Dr. Dyer is amazing. The best teacher I have EVER had. Challenging and respectful. He gives you a new perspective on economics and life. I would take ANY class he teaches.

By far the best professor I had at NU. Take his history of thought class or one of his ec history classes. He made me realize that economics is stimulating and thought provoking, not just number crunching and models. He is the reason I went to grad school.

Prof Dyer really made me interested in Economics Id recomend his classes to anyone. Anyone who doesnt get him is just not trying hard enough. Any chance to take a class with him the opportunity was jumped at and grabbed
The best teacher that I have had at Northeastern by far.

Professor Dyer is the ****. I would argue that he is really the only decent Professor in the department. Most of the others have their heads up their asses. And for all the clowns that couldn't handle Dyer... you're just too simple
So hard and chain smoked. Kind of a hippie guy who taught theory better than numbers and then tested on the numbers.
No Comments
Very helpful and committed to teaching SCUBA.
Sign up early. Dan is always willing to help. Definitely passionate about scuba.
Dan is an awesome instructor, swim lessons haven't been this much fun since I was 6
Sign up early because everyone wants it. Best class at NU. Dan is the man!
Best class ever!  He's great and fun.  The only class i wouldn't miss. Ha
Very generous with her extra credit and is willing to slow down the class and offer chances to get extra points for almost half of the assignments in the class. She is very caring and nice.
Class is crowded with Homework and quizzes. Overall interesting class combining lectures and Lab
flexible instructor and energetic. She is knowledgeable and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Heavy lecture and materials
Good course,
Despite the challenging and boring nature of the material, Prof. Ebrahimi's guidance and support significantly improved students' confidence and grades throughout the semester.

The lectures are quite intense, and the material is overwhelming. Despite missing some homework and lab submissions, I was able to get the grades I expected thanks to the bonus credits. Just make sure to talk to her during office hours.
Very easygoing and helpful instructor. Despite the huge workload, our entire team got A's. She is very enthusiastic about the course and cares about students' success.

This is a challenging class with a heavy workload of homework and labs, as it combines material that was previously taught in two separate courses. However, the section taught by Professors Ebrahimi and Iman is much more manageable and runs smoothly.

Professor Ebrahimi is very kind and approachable. At the beginning, she was not entirely sure about our needs, but by the middle of the semester, she recognized this and provided additional support and extra credit to help us succeed.
She is great very helpful and dedicated. She has always ensured that I was all on track and can catch up with my grades.

Prof. Ebrahimi is alright. It's unfortunate she requires attendance (5% of grade), and it might be the nature of the class, but the lectures are monotonous and mind numbing. However, she does genuinely want you to succeed and provides bonus point questions on quizzes and EC for a Trace review. Read the required textbook and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor gives quizzes that are way, way harder than the other sections and tries to make the students feel bad for not understanding her super confusing lectures, which are filled with tons of mistakes and overly convoluted explanations.

The professor is super energetic and really friendly! She is very good teacher and really cares that we understand the materials.  The class was pretty intense for a 2000-level course with a lot of homework and labs, but she has been flexible with rescheduling stuff and offering bonus tax. Definitely not boring compared to other!

Professor rarely showed up, I learned more from the TAs then I learned from the professor herself. Lots of homework. Overall the course was not bad it was just difficult to learn the material because the professor never showed up but would still have the class taught

Very clear lecturer and excellent at responding to questions. A few in class assignments that basically guaranteed As. 2 open note tests w/ multiple choice, fill in the blank, and short answer. Very accommodating with deadlines and cares about her students in and out of the classroom.
Lectures are pretty standard but her tests are literally the most straightforward tests ever so as long as you attend lecture and take notes you are guaranteed to do well on them.

She's an awesome teacher and extremely kind and flexible. Even after NU removed zoom requirements, she kept hers open in case any of us were absent and could only attend virtually! She's quick to respond to emails and clearly wants her students to learn in the most effective way possible. She always looks for feedback and is so down to earth!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Basic class in the sense that the content is very surface level and redundant. Prof Eby is very nice and accomodating. Multiple out of class activities, in class debates, 2 exams, and final group debate where you create your own debate. Overall interesting activities and pretty easy.

Mix of lectures, activities, field trips, exams, and presentations. Material could get a little boring or redundant at times but overall interesting and saw real world applications. Group article discussions and solo final presentations, 2 exams (midterm and final). Lecture slides not super clear so def come to class & take notes.

Really nice professor, easygoing & willing to help. Really cares about students' feedback. Like how grading is balanced with exams and projects, but can be a lot of homework. Clear about grading. Tests aren't terrible. Glad tests aren't ALL short answer. Interesting class that made me even more excited to pursue an environmental studies minor.

Dr. Eby is a really great professor. She is empathetic, approachable, and incredibly knowledgeable. She checks in with every student to make sure they are able to succeed, and she goes out of her way to help students when they are stuck on a project or confused by the material. Can't recommend her courses enough!

I've had Prof Eby for a few classes. Shes extremely nice and is an interesting lecturer if you like the material. She's easy going and always willing to help out if you have questions. She loves talking about research she's done as well which is cool.

This class is boring and she is not a good teacher. Her lectures have no flow or consistency, likely because she looks at her notes every 5 seconds which makes it seem like she doesn't really know what she's talking about even though I know she does. She seems like a kind person, but just is not a very good teacher. Pro: course isn't too difficult

Professor Eby is really helpful and wants you to succeed. For the final project(big chunk of your grade) you get to choose a topic that interests you. There was a huge range of topics and Prof Eby makes sure that your topic is do-able and certainly does not want you to fail. There's a graded worksheet each lab due the next lab, but she helps a lot.

This class is certainly lecture heavy, but it is necessary to go to lecture to do well in lab.  The lab work is the bulk of this class, be prepared to hunker down in front of a computer to get it right.  Tests are manageable if you study the lecture slides against the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved having Professor Eby as a teacher.  She's interested in getting to know her students, especially if you show up and get engaged in class.  She is also very passionate about her research and gives great examples based on her actual work.  Her tests are manageable, I got A's on most of them and didn't need to study for long periods of time.

If you don't need to take this class, do not take it and take something else to fulfill your credit. This class is tough and only those who seemed to enjoy it were going into a background of marine or environmental sciences. Her lectures are pretty boring if you're not into this stuff and the class has a lot of  statistical equations to memorize
I had fun...

Great guy! Passionate and good at teaching. It's maybe 3-5 hours of homework a week which I'd say is below average for engineering classes. Extremely interesting course material and exams are very fair. I didn't study much, but did all the homeworks, and got consistent Bs. Can't complain. Probably the best person to take energy systems with.

Professor Eckelman is a really really really nice guy who knows so so much about this course.
